- previsualization-application — 2026-09-08 — the shot-planning machine of screen production ("see it before you shoot it") whose defining core is exactly four jointly-held structures: the shot sequence as the plan of record (the scene-to-be held as an ordered, revisable sequence of shots grouped into scenes/sequences, each shot a planned camera view of a moment not yet produced; remove → shot-list app with no visualization) + a representational staging space (subjects/environment staged and each shot's view defined there — drawn panels with camera frames / 2D floor plan with camera-and-actor symbols / 3D set with posed actors, props and lights; substrate = product philosophy NOT invariant [sampled floor-plan product has no 3D, sampled board product is predominantly 2D]; remove → documents with nothing staged to look at) + timed rough playback (the animatic — the sequence plays as a deliberately lower-fidelity moving picture with durations, commonly sound, watching it is the evaluation act; remove → static board/layout tool = storyboard territory) + production-facing artifacts out (boards/storyboards, shot lists, camera diagrams/setup data, edit-ready animatic sequences incl. NLE-interchange; remove → creative 3D/diagram tool with no production loop); jointly-held is load-bearing (1 alone = shot list; 2 alone = set builder/diagram tool; 3 alone = video player/editor; 4 alone = office documents; 1+2 without 3 = static boards; 2+3 without 1 = 3D animation/diagram tool used creatively; 1+3 without 2 = arbitrary-frame animatic assembly — the storyboard seam); historical check passed at analog level (Leica reels/animatics + floor-plan blocking with standees and the director's viewfinder — combined analog practice satisfies all four legs; definition names no 3D engine/LiDAR/AI/cloud/era machinery); standard capabilities NOT definitional: camera realism (formats/lens/DOF — strong 3/4, board pole carries aspect-ratio frames only), within-shot motion machinery (tweens/keyframes), sound in the animatic (absent today in the floor-plan product), script import (explicitly roadmap-absent in same product), NLE round-trip vs one-way export (variant), lighting tools, libraries/templates of sets+camera setups, team sharing/sync, print surfaces, burn-ins/transitions, panel-timing capture; L3 vendor detail kept in notes: snap/replace shot-record semantics + percolation of set changes into snapped shots, diagram↔shot-list continuous two-way sync, Conformation feature mapping, Physical/Floating/Prop camera taxonomy, PoseCap/LiDAR-scan/AR-virtual-camera/AI prop-actor generation; boundaries: vs Storyboard Application JOINT REVIEW FLAGGED (§04.19 sibling unprocessed — shared panel/scene/animatic zone; a storyboard-industry-standard product ships full animatic+conformance while previz products export storyboards and one previs product self-labels "Storyboard Software"; candidate discriminator = center of gravity drawn-board craft vs staged-scene/camera-blocking planning; keep-both recommended, decision left to that pass), vs 3D Animation (plan vs finished performance; - student-success-platform — 2026-09-09 — the higher-education institution's student-success operation platform whose defining core is exactly four jointly-held structures: the enrolled-student success population of record (persistent identified student records enriched with success context — academic standing, engagement, support history — drawn from across the institution's systems, held and managed at both individual and cohort/population grain across terms; remove → SIS report layer / student data warehouse) + proactive success signals (students who may be off-track surfaced to staff without student-initiated contact — faculty-raised early alerts & progress reports, rules-based flags, engagement indicators, or predictive persistence models; the mechanism is a variant axis, the proactive surfacing is the invariant; remove → a reactive relationship tool or a passive report) + the coordinated intervention loop (each signal becomes tracked work across the institution's cross-office success network — screened/routed, assigned outreach [appointments, messages, tasks, notes, referrals] carried to recorded resolution, at single-student and campaign/population scale; remove → an alert feed nobody works, or a dashboard nobody coordinates through) + the success-outcome measurement layer (retention/persistence/progression tracked as managed measures at cohort/institution grain, with intervention/initiative effectiveness commonly attributed against those outcomes; remove → care coordination without the institutional outcome loop, or IR reporting over nothing); jointly-held load-bearing (1 alone = student data warehouse; 2 without 1+3 = alert feed; 3 without 1+2 = generic casework; 4 without 1–3 = BI/IR dashboard; 1+2 without 3 = watchboard nobody acts on; 1+3 without 2 = responsive casework = advising/case territory; 2+3 without 1 = anonymous alert handling; 1+2+3 without 4 = coordinated care without the outcome loop, the advising-adjacent pole); anti-overfit: predictive ML NOT definitional (faculty-raised flags and rules-based leading indicators satisfy the signal leg; paper-era retention office — early-alert referral forms + caseload cards + term-to-term persistence tallies — satisfies all four legs, historical check passed), advising machinery common-NOT-definitional (advisors one staff class inside the loop at every sampled product), case/referral objects common-NOT-definitional, campaigns/nudges/success plans/student companion apps/wellbeing pulse checks/AI layers/SIS-LMS integration spine all standard-NOT-definitional, enrollment-funnel and advancement machinery bundled-adjacent NOT definitional; JOINT REVIEW DISCHARGED — vs academic-advising-platform keep-both RATIFIED on that pass's proposed center-of-gravity seam, confirmed from this side (see Boundary Issues); boundaries held vs student-information-system-sis (official record vs operation layer; vendor-drawn SIS-contrast FAQ in-sample), student-case-management (issue casework vs population loop), student-services-portal (student front door vs staff operation), enrollment-management/recruitment-CRM (funnel vs persistence), customer-success-platform (§07 name collision), institutional-effectiveness-platform (program-grain vs student-grain measurement); sample: EAB Navigate360 + Civitas Learning Student Impact Platform + Watermark Student Success & Engagement + Salesforce Education Cloud Student Success module (all official product-page strength; help centers not reached — Watermark HC category confirmed only; no numeric limits asserted in final doc) (research/student-success-platform.md, applications/student-success-platform.md)

- contaminated-site-management (§21, processed 2026-09-07) vs environmental-data-platform (§21 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the environmental family — all four sampled products (ESdat, EQuIS, Locus EIM, EnFlection) are simultaneously strong candidates for the environmental-data-platform leaf; this pass holds the Type on the site-centered spine (site record + contamination profile + cumulative evidence + managed progression + retained register) vs a data-corpus center without a contamination lifecycle; joint review recommended when environmental-data-platform is processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with the site-lifecycle seam (current framing) or re-scope this leaf's population toward register/case-led products; secondary seams recorded for environmental-site-assessment (assessment execution vs assessment-as-record handoff) and environmental-remediation-management (project execution vs lifecycle phase + data streams; one sampled product spans remediation projects + O&M — overlap specimen), both siblings unprocessed — cross-reference recommended; agency/register pole (regulator cleanup-site registers with status codes and public lookup) documented at reduced strength — no agency register product directly reachable (TerraBase 403, state portals 403/404, Trihydro Azimuth retired), so if that pole turns out to be the environmental-data-platform pass's center of gravity, the two leaves may need a joint re-draw

- configure-price-quote-cpq (§07, processed 2026-09-07) vs sales-pricing-application + deal-desk-commercial-approval-platform + sales-order-capture + contract-to-order-platform (§07 siblings, unprocessed): CPQ embeds a quote-time pricing engine, discount-approval gates, and ends by design at the accepted quote as the commercial commitment; the pricing-management discipline (setting/governing prices), the cross-functional deal-policy center, and the order-capture/contract-to-order center belong to the unprocessed siblings — joint review recommended when each is processed (research/configure-price-quote-cpq.md §Boundary Findings)
- configure-price-quote-cpq (§07, processed 2026-09-07) vs product-configuration-management (§16 Manufacturing, unprocessed): sell-side configuration (valid sellable offer + computed price + quote) vs build-side configuration (BOM/variants/engineering change); the engineer-to-order CPQ pole (manufacturability validation at point of sale, design automation, configuration-lifecycle suites, on-prem) strains toward the manufacturing family while keeping the commercial quote loop at center — cross-check recommended when that leaf is processed (research/configure-price-quote-cpq.md §Boundary Findings)

- electrical-service-management (§29, processed 2026-09-07) vs small-business-field-service-management (§29 sibling, unprocessed): the researched five-product sample (Housecall Pro, Service Fusion, Kickserv, BuildOps, ServiceTitan) shows the identical structural spine (customer+location → electrical job lifecycle → electrician dispatch → invoice/payment) in both; the difference is trade semantics — electrical work as job content, electrical pricing/payment mechanics (flat-rate price books, per-line commissions, surcharging, phased billing), electrical-tuned dashboards, and the commercial-electrical extension (site-equipment/panel histories, certification-aware dispatch [single-product], compliance-form workflows, project/AIA-style billing); vendors themselves ship "electrical" as a preconfigured trade layer of one platform (Housecall Pro's own words: "preconfigured"; Service Fusion ~30 clone industry pages; ServiceTitan ~20 trade pages; Kickserv demonstrates the trade-agnostic pole) — probable trade-Variant relationship rather than two independent Types, consistent with the appliance-repair-management and cleaning-business-management passes; flagged for joint review when Small Business Field Service Management is processed (research/electrical-service-management.md §Boundary Findings 1); secondary note: commercial electrical poles bundle project machinery drifting toward Construction Project Management (§17, processed) — that pass's service-vs-project split is compatible with this pass's boundary and cross-reference is recorded in the leaf.

- sales-forecasting-platform (§07, processed 2026-09-07) — RESOLVES two prior flags: (1) DISCHARGES the revenue-intelligence-platform pass's joint-review flag from the forecasting side: ratified the adopted discriminator with forecasting-side evidence — sampled CRM-native forecast modules (Dynamics 365, HubSpot) carry no captured-engagement machinery in their forecasting features, and standalone forecasting platforms (Clari Forecast, Aviso) were sampled at forecast-module scope where their wider platforms include capture; split confirmed: Revenue Intelligence Platform = captured-engagement foundation + pipeline/deal inspection + projection together (an insight layer that observes selling activity), Sales Forecasting Platform = forecast production/roll-up as the primary object on CRM pipeline data without a captured-engagement foundation (CRM-native forecast modules and spreadsheet roll-ups belong to the forecasting side); both Types stand as separate leaves, both documents cross-reference; residual note: at module level the market sells forecasting inside revenue-intelligence platforms — treated as packaging, not Type merger. (2) RESOLVES the budgeting-forecasting/financial-planning-analysis passes' secondary flag: seam held on data source (sales-owned deal pipeline vs finance-owned financial planning model), owning function (sales org vs finance), and cadence (in-period restatement vs annual/quarterly planning cycle); sales/quota planning modules inside budgeting platforms are classified by object — quota/target allocation over the planning model → Quota Management/FP&A side, in-period pipeline projection → this side; recommend keeping all three as separate Types with cross-references (no umbrella-vs-slice product-partition problem comparable to the FP&A/B&F case was observed on the forecasting side)

- inventory-management-system (§10, processed 2026-09-07) — family calibration note for the inventory family (retail-inventory-management §05.12 processed; restaurant-inventory-management §26 and telecom-inventory-management §19 unprocessed): the generic Type's defining core is written smaller (stock records + recorded events, 2 properties) than the retail instantiation's (which includes count reconciliation as core) because this pass's broader sample includes a count-less minimal pole (Sortly-class trackers correct by editing quantities with reasons); both calibrations are sample-driven and defensible — domain instantiations may carry stricter cores; when the restaurant/telecom inventory leaves are processed, decide per-domain whether count discipline is core or standard and cross-reference this note; no alias/merge risk between the generic leaf and the retail leaf — distinct domain instantiations confirmed from both sides

- digital-waiver-management (§26, processed 2026-09-07): standalone Type confirmed — a dedicated specialist market exists (Smartwaiver/Wherewolf/WaiverSign/eWaiverPro-class products whose center IS the waiver loop); waiver modules embedded inside booking/venue/registration platforms (FareHarbor, ROLLER — access-gated, not directly examined) are a packaging variant, consistent with the attraction-ticketing pass recording waivers as L2 in its capability ring; seam vs event-registration-platform (§26 sibling, unprocessed) flagged for that pass — waiver-as-registration-step is a capability, not this Type; no generic e-signature leaf exists in the directory — the participation-shaped (participants/minors/groups/kiosks/check-in) vs envelope-shaped (multi-party document routing) split is recorded in the leaf itself

- construction-reality-capture-platform (§17, processed 2026-09-07) — boundary notes held: vs construction-field-management the seam is a designed handoff (capture-pinned notes → punch/observation/issue records; one sampled vendor ships two-way conversion and an embedded viewer inside the PM platform), vs construction-project-management (dated ground-truth supplier into the container, no schedule/cost/coordination semantics of its own), vs bim-authoring + bim-coordination (model uploaded/aligned/overlaid as consumed reference, never authored or clash-coordinated), vs photogrammetry-application (§04.13, unprocessed — general 3D-from-photos creation vs construction-scoped record system; photogrammetry appears inside this Type as one processing mechanism; joint review recommended), vs building-condition-assessment (§17 processed; construction-phase visual accumulation vs portfolio condition ratings — facilities-assessment pole of one sampled product is adjacent), vs construction-closeout-management (capture record is one input to closeout assembly), vs digital-twin-platform (§16, unprocessed — vendor "digital twin" language here means the as-built visual record of a structure, not operations-twin machinery; light flag for joint review if that pass treats construction twins as core); taxonomy notes: live fixed-camera construction monitoring (webcam-class vendors) has no §17 leaf — continuous live streams lack plan anchoring/navigable dated captures, recorded as adjacency rather than a new-leaf request; market label "reality capture" also covers laser-scan registration ecosystems (point-cloud tooling vendors), a sibling tooling category whose center is scan processing, not the project record

- interview-scheduling-platform (§09, processed 2026-09-07) vs interview-management-platform (§09 sibling, unprocessed): the directory holds both leaves and sampled products bundle pieces of both (one flagship ships interviewer training/shadow scheduling/analytics; a conversational-suite product prompts post-interview interviewer feedback), so the seam must be ratified when that leaf is processed — this pass's proposed split: scheduling logistics (who/when/availability/reminders/booking lifecycle) = Interview Scheduling Platform; evaluation + program machinery (scorecards, structured interview programs, interviewer certification/training programs) = Interview Management Platform; if the market does not support a separable product class, the Interview Management leaf risks being a suite-framing variant of this Type or of the recruiting platform — joint review recommended. Secondary note: applications/appointment-scheduling-application.md's related-types row describes this Type as "a recruiting-specific deployment of the scheduling-link pattern" — refined (not contradicted) by this pass: interviewer-pool and ATS-anchoring semantics are load-bearing, not merely a deployment of scheduling links.

- data-exchange-platform (§13, processed 2026-09-07): (1) ANSWERS the data-catalog pass flag "data products / marketplace layer hardening inside catalog suites (3/5) — watch whether it deserves a distinct leaf" — the distinct leaf exists and is Data Exchange Platform (core population = dedicated hyperscaler exchange services + lakehouse sharing platforms); catalog vendors' embedded data-marketplace/exchange surfaces are a packaging variant, not grounds for merging catalog+exchange (catalog describes, exchange entitles+delivers); (2) three-way inter-org data movement seam vs managed-file-transfer (§13) and edi-platform (§13), both unprocessed at this pass — recorded split: MFT = transfer-event file movement, EDI = standardized business-transaction documents, exchange = dataset offerings with entitlements; joint review recommended when those leaves are processed; (3) vs data-integration-platform / data-replication-platform / data-virtualization-platform (§13 siblings, unprocessed) boundary held on intra-org movement vs inter-org entitlement — cross-check at their passes recommended; (4) naming-collision note: vendor feature labels ("Data Exchange" as a Snowflake feature, "private exchange" at Databricks, "data marketplace" industry label) overlap the Type name — no separate data-marketplace leaf exists in the directory and none is needed; the marketplace face is a non-definitional surface of this Type.

- election-management-system (2026-09-07): (1) umbrella-labeling pressure — the market uses "Election Management" loosely: one sampled vendor categorizes its central-count tabulation product under an "Election Management" bucket, and vendors commonly co-package EMS + Voter Registration + Results Reporting as one product family; recommend joint review with voter-registration-system and election-results-management when those leaves are processed; (2) realization note — in the US market the Type is mostly realized as the definition/production component inside a certified voting system rather than as a standalone product (broader administration-suite and standalone realizations exist); treated as a packaging variant, not a separate Type

- digital-concierge (§26, processed 2026-09-07) vs hotel-guest-experience-platform (§26 sibling, unprocessed): thinnest seam in the family — one sampled product (INTELITY) self-titles "Guest Experience Platform" while its own page title pairs the label with "Digital Concierge", and the concierge center ships both standalone (Kipsu, HiJiffy) and as the guest-services module of hotel-operations suites (ALICE) or guest-experience suites (INTELITY); this pass holds the type on center of gravity (guest-initiated service-request intake + fulfillment as the product's heart vs guest-lifecycle-wide machinery: check-in/keys/upsells/surveys/authorizations) — recommend joint review when hotel-guest-experience-platform is processed to ratify keep-both-with-seam vs variant presentation; secondary cross-reference note: hospitality guest-messaging/chatbot products could also be claimed by the customer-support-chat / customer-service-chatbot-platform leaves (§07) — the adopted discriminators are stay anchoring and physical-service fulfillment semantics, cross-reference recommended when those leaves are processed.
- international-commerce-management (§05.24, processed 2026-09-07) vs cross-border-commerce-platform (§05.24 sibling, unprocessed): market evidence does not support two distinct product categories under the two leaf names — sampled products self-label variously ("cross-border ecommerce platform" / "global ecommerce platform" / "international selling") while all carry the same merchant-side management core (market as managed unit + per-market proposition + per-market obligations + central oversight); likely ALIAS or a packaging-angle split (management discipline vs enabling-infrastructure/MoR layer); JOINT REVIEW recommended when cross-border-commerce-platform is processed; also checked from this side: vs global-trade-management (§10, processed) — complementary consumer-selling vs trade-operations split confirmed, no seam conflict with the GTM pass's flags
- construction-project-management (§17, processed) — joint-review flag from construction-field-management DISCHARGED from the PM side: the field-vs-project split drawn there (day record + field work items vs schedule/cost/contracts/document register/coordination workflows) is confirmed from the PM side; PM platforms host field tools as modules inside the project container (research/construction-project-management.md §Boundary Findings 2)
- construction-project-management (§17, processed) — umbrella confirmation + sibling seams: RFI Management, Submittal Management, Change Order Management, Progress Billing, Daily Log Application, Punch List Management, Construction Quality/Safety Management are realized as modules inside PM platforms (each remains a legitimate point Type — cross-reference recommended when those leaves are processed); joint review recommended vs Construction Scheduling (deep CPM engine vs schedule dimension — one sampled flagship PM product ships no native schedule and integrates scheduling tools), vs Project Controls Platform (measurement/analysis layer over PM-originated data), vs Construction Contract Administration (contract lifecycle center vs coordination spine), vs Construction Bidding Platform (multi-bidder bid-day machinery vs bid packages as one capability); boundary vs generic Project Management Application (§03.07) held: the multi-organization contractual community + formal cross-party workflow machinery is the seam (research/construction-project-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- elearning-authoring-tool (§23, processed 2026-09-07) — flag for the learning-management-system-lms pass (§23 sibling, unprocessed): the authoring/LMS seam is an interlock, not a wall — every sampled authoring tool publishes SCORM/xAPI packages "to your LMS" (creation produces a portable deliverable; delivery manages learners/enrollment/completion), while the reverse direction is a gradient: LMS-native course builders are capability slices, but an LMS that bundles a full authoring environment (standards export, question engines, branching) approaches this Type from the other side; when the LMS leaf is processed, apply the publishable-deliverable/full-authoring-environment test and consider joint review; secondary consistency note: the educational-content-platform pass's recorded seam ("production surfaces fill the platform's own library, not standalone authoring") was verified and held from the authoring side; minor seam vs survey-platform/questionnaire leaves (§03.11): standalone quiz-maker siblings exist inside authoring suites (one sampled vendor ships its quiz maker as a separate product) — in-content instructional assessment vs respondent-data collection is the discriminator
- digital-collection-portal (§27, processed 2026-09-07) — DISCHARGES the archaeological-collection-management pass's CMS-sibling "probable Capability relationship" flag for this leaf: the portal was verified as an independently marketed product half (a publishing companion module sold separately, a separately installable open-source front-end, a hosted SaaS publishing capability, and a standalone cross-institution aggregator service) — Type stands, with module/companion deployment documented as the dominant shape rather than a disqualifier; joint review still recommended when museum-collections-management is processed.
- digital-collection-portal (§27) vs digital-library-platform (§23): gray zone — the DLP pass lists "public collection portal" as one of its interfaces and "publication/exhibition-centered" as a DLP variant; this pass draws the line at ownership of the item store and curation machinery (DLP definitional = ingest/describe/review/maintain; portal = publication surface over records owned elsewhere; bundling products contain both roles in one suite) — flagged for joint review.
- digital-collection-portal (§27) aggregator variant vs library-discovery-platform (§23): both federate many sources; held apart by unit and purpose (collection-item record with media/rights/attribution and public item pages vs bibliographic resource discovery) — genuine tension noted for joint review.

- data-catalog (§13, processed 2026-09-07) — vs metadata-management-platform (§13 sibling, unprocessed): the softest seam in the data family — metadata management is the broader discipline (collect/store/standardize/govern/publish metadata itself as enterprise content, incl. standards/models/exchange) while the data catalog is its discovery-facing instantiation (inventory of external data assets + descriptive context + search/browse); governance-first suites collapse the two into one product; boundary held for this pass on the primary object of work (asset inventory + its discovery/understanding loop vs metadata as governed content); recommend joint review when metadata-management-platform is processed. Secondary flag: data products / marketplace layer is hardening inside catalog suites (3/5 sampled products — Alation, Collibra, Microsoft Purview — ship it as a distinct app surface; Atlan ships data products as a capability) — watch whether it deserves a distinct leaf. Tertiary: vs data-governance-platform (§13 sibling, unprocessed) — boundary held on inventory+discovery loop vs policy/stewardship/compliance workflows; governance vendors embed catalogs as their visible surface, so recommend cross-reference when that leaf is processed (research/data-catalog.md §Boundary Findings)

- donor-management-system (§25, processed 2026-09-07) — two joint-review flags for §25 siblings unprocessed at the time of this pass: (1) vs online-donation-platform + fundraising-management-platform — vendors sell all three together and each side embeds a slice of the others (donor-management products ship donation forms writing back; fundraising platforms ship donor CRMs; one sampled fundraising vendor's own FAQ separates "managing donor relationships and supporter data" from "running campaigns, processing donations, tracking performance" while noting modern products combine both); adopted discriminators for this pass: system-of-record side (org-side constituency database vs donor-facing collection flow) and center (constituency stewardship vs campaign machinery); recommend joint review when both siblings are processed; (2) vs nonprofit-crm — term collision: the market calls donor databases "nonprofit CRMs" (sampled vendors self-label CRM while centering donors) while a fuller Nonprofit CRM extends the constituent base to members/volunteers/clients (the open-source constituent suite's component breadth is the structural tell); candidate outcomes: donor management as the donor-centered sibling of Nonprofit CRM (parallel to church-giving vs ChMS) or consolidation view; adopts the constituent-relationship-management pass's recommendation that the nonprofit-crm pass claim the nonprofit usage of "CRM" and record the shared family shape (research/donor-management-system.md §Boundary Findings 1–3)

- construction-field-management (§17, processed 2026-09-07) — suite-level umbrella Type whose standard capabilities are themselves directory leaves (Daily Log Application, Punch List Management, RFI Management, Submittal Management, Construction Quality Management, Construction Safety Management): recommend subordination/cross-reference review when those leaves are processed; also recommend joint review vs Construction Project Management (§17) — vendors sell field management as part of PM platforms, and the field-vs-project split is drawn on objects (day record + field work items vs schedule/cost/contracts)
- dashboard-platform (§13, processed) vs business-intelligence-platform (§13, processed): the BI pass's joint-review flag DISCHARGED from the dashboard side — verdict: Dashboard Platform stands as a distinct sibling Type, not an alias/capability-slice; evidence: a self-sustaining display-first population that never grows the BI structure (one vendor's explicit "is this a BI tool? No" positioning, a template-automated client-reporting pole, a formula-per-panel pole that explicitly works without a warehouse), vendors police the seam themselves (published BI-vs-dashboard-visibility comparisons; in-product dashboard-vs-report distinctions), and the centers of gravity differ (BI = governed artifact lifecycle + shared model layer + broad artifact estate; dashboard = the dashboard artifact + connect→compose→keep-current→distribute loop with thin modeling/governance); structural tests recorded both directions (strip BI to dashboard composition+sharing → dashboard platform; add semantic layer + governed broad estate → BI — observable as one sampled product's live trajectory); residual overlap (BI ships dashboards as flagship artifact; query/AI surfaces bundle into dashboard products) documented symmetrically on both sides; secondary seams recorded: vs Reporting Platform (standing display vs document output; scheduled snapshots as the capability seam), vs Data Visualization Application, vs Ad-hoc Query Application, vs Observability/Infrastructure Monitoring (dashboard-first engineering products treated as this Type's pole), vs Personal Dashboard (§03.13, name collision only), vs Status Page Platform (research/dashboard-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- construction-estimating (§17, processed) — three sibling-seam notes for leaves unprocessed at the time of this pass: (1) vs Quantity Takeoff — the sharpest seam: takeoff output is quantities (money optional), estimating output is a priced decision-ready total; estimating runs entirely without takeoff (template-driven sample) and takeoff exists without pricing, yet 3 of 5 sampled estimating products bundle both — recommend the takeoff pass adopt the remove-pricing/remove-measuring discriminator and treat bundling as packaging, not type identity; (2) vs Construction Bidding Platform — quote-leveling/bid-day machinery appears inside GC-side estimating products (one sampled product's quote management; another's subcontractor comparison documented as not available in the USA) while multi-bidder distribution/collection is the sibling Type — joint review recommended when that leaf is processed; (3) vs Preconstruction Management — one sampled vendor markets its entire takeoff+estimate+field suite as a "preconstruction platform" (umbrella risk); estimating should remain the contained pricing Type. Consistency note: the construction-cost-management pass's fixed seam (pre-award pricing vs post-award control; budget-from-estimate handoff) is confirmed from the estimating side (research/construction-estimating.md §Boundary Findings)

- document-editor (§03.01, processed) vs markdown-editor (§03.01 sibling, unprocessed at time of this pass): seam recorded — the discriminator is the formatting model (explicit user-controlled character/paragraph formatting visible during writing vs markup source edited as text with rendering deferred to a separate step); document-editor pass held the boundary from its side and recommends the markdown-editor pass hold it from its side; related non-blocking note: the document-editor ↔ collaborative-document-editor seam is porous in one direction (every sampled single-author editor has added collaboration), already recorded by the collaborative-document-editor pass — the adopted discriminator on both sides is whether the shared live merged document is the primary object.

- revenue-intelligence-platform (§07, processed) vs sales-forecasting-platform (§07 sibling, unprocessed): heavy object overlap — forecast submission/roll-up machinery lives in both, and two of five sampled RI products market forecasting as a flagship module while a third (Clari) is forecast-heritage; adopted discriminator for this pass: Revenue Intelligence Platform = captured-engagement data foundation + pipeline/deal inspection + projection together (an insight layer over the CRM that observes activity), Sales Forecasting Platform = forecast production/roll-up as the primary object, typically working directly on CRM fields without a captured-engagement foundation (spreadsheet roll-ups and CRM-native forecast modules belong to the forecasting side); recommend joint review when sales-forecasting-platform is processed to ratify or revise the split; secondary note: category label instability — vendors self-relabel to "revenue platform/orchestration/revenue AI" and consolidated during 2025–2026 (People.ai→Backstory, BoostUp→Terret, Clari+Salesloft merger), so leaf naming should anchor on the market-recognizable "revenue intelligence" label (Gong's own category page title, G2 "Revenue Operations & Intelligence") rather than vendor self-labels.

- cyber-incident-response-platform (§15, processed) vs soar (§15 sibling) and soc-platform (§15 sibling): market-realization flag — the incident-response case core is realizable without automation (historical check passed), so the leaf is NOT judged an alias of SOAR, but in the five-product sample zero products market primarily under an "incident response platform" label: the case-management layer is delivered inside SIEM (Sentinel), SOAR (Cortex XSOAR, Splunk SOAR), and TI (ThreatConnect) platforms; recommend joint review with soar and soc-platform to decide keep-both-with-seam vs variant presentation, with the adopted discriminator: automation/orchestration as center of gravity (SOAR) vs the incident case + response lifecycle + recorded response activity as center of gravity (this leaf); secondary note: the heritage standalone-IRP lineage (IBM Resilient-class) could not be verified from primary sources (IBM docs 403 ×2) and no reachable standalone pure-play IR case product was found to confirm the standalone pole's current market presence — the pole is documented structurally only (research/cyber-incident-response-platform.md §Taxonomy Note)

- construction-cost-management (§17) — seam with two sibling leaves still unprocessed at the time of this pass: Change Order Management (change workflow is a contained mechanism inside the cost loop; both appear as separate directory entries while sampled suites realize change as a tool family inside cost) and Progress Billing (revenue mirror sharing the schedule-of-values/retainage vocabulary with opposite money flow); boundaries were held in this pass, but a joint review when those leaves are processed would keep the three-way split stable.

- directory-application (§02.11, processed) — (1) Member Directory (§25) is most plausibly a domain-scoped instance of Directory Application (same core: bounded roster + standing entries + lookup + contact attributes) rather than a structurally independent Type — no member-directory product was reachable for direct evidence in this pass; joint review recommended before any merge decision; (2) in-family seam with Listings Platform (§02.11) needs joint care: both organize retrievable records and real products blend both (directory + current offers); the proposed discriminator is record temporality (standing entity record vs expiring/consummable offer); (3) drift-orbit note: several directory products sell the same catalog as API/bulk data (identity verification, enrichment, KYC/AML) — the lookup surface stays in this Type while the data-supply business belongs to §07/§13/§15 data-platform Types; products straddling both should not force a reclassification of either.

- classifieds-platform (§05.03, processed) — (1) RESOLVES the resale-marketplace pass flag with classifieds-side evidence: Leboncoin supports in-person sale with meeting-day payment validation inside its messaging, Kleinanzeigen frames off-platform (PayPal) payment as "outside our protected process" — a protection warning, not a rule violation — and Kijiji publishes police safe-exchange-zone guidance; the structural test now holds from both sides (remove the mediated transaction → classifieds; make it mandatory → marketplace), both leaves stand. (2) vs sibling Listing Marketplace (§05.03, unprocessed): the market spans a pure ad-contact pole (Kijiji-class) and a transaction-service-heavy pole (Leboncoin/Kleinanzeigen/Subito-class); this pass defines the Type by the ad-contact model with transaction services optional — if Listing Marketplace is intended as the transaction-first pole the two leaves need an explicit division of labor, if synonymous it is an Alias; joint review recommended. (3) vs Online Marketplace / Multi-vendor Marketplace (§05.02, unprocessed): supply-identity seam (transient self-published one-off ads vs merchant catalogs with inventory/cart/checkout); horizontal marketplaces blur at the edges (eBay heritage spans both); joint awareness recommended. (4) Prior-pass consistency confirmed from this side: babysitting-marketplace removal test (strip caregiver profiles + two-sided roles → classifieds) and association-job-board test (keep only listings without candidate machinery → classifieds) both hold (research/classifieds-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- digital-sculpting-application (§04.13, processed) vs 3d-modeling-application (§04.13 sibling, unprocessed): mode-level seam flag — the discriminator held this pass is the primary instrument (brush deformation of a continuous surface vs discrete component construction of geometry), and the market polices the seam in-product (separate Sculpt vs Modeling rooms in one pipeline app; a sculpt workspace beside a modeling toolset in the suite; sculpt-first vendors ship polygon-modeling/booleans as secondary capability), but suite products legitimately host both Types as modes — recommend the 3d-modeling-application pass treat sculpt-mode-within-suite as an adjacent mode rather than a duplicate leaf and cross-reference this boundary; secondary gray zone toward texture-material-authoring: displacement-class painting (sculpt apps' displacement/normal map baking and micro-vertex painting) blurs shape vs surface appearance (research/digital-sculpting-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- court-case-management-system vs court-e-filing-platform (§24 sibling, unprocessed): the filing-intake seam is realized in the market both as a separate integrated product (filing tool reviewed/accepted/rejected outside the CMS, integrated with it) and as one bundled program (federal "Case Management/Electronic Case Files" — filing and case management in a single system); the CMS is the record of reference, e-filing is intake machinery — flagged for joint review when the e-filing leaf is processed (research/court-case-management-system.md §Boundary Findings)
- checkout-platform (§05.06, processed) vs shopping-cart-platform (§05.06 sibling, unprocessed): sibling-seam flag — boundary defined structurally this pass (cart = pre-commitment accumulation/editing of intended items; checkout = completion transaction of an initiated purchase; seam = the checkout button), but the market observation is that standalone cart products have been almost entirely absorbed into commerce platforms, and cart↔checkout pairs are bundled everywhere; recommend joint review when shopping-cart-platform is processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with accumulation-vs-completion seam (current framing), or re-scope the cart leaf as a capability slice absorbed by commerce platforms (research/checkout-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- checkout-platform (§05.06, processed) vs payment-gateway / payment-processing-platform (§08, both processed): consistency note — this pass adopts the seam already recorded by those passes (gateway/processing = acceptance + authorization + transaction lifecycle; checkout = payer-facing completion experience); the gradient case (hosted payment pages as gateway acceptance surfaces; a processing platform's checkout product — Stripe Checkout) is acknowledged and recorded rather than resolved; no taxonomy change proposed (research/checkout-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- retail-pricing-management (§05.14, processed) — taxonomy note extending the promotion-management pass: the market increasingly sells unified price+promotion+markdown optimization platforms (Revionics lifecycle platform; Oracle LPO as a separate optimization service over the same data spine; the Gartner "Retail Unified Price, Promotion and Markdown Optimization Applications" category name cited by Competera) — the three §05.14 leaves (retail-pricing-management / promotion-management / markdown-optimization-application) are three levers of one platform family, separable by lever (everyday price / temporary event / permanent clearance); boundaries held structurally this pass; joint review of all three siblings recommended once markdown-optimization-application is processed (research/retail-pricing-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- commercial-kitchen-management (§20, processed) vs kitchen-display-system-kds (§26, unprocessed): market naming collision — Crunchtime sells its KDS under the product name "Kitchen Management" (direct vendor evidence); recommend the KDS pass explicitly address the collision and cross-reference this leaf; secondary taxonomy observation: a recipes+costing system without production planning or food-safety execution (meez pole taken strictly) drifts toward a Recipe Management Type that has no directory leaf — recorded, not silently merged (research/commercial-kitchen-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- creator-media-kit-builder (§27, processed) vs link-in-bio-platform + creator-sponsorship-management (§27 siblings, unprocessed): reader-side seam recorded for joint review — the media kit's reader is an external commercial decision-maker while the link-in-bio page's reader is the creator's own audience; sampled products ship both as distinct surfaces inside one account, so feature presence is explicitly NOT the seam — apply the reader test (who reads the surface) when link-in-bio-platform is processed; vs creator-sponsorship-management the kit is only the pitch artifact (a deal-request capture on the kit is the handoff seam, not deal management) — apply the object test (pitch document vs deal workflow) when that sibling is processed; family note: this Type is a domain instantiation of the candidate-side document-authoring family (sibling of Resume Builder §09, whose pass recorded the same family pattern) (research/creator-media-kit-builder.md §Boundary Findings)

- retail-inventory-management (§05.12, processed) vs store-inventory-application (§05.12 sibling, unprocessed): scope-variant flag — researched evidence (Square/Erply/NetSuite/Cin7) shows one Type operating at two scopes, store-scoped (single location's stock, counts, receiving) and chain-scoped (HQ central purchasing, distribution, cross-store transfers), with no structural difference found that would make a second Type; recommend joint review when store-inventory-application is processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with a store-vs-chain scope seam, or consolidate as one Type with scope variants (research/retail-inventory-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- case-law-research-platform (§11, processed) vs legal-research-platform (§11 sibling, unprocessed): coupling flag — every commercial product sampled at this node (Westlaw, Lexis+, Bloomberg Law, vLex) bundles statutes, regulations, and secondary sources around the case-law core, so the market realization of this leaf is mostly as the case-law core of a broader Legal Research Platform; the leaf is kept as a distinct Type because the case-law-specific structure (opinion corpus + precedent citation graph + authority validation) is real, is what these products are organized around (both dominant vendors market citator-first), and the free pole (CourtListener) demonstrates the minimal statutes-free form; recorded seam test: first-class non-decision research content/workflows → Legal Research Platform; opinion corpus + citation network + authority validation as the organizing center → this Type; recommend joint review when legal-research-platform is processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with content-scope seam (current framing), or fold this leaf as the case-law facet of Legal Research Platform (research/case-law-research-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- research-panel-platform (§06, processed) vs market-research-platform / consumer-research-platform (§06 siblings, both unprocessed) and survey-platform (§03.11, unprocessed): sharpest seam is the system of record — the panel platform's managed object is the standing member population (recruit → profile → sample → field → record → reward → maintain), while MR platforms center the study lifecycle (design → field → analyze) and sample buying, and survey platforms center instrument authoring/fielding to non-persistent respondents; convergence is real (panel platforms embed or integrate survey engines; MR platforms sell sample) so the recorded test is: remove the standing managed population → survey/MR platform; remove the study tooling → panel platform; recommend joint review when those leaves are processed (research/research-panel-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- research-panel-platform (§06, processed) vs community-platform family (§01.06 siblings, unprocessed): MROC/insight-community straddle flag — sampled vendors sell large survey panels and small always-on communities on identical machinery (member records + sampling + fielding + incentives + health), explicitly distinguishing them only by size and usage cadence (vendor framing, not asserted as fact), so the insight community is documented as a panel-platform variant, not a separate Type; the structural test recorded is operator-structured research participation vs member-initiated conversation/content; recommend joint review when §01.06 leaves are processed. Sample exchanges (Cint Exchange/Dynata-class) held distinct by the member-relationship test (who stewards the members, why the members exist — operator's research program vs monetization supply); Cint Engage (panel-management machinery attached to a monetization outlet) recorded as the hybrid pole (research/research-panel-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- climate-risk-management (§21, processed) vs physical-climate-risk-platform / climate-scenario-analysis (§21 siblings, both unprocessed): large product overlap — the sampled process-carrying products (XDI, Jupiter) are simultaneously the strongest physical-risk-engine candidates, and scenario machinery straddles all three; working seams recorded: physical-climate-risk-platform = physical-only hazard/loss computation engine side (no org-side risk process over maintained assessments), climate-scenario-analysis = scenario projection machinery without a managed exposure population, climate-risk-management = the organizational risk loop (exposure population + maintained assessments + prioritization/decision/monitoring/disclosure cycles) regardless of which family the engine covers or where the engine lives (embedded vs licensed data); secondary drifts recorded: investor-data pole (ISS STOXX-class) dissolves into climate data/analytics products, disclosure-led pole (Manifest-class) dissolves into ESG disclosure management; recommend joint review when the two sibling leaves are processed — candidate outcomes: keep-all-three with process-scope seams (current framing), or consolidate engine-side products under physical-climate-risk-platform (research/climate-risk-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- career-site-platform (§09, processed) vs job-board (§09 sibling, unprocessed): naming-collision flag — ATS vendors call their hosted single-employer public surface an "(external) job board" (Greenhouse observed in official docs), while the directory's Job Board Type is multi-employer aggregation; recorded seam is the ownership test (whose openings the public surface lists: one employer's own under its brand/domain vs many employers behind a neutral venue); recommend the job-board pass adopt this test explicitly and treat ATS-hosted single-employer boards as career-site surfaces, not Job Board instances (research/career-site-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- career-development-platform (§09, processed) vs career-pathing-application (§09 sibling, unprocessed): soft boundary — path *architecture* (building/maintaining the org's role/level/path library) vs employee *development planning* against that library; every sampled product (Fuel50, SAP CTD, Oracle Grow, Cornerstone, Leapsome) folds path architecture and plan execution into one platform, and the competency-led pole implements the anchor as framework levels rather than visual paths, so "career pathing" may be a capability slice of this Type (or of Skills Management) rather than an independent Type; recommend joint review when career-pathing-application is processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with architecture-vs-execution seam, or re-scope as capability (research/career-development-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- career-pathing-application (§09, processed) — joint-review flag from career-development-platform DISCHARGED: keep-both with the architecture-vs-execution seam — career pathing owns the organization's career structure (roles/levels/progression links + per-node requirements) and its employee-facing exploration; career development platform owns the employee's development plan; vendor-documented separation (TalentGuard ships Career Pathing and Development Planning as separate modules — "plan the move" vs "close the gap"; Lattice FAQ separates Career Tracks from IDPs; Fuel50 FAQ separates Skills Architecture from what it powers downstream), and Progression demonstrates a standalone architecture-pole product with no development-plan object; boundary remains soft because the market overwhelmingly bundles both sides on one substrate (all six sampled products include plan-execution somewhere in the suite) — if either leaf is ever consolidated, revisit at substrate level; secondary seams recorded: vs skills-management (library instrumental vs primary), vs internal-talent-marketplace (structure+exploration vs open-opportunity matching), vs succession (all-roles vs critical-role), vs org-chart (role progression+requirements vs people reporting) (research/career-pathing-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- dating-community-platform (§01.07, processed) — joint-review flag from dating-application DISCHARGED: family split kept — Dating Application (1:1 candidate loop organizes; mediated contact gate definitional) vs Dating Community Platform (community container + partner discovery integrated; contact gate optional — open/verified/subscription-gated messaging equally common because the community context carries the trust load); seam test = which structure organizes the product and whether community participation is a designed path to meeting partners; Her-class hybrids (full candidate loop + first-class communities) documented as the overlap zone on both sides; Kippo/Stir-class interest/life-stage niches without community structures confirmed as Dating Applications; relationship-discovery-application still reads as probable umbrella alias (unchanged, for its own pass); secondary flags: Hornet-class social-network-shaped products straddle vs Interest-based Social Network (root-page evidence only, unresolved); member-created-event liability disclaimers and verification-before-communication recorded as common community-governance patterns (research/dating-community-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- creator-audience-analytics (§27, processed) vs social-media-analytics-platform (§06 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the analytics cluster — identical mechanics (connected accounts, per-network metric dashboards, competitor benchmarking, reports) are sold to both creators and brands/agencies, and sampled products straddle deliberately (Metricool and Iconosquare market to creators and brands/agencies alike; TubeBuddy sells Teams & Brands plans), so features cannot separate the Types; working seam = operator + data subject + decision loop (creator measuring their own audience for content/growth decisions vs marketing team measuring brand presence/campaigns); also recorded: platform-native analytics (YouTube Studio-class) is the built-in capability baseline rather than a separate Type, and the third-party Type's reason to exist is what native tools lack (cross-platform unification, independent history accumulation, competitor tracking, benchmarks, reporting); recommend joint review when social-media-analytics-platform is processed (research/creator-audience-analytics.md §Boundary Findings)

- dating-application (§01.07, processed) vs matchmaking-platform / relationship-discovery-application / dating-community-platform (§01.07 siblings, all unprocessed): intra-family joint-review flags — (1) sharpest seam is dating-application vs matchmaking-platform: the working test is who selects the candidates (user self-serves the candidate loop — profile/discover/like/gate/chat — vs a service, human or curated machinery, selecting and introducing candidates, often with assisted communication and offline/event components; marriage-oriented matrimonial platforms lean the matchmaking side), (2) relationship-discovery-application reads as a probable umbrella alias of the same loop, (3) dating-community-platform centers community surfaces (events/groups/content) around dating rather than the 1:1 candidate loop; recommend joint review when each sibling is processed — candidate outcomes are keep-the-family-split with the who-selects test, or umbrella consolidation (research/dating-application.md §Boundary Findings)
- dating-application (§01.07, processed) cross-family straddle note: friend-discovery products share the exact skeleton (profile → discover strangers → interest → contact) with weaker consent gating and friendship intent, and one sampled dating product embeds friend-finding as a first-class second mode inside the same app — multi-mode products are one product spanning two Types by mode; flag for awareness when friend-discovery-application (§01.05) is processed
- global-trade-management (§10, processed) vs customs-compliance-platform (§10 sibling, unprocessed): adjacent slices of one trade-compliance market — customs-declaration-first products (country-specific declaration preparation/filing for customs authorities, often broker-operated) satisfy GTM's classification+transaction+customs-output structures but lack the transaction-level compliance determination (screening/licensing outcome recorded on the transaction), FTA/origin program management, and duty deferral/refund program management; the GTM pass documented the full-program Type and held the seam as "does the product record the compliance determination of the transaction, or only prepare declarations"; recommend joint review when customs-compliance-platform is processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with the determination-vs-declaration seam (current framing), or re-scope customs-compliance-platform as the declaration/filing slice including broker-side products (research/global-trade-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- climate-adaptation-planning (§21, processed) vs decarbonization-planning-platform (§21 sibling, unprocessed): structural-twin flag for joint review — the two Types share the identical planning loop (evidence → plan artifact → discrete actions → tracked implementation → monitoring/evaluation feeding revision); the only structural difference is the content domain (climate hazards/adaptive capacity vs emissions sources/reduction levers), and the market commonly carries both domains in one integrated climate-plan product (observed at Futureproofed; adaptation is a measures domain beside mitigation) — candidate outcomes: keep-both with the content-domain seam (current framing), or consolidate as one "climate action planning" Type with mitigation/adaptation domains; secondary note: the Type is partially carried by generic public-sector plan-execution machinery (Envisio pole) — when strategic-plan-execution / government-performance-management leaves are processed, apply the climate-hazard-anchor test to decide whether climate plans are a variant there or a distinct Type here (research/climate-adaptation-planning.md §Boundary Findings)

- cap-table-management (§08, processed) vs investor-portal / fund-administration-platform / deal-management-for-private-equity-vc (§08 siblings): boundaries held on the defining core — cap table centers one company's ownership record (holders × securities × holdings + computed ownership + event history), investor-portal is a distribution surface onto records, fund administration centers a fund's LP/GP structure, PE/VC deal management flips the operator to the investor side; market bundles heavily across all four (one dominant vendor sells each), recommend joint review when the sibling leaves are processed (research/cap-table-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- cap-table-management (§08, processed) absorption flag: public-company share plan administration (trading windows, release elections, plan settlement) has no dedicated directory leaf anywhere; sampled vendors either span private cap table → public share plans or are plan-administration heritage — currently absorbed here as a Variant posture; if the private-market taxonomy is ever refined, share plan administration is the likeliest candidate for a separate leaf (research/cap-table-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- circular-economy-platform (§21, processed) — umbrella-structure flag: the market label "circular economy platform" spans five distinct product poles sharing one minimal core (asset reuse exchange / secondary-material B2B trading marketplace / supply-chain traceability & DPP / circularity measurement & reporting / incentivized collection networks); documented as one Type with pole variants per taxonomy policy; if finer granularity is ever needed, the traceability and measurement poles are the likeliest candidates for separate leaves (research/circular-economy-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- circular-economy-platform (§21, processed) boundary flags: (1) vs sustainability-management-platform / esg-reporting-platform (§21 siblings, unprocessed) — the circularity-measurement pole sits closest to that seam (material-loop objects vs org-wide ESG program); joint review recommended when those leaves are processed; (2) the scrap-trading pole is marketplace-shaped vs online-marketplace / resale-marketplace (§05) — distinguishing residue is secondary-material identity (grades/specs/verification) + circular outcome accounting; (3) vs processed recommerce-platform (§05.19) — brand-operated consumer resale vs organizational/B2B circulation infrastructure, audiences and outcome accounting differ; (4) vs processed carbon-accounting-platform (§21) — emissions inventory (activity × factor) vs material loops; both feed ESG reports but do not converge (research/circular-economy-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- clinical-documentation-platform (§22, processed) vs medical-coding-platform (§22 sibling): market convergence flag — sampled documentation products now emit coding output at authoring time (coding suggestions; ICD-10/HCC/E&M with clinician attestation documented at one sampled product) and the Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI) sub-market has no dedicated directory leaf, so this leaf absorbs it as a variant posture (review-and-query over existing documentation); L0 boundary held (produce/refine/finalize documentation vs code assignment), joint review recommended when medical-coding-platform is processed; ambient-AI-scribe sub-market likewise absorbed here (no separate leaf)

- regulatory-change-management (§11, processed) vs compliance-management-platform / governance-risk-compliance-platform (§11 siblings, unprocessed): boundary held on the primary record — RCM's system of record is the regulatory change event + recorded applicability/impact decision + owned response trail (the change feed IS the center), while Compliance Management centers the standing obligations/activities program the changes feed and GRC is the umbrella platform; market bundles heavily in both directions (Ncontracts sells change visibility inside "Compliance Management"; NAVEX sells RCM as a separate module; the financial-compliance-management pass recorded the same seam from the other side) — recommend joint review when those leaves are processed (research/regulatory-change-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- regulatory-change-management (§11, processed) vs regulatory content/news services (no directory leaf): a regulatory-update feed without applicability judgment + owned response machinery is a content product, not this Type — the response loop is the spine; content houses and workflow tools converge from both sides (all four sampled products supply content AND workflow), so the Type holds; recorded so future passes don't merge regulatory news feeds into RCM (research/regulatory-change-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- referral-marketing-platform (§06, processed) vs affiliate-management-platform (§06 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the growth cluster — the two Types share tracking mechanics (personal links/codes, click/coupon attribution) and the same vendors ship both natively in one product (3 of 6 sampled products run referral + affiliate side by side: ReferralCandy affiliate campaigns, ReferralRock partner/affiliate program type, Extole influencer & ambassador; ReferralHero and Friendbuy likewise), so products cannot separate the Types; working seam proposed from the referral side = participant population + incentive shape: referral participants are the brand's own existing customers sharing with personal contacts (rewards = friend offers/discounts/credit/gifts; two-sided common but one-sided widespread), affiliate participants are registered external partners earning commissions on tracked sales, with different enrollment (automatic from the customer base vs application/approval from the public); recommend joint review when affiliate-management-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are two Types with the participant test as the recorded seam, or one Type with referral as a participant-variant (research/referral-marketing-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- referral-marketing-platform (§06, processed) vs loyalty-program-management + customer-advocacy-platform (§06 siblings, unprocessed): loyalty seam = what the reward attaches to (another person's qualifying conversion vs the customer's own repeat purchase) while currencies (points/store credit) and vendors are shared (Friendbuy runs referral + loyalty on one platform; ReferralCandy ships loyalty campaigns) — straddle zone is real; advocacy seam = referral-first program machinery (offer design/attribution/reward fulfillment) vs reviews/UGC/references bundled as one advocacy motion (Mention Me straddles by positioning referral as the core of customer advocacy); recommend joint review when each sibling is processed (research/referral-marketing-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- candidate-profile-platform (§09, processed) taxonomy + sibling flags: (1) the leaf name is a descriptive construction, not a market category — the sampled market names the referent Talent CRM / Candidate CRM / Talent Engagement Platform / Talent Intelligence Platform, and every ATS ships a "candidate profile" as its central pipeline record; the Type is real specifically as the standalone profile-record layer outside the hiring pipeline (pre-application prospects, silver medalists, passive talent, talent communities), interlocking with the ATS at the apply seam and the rediscovery seam; recommend the taxonomy owner treat it as the profile-layer Type with the ATS-embedded CRM module as a packaging variant. (2) vs candidate-search-platform (sibling, unprocessed): managed-object seam (persistent person record vs query over a corpus); SeekOut straddles deliberately (search-first product with a profile-management core) — recommend joint review when candidate-search-platform is processed. (3) vs talent-sourcing-platform (sibling, unprocessed): record layer vs identification/outreach activity; products bundle both — same joint-review pass recommended. (4) two-sided candidate-authored profile marketplaces (employers browse candidate-owned profiles) are a different Type (marketplace family) — reasoned structurally, not sampled (research/candidate-profile-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- content-curation-platform (§02.08, processed) vs feed-reader / content-aggregator / personalized-content-feed (§02.08 siblings, all unprocessed): intra-family seams held structurally in this pass — the test is what the managed artifact is (curated persistent collection vs stream) plus who selects (human curator vs algorithm vs nobody-in-particular); direct market evidence: elink sells Bookmark Manager, RSS Feed Reader, and Content Curation as three separate solution pages of one product, Curata centers human review over automated discovery, and fully automated curation products (Paper.li-class) have exited the market (domain repurposed); recommend joint review when each sibling is processed (research/content-curation-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- content-curation-platform (§02.08, processed) vs bookmark-manager (§02.13 sibling, unprocessed): seam = audience-facing presentation as a first-class surface (curation) vs personal saving/retrieval (bookmarks); Wakelet self-describes its items as "a modern take on bookmarks" while centering collections + sharing + profile publication — the straddle zone is real and products legitimately span both; recommend joint review when bookmark-manager is processed
- content-curation-platform (§02.08, processed) — straddle note for §01.05: Pinterest-class visual discovery (boards as collections inside a social network) is the known boundary case between this Type and Social Networking; not sampled in this pass; flag for joint review when the §01.05 social leaves are processed

- recurring-commerce-management (§05.16, processed) vs subscription-commerce-platform (§05.16 sibling, unprocessed): probable alias/umbrella — all four sampled products (Recharge, Skio, Ordergroove, Cratejoy) self-describe as "subscription platform" for the same referent, and Recharge's own documentation uses "recurring commerce" as the activity name for what these platforms do; no sampled market product maps to only one of the two labels; if both leaves are kept the only defensible seam is emphasis (commerce enablement/enrollment/checkout-integration vs ongoing operations/lifecycle/retention), but every sampled product straddles it; recommend joint review when subscription-commerce-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are alias consolidation or a recorded emphasis seam (research/recurring-commerce-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- subscription-commerce-platform (§05.16, processed 2026-09-08) — RESOLVES the alias flag from the subscription-commerce-platform side via joint review: ALIAS/UMBRELLA CONFIRMED through independent sampling (Subbly, Bold Commerce, Appstle, Smartrr — self-labels "subscription-first commerce platform" / "repeat commerce company" subscription app / retention-focused subscription suite / "subscription platform"); the eight products across both passes form ONE competitive set with bidirectional migration and comparison links (Bold publishes migrate-from articles for Recharge/Skio/Ordergroove/PayWhirl/Stay Ai/Seal/Yotpo; Smartrr case-studies migrations from Bold/Recharge/Yotpo and documents a Recharge coexistence integration; Subbly lists Recharge/Cratejoy/Bold/PayWhirl among 10 migrate-from platforms; Appstle publishes per-competitor comparisons vs Bold/Recharge/Skio/Ordergroove); the defining cores derived independently by both passes are structurally identical (commitment → schedule → per-cycle execution → managed lifecycle); the only candidate seam (commerce-enablement vs operations emphasis) FAILED — every sampled product straddles it; RECOMMENDATION: alias consolidation as one Type with two market labels if the directory is ever revised; until then both leaves remain documented with identical defining cores and mutually cross-referencing Related-Types entries (research/subscription-commerce-platform.md §Alias test)
- cloud-ide (§12, processed) vs dev-container-workspace-platform (§12 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the dev-tooling cluster — both revolve around container-based, config-defined development environments (devcontainer.json/devfile), and the sampled Cloud IDEs (Codespaces, Che, Ona) are built on exactly that substrate; the working seam proposed from the cloud-ide side is locus of operation: a dev-container/workspace platform defines, shares, and provisions environments that may run on the developer's own machine and be consumed through any local editor, while a Cloud IDE hosts and lifecycle-manages the remote compute and delivers the editing+execution experience as a service; mechanism convergence (desktop IDEs attaching to remote environments via extensions) blurs the seam at the mechanism level but the locus test resolves it; recommend joint review when dev-container-workspace-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are keep-both-Types with the locus test as the recorded seam, or a two-leaf structure (environment-definition platform + hosted environment service) (research/cloud-ide.md §Boundary Findings)
- cloud-ide (§12, processed) — naming-drift note, no action required: the market label has moved cloud IDE → cloud development environment (CDE) → agentic environment platform; sampled vendors no longer self-identify as IDEs (Che: "cloud development environments"; Ona: "platform for background agents"; Replit: AI-first build platform) while the referent (managed remote workspace + client editor + remote execution) is stable across all eras sampled; the directory leaf name "Cloud IDE" remains valid as the historical market name; also note the name collision with web-development-ide (§12 sibling) is orthogonal axes (target domain vs hosting locus), not overlap

- classroom-management (§23, processed) vs virtual-classroom (§23 sibling, unprocessed): joint-review flag — a virtual classroom delivers the lesson itself online (video/whiteboard/lesson surface) for remote teaching, while classroom management observes and controls an in-room or device-equipped class; overlap risk is real because device-management products explicitly support remote learners (LanSchool "in the classroom and remotely", NetSupport corporate training) but their surface remains control/monitoring, not lesson delivery; recommend joint review when virtual-classroom is processed (research/classroom-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- classroom-management (§23, processed) vs student-behavior-management (§23 sibling, unprocessed): GRADIENT boundary — in-class conduct recording (points/rewards) is classroom management, while school-wide discipline machinery (referrals, sanctions, detention administration, PBIS program management) is the sibling Type; Satchel One's Behaviour module contains the school-wide machinery (sanctions, detentions, referred incidents, thresholds) inside a platform that also carries classroom-management modules, so the seam runs through products, not between them; recommend joint review when student-behavior-management is processed (research/classroom-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- classroom-management (§23, processed) vs student-attendance-system (§23 sibling, unprocessed): module-vs-Type flag — the in-class register (Satchel class register/Attendance Pro, NetSupport printable student register) is a classroom-management capability, while school-wide attendance records, statutory reporting, and absence management belong to the sibling Type; recommend joint review when student-attendance-system is processed (research/classroom-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- classroom-management (§23, processed) — name-collision note: "classroom management" in childcare software means rooms/capacity/staff-to-child ratios (see processed childcare-management-system, whose in-home tier explicitly excludes classroom management); same words, different object world — no action needed beyond awareness when processing education vs childcare leaves

- business-rules-management-system (§10, processed) vs decision-management-platform (§10 sibling, unprocessed): umbrella-vs-core overlap — the market increasingly brands this space "decision management" (IBM ODM's own page calls it a decision management platform; Sparkling Logic SMARTS calls itself a decision management platform; InRule calls itself a decision platform), and every "decision platform" sampled still contains a complete BRMS core (authoring/repository/engine); observable distinction: the BRMS's managed artifact is the rule asset, while a decision management platform additionally treats predictive models/strategies/decision analytics as co-equal managed artifacts; recommend joint review when decision-management-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are umbrella+core two-leaf structure (recommended) or alias consolidation (research/business-rules-management-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- business-process-management-platform (§10, processed) vs workflow-management-platform (§10 sibling, unprocessed): GRADIENT boundary, not crisp — both model multi-step human work and modern low-code workflow products increasingly carry engine-grade features; the working seam proposed from the BPM side: BPM's central managed artifact is a governed, versioned, engine-executed end-to-end process model with instance state/history/migration and full lifecycle tooling, while lightweight workflow tools center on configured routing recipes for recurring work patterns; L0 alone does NOT separate the two (historical workflow engines and modern workflow tools both satisfy it) — recommend joint review when workflow-management-platform is processed
- climbing-gym-management (§28, processed) vs gym-management-system (§28 sibling, unprocessed): segment-sibling relationship — the defining business core (visitors/entitlements/check-in/money/booking/POS) is shared and a generic product (GymMaster-class) can run it, while the climbing leaf's independent identity rests on the climbing-specific structures around that core (waiver-gated participation as flagship workflow, proficiency/belay-certification flags surfaced at check-in, the perishable wall/routesetting inventory — the latter frequently delivered by a companion product rather than by the management system itself); the same pattern presumably holds for the other vertical siblings (martial-arts-school-management, swim-school-management, gymnastics-club-management, dance-studio-management); recommend joint review when gym-management-system is processed — candidate outcomes are keep-all-vertical-leaves (each documenting its activity-specific structure layer over the shared core) or a consolidation view treating them as segment variants (research/climbing-gym-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- financial-risk-management-platform vs market-risk-platform / credit-risk-platform / liquidity-risk-platform (§08 siblings, unprocessed): umbrella-vs-slice — the market sells risk capability per risk type (same vendors ship per-risk-type solutions under one risk-management family: Murex "MX.3 for Enterprise Market Risk/Credit Risk/Liquidity Risk" brochures; SAS and Oracle per-risk-type solutions under one family) while the financial-risk-management leaf documents the institution-wide cross-risk management layer (shared data foundation, cross-risk aggregation, consolidated limits, enterprise reporting); recommendation: keep all four leaves (hub + slices, each form also exists standalone); flagged for joint review when the siblings are processed (research/financial-risk-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- financial-risk-management-platform vs regulatory-reporting-platform (§08 sibling, unprocessed): adjacent, often bundled — risk platforms produce the risk figures and ship regulatory content packs; a regulatory reporting platform's center is the report production/submission machinery (taxonomies, validations, submissions); flagged for joint review when that sibling is processed.
- actuarial-modeling-platform joint-review flag (vs financial-risk-management-platform / market-risk-platform / regulatory-reporting-platform): DISCHARGED from the financial-risk-management side — centers confirmed distinct (liability/product projection feeding capital and risk processes vs institution risk-position measurement/monitoring); adjacency stands, no duplicate; market-risk-platform and regulatory-reporting-platform sides remain open until those siblings are processed.
- business-contract-administration (§10, processed) vs contract-lifecycle-management (§11 sibling, unprocessed): PROBABLE ALIAS / same product category — Contract Logix's own article states "A contract administration system, also referred to as contract management software or contract lifecycle management software"; Docusign FAQ treats "CLM or contract management" as one thing; all 5 sampled CLM products cover both the administration emphasis (obligations/renewals/amendments) and the lifecycle emphasis (drafting/negotiation/approval). The directory's §10 (Enterprise Ops) vs §11 (Legal) split appears to reflect ownership angle, not distinct products. Recommend joint review: either merge, or define a real seam (e.g., post-award administration vs full lifecycle incl. legal drafting) before processing the CLM leaf. Secondary flag: contract-analytics-platform (§11) looks like a capability slice of the same systems (extraction/reporting/risk scoring embedded in all sampled products).
