- certificate-lifecycle-management (§14, processed) vs pki-management (§14 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in this cluster — CLM manages the population of issued certificates and their lifecycle (connecting to certificate authorities as external services via connectors/protocols); PKI Management would operate the issuing infrastructure itself (roots/intermediates, CA hierarchies, certificate policies, revocation infrastructure, CA key custody); evidence the seam is real: the same vendors ship the two as separate products (Keyfactor Command vs EJBCA, DigiCert Trust Lifecycle Manager vs Private CA/CA Manager, CyberArk Certificate Manager vs Zero Touch PKI) while bundling them commercially, and CLM docs consistently treat CAs — including the customer's own private CA software — as configurable connections; recommend joint review when pki-management is processed — candidate outcomes are two Types (certificate population vs issuing infrastructure) with a documented overlap zone for products that do both (research/certificate-lifecycle-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- quota-management (§07, processed) — market-structure note for joint review: in the current market this Type is almost always delivered as a module/use case inside a larger product (SPM suites, planning platforms, comp suites, RevOps platforms, rep-facing comp products); no pure standalone quota-only vendor surfaced in the sample — the leaf stands as the target-object Type (quota object + allocation machinery + attainment loop) with delivery posture recorded as a variant, mirroring the module-delivery note already recorded for business-case-management-platform; seams vs Sales Compensation Management (quota is input to comp; same vendors ship both as separate products — Varicent Sales Planning vs Incentives, Xactly Plan/Manage vs Incent, Anaplan quota vs Sales Incentives, CaptivateIQ Planning vs Incentives, Fullcast Plan vs Pay), Territory Management (coupled via quota-to-territory assignment; distinct objects/workflows), Sales Forecasting (target vs prediction), Sales Performance Management (umbrella category), OKR/Goal Management (generic goals) all held clean in this pass; recommend joint review when sales-compensation-management, sales-performance-management, and territory-management (§07 siblings, unprocessed) are processed (research/quota-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- church-giving-platform (§25, processed) vs online-donation-platform (§25 sibling, unprocessed): probable vertical-specialization pair — the church Type shares the gift/designation/receipt/recurring skeleton with generic nonprofit donation platforms, and Givelify serves both markets from one product (explicit "places of worship" + "nonprofits" use cases), but the church variant carries a distinct object layer: member-database-linked giver attribution, congregational funds vocabulary, year-end giving statements as a first-class deliverable, and ChMS integration fabric; boundary held in this pass on that object layer + vendor ecosystem; recommend joint review when online-donation-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are two Types (congregational vs generic) or a consolidation view treating church giving as the congregational variant pole; secondary note: ChMS contribution modules (e.g., ParishSOFT Offering) overlap the record half — seam held on center of gravity (giving process vs parish life) (research/church-giving-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- business-case-management-platform (§10, processed) — naming ambiguity flagged for joint review: "Business Case Management" is occasionally used in the market to mean operational case management for businesses (enterprise case management class); product evidence (Definitive Pro / Planview / Clarity / Triskell / Wellspring Accolade) supports the investment-proposal reading for this leaf, as does its directory position between Procedure Management and Business Continuity Management; if an enterprise-case-management-style leaf is ever processed, keep the two Types distinct (investment proposal + financial appraisal + approval gate vs operational case instances) — see research/business-case-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings; related note: in the current market this Type is usually delivered as a module inside PPM/SPM suites (Planview, Clarity, Triskell) — the leaf stands as the decision-governance slice; recommend joint review with project-portfolio-management-application (§03.07, unprocessed) when it is processed

- collaborative-workspace (§03.12, processed) vs team-workspace-platform (§03.12 sibling, unprocessed): probable near-alias/partial overlap — both leaves share the workspace-container concept (persistent shared container + membership + governance); working differentiation recorded in this pass: collaborative workspace = content-centric container (organized around natively authored content items — Notion/Confluence/Coda/Nuclino class), team workspace platform = hypothesized communication/suite-centric container (organized around conversations and app surfaces — Slack/Teams/suite class), but the sibling leaf was not researched (one leaf per pass) so the seam is a hypothesis; recommend joint review when team-workspace-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are two Types (communication-centric vs content-centric) or a consolidation view (research/collaborative-workspace.md §Boundary Findings)

- collaborative-workspace (§03.12, processed) vs wiki-application / enterprise-wiki (§02.06, unprocessed): real straddle — Confluence is wiki-heritage yet positions and documents itself as a team workspace (spaces + page tree + membership governance), and workspace products ship wiki/knowledge-base modes; boundary held on organizing principle (emergent interlinked topic-page graph with open editing vs governed container holding heterogeneous content with membership); recommend joint review when wiki-application and enterprise-wiki are processed (research/collaborative-workspace.md §Boundary Findings)

- financial-market-data-terminal (§08, processed) vs investment-research-platform (§08 sibling, unprocessed): research-flavored terminals straddle — TIKR ("TIKR Terminal") keeps the terminal's instrument/function spine but its center of gravity is research content and workflow (long-history financials, valuation model builder, transcripts, guru/13F portfolios), and its own competitor set spans both terminals (Bloomberg/FactSet) and research platforms (Sentieo/AlphaSense/Seeking Alpha); boundary held in this pass on the center (instrument-centered live-data workspace vs research content/workflow), removal test recorded (remove live market data → research platform); recommend joint review when investment-research-platform is processed (research/financial-market-data-terminal.md §Boundary Findings)

- financial-news-research-platform (§08, processed) vs investment-research-platform (§08 sibling, unprocessed): provisional seam — this Type centers on a platform-edited news+analysis stream for a broad investor audience with instrument-anchored persistent pages and an informational-only posture; investment-research-platform expected to center on institutional research workflow over documents (filings/transcripts/expert calls) for professional teams; overlap zone is research content itself (transcripts, earnings coverage, research reports), and TIKR-class products already straddle terminal/research (flagged in the terminal pass) — recommend joint review when investment-research-platform is processed (research/financial-news-research-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- financial-news-research-platform (§08, processed) vs news-application / news-aggregator (§02.04, unprocessed): finance-vertical news products (MarketWatch-class) held inside this Type on instrument anchoring + attached market data + investment-decision purpose + first-party editorial/analytical layer; mild flag in case §02.04 processing claims domain-vertical news products — revisit then if needed

- collaborative-spreadsheet (§03.03, processed) vs spreadsheet-application (§03.03 sibling, unprocessed): the split is capability-layer, not product-based — the same vendors (Excel, Numbers, Zoho Sheet, Google Sheets) each serve both single-user and live-shared modes of one spreadsheet grammar; the leaf boundary is the shared-live collaboration layer (one shared persistent workbook + concurrent multi-user merge), and pre-cloud multi-user file-sharing patterns fall on the Spreadsheet Application side of the seam; recommend joint review when spreadsheet-application is processed (research/collaborative-spreadsheet.md §Boundary Findings)

- financial-compliance-management (§08, processed) vs compliance-management-platform (§11 sibling, unprocessed): closest boundary pair in the taxonomy — both center obligations/activities/policies/evidence machinery and the market sells both shapes under near-identical names ("compliance management software"); boundary held in this pass on domain specificity: financial compliance management is the finance-domain instance (obligations from financial regulators, examiner-facing books-and-records evidence posture, finance-specific conduct objects — registered persons, personal trading with broker data feeds, restricted lists, MNPI/insider lists, pay-to-play, individual accountability regimes), while the generic Type lacks the conduct-object layer and the exam posture; removal test recorded: remove the financial-regulatory context → generic Compliance Management Platform; remove employee-conduct objects → obligations-centered compliance management still fits (banking pole, Ncontracts-class), so conduct is not defining; recommend joint review when compliance-management-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are two domain Types (finance vs generic) or a consolidation view treating financial as the finance-domain variant pole (research/financial-compliance-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- bug-tracking-system (§12, processed) vs issue-tracker (§12, likely unprocessed sibling): both leaves exist separately but the modern market overwhelmingly ships bug tracking as a configured use of general work-item trackers (Jira, YouTrack, GitHub Issues, GitLab) while standalone defect-centric products persist (Bugzilla, MantisBT, self-hosted/open-source ecosystems); boundary held in this pass on record model + lifecycle semantics (defect record with observed-vs-expected character and fix/verify-shaped state machine vs uniform work items with plan/execute-shaped state machine), with the removal test recorded both directions; recommend joint review when issue-tracker is processed — candidate outcomes are full separate Types (defect-centric pole vs general-tracker pole) or a consolidation view treating bug tracking as the defect-centric variant pole of issue tracking (research/bug-tracking-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- cashless-venue-platform (§26, processed) vs campus-card-management (§23, processed): structurally parallel credential-spending loops (issued credential + bound account + charged service points + central lifecycle) across two domains — boundary held on center of gravity (institution identity/entitlement program in education vs commercial in-venue spending in entertainment/hospitality; campus card's spending accounts are one entitlement among access/meal-plan/identity privileges, and its integration spine is the SIS rather than venue POS/games), but the two Types share the same loop shape and market vocabulary ("cashless campus") — recommend a light joint review to confirm the docs' cross-boundary statements stay consistent; no conflict with attraction-management-system (admission/spending seam held, consistent with that pass's own L2 placement of cashless wristbands) (research/cashless-venue-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- proposal-management (§07, processed): the RFP-response pole (Loopio/Responsive-class products — seller-side response to buyer solicitations: RFP/RFI/DDQ/security questionnaires) fits the Type's defining core (offer record → in-application assembly → delivery/submission → recorded decision) but its center of gravity is response-program operations (governed answer library, SME assignment/review cycles, readiness analytics) rather than the buyer-facing proposal document; Responsive unreachable (403) so the pole rests on Loopio plus Loopio's own category framing — if an "RFP Response Management" leaf is ever added, re-examine the variant split in applications/proposal-management.md; secondary note: two sampled products (PandaDoc deal rooms, GetAccept digital sales rooms) drift toward a shared buyer-facing deal-execution workspace containing the proposal — no directory leaf exists for "digital sales room"; recorded in case coverage is planned (research/proposal-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- building-condition-assessment (§17, processed) vs property-inspection-application (§17 sibling, unprocessed): adjacent poles of building inspection flagged for joint review — this Type's center is the portfolio condition survey translated into cost-quantified capital renewal outcomes (FCI-style indices, deferred-maintenance backlog, multi-year capital plan), while transaction-driven single-property inspection (buyer/lender due-diligence report) belongs to the sibling; Gordian sells "Due Diligence" as an add-on assessment service, confirming the adjacency; recommend joint review when property-inspection-application is processed; secondary market note: Accruent's current product index no longer lists VFA (the historical FCA incumbent; product URLs 404×3) while Gordian's site links a VFA Support Portal — consolidation observed, mechanics unverified, recorded as market observation only (research/building-condition-assessment.md §Boundary Findings)

- brokerage-platform (§08, processed) answers the joint-review flag from professional-trading-terminal (three-way seam retail-trading-platform / professional-trading-terminal / brokerage-platform): seam confirmed from the brokerage side — the brokerage platform's defining center is the account relationship (broker-gated account creation for an identified owner, value movement across the account boundary via designated funding sources and in-kind transfers, broker-maintained cash/position records with statements, trading as a capability of the account rather than the account's reason to exist); structural tests recorded: remove account administration → trading surface (Retail Trading Platform), remove the trading loop → statement portal, remove the broker gate → investment tracking app; straddles real and expected (Robinhood merges account+trading in one app, Schwab attaches thinkorswim, Zerodha ships Kite beside Console) — retail-trading-platform remains unprocessed, so the joint-review flag stands for that sibling; secondary flags: (1) crypto-inside-brokerage convergence — all three samples operate crypto through separately licensed entities with distinct protection regimes, joint review with cryptocurrency-exchange recommended when it is processed; (2) recorded judgment call: periodic statements/tax documents were placed as presentation of the custody records (L1) rather than in the defining core — a reviewer may reasonably argue periodic transaction confirmation is definitional (research/brokerage-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- promotion-management (§05.14, processed): taxonomy gap note — the CPG/manufacturer-side mirror Type (Trade Promotion Management: planning/funding promotional events through retailers, trade-fund collaboration, deduction/claim settlement — served by DemandTec's Trade Performance suite and the broader TPM/TPx category) has no directory leaf; no conflict with any existing leaf, recorded in case coverage of the trade-spend domain is planned; sibling boundaries held structurally only — retail-pricing-management and markdown-optimization-application (§05.14 siblings) are unprocessed, recommend joint review when they are (research/promotion-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- financial-advisor-platform (§08, processed) vs wealth-management-platform (§08 sibling, unprocessed): probable partial overlap flagged — market vocabulary straddles ("wealth management platform" names both institution-side platforms — broker-dealer/bank home office, product shelf, supervision — and the portfolio+reporting stack, while "advisor platform / advisor tech stack" names the advisor practice system; Orion itself runs both poles as separate divisions, Advisor Tech vs Wealth Management) — boundary held on operator + record center (advisor-operated practice system over a book of client households vs institution-side wealth business platform) — recommend joint review when wealth-management-platform is processed; secondary taxonomy note: the category is naturally a stack of point solutions (planning + portfolio + CRM + portal + billing + compliance) — the Type is modeled at the practice-system level (household + position + work products) with stack composition as variant posture, and planning-led products (eMoney, MoneyGuidePro, RightCapital) are legitimately instances of this Type since the directory has no separate financial-planning-software leaf (research/financial-advisor-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- expense-tracking-application (§08, processed) vs budgeting-application (§08 sibling, unprocessed): the two Types overlap on structure (categories, records, budget comparison) and separate only on center of gravity (plan-first allocation container vs record-first classified log); all four sampled expense trackers include budgets as a comparison layer over the record, and per PFM's earlier flag the strongest budget-first products implement the full record layer underneath the budget container — recommend joint review when budgeting-application is processed; secondary note: expense-management-platform remains unprocessed (prior batch run FAILED per batch.log), so the personal-vs-corporate expense boundary is held structurally only (research/expense-tracking-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- brand-asset-guideline-platform (§06, processed) vs brand-management-platform (§06 sibling, unprocessed): umbrella-vs-slice probable overlap flagged — market positioning straddles (DAM-first sampled products market themselves as "brand management" solutions while centering the asset+guideline record; pure-play vendors span guidelines, assets, and adjacent brand operations under one label) — recommend joint review when brand-management-platform is processed; secondary taxonomy note: the directory has no general-DAM leaf — DAM platforms are the dominant substrate for this Type and the boundary (brand-expression center + usage-rule layer + wider consumption surface vs whole-asset-estate management) is held only by center of gravity, which may matter if a DAM leaf is ever placed; guidelines-only brand-book publishing tools (no governed asset library) fall outside this Type (research/brand-asset-guideline-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- equipment-administration-platform sibling-pass answer to the enterprise-asset-registry joint-review flag (both §10): the registry pass left the test "if the sibling pass finds circulation workflow without a durable per-item record system at the center, the two remain separable Types" — the sampled equipment-administration products (Cheqroom, EZO, Sortly, Timly) never show circulation without the record backbone, so the two Types are separable only by center of gravity (equipment administration = running the reserve→hand out→use→return→service→re-circulate loop as the primary job; enterprise asset registry = the enterprise's durable record of holdings that custody flows bind to); products genuinely straddle (EZO leans record+custody, Cheqroom circulation, Sortly inventory/record-first) and market labels are shared ("equipment management"/"asset tracking" software) — recommend the taxonomy owner resolve jointly (merge vs keep-as-emphasis-pair); secondary light flag: Tool Management (§16) behaves as a segment overlay of this Type (Timly markets equipment management and tool management as sibling solutions on one site) (research/equipment-administration-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- product-usage-adoption-platform (§07, processed): the directory has no leaf for guidance-first digital-adoption products (the in-app onboarding/walkthrough category — e.g., products whose center is delivering tours/checklists rather than measuring usage); the market term "product adoption platform" is used by both measurement-centered and guidance-centered products, so if such a leaf is added later the guidance-module boundary in applications/product-usage-adoption-platform.md should be re-examined jointly; secondary: Gainsight PX deliberately straddles the usage-platform vs Customer-Success-Platform seam (PX objects sync into CS objects) — relevant when customer-success-platform and customer-health-monitoring leaves are processed (research/product-usage-adoption-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- bookkeeping-application (§08, processed) vs accounting-software (§08, processed): the same market products (Wave/Xero/FreshBooks/Zoho Books) are marketed as both "accounting software" and "bookkeeping software" — the two leaves sit over one continuous SMB financial-software category; documented by center of gravity (bookkeeping = operational record-keeping workflow keeping books current/verifiable/handoff-ready; accounting = books engine with balanced double-entry posting + statement derivation), with vendor-stated seams (Wave guide: "bookkeeping is day-to-day... accounting turns records into reports"; FreshBooks bookkeeping-service page: categorize/reconcile/tidy the general ledger) — recommend joint review to confirm both docs' cross-boundary statements remain consistent; secondary seams held: vs General Ledger System (enterprise scale), Invoicing Application (billing operation vs capture surface), Expense Tracking (no books semantics), Personal Finance Management (personal entity), Tax Preparation (consumes the books)

- biodiversity-management vs nature-risk-management / natural-capital-management (§21 siblings, both unprocessed): probable overlap flagged — sampled finance-pole products (portfolio nature-risk analytics) implement the risk-decision slice (screen → score → materiality → disclosure) of biodiversity management's canonical loop and legitimately fit either label, while natural-capital management shares the geospatial condition substrate but centers ecosystem-services valuation/accounting instead of species/habitat impact/dependency records; boundary held on record+measurement+monitoring depth (biodiversity management spans record → assess → act → monitor → disclose incl. primary data capture) — recommend joint review when both sibling leaves are processed; also held vs Conservation Management (org-impact interface vs conservation delivery), Environmental Monitoring (physico-chemical telemetry vs living-diversity records), ESG platform (KPI aggregation vs site-anchored species/habitat machinery), EIA platform (project lifecycle vs portfolio/state) (research/biodiversity-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- bim-coordination vs bim-authoring (§17 siblings): boundary held cleanly on the system-of-record test (authoring owns the elements and their data; coordination owns the federation, checks and issues; in-authoring clash checks are a convenience layer) — consistent with the bim-authoring pass, which assigned this work downstream; open question flagged: rules-based model validation (Solibri-class checking, IDS requirement checking) is currently embedded inside coordination products — if standalone validation platforms emerge, whether it deserves a separate Type should be reviewed (research/bim-coordination.md §Uncertainties)

- calendar-application vs shared-team-calendar / resource-calendar (§03.08 siblings): research suggests the siblings are audience/object variants of the same defining structure (shared team calendar = the Type's sharing+permission machinery pointed at an organization; resource calendar = a calendar owned by a bookable resource such as a conference room, consumed through free/busy rather than personal planning — evidenced via Outlook group schedules and Apple resource-schedule views) rather than independent Types — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed; boundary vs §03.09 scheduling leaves held cleanly on center of gravity (negotiating a time across people vs maintaining the persistent event record) (research/calendar-application.md §Boundary Findings)
- product-catalog-management vs product-information-management-pim (§05.04 siblings): market usage inconsistent — commerce platforms embed content authoring inside catalog management while PIM vendors publish buyer-facing "catalog sites"; boundary held on center of gravity (PCM = maintain the sellable offer — structure/variants/categories/prices/availability — for one's own sales channels; PIM = govern product content as master data and syndicate it to other parties' selling systems incl. GDSN/retailer endpoints); recommend joint review when the PIM leaf is processed; Digital Product Catalog (§05.04) confirmed as the published buyer-facing output of catalog management, not the management surface; also note the Type is overwhelmingly realized as a module of commerce platforms/POS rather than standalone products (research/product-catalog-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- procurement-management-platform vs procure-to-pay-platform (§10 siblings, both now processed): resolved by center of gravity — P2P defines the transactional chain (approved demand → PO → receipt → matched invoice → payment-ready payable) with invoice matching as the definitional gate; PMP defines the procurement operation (managed supplier base incl. onboarding/qualification, governed demand, sourcing context, policy/spend control) whose endpoint is the managed purchase and supplier relationship, handing receipts/commitments downstream to finance; all 5 sampled suites (SAP Ariba, JAGGAER, Procurify, Tradogram, Zip) ship both centers in one product and Zip explicitly brackets both ("intake-to-pay") — probable partial-superset adjacency; recommend joint review for possible merge/re-scope or an explicit center-of-gravity split; related sibling boundaries held on object/center tests: Purchase Order Management (PO-object lifecycle), Strategic/E-sourcing (events→contract), Supplier Management (supplier lifecycle as primary object), Spend Analysis (analytics-only), Supplier Portal (external slice); Government Procurement Platform remains sector-adjacent (solicitation/bid/public-records machinery) per the earlier P2P flag (research/procurement-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- bill-of-materials-management vs product-lifecycle-management-plm packaging gradient (§16 siblings): market gravitates to PLM-branded packaging (Duro self-labels PLM; OpenBOM lists a PLM capability; Aligni pairs PLM+MRP) while the BOM-management core remains extractable and independently sellable (OpenBOM, Aligni; formerly Arena's BOM-branded entry tier) — leaf documented as the item/BOM/revision-structure-centered Type with the suite-module pattern stated in Variants; boundary criterion = center of gravity (structural definition + controlled evolution as the managed world vs the full lifecycle estate of CAD vaulting/documents/requirements/quality); recommend joint review when the PLM leaf is processed (research/bill-of-materials-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- bill-of-materials-management vs engineering-change-management (§16 sibling): every sampled BOM product embeds a change workflow (change request → change order → approval → released revision) scoped to items/BOMs/revisions as a standard capability — flagged so that the Engineering Change Management leaf stays reserved for change-centered products whose primary managed objects span wider engineering artifacts (documents, files, specifications); if that leaf is defined broadly, partial-alias risk exists — recommend joint review when it is processed

- book-distribution-management module-vs-type note (§27): in the reachable market the distribution operation ships mostly as a module of publishing management suites (Klopotek O2C inside the Klopotek suite; Stison/Consonance carry the data/terms/sales layer while physical fulfillment is delegated to distributors) rather than as clearly standalone products; leaf documented as the functional core (titles × trade accounts × orders × stock × fulfillment→sales records) with the suite-module pattern stated in Variants; boundary held vs Publishing Metadata Management (metadata distribution to trading partners — Firebrand Eloquence pattern — is the metadata leaf's territory) and vs generic OMS/WMS (bibliographic identity + trade terms + ONIX/EDI conventions + returnable-stock economy are the separators); name-collision guard: Music Distribution Platform (streaming supply chain) and Press Release Distribution Platform are unrelated Types; sourcing limitation: dedicated distribution products Titleplay (403), CatS, Publishers Assistant, Broadland, virtuos (transport errors) and web.archive.org unreachable on 2026-09-06 — no operational claims drawn from them (research/book-distribution-management.md §Boundary Findings).

- enterprise-risk-management vs governance-risk-compliance-platform / operational-risk-management (§11 siblings): ERM confirmed as a valid standalone Type (register-centric core: shared taxonomy + standardized assessment + recorded response + enterprise roll-up), but in the live market it is almost always delivered as a module/solution inside broader GRC/IRM/RMIS platforms (Archer, LogicGate, Riskonnect, LogicManager all sell it this way) — documented as the risk-centered application of the GRC suite; boundary vs ORM is porous (Archer sells them as one combined use case; LogicGate/Riskonnect sell them separately; both share risk records/controls/self-assessments/loss events, differing on center of gravity: process-level losses/controls vs enterprise roll-up to leadership) — recommend joint review when Governance Risk & Compliance Platform and Operational Risk Management are processed; sourcing limitation: ServiceNow IRM (2× timeout), MetricStream (403), IBM OpenPages docs (403) unreachable — platform-module market form under-represented; evidence rests at product-page/help-structure level for the four sampled products (research/enterprise-risk-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- banking-operations-management vs banking-back-office-platform (§08 siblings; joint review now possible — both leaves processed): research confirmed the execution test is the only clean separator (back-office platform executes validate→authorize→execute with posting/transmission; operations management observes/coordinates/measures without executing), but the market rarely sells the management layer standalone — it ships as embedded surfaces inside execution platforms (Oracle Banking Payments Exception Queues + Dashboard user guides; Volante/Finastra hub dashboards per the sibling pass), as vendor "operations" portfolio categories bundling execution platforms with analytics and services (Jack Henry, Fiserv), as WFM-derived back-office operations suites (Verint Operations Visualizer/Productivity/Manager), and as domain-specific oversight tools (Alogent AccuAccount exception tracking); leaf documented as the management layer with the overlap stated explicitly in the final doc; recommend joint review of the three §08 siblings (Core Banking System / Banking Back-office Platform / Banking Operations Management) for possible merge or re-scoping; secondary thin boundary vs Workforce Management Platform (standalone products of this Type are often WFM vendors' banking offerings); sourcing limitation: no general web search available this pass (DDG/Bing/Mojeek/Brave/Ecosia unreachable or localized) and FIS/Pega/Appian returned access errors, so the "no standalone category under this exact name" finding is calibrated to the researched sample only (research/banking-operations-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- beauty-service-marketplace vs service-marketplace / local-service-marketplace (§05.02/§29) + operator-side beauty leaves (salon-management-system, beauty-professional-business-app, barbershop-management, spa-management-system): documented as the beauty-domain sibling marketplace per the babysitting-marketplace precedent — boundary held on domain structuring (provider-defined beauty service menus with duration/price, licensing/vetting norms, beauty categories) and on whose surface is primary (cross-provider consumer discovery vs running one business); vendor bundling of both surfaces in one brand (SaaS-first posture) confirmed from the consumer side, consistent with flags recorded by beauty-professional-business-app and barbershop-management passes; joint review recommended when Local Service Marketplace and Service Marketplace are processed; sourcing limitation: Fresha/Booksy/Treatwell (beauty-native marketplaces), Urban Company (full-stack managed model), Blys/Soothe unreachable (403/JS shells, abandoned per network rules) — no commercial-economics claims (commissions/fees/payouts) asserted anywhere; evidence rests on Vagaro (Tier-1 consumer help center), Mindbody/Glamsquad/Mobile Styles (Tier-2 official sites) (research/beauty-service-marketplace.md §Boundary Findings)
- process-mining-platform sourcing limitation: Celonis technical docs (docs.celonis.com) authentication-gated (401; official product pages only, Tier-2 evidence), SAP Signavio unreachable (help.sap.com JS shell ×2, signavio.com 404 — retained as market-anchor representative only, no operational claims drawn from it), Apromore docs portal unreachable (transport error/404; official product pages used) — no precise vendor parameters (refresh cadences, object limits, threshold defaults) asserted anywhere in the final doc; vendor rebranding toward "process intelligence / execution management" recorded as a naming trend, not a Type change — analyst category name "Process Mining Platforms" matches the leaf; boundaries held vs BPM Platform (model-driven execution vs event-driven observation), Task Mining Platform (desktop UI-level vs business-transaction level), RPA Platform (execution vs observation), BI Platform (case-sequence derivation vs generic aggregation) (recorded in Sources of applications/process-mining-platform.md)
- beneficiary-management vs nonprofit-case-management (§25 siblings): the products that implement beneficiary management all market themselves as case management (Apricot "case management at scale", ActivityInfo case-management use case, CommCare case-management platform) — boundary held on a center-of-gravity test (population registry + what was delivered to it vs a bounded casework episode driven by an accountable caseworker to closure), but market vocabulary does not separate the two names; flagged for joint review when Nonprofit Case Management is processed (research/beneficiary-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- beneficiary-management homonym guard: "beneficiary" in insurance (designated payout recipient on a policy) is a data field inside Insurance Policy Administration Systems, not this Type — recorded so the two are never merged; also adjacent: Monitoring & Evaluation Platform (indicators vs people; ActivityInfo bridges both deliberately) and Social Services Case Management / Public Benefits Management (same mechanics, government operator and statutory eligibility) (research/beneficiary-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- beneficiary-management sourcing limitation: CommCare public help wiki (dimagi.atlassian.net) and docs.commcarehq.org unreachable (transport errors ×2), Apricot help center unreachable (403 on /products path; /product/apricot product page used), Salesforce NPSP docs 403 (CRM-module philosophy evidenced via CiviCRM instead), RedRose (humanitarian beneficiary-registration category) JS-only shell — evidence rests on official product pages + ActivityInfo docs index + CiviCRM user guide; no precise operational details (permission matrices, record limits, status vocabularies) asserted anywhere (recorded in Sources of applications/beneficiary-management.md).
- banking-back-office-platform vs banking-operations-management (§08 siblings; Banking Operations Management not yet processed): the market does not clearly separate the two names — vendors sell "operations" as a category spanning core platforms + branch/teller operations + payment processing (Jack Henry), and universal suites bundle core + back office so the ledger/workbench boundary blurs; boundary held on the execution test (back-office platform executes transactions through validate→authorize→execute with human exception repair; "operations management" reads as the monitoring/oversight layer that observes and coordinates without executing), but the sibling leaf likely overlaps or aliases this Type — flagged for joint review when Banking Operations Management is processed (research/banking-back-office-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- banking-back-office-platform sourcing limitation: Infosys Finacle/EdgeVerve (403 ×2), TCS BaNCS (403 + transport error), FIS (timeout), ACI Worldwide (404 on deep URL) unreachable on 2026-09-06; Temenos documentation portal login-gated (marketing pages only, positioning-strength claims); Oracle Banking Payments deep guide content not retrievable (HTML covers only; PDFs >5MB or binary) — exception-queue mechanics asserted from the documented module structure plus cross-vendor prose; no precise operational figures (STP rates, cut-off times, approval thresholds) stated as general facts (recorded in Sources of applications/banking-back-office-platform.md).
- application-deployment-management naming ambiguity (§14 vs §12): the phrase "application deployment" is also standard vocabulary for server-side release tooling (CD pipelines deploying build artifacts to servers/environments — Octopus Deploy/UrbanCode-style) — documented per directory neighborhood as the endpoint/IT-admin software-distribution Type (section 14, next to Patch Management and UEM); server-side application deployment belongs to Continuous Delivery Platform / Release Management Platform (section 12); flagged so the two are never merged; adjacent boundaries held vs Patch Management (content = vendor-published updates), UEM (config/compliance objects), Desktop & Application Delivery (virtual delivery, no endpoint install) (research/application-deployment-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- beat-making-application vs digital-audio-workstation-daw / loop-based-music-production-application / music-production-application (04.09/04.10 siblings): market labels blur — one sampled product is marketed as "Free DAW Software" (Akai MPC Beats page title) and another self-describes as "the modern DAW for making beats" (Serato Studio); boundary held on center-of-gravity tests (rhythm-anchored pattern composition + sampling vs general multi-track recording/editing vs pre-made loop assembly), a gradient not a wall; flagged for joint review when DAW and Loop-based Music Production Application leaves are processed (research/beat-making-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- beat-making-application sourcing limitation: Akai marketing site (JS shell + 404 ×2) and FL Studio online manual (404 + nav-only render) unreachable on 2026-09-06 — Akai evidence rests on official support-KB article titles, FL evidence on the official features page; no precise vendor numbers (track/instrument/library counts, pattern-length options, project limits) asserted in the final doc (recorded in Sources of applications/beat-making-application.md).
- private-market-investment-platform naming hazard (§08): the leaf name could be misread as LP-side institutional private-market investment management (eFront/AltV-style portfolio suites) — that reading is Portfolio Management System territory (already processed); market usage of the phrase (fund-access platforms, pre-IPO marketplaces, retail startup-investing platforms) is the investor-side access platform, and the leaf was documented as such; flagged for human review of directory intent (research/private-market-investment-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- private-market-investment-platform sibling flags (§08, unprocessed leaves): Investor Portal behaves as a capability slice (LP-facing documents/statements of a GP-operated fund relationship; no discovery/eligibility/subscription) that this Type also tends to provide for the investments it originates — joint review suggested; Fund Administration boundary held on GP-side back office vs investor-side access (Carta's own support taxonomy separates them; platforms consume fund admin as a service); equity crowdfunding (Wefunder/Republic-style) has no dedicated directory leaf and fits this Type as the retail variant — recorded in case a leaf is ever added (research/private-market-investment-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- private-market-investment-platform sourcing limitation: iCapital, Yieldstreet, Forge Global, Republic, Securitize, CAIS, Fundrise all unreachable on 2026-09-06 (403/timeout/transport errors, abandoned after 1–2 attempts each) — sample rests on Moonfare + EquityZen + Wefunder (Tier-1 help/FAQ docs) with Carta + AngelList as boundary anchors; the wealth-channel distribution variant is described structurally only; no operational claims about unreachable products; no precise vendor figures (minimums/fees/timelines/cadences) in the final doc (recorded in Sources of applications/private-market-investment-platform.md).
- bed-capacity-management vs patient-flow-management (sibling under §22): boundary is porous in the market — vendors market one capability cluster under both names (Oracle Health sells a product literally named "Patient Flow" whose documented features automate bed selection/EVS requests; TeleTracking markets its bed-centric suite as "Throughput — Integrated Patient Flow"; LeanTaaS names its capacity product "Inpatient Flow"); boundary held on the object test: patient flow = person-centric journey (stages/timing of the patient's movement through care), bed & capacity = space-centric resource (per-bed state, readiness cycle, placement decisions, capacity planning); products routinely bundle both layers; analytics-only capacity overlays kept inside the Type on the KLAS "capacity management" category framing, possible future split; flagged for joint review when Patient Flow Management is processed (research/bed-capacity-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- bed-capacity-management sourcing limitation: no sampled vendor publishes public operational documentation for bed/capacity modules (TeleTracking Knowledge Bridge login-gated, CenTrak knowledge center gated, LeanTaaS/Oracle Health expose official solution pages only) — evidence rests at Tier-2 official solution-page level; no precise state vocabularies, thresholds, timers, or defaults asserted anywhere; placement rule engines (isolation/level-of-care constraints) recorded as implied-but-undocumented; MEDITECH acute-care page fetched but generic (rejected as representative); failed fetches not retried: leantaas.com/products/iqueue/, centrak.com/patient-flow, oracle.com/health/capacity-management/ (404 ×1 each) (recorded in Sources of applications/bed-capacity-management.md).
- api-security-platform sourcing limitation: Salt Security docs site unreachable (transport error; official product pages only, Tier-2 evidence) and Akamai API Security techdocs JS-rendered/unreachable (documented `.md` fallback also returned an empty shell) — Salt used only to confirm cross-product commonality of discovery/posture/protection, Akamai treated as market context with no evidentiary weight; no precise vendor parameters (audit scores, thresholds, sampling rates, numeric limits) asserted anywhere in the final document (recorded in Sources of applications/api-security-platform.md). Boundary vs WAF / API Gateway Management Console held on structural removal tests (remove the API-semantic inventory → WAF; remove security findings → gateway console/analytics); no taxonomy conflict found.
- b2b-e-commerce-platform vs wholesale-commerce-platform / dealer-distributor-commerce-portal (siblings under 05.17): wholesale selling is typically executed on a platform of this Type (org accounts + account-gated trade pricing + catalog ordering) and a dealer portal applies the same structure to the manufacturer→dealer channel — probable Alias/Variant relationships; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/b2b-e-commerce-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- b2b-e-commerce-platform sourcing limitation: OroCommerce (B2B-native open-source) docs unreachable (transport errors ×2 on 2026-09-06, dropped as a source), Shopify Help Center HTTP 403 (substituted with official shopify.dev B2B docs), BigCommerce Help Center script-rendered (substituted with official developer docs), Sana help center unreachable ×2 (evidence rests at official-site Tier-2 level); no precise vendor numbers (credit limits, approval thresholds, price-list counts, plan entitlements) asserted anywhere; punchout/procurement-gateway integration not verified in the sample and not asserted (recorded in Sources of applications/b2b-e-commerce-platform.md).
- banquet-management vs catering-management / venue-management-system (§26 siblings, not yet processed): heavy product overlap — sampled products span on-premise function execution and off-premise catering (Caterease, Tripleseat's catering segment), and hotel vendors market the same structure as "sales & catering software"; boundary held on center-of-gravity tests (banquet = booked function in the venue's own function spaces: diary + BEO + on-premise execution; catering = food production/delivery; venue management = space inventory for any use, without the F&B/BEO layer); flagged for joint review when Catering Management and Venue Management System are processed (research/banquet-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- personal-finance-management-application vs budgeting-application (siblings under §08): the strongest budget-first product in the sample (YNAB) implements the entire PFM core underneath its budget container (accounts with on_budget flag, transactions, categories, payees, months), so the two Types overlap on structure and separate only on center of gravity (budget as the sole organizing object vs whole-picture with budgeting as one capability); the three subset siblings (Expense Tracking, Net Worth Tracker) and the read-only-vs-bank-app boundary are held on structural removal tests; flagged for joint review when Budgeting Application is processed (research/personal-finance-management-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- privacy-management-platform vs GRC / Compliance Management / Third-party Risk / DSPM / Data Catalog-Governance family (§10/§11/§13 siblings, mostly not yet processed): boundary held on the object model, not the feature list — privacy platform's spine is personal-data processing records + privacy obligations + discharge/evidence loop with individual-rights machinery (rights requests, consent records); GRC = domain-generic risks/controls/requirements, TPRM = vendor-relationship-centered, DSPM/catalog = data posture/use without obligations or rights; suite gradient is real (sampled privacy vendors bundle vendor privacy risk, incident management, AI governance) — flagged for joint review when Governance Risk & Compliance Platform, Compliance Management Platform, and Third-party Risk Management are processed; also noted: the directory has no standalone Consent Management Platform leaf — web consent/banner tools are the capture layer of this Type's consent capability, recorded in case one is ever added.
- personal-finance-management-application sourcing limitation: PocketSmith help center unreachable (transport errors ×2 on 2026-09-06, abandoned) and YNAB user help center script-rendered (empty fetch; ynab.com/method timeout) — YNAB evidence rests on its official API documentation (object model/scopes/terms) only; no claims about PocketSmith or YNAB user-facing method details anywhere; no precise vendor numbers (bank coverage, prices, limits, history depth) asserted (recorded in Sources of applications/personal-finance-management-application.md).
- audience-response-system cross-domain placement & Polling Application adjacency (§26 vs §03.11): the leaf sits under Events, but research shows education (lectures) and corporate meetings are equally primary habitats for the sampled products — the placement captures only one habitat; boundary with Polling Application held on the session-instrument test (facilitator-run live session + real-time aggregate shown back to the same room — async/embedded poll tools without the live loop are polling, not ARS); ARS products bundling survey/self-paced modes is extension into Survey Platform territory, not Type merger; native polling embedded inside webinar/meeting platforms is a capability of those Types, not a standalone ARS instance; flagged for joint review when Polling Application is processed (research/audience-response-system.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-video-editing-application placement & gradient (§04.21 vs §04.06): the leaf sits under Generative Video, but its defining material is user-supplied existing footage — generative operations are a common capability, not the definition; and the boundary with Video Editor / NLE is a locus-of-execution gradient (system executes edits as primary interaction vs human executes on a timeline), with hybrid products (CapCut, Runway Studio) spanning both loci and NLEs increasingly embedding AI aids; boundary held on the material test (existing footage vs footage created from a prompt) and the execution test; flagged for awareness when Video Editor / NLE and AI Video Generator leaves are processed (research/ai-video-editing-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-video-editing-application sourcing limitation: Veed help center unreachable (timeouts ×2 on 2026-09-06) — a fifth "web AI editor for business" posture unverified; sample rests on Descript + OpusClip + Runway (Tier-1 help docs) + CapCut via its Chinese sibling site capcut.cn (international CapCut docs not directly reachable; parity assumed, not verified); no precise product limits (clip-length/resolution ceilings, language/timeline counts) asserted in the final doc (recorded in Sources of applications/ai-video-editing-application.md).
- ai-research-assistant vs answer-engine / academic-search-engine (§02.03 family gradient): market language straddles the boundaries — general answer products are adding deep-research/project-workspace features that drift into this Type, and Consensus self-describes as an "AI-powered academic search engine" while being assistant-shaped; boundary held on the structural tests (research-material substrate + AI-performs-the-reading + persisted research artifacts); flagged for joint review when Answer Engine and Knowledge Question Answering Application are processed (research/ai-research-assistant.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-research-assistant sourcing limitation: NotebookLM (support.google.com/notebooklm, notebooklm.google.com), SciSpace (scispace.com) and Scite (scite.ai) unreachable after 2 attempts each on 2026-09-06 — sample rests on Elicit + Consensus (Tier-1 help docs), Humata + Scholarcy (Tier-1 official pages/guide); the user-document-grounded philosophy is evidenced by Humata/Scholarcy rather than the (unreachable) notebook-style products; no claims made about the unreachable products; no corpus sizes/upload limits/plan mechanics asserted anywhere in the final doc (recorded in Sources of applications/ai-research-assistant.md).
- air-quality-monitoring indoor/outdoor scope: sampled products (Kaiterra, IQAir) span indoor IAQ and outdoor ambient monitoring under one core model (points + pollutant time series + current/history), so indoor IAQ was held as a Variant, not a separate Type; if a future "Indoor Air Quality Monitoring" leaf is added to the directory, revisit whether it is an Alias of this Type or a distinct Type with building-specific rules (research/air-quality-monitoring.md §Boundary Findings).

- ad-delivery-platform vs ad-server (siblings under §06): every sampled product self-identifies as an "ad server"/"ad serving" system (Kevel "fully featured ad server", AdButler "ad serving platform", Revive "ad serving tool", Xandr Monetize's explicit "Ad server" role) and no market evidence of a distinct "ad delivery platform" category was found — "ad delivery" is the delivery-centric framing of the same request-time selection engine; probable Alias — flagged for joint review when Ad Server is processed (research/ad-delivery-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- attraction-management-system sibling-leaf cluster (§26): research indicates Attraction Ticketing, Cashless Venue Platform, and Digital Waiver Management are slices of the same underlying admission-business Type, and Theme Park Management / Zoo-Aquarium Visitor Operations / Museum Visitor Experience Platform / Family Entertainment Center Management are segment- or layer-variants of it (Theme Park Management = park physical operations layer; Museum Visitor Experience = visitor experience layer; FEC/Zoo = segment postures); each sibling deserves its own research pass to confirm slice-vs-variant-vs-independent-Type status before any taxonomy change (research/attraction-management-system.md §Boundary Findings).

- alumni-management vs university-advancement-platform (§23 siblings): heavy real-world overlap — alumni relations is routinely packaged inside advancement suites, and alumni platforms position themselves as engagement layers over advancement CRMs as system of record (Almabase TrueSync→RE NXT; Graduway→RE NXT/Salesforce "advancement system of record"); the split holds on centers of gravity (alumni register + engagement relationship vs gift pipeline/fundraising operations over all constituents) and engagement-shaped products exist without fundraising pipelines, but joint review suggested when University Advancement Platform is processed; also adjacent: corporate alumni networks (employer-based affiliation, same engagement machinery — Hoopstr, Hivebrite) kept outside this leaf's core (research/alumni-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- alumni-management sourcing limitation: Hivebrite and Almabase help centers unreachable on 2026-09-06 (timeouts/transport errors ×2 each; hivebrite.io/alumni-management-software 403) — evidence is Tier-2 official product pages + 360Alumni Tier-1 KB index; no precise record-field lists, lifecycle state names, or engagement-scoring formulas asserted (recorded in Sources of applications/alumni-management.md).

- raster-image-editor vs digital-painting-application: boundary is a primary-job gradient (edit existing pixels vs create artwork from scratch), not a structural wall — vendor evidence (Krita manual) supports the current 04.02 split, but the two leaves share nearly all L1 machinery and may deserve a joint review pass when Digital Painting Application is processed.
- email-client vs webmail-application: the two leaves share the entire L0 core model (mail account + envelope message + send/receive + persistent store) and differ only by delivery surface (installed app vs browser) and typical provider coupling — documented in research/email-client.md §Boundary Findings; may deserve a joint review pass when Webmail Application is processed.
- mobile-pos vs retail-point-of-sale (05.10 siblings): joint review flagged by the 2026-09-06 retail pass DISCHARGED 2026-09-08 — keep-both RATIFIED as two surface-defined Types sharing one sale spine: Mobile POS L0 = retail spine + portability of the sale surface (seller-carried phone/tablet/handheld with paired/attached/built-in payment capture taken to the exchange; no fixed counter required); evidence: named market category with vendor-articulated definitions (Shopify's own mPOS guide + countertop/mobile/multichannel POS-types FAQ; PayPal POS "On-the-go" lead segmentation; SumUp portable-first kit), mobile-native products where the portable device is the entire POS (no-premises micro-merchant pole), and surface-class consequences users/hardware/rules (reader pairing + software-only acceptance, paperless base with optional counter peripherals, device-stays-with-seller security, connectivity/offline posture); nesting documented in both directions (retail doc's variant table ↔ mobile doc's Related Types); residual risk recorded: vendors ship all three 05.10 forms as modes/editions of one product (Erply editions, Shopify taxonomy), so the trio is the canonical merge candidate if surface-defined siblings are ever consolidated (email-client/webmail precedent); omnichannel-pos remains unprocessed and still flagged for the same joint review
- retail-point-of-sale vs mobile-pos / omnichannel-pos (siblings under 05.10): both siblings implement the same L0 core (priced catalog → sale → tender → completed transaction) and differ only by surface form factor (Mobile POS) or channel-integration depth (Omnichannel POS); vendors themselves ship them as configurations/editions of one product — likely Variants/Aliases rather than independent Types; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/retail-point-of-sale.md §Boundary Findings).
- retail-point-of-sale vs restaurant-pos: the two Types share the entire transaction spine (catalog-configured order → transaction → payment) and differ in sale semantics (immediate paid sale + returns vs table/check/service-period lifecycle); vendors ship both as modes of single products, so the boundary is semantic, not structural — documented in research/retail-point-of-sale.md; no taxonomy change proposed.
- identity-access-management-iam vs single-sign-on-sso / multi-factor-authentication-mfa (siblings under 15): both are capabilities that every sampled modern IAM bundles as L1 components (federation, factor management); a standalone SSO/MFA product lacks identity lifecycle and central administration as primary structure, so the leaves likely behave as Capabilities/Variants of IAM rather than independent Types — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/identity-access-management-iam.md §Boundary Findings).
- identity-access-management-iam vs directory services (no dedicated leaf in section 15): the on-prem directory service (AD DS era) already satisfies the IAM L0 (administered identities + sign-in authn + object access control + policy administration), so "directory service" and "IAM" differ by deployment-era gradient, not structure; no directory leaf exists to conflict with, recorded as an observation only (research/identity-access-management-iam.md §Boundary Findings).
- electronic-health-record-ehr vs CPOE / Clinical Decision Support System / Electronic Prescribing / Medication Management Platform (siblings under 22): in the researched sample all four are L1 capabilities of the EHR (order entry, decision rules, medication orders, prescribing) rather than independent Types; standalone products exist in some markets — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/electronic-health-record-ehr.md §Boundary Findings).
- electronic-health-record-ehr vs Home Health EHR / Long-term Care EHR (siblings under 22): both are care-setting variants implementing the same L0 core model with setting-specific documentation and regulatory overlays — likely Variants rather than independent Types; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/electronic-health-record-ehr.md §Boundary Findings).
- electronic-health-record-ehr EMR/EHR terminology: the leaf name carries both terms; research shows the market (incl. ONC-certified open source) uses them interchangeably and the historical EMR-vs-EHR distinction describes an interoperability posture (L2), not two structures — treated as one Type, no taxonomy change proposed (research/electronic-health-record-ehr.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-coding-agent vs ai-coding-assistant (siblings under §12): the boundary is who holds the execution loop (assistant = human performs each step; agent = AI performs the loop, human directs/reviews) — an autonomy gradient, not a wall; vendors ship both structures inside one product line (agent modes inside assistant products, assistant modes inside agents), so the two leaves likely need a shared "autonomy gradient" framing — flagged for joint review when AI Coding Assistant is processed (research/ai-coding-agent.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-coding-agent vs ai-software-engineering-agent (siblings under §12): the researched product marketed as an "AI software engineer" implements the identical L0 structure (task → autonomous tool loop → reviewable changes); "AI software engineer" is positioning (ticket-level delegation, team-member framing, cloud-only delivery), not a distinct structure — probable Alias/Variant of AI Coding Agent; flagged for joint review, no taxonomy change made unilaterally (research/ai-coding-agent.md §Boundary Findings).
- fleet-management-system vs vehicle-telematics-platform (sibling under §18): telematics is the data-acquisition/connectivity layer, FMS is the management application over it; the researched sample shows FMS bundling telematics as L1 (proprietary hardware, integrations, or device-agnostic) and one vendor's own FAQ defining FMS as the layer "over" telematics data; test = remove the oversight loop → telematics remains; remove the live feed → register-led FMS remains — flagged for joint review when Vehicle Telematics Platform is processed (research/fleet-management-system.md §Boundary Findings).
- fleet-management-system vs ev-fleet-charging-management / autonomous-fleet-management (siblings under §18): in the researched sample EV energy/charging and autonomy appear as L2 overlays on the same FMS core (charge monitoring inside a fleet platform), suggesting Variant status; network-scale charging management may still be an independent infrastructure Type — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/fleet-management-system.md §Boundary Findings).
- fleet-management-system vs robot-fleet-management / mining-fleet-management / marine-fleet-management (siblings under §16/§18/§20): the same register + activity + oversight pattern generalizes to non-road fleets, but those leaves carry domain-specific telemetry/operations the road-vehicle core model does not capture — related Types sharing an oversight pattern; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/fleet-management-system.md §Boundary Findings).
- fleet-management-system vs driver-management (sibling under §18): driver records/assignment/scores are L1 inside FMS in all sampled products; a standalone Driver Management leaf would center the driver rather than the fleet — probable Capability/Variant relationship; flagged for joint review when Driver Management is processed (research/fleet-management-system.md §Boundary Findings).
- 2d-animation-application vs motion-graphics-application (sibling under 04.07): gradient boundary, not a wall — both share keyframes, layers, and effects; the difference is center of gravity (authored drawings + character performance incl. frame-by-frame cels vs moving finished graphic/typographic material); overlap zone is real (rig tools animate graphics; MG tools animate characters via plugins) — flagged for joint review when Motion Graphics Application is processed (research/2d-animation-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- 2d-animation-application vs character-animation-application (sibling under 04.08): in the researched sample, character rig animation is a workflow/capability inside general 2D animation products (rig-first products still satisfy the 2D-animation core; hand-drawn products lack rigging entirely) — probable Variant/Capability rather than independent Type; flagged for joint review when Character Animation Application is processed (research/2d-animation-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- a-b-testing-platform vs digital-experimentation-platform (sibling under §06): the researched sample shows one shared defining core (variants + randomization + measured comparison + decision) expressed in two philosophies — marketing/CRO-first (visual editor, client-side web surface, campaign packaging) vs engineering-first (server-side parameters, feature-flag and warehouse integration); vendors themselves ship both under one roof (Optimizely Web/Feature Experimentation lines, VWO Testing/Feature Experimentation, Statsig self-describes its core as A/B RCTs) — probable audience-gradient split rather than two structures; flagged for joint review when Digital Experimentation Platform is processed (research/a-b-testing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- a-b-testing-platform vs conversion-rate-optimization-platform / landing-page-optimization-platform (siblings under §06): CRO is the practice/goal and A/B testing the instrument (market "CRO platforms" are supersets bundling testing + behavior analytics + personalization + program management); Landing Page Optimization is the same core restricted to a surface — probable superset-framing and Variant status respectively; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/a-b-testing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- account-abuse-protection vs fraud-prevention-platform (sibling under §15): the two Types share the entire event→risk→decision loop and are frequently one product (Sift spans account takeover + payment fraud on one decisioning engine); the structural test is the protected object — account lifecycle (access/creation/account-linked privileges) vs transactions/payments (order fraud, chargebacks, cash-out) — a scope gradient, not a wall; flagged for joint review when Fraud Prevention Platform is processed (research/account-abuse-protection.md §Boundary Findings).
- account-abuse-protection vs multi-factor-authentication-mfa (sibling under §15): MFA is the challenge factor; account abuse protection is the decision system that determines when step-up is warranted and orchestrates it (documented mitigation examples across sampled products include "require MFA") — Capability relationship, consistent with the earlier IAM-vs-MFA flag; flagged for joint review when MFA is processed (research/account-abuse-protection.md §Boundary Findings).
- account-abuse-protection workforce variant: Microsoft Entra ID Protection is structurally isomorphic (sign-in events → risk level → risk-based access decision + risky-user reports + confirm-safe/confirm-compromise) but lives inside an identity platform and targets workforce identities; no dedicated workforce identity-threat-protection leaf exists in §15 — recorded as an observation that the leaf's definition must not be consumer-only; possible Variant relationship with IAM to be considered in a joint review (research/account-abuse-protection.md §Boundary Findings).
- 311-citizen-service-request-platform naming: the leaf embeds "311", a North American program brand; researched Type is global (UK FixMyStreet, EU CitySDK cities, Malaysia, Switzerland) and satisfies the core with no 311 number and no call center — treated as a regional program wrapper (L2), no rename made unilaterally (research/311-citizen-service-request-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- 311-citizen-service-request-platform vs constituent-relationship-management (sibling under §24): Accela itself markets the module as "Service Request Management (SRM/CRM)", and several 311 platforms bundle constituent profiles/history; the structural test is request lifecycle vs relationship history — probable adjacency/overlap to resolve in a joint review when Constituent Relationship Management is processed (research/311-citizen-service-request-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- 3d-animation-application vs character-animation-application (sibling under 04.08): in the researched sample, character rigging/animation (bones/IK/skinning/pose libraries) is a capability inside every sampled general 3D animation product (Blender rigging section, C4D rigging tags, Houdini character section) — probable Variant/Capability rather than independent Type; mirrors the 2D-side flag; flagged for joint review when Character Animation Application is processed (research/3d-animation-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- 2d/3d-animation-application vs character-animation-application (04.08 sibling cluster; all three leaves now processed): joint review input recorded — dedicated character-animation products (Spine, Cascadeur, Live2D Cubism, Cartoon Animator; Adobe Character Animator as unreachable market reference) do form a recognizable Type organized around the articulated character as the central persistent object + rig-driven performance, while the siblings' observation also stands (character rigging/animation ships as a capability inside every general 2D/3D animation product sampled); boundary is a gradient, discriminating test = the character rig (not the scene or the frame) is the application's persistent unit of work and the appearance is imported rather than drawn/modeled; rig-first 2D products satisfy both cores (overlap zone); recommendation: keep all three leaves with the gradient stated in each final doc, no merge (research/character-animation-application.md §Boundary Findings)
- 3d-animation-application vs procedural-3d-creation-application (sibling under 04.13): gradient, not a wall — the canonical procedural product (Houdini) is simultaneously a full 3D animation application with a conventional keys/tracks/curves/playback core; the split is center of gravity (node-network content generation vs time-varying scene state) — flagged for joint review when Procedural 3D Creation Application is processed (research/3d-animation-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- 3d-animation-application vs motion-graphics-application (sibling under 04.07): MoGraph-style procedural motion systems (cloners/effectors/fields) are 3D motion design inside a 3D animation suite, blurring the MG boundary from the 3D side; consistent with the 2D-side flag — flagged for joint review when Motion Graphics Application is processed (research/3d-animation-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- abm-platform vs marketing-automation-platform / demand-side-platform / sales-intelligence-platform (§06/§07 siblings): the boundary is the primary object (account vs lead/contact vs anonymous audience), not feature presence — MAP vendors bundle ABM modules, ABM platforms bundle execution channels, and vendors ship ABM+sales-intelligence as one suite; category consolidation (Engagio→Demandbase 2020, Terminus→DemandScience 2025, RollWorks→AdRoll ABM rebrand) and "ABX" repositioning indicate one Type with naming drift, not new structures — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/abm-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- after-school-program-management vs childcare-management-system / daycare-preschool-management (siblings under §29): the two Types share the entire family-enrollment-attendance-billing spine; the boundary is care context (full-day licensed care with rooms/ratios/daily-reports vs scheduled part-day programs around the school day) — a gradient, not a wall; childcare suites explicitly sell into before/after-school segments (Procare) — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/after-school-program-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- after-school-program-management vs camp-management-system (sibling under §29): same core spine; difference is schedule shape (recurring weekly school-year programs vs seasonal consecutive-day sessions, often overnight); sampled vendors implement classes and camps as sibling object types inside one product (iClassPro Class vs Camp sections; Sawyer Semester vs Camp/Event schedule types; CourseStorm "class & camp") — related Types sharing a core, not duplicates; flagged for joint review when Camp Management System is processed (research/after-school-program-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- after-school-program-management vs course-registration-system (§23): registration-first products (CourseStorm) serve both adult community education and kids programs with the same catalog+registration+roster machinery; a kids-program deployment arguably satisfies this leaf's core — overlap to resolve in a joint review when Course Registration System is processed (research/after-school-program-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- after-school-program-management market terminology: in the youth-activity-business segment this Type is marketed as "class management software" (Jackrabbit, iClassPro); no separate youth-activity class-management leaf exists in the directory, so no conflict — recorded as terminology observation only (research/after-school-program-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- ad-hoc-query-application vs sql-workbench / analytical-query-editor (siblings under §13): the two sides share the entire compose→run→read→refine loop; the boundary is audience + authoring abstraction (SQL statement vs question; raw database vs governed data space) — a gradient, not a wall; sampled products blur it (Metabase embeds a full SQL editor with one-way builder→SQL conversion; Zoho Query Tables are SQL; ThoughtSpot Views are saved SQL) — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/ad-hoc-query-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- ad-hoc-query-application vs business-intelligence-platform (sibling under §13): in the current market the ad-hoc question loop is almost always bundled inside BI platforms (all four sampled products ship dashboards + sharing + governance around the loop); the leaf is best understood as the bundle's interactive core (Question/Answer as the named core objects) — probable capability-of-suite framing to resolve in a joint review when Business Intelligence Platform is processed (research/ad-hoc-query-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- additive-manufacturing-software vs cam / cnc-programming-application (siblings under §16): both turn CAD models into machine-executable instructions; the boundary is the machine process (subtractive cutting toolpaths vs additive layer slicing) plus printability-specific work (supports/orientation) that only exists on the additive side; some CAD/CAM suites bundle both — flagged for joint review when CAM is processed (research/additive-manufacturing-software.md §Boundary Findings).
- additive-manufacturing-software umbrella-term risk: the market phrase covers slicers, build preparation, fleet management, simulation, and analytics; this leaf is anchored on the per-job preparation→instruction core, while printer-fleet/production management (UltiMaker Digital Factory, Prusa Connect, GrabCAD Print Server/Streamline/Control) is a distinct adjacent structure that all three sampled vendors ship as separate products — flagged for joint review when Manufacturing Execution System / print-farm-adjacent leaves are processed (research/additive-manufacturing-software.md §Boundary Findings).
- advanced-distribution-management-system-adms vs distribution-management-system-dms (sibling under §19): the researched market uses "ADMS" as the umbrella term for the integrated platform (SCADA + DMS applications + OMS on one network model/UI); every sampled vendor markets "ADMS" for the integrated whole and Oracle's own guide is titled "ADMS Implementation Guide" while the applications layer keeps DMS-style names (power flow, FLISR, VVO) — probable supertype/alias relationship; flagged for joint review when DMS is processed (research/advanced-distribution-management-system-adms.md §Boundary Findings).
- advanced-distribution-management-system-adms vs outage-management-system-oms (sibling under §19): OMS is a module/pillar inside every sampled ADMS, but a standalone call-center-centric OMS without real-time network operations exists; structural test = real-time network monitoring/control on a connected network model (remove it → OMS remains; remove OMS → ADMS remains) — Capability/module relationship; flagged for joint review when OMS is processed (research/advanced-distribution-management-system-adms.md §Boundary Findings).
- advanced-distribution-management-system-adms vs scada (§16) / energy-management-system-ems / derms / grid-operations-platform (§19 siblings): SCADA is the point-based telemetry/control substrate — the connected network model is the ADMS differentiator; EMS is the same structural pattern applied to the transmission network (related Type sharing a pattern, like fleet vs robot-fleet); DERMS appears both as an ADMS module and as a separate integrated platform; Grid Operations Platform is a generic umbrella term — all flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/advanced-distribution-management-system-adms.md §Boundary Findings).
- advanced-distribution-management-system-adms naming: "Advanced" is a market-era convergence label (distribution SCADA + DMS applications + OMS merging into one platform), not a structural test — the definition deliberately keeps FLISR/VVO/DERMS out of the core so older DMS-style deployments (network model + monitoring + control, no OMS) still fit while point-based SCADA and call-center-only OMS are excluded; recorded as an observation, no taxonomy change proposed (research/advanced-distribution-management-system-adms.md §Boundary Findings).
- account-reconciliation-platform vs financial-close-management (sibling under §08): both track status/due dates and vendors ship them as one suite (FloQast Checklist↔Reconciliations, BlackLine Task Management, Trintech Close Management, Oracle FCCS); the structural test is the central record — task/checklist (close management) vs two-sided balance comparison with attributed sign-off (reconciliation) — flagged for joint review when Financial Close Management is processed (research/account-reconciliation-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- account-reconciliation-platform vs accounting-software (§08): SMB accounting products embed a bank-reconciliation feature that satisfies the two-sided comparison but lacks the managed account population + certification structure — capability-inside-broader-Type relationship; no dedicated bank-reconciliation leaf exists, recorded as observation only (research/account-reconciliation-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- account-reconciliation-platform vs transaction matching (no dedicated leaf in §08): transaction-level matching between high-volume data sources is sold as separate products (BlackLine Transaction Matching, Trintech ReconNET/Cadency Match/Adra Matcher, FloQast AI Transaction Matching, Oracle ARCS matching) and feeds reconciling items/journal entries into account reconciliations — treated as a variant/capability within this Type's suite space; flagged for taxonomy review if a Transaction Matching leaf is ever added (research/account-reconciliation-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- 3d-modeling-application vs digital-sculpting-application (sibling under 04.13): gradient, not a wall — modeling is topology/structure-first (element-level editing), sculpting is surface-first (brush deformation, topology secondary or dynamically regenerated); vendors ship both as distinct toolsets inside one product (Blender modeling vs sculpting feature pages; C4D lists sculpting as secondary) and Maxon sells ZBrush as the dedicated sculpting product — flagged for joint review when Digital Sculpting Application is processed (research/3d-modeling-application.md §Boundary Findings).
