- 3d-modeling-application vs procedural-3d-creation-application (sibling under 04.13): gradient — direct element editing vs rule/node-driven generation; modifier/generator/deformer stacks (Blender modifiers, C4D generators) are semi-procedural structures inside direct-manipulation products, blurring the line; mirrors the flag from the 3d-animation side — flagged for joint review when Procedural 3D Creation Application is processed (research/3d-modeling-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- 3d-modeling-application vs mechanical-cad (§16): precision/engineering-intent gradient — architecture-leaning modelers (SketchUp: real-world measurements, IFC classification, CAD interchange) straddle toward CAD/Architecture Design, while 3D suites merely import CAD formats (C4D: STEP/CATIA/Solidworks) — flagged for joint review when Mechanical CAD is processed (research/3d-modeling-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- 3d-modeling-application vs 3d-animation-application (sibling under 04.08): shared substrate (3D scene of transformable objects); the boundary is the time dimension — modeling's deliverable is a static reusable asset, animation's is a rendered moving image; suite products bundle both, SketchUp (modeling-side) has no geometry keyframing — clean split, recorded as observation only (research/3d-modeling-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- 3d-rendering-application vs 3d-animation-application (sibling under 04.08): rendering products ship presentation-level motion primitives (camera paths/keyframes, turntables, sun/door/cloud animation in archviz renderers; one-click turntables in product-design renderers) that overlap the animation surface; the test is motion as presentation aid over a staged scene vs authored time-varying scene state as the core job — a gradient, not a wall; flagged for joint review when 3D Animation-adjacent leaves are revisited (research/3d-rendering-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- 3d-rendering-application vs texture-material-authoring-application (sibling under 04.14): a game-art suite spans bake+texture+render in one product, straddling the sibling boundary; the structural test is the primary deliverable (material/texture assets vs rendered images) — gradient; flagged for joint review when Texture / Material Authoring Application is processed (research/3d-rendering-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- 3d-rendering-application vs rendering-management-application (sibling under 04.14): vendors themselves split render execution from job logistics (KeyShot Network Rendering as a separate product with its own manual; Chaos cloud/farm ecosystem; Lumion KB treats farm/node availability as a distinct question) — clean structural split, recorded as confirmation, no conflict expected (research/3d-rendering-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- 3d-rendering-application packaging caution: the dominant modern delivery is a rendering engine as plugin/extension inside host DCC/CAD applications (or bundled in a suite), not a standalone app; the leaf definition is written intake-agnostic (import/live-link/host/text) so it does not overfit the standalone form — definitional note, no taxonomy change (research/3d-rendering-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- agent-development-platform vs agent-orchestration-platform (sibling under §13): in the researched sample multi-agent composition is an in-product capability of every agent development product (handoffs/agents-as-tools, template workflow agents, graphs, agent flows), and the canonical open-source agent framework self-describes as an "orchestration framework and runtime" — probable capability/overlap rather than two structures; a standalone orchestration platform would center on coordinating pre-existing agents at runtime; flagged for joint review when Agent Orchestration Platform is processed (research/agent-development-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agent-development-platform vs agent-evaluation-platform / agent-observability-platform / agent-tool-computer-use-platform (siblings under §13): all three appear as bundled standard capabilities in every sampled product (tracing/eval in LangSmith, AgentCore Evaluations/Observability/Browser/Code Interpreter, ADK evaluation module, Copilot Studio evaluations/analytics, OpenAI built-in tracing) — capability relationship; standalone products exist but the bundle dominates; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/agent-development-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agent-development-platform vs llm-application-development-platform (sibling under §13): gradient boundary drawn by vendor docs themselves (model API = developer owns the loop; agent SDK = runtime manages turns/tool execution/sessions); products straddle it (one framework line ships both layers) — flagged for joint-review framing when LLM Application Development Platform is processed (research/agent-development-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- organization-design-platform vs org-chart-management (sibling under §09): both hold the same structural model; the tested difference is the scenario/impact loop (propose → measure → apply alternative structures) — Nakisa ships Org Chart Suite and Org Design Suite as two separate products (vendor-confirmed split) while ChartHop bundles both in one platform; probable adjacent-Types-with-shared-core relationship — flagged for joint review when Org Chart Management is processed (research/organization-design-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- organization-design-platform vs workforce-planning-platform (sibling under §09): shared headcount/cost metrics but different center of gravity (structure comparison vs demand/supply over a time horizon); vendors bundle both (ChartHop Headcount Planning module, Nakisa Strategic Workforce Planning Suite, OrgVue workforce-planning solution) — flagged for joint review when Workforce Planning Platform is processed (research/organization-design-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agent-evaluation-platform vs agent-observability-platform / llm-observability-platform (siblings under §13): evaluation's central record is the scored run against criteria while observability's is the execution trace; evaluation consumes traces (online scoring, span-level evals, datasets-built-from-traces) and all five sampled products bundle tracing — gradient, not wall; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/agent-evaluation-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agent-evaluation-platform vs llm-evaluation-platform / agent-development-platform (siblings under §13): all sampled evaluation products serve single-turn LLM apps and agents as one workload family (agent-specific differentiator = agentic system under test + execution/trajectory scoring surface), and the earlier agent-development-platform pass found evaluation bundled in every dev product — probable gradient/capability framing; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/agent-evaluation-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- outreach-sequencing-platform vs sales-engagement-platform (sibling under §07): the market defines "sales engagement software" by exactly this sequencing machinery (Salesloft's own FAQ: "combines sales cadence tool capabilities, automation rules, and AI"), and the two archetypal SEPs (Outreach, Salesloft) are sequencers at enterprise scope while Reply.io/lemlist are sequencers at SMB scope — probable one-Type-two-scopes / umbrella-instance relationship; this leaf is defined by the sequencing core with the enterprise SEP bundle treated as a variant — flagged for joint review when Sales Engagement Platform is processed (research/outreach-sequencing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- outreach-sequencing-platform source limitation: Outreach support site (404s) and Salesloft help center (JS-rendered) were inaccessible on 2026-09-06; operational mechanics for those two products are asserted only at product-page positioning level, while sequence mechanics (reply-stop, bounce handling, OOO pause, delays-vs-sending-days, triggers) are verified from Reply.io and lemlist Tier-1 docs — recorded in Sources of applications/outreach-sequencing-platform.md.
- employee-communication-platform vs internal-communication-application (sibling under §09): probable Alias — the market uses "internal communications software/platform" and "employee communication platform/app" interchangeably for the same products (Staffbase maintains separate SEO pages for both terms describing one platform; Workvivo titles the same page "#1 Rated Employee Communication App" and "Internal Comms"; Firstup's solutions page is "Internal Communications"); no structural difference found — flagged for joint review when Internal Communication Application is processed (research/employee-communication-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-communication-platform vs intranet-platform (§10): center-of-gravity gradient, not a wall — intranet is pull-based portal/knowledge home, ECP is managed targeted distribution with reach measurement; the same vendors ship both (Staffbase/Firstup/Workvivo/LumApps all bundle intranet modules) and analyst coverage (Gartner MQ "Intranet Packaged Solutions") places these same products in the intranet category — flagged for joint review when Intranet Platform is processed (research/employee-communication-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-communication-platform vs employee-engagement-platform / employee-experience-platform (siblings under §09): gradient/umbrella — engagement platforms center surveys/recognition/listening while ECP centers targeted distribution, and "employee experience platform" is umbrella positioning used by the same vendors (Staffbase, Workvivo) for the same structure; Workvivo deliberately spans both — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/employee-communication-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-fitness-coach vs workout-programming-application / online-fitness-coaching / workout-tracking-application (§28 siblings): the structural test is who adapts the plan — software (AI coach) vs human trainer/coach (programming, online coaching) vs nobody (tracker/static plan library); vendors increasingly bundle all three (human-coach platforms adding AI assist, coaches bundling tracking), and one sampled hardware product ships human-coach programs and AI-generated workouts side by side with AI recommendations deferring to active programs — a gradient, not a wall; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/ai-fitness-coach.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-fitness-coach "AI" terminology: the defining property is software performing the coach loop (generation + adaptation), not the implementation technology — pre-LLM algorithmic products satisfy the Type and LLM-era rebranding does not change it; definition deliberately keeps rules/ML/LLM choice out of the core, recorded as an observation, no taxonomy change proposed (research/ai-fitness-coach.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-advising-platform vs student-success-platform (sibling under §23): the market largely sells one converged category under both names — EAB Navigate360 self-describes as a student-success CRM and Civitas as an impact platform, either of which could be documented under either leaf; the working distinction is center of gravity (advisor–student relationship + advising workflow vs institutional retention analytics/population health/initiative measurement), with a structural test (remove the analytics layer → advising platform remains; remove the advising core → analytics + coordination remain) — flagged for joint review when Student Success Platform is processed (research/academic-advising-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-advising-platform vs school-counseling-management (sibling under §23): same structural pattern (counselor–student appointments, notes, plans, alerts) with a different population (K-12) and plan semantics (postsecondary/graduation planning, no degree audit) — a gradient, not a wall; flagged for joint review when School Counseling Management is processed (research/academic-advising-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-advising-platform vs student-case-management (sibling under §23): alert handling inside advising platforms uses case-like objects (cases & referrals, shared-note case tools), but the center differs — ongoing advising relationship vs issue-driven case lifecycle; case is one object type inside this Type — flagged for joint review when Student Case Management is processed (research/academic-advising-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-advising-platform degree-audit observation: degree audit/planning is a capability inside advising platforms (planning-first products) and inside SISs (DegreeWorks/uAchieve lineage); no dedicated degree-audit leaf exists in §23, so no conflict — recorded as an observation supporting keeping planning out of the defining core (research/academic-advising-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-integrity-plagiarism-platform vs online-proctoring-platform (sibling under §23): both are bought under the "academic integrity" umbrella but the structural test is clean — proctoring observes the live exam-taking process, this Type analyzes submitted written artifacts after the fact; remove one and the other remains intact — recorded as a clean split, no taxonomy change proposed (research/academic-integrity-plagiarism-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-integrity-plagiarism-platform "Academic Integrity" naming: the leaf's integrity half is realized in-market as evidence support (similarity/authorship reports, investigator dashboards), not misconduct case management — hearings/sanctions/conduct records belong to student-conduct systems outside this Type; also a gradient boundary vs consumer content-originality checkers (same core loop, no institutional roles/repository/policy context) — recorded as observations, no taxonomy change proposed (research/academic-integrity-plagiarism-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- accounting-software vs bookkeeping-application (sibling under §08): probable Alias/Variant — vendors use the terms interchangeably for the same products (Xero's own page says bank feeds import "into Xero bookkeeping software"; Zoho maintains a "Bookkeeping Software" page pointing at Books; FreshBooks ships a "Bookkeeping" feature page inside its accounting product); bookkeeping names the activity, accounting software names the product category — flagged for joint review when Bookkeeping Application is processed (research/accounting-software.md §Boundary Findings).
- accounting-software vs general-ledger-system (sibling under §08): the GL is this Type's ledger engine alone (CoA + journal + trial balance) without the SMB AR/AP/bank/tax surfaces and owner/bookkeeper UX; related Types sharing an engine, not duplicates — flagged for joint review when General Ledger System is processed (research/accounting-software.md §Boundary Findings).
- accounts-payable-automation vs invoice-processing-platform (sibling under §08): the market treats invoice processing as the document-centric front half of the AP cycle (Tipalti lists "Invoice Processing" as a sub-module of AP Automation; Basware's AP-automation page is entirely invoice processing; Stampli maintains separate educational pages where processing is a stage of the AP cycle) — structural test: processing ends at a validated/routed document, AP automation ends at a posted (and usually paid) payable — probable capability/parent-child relationship rather than two independent Types; flagged for joint review when Invoice Processing Platform is processed (research/accounts-payable-automation.md §Boundary Findings).
- accounts-payable-automation source limitation: Stampli (support.stampli.com) and BILL (help.bill.com) help centers unreachable on 2026-09-06 (2 transport errors each); all product evidence is Tier-2 product pages with operational FAQs — interface-level mechanics asserted only conceptually in the final document, vendor-marketed numbers excluded (recorded in Sources of applications/accounts-payable-automation.md).
- animal-shelter-management vs pet-adoption-platform (sibling under §29): the sharpest boundary — operator-facing custody system vs consumer-facing discovery/listing; RescueGroups itself ships "Pet Adoption Portal" and "Data Management" as two separate services, ASM's listing output is a publishing function, and 24PetShelter lists online listings as roadmap (a shelter product can exist without listings); structural test = remove the custody lifecycle → adoption platform remains; remove public discovery → shelter management remains — flagged for joint review when Pet Adoption Platform is processed (research/animal-shelter-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- animal-shelter-management vs animal-control-management (§24): field/enforcement operations (incidents, dispatch, citations, licensing) vs custody operations; ASM ships animal control as an explicitly removable optional module while Chameleon/ShelterBuddy bundle both for municipal customers ("fully supports BOTH your Shelter and Field Services") — related Types frequently merged in municipal products; flagged for joint review when Animal Control Management is processed (research/animal-shelter-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- animal-shelter-management vs veterinary-practice-management / pet-boarding-management (§29 siblings): custody-based care vs client-based clinical business / owner-retained-custody boarding; ASM's own manual separates Clinic and Boarding into distinct optional modules beside the shelter core — vendor-confirmed structural separation; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/animal-shelter-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- animal-shelter-management sourcing limitation: Shelterluv (major modern US vendor) unreachable (403 + JS-only help center) and PetPoint operational docs behind login; sample anchored by ASM Tier-1 manual + RescueGroups guide, with PetPoint/Chameleon/24PetShelter/ShelterBuddy at product-page evidence level — recorded in Sources of applications/animal-shelter-management.md.
- employee-engagement-platform vs employee-survey-platform (sibling under §09): every sampled engagement platform contains a full survey engine; the differentiator is the workforce program frame (employee population + confidentiality machinery + engagement analytics + action loop) — a superset/capability gradient, not a wall; generic-audience survey tools remain the Survey Type — flagged for joint review when Employee Survey Platform is processed (research/employee-engagement-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-engagement-platform vs employee-recognition-platform (sibling under §09): WorkTango ships Surveys & Insights and Recognition & Rewards as separate products bundled into one suite (direct vendor evidence), and Culture Amp/Officevibe bundle recognition as secondary modules — recognition is adjacent, not part of the engagement core; test = remove the measurement loop → recognition platform remains — flagged for joint review when Employee Recognition Platform is processed (research/employee-engagement-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-engagement-platform vs employee-experience-platform (sibling under §09): "employee experience platform" is umbrella positioning used by the same vendors (WorkTango "holistic Employee Experience Platform", Qualtrics Employee Experience, Workleap) for bundled structures — probable umbrella/alias, consistent with prior flags from the employee-communication-platform pass — flagged for joint review when Employee Experience Platform is processed (research/employee-engagement-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-engagement-platform vs employee-communication-platform (sibling under §09): opposite directions (listening/measurement vs targeted distribution) with real overlap — engagement platforms carry survey communications, comms platforms carry pulse surveys, and Workvivo-class products span both; consistent with the prior flag; center-of-gravity test recorded — flagged for joint review when those leaves are revisited (research/employee-engagement-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-engagement-platform sourcing limitation: Workday Peakon article pages are JS-rendered and unreachable (structure-level evidence only); Qualtrics engagement-specific support section unreachable (product-page evidence); WorkTango used for positioning/boundary evidence only — confidentiality thresholds are product-specific and configurable, no universal defaults stated (research/employee-engagement-platform.md §Source-access Limitations).
- advanced-metering-infrastructure-ami vs meter-data-management-system-mdms (sibling under §19): the head-end centers on the communicating device estate (collect/command/monitor/manage) while MDMS centers on billing-quality data records (validate/estimate/edit/store/share); Itron ships OpenWay (AMI) and IEE (MDMS) as separate product lines and Landis+Gyr ships Emerge (HES) and MDMS as separate products — but terminology drifts: Temetra (collection) and Neptune 360 (collection+analysis) are both marketed as "meter data management" — flagged for joint review when MDMS is processed (research/advanced-metering-infrastructure-ami.md §Boundary Findings).
- advanced-metering-infrastructure-ami vs AMR (no dedicated leaf in the directory): automated meter reading (mobile walk-by/drive-by or one-way collection) is a distinct offering at Itron and Neptune, with explicit migration tooling bridging the two (Temetra "migration from AMR to AMI"); structural test = fixed two-way field-area network vs mobile collection; no directory conflict exists, recorded as an observation (research/advanced-metering-infrastructure-ami.md §Boundary Findings).
- outside-counsel-management vs legal-spend-management (sibling under §11): the market uses "legal spend management" as the umbrella name for the same products — Brightflag maintains a /legal-spend-management/ page for its e-billing platform, CounselLink+ won a third-party "Legal Spend Management Solution Provider of the Year 2025" award, Mitratech's nav places "Legal Spend Management" over the same matter+eBilling stack, and Onit's solution page is titled "Legal Spend & Matter Management"; working distinction = firm-relationship lifecycle (registry→engagement→terms→invoices→evaluation) vs the money across all legal spend (budgets/accruals/analytics incl. non-firm vendors) — probable near-alias; flagged for joint review when Legal Spend Management is processed (research/outside-counsel-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- outside-counsel-management vs legal-matter-management (sibling under §11): every sampled OCM product bundles matter management (the ELM bundle); structural test = remove the firm-relationship layer (registry/terms/invoice gate) → matter management remains, remove matter depth (documents/deadlines/calendar) → OCM remains; OCM leaf is defensible as the firm-relationship-centered view but products ship them together — flagged for joint review when Legal Matter Management is processed (research/outside-counsel-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- outside-counsel-management sourcing limitation: Thomson Reuters Legal Tracker (legacy-lineage sample) unreachable (transport errors + 404) and vendor help centers not reachable for any sampled product; observations rest on official product pages and vendor-authored guides; exact invoice state names, numeric limits, and defaults intentionally not stated — recorded in Sources of applications/outside-counsel-management.md.
- agent-observability-platform vs llm-observability-platform (sibling under §13): probable alias — Datadog renamed its product from "LLM Observability" to "Agent Observability" (docs page title/breadcrumbs; URL path still /llm_observability/) while keeping the identical span/trace data model, and all four sampled products (Langfuse, LangSmith, Phoenix, Datadog) serve single-turn LLM apps and agents with one data model — Datadog's own docs frame inference→workflow→agent as a complexity gradient of the same tracing tier; the agent-specific content is the step vocabulary (tool calls, agent containers) + sessions, not a separate structure — flagged for joint review when LLM Observability Platform is processed (research/agent-observability-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agent-observability-platform vs agent-evaluation-platform / agent-development-platform (siblings under §13): gradients confirmed from the observability side — central record = execution trace ("what happened") vs scored run ("how good"); every sampled observability product bundles quality attachment (scores/feedback/annotations/managed evaluations) and trace→dataset export, consistent with the evaluation-pass flag; and the dev-platform pass's finding that observability is a bundled L1 capability is confirmed by this pass's standalone products existing alongside — both joint-review flags stand (research/agent-observability-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- appliance-repair-management vs small-business-field-service-management (sibling under §29): the researched sample (Housecall Pro, Service Fusion, Kickserv) shows the identical structural spine (customer+location → job lifecycle → technician dispatch → invoice/payment) in both; the difference is trade semantics (repair jobs, callbacks, warranty-period scheduling, parts, flat-rate repair pricing, before/after documentation) — vendors themselves ship appliance repair as a re-skinned configuration of one FSM product (Service Fusion maintains ~30 clone industry pages) — probable trade-Variant relationship rather than two independent Types; flagged for joint review when Small Business Field Service Management is processed (research/appliance-repair-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- appliance-repair-management vs auto-repair-shop-management (sibling under §29): both are "repair management" but the execution surface differs — field-based (technician travels to the appliance at the customer's location; dispatch/routing central) vs shop-based (vehicle brought to bays; work order lives at the shop) — related Types sharing a repair pattern, not duplicates; flagged for joint review when Auto Repair Shop Management is processed (research/appliance-repair-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- appliance-repair-management sourcing limitation: Jobber (403 ×2), ServiceTitan (JS-rendered site, API docs 404), Workiz (404 ×2), FieldPulse (404 ×2) unreachable on 2026-09-06; sample anchored by Housecall Pro + Kickserv Tier-1 help docs and Service Fusion Tier-2 product pages; enterprise-tier structures (ServiceTitan-class price-book governance, membership programs, equipment registries) unverified — recorded in Sources of applications/appliance-repair-management.md.
- employee-experience-platform vs employee-communication-platform / employee-engagement-platform / intranet-platform / employee-service-portal / employee-recognition-platform (§09/§10 experience-cluster siblings): the researched sample (Microsoft Viva, Qualtrics EmployeeXM, Workvivo, Simpplr; cross-ref Staffbase, WorkTango, Firstup, Culture Amp) shows every EX-labeled product is a multi-domain consolidation whose domains are the sibling Types themselves, with different domain sets per vendor (suite/listening-first/destination-first/intranet-first); the only candidate defining property is the consolidation posture (shared HR-sourced population + ≥2 domains on one platform + platform-operated employee surfaces + unified cross-domain measurement) — probable umbrella positioning over the sibling Types rather than a distinct single-domain structure, confirming the two prior sibling-pass flags; flagged for a §09 experience-cluster joint review when the remaining sibling leaves are processed (research/employee-experience-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-experience-platform vs digital-employee-experience-management (§14): same two words, different structure — DEX monitors endpoint/application performance telemetry owned by IT (observability estate) while EX platforms deliver and measure HR/comms-owned organizational experience (content, listening, journeys, services); different buyers, objects, and rules; the leaf definition explicitly excludes IT telemetry to prevent a name-based collision (research/employee-experience-platform.md §Boundary Findings).

- academic-paper-reader vs reference-manager (sibling under §23): the paper-reading surface is overwhelmingly implemented as a capability inside reference-management products (all sampled reference-manager vendors ship a built-in reader; ReadCube's help center names "Read & Annotate" a top-level category; Paperpile lists "Highlight and annotate" as a feature page), while standalone realizations of this Type re-emerge only as AI-augmented corpus readers (Semantic Reader) or general reading apps (Readwise Reader) — probable Capability/center-of-gravity relationship rather than two fully independent structures; the split is reading-and-annotation vs citation-database-and-bibliography; flagged for joint review when Reference Manager is processed (research/academic-paper-reader.md §Boundary Findings).

- accounts-receivable-management vs collections-automation-platform (sibling under §08): both center collection activity; the structural test is loop completeness — receivable ledger + cash application + books linkage (AR management) vs pursuit workflow alone (collections automation); in the current market every sampled AR product leads with collections and "collections management" branding appears both inside AR suites and as standalone point products — flagged for joint review when Collections Automation Platform is processed (research/accounts-receivable-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- collections-automation-platform pass DISCHARGED the accounts-receivable-management joint-review flag WITH A REFINEMENT: the loop-completeness test does not hold against the collections-first market — 4/5 sampled collections products include cash application, 5/5 maintain continuous books sync with write-back, and 5/5 offer payment capture/portals — so the two Types are one family on a center-of-gravity gradient: collections automation centers the pursuit operation (receivable population as substrate, pursuit object model richest — workflows/actions/promises/disputes/worklists; cash application a closing bridge), AR management centers the receivable population as a whole (cash application a first-class discipline, deductions factories, credit-to-cash span); corroborating market pattern: AR suites ship collections as a named module (HighRadius O2C) while collections-first vendors ship cash application/credit/disputes as satellites (Gaviti/Chaser); recommendation recorded for human decision: keep both leaves with the gradient boundary, or consolidate under one canonical Type with the other as a packaging variant — joint review still recommended; ADDITIONALLY FLAGGED: the directory carries "Collections Automation Platform" AND "Collections Platform" as separate leaves under §08 while market usage of "collections platform" overlaps this pass's ground (several sampled products answer to that label) — risk of duplication/collision; joint review needed to assign distinct canonical cores (e.g. B2B AR collections automation vs financial-institution/consumer delinquency collections) or merge
- accounts-receivable-management vs invoicing-application (sibling under §08): products bundle both directions (Billtrust/Invoiced create and deliver invoices; Upflow deliberately creates none and ingests from ERP/billing systems) — the boundary is invoice authoring/issuance vs the outstanding-receivable population's journey to paid; flagged for joint review when Invoicing Application is processed (research/accounts-receivable-management.md §Boundary Findings).
