- academic-timetabling vs course-registration-system (sibling under §23): the two interlock around the same course sections but the direction of work differs — registration captures student-side demand (which sections students take), timetabling constructs institution-side supply (when/where sections meet without conflicts); UniTime ships both as separate components (course timetabling + student scheduling/sectioning) and course requests feed the solver's student-conflict minimization — related Types sharing a data flow, not duplicates; flagged for joint review when Course Registration System is processed (research/academic-timetabling.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-timetabling exam timetabling: in the researched sample exam scheduling always appears as a module/extension of a timetabling product (UniTime separate module with own solver/periods/seating; Celcat extension), not a separate purchase — same core pattern (activities → periods → rooms → conflict minimization) with different objects (exam periods, seating capacity, invigilators, direct/back-to-back/>2-a-day conflicts) — probable Variant/Capability rather than independent Type; flagged for joint review if an examination-scheduling leaf is processed (research/academic-timetabling.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-timetabling vs resource-calendar / enterprise-resource-scheduling-platform (§03.08/§10): generic resource scheduling lacks the teaching-activity model (curriculum attachment, cohorts, teaching loads, academic terms); all sampled timetabling products embed room/event booking as a capability against the same inventory (Celcat Room Booking, aSc booking, UniTime Event Management) — capability-inside-Type relationship, recorded as observation (research/academic-timetabling.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-timetabling sourcing limitation: operational help-center docs reachable only for UniTime (manual-level); Celcat support portal gated, aSc help URL 404, Untis help center timed out ×2 — claims about those three products kept at feature level, no precise limits/defaults asserted (recorded in Sources of applications/academic-timetabling.md).
- aftermarket-service-management vs cmms-enterprise-asset-management-eam (sibling under §16): the boundary is asset ownership — EAM/CMMS maintains the operator's OWN production assets, aftermarket service manages SOLD units at customer sites; vendors bundle both in one product line (SAP FSM explicitly covers "asset and customer service work"; Siemens Teamcenter SLM ships a closed-loop integration with IBM Maximo for execution) — gradient, not a wall; flagged for joint review when CMMS/EAM is processed (research/aftermarket-service-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- aftermarket-service-management vs generic Field Service Management (no generic FSM leaf in §16; only Utility FSM and Telecom Field Service exist in §19): all four sampled products (PTC ServiceMax, IFS FSM, SAP FSM, Siemens SLM) are marketed as FSM/SLM, so this leaf must carry the asset-centric service market; proposed structural test = installed-base + entitlement anchoring (unit-identified work objects with coverage) vs generic job dispatch with equipment as incidental detail — gradient; flagged for joint review if a generic FSM leaf is ever added (research/aftermarket-service-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- aftermarket-service-management vs warranty management / MRO (no dedicated leaves in §16): warranty registration/claims adjudication without work-order fulfillment appears in the sample as an embedded capability (ServiceMax dealer workflows, IFS depot warranty claims, SAP contract/warranty connection), and aviation/defense MRO implements the same core with deeper as-maintained configuration + regulatory data exchange (GEIA-STD-0007) — recorded as capability/variant observations, no taxonomy change proposed (research/aftermarket-service-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- aftermarket-service-management sourcing limitation: no Tier-1 operational docs reachable for any sampled product (SAP Help Portal JS shell; docs.ifsworld.com and documentation.servicemax.com transport errors; Mize transport errors ×2 abandoned; search engines timed out ×2) — all evidence is Tier-2 official product pages; no precise state names/limits/defaults asserted anywhere; mid-market aftermarket-native segment under-evidenced (recorded in Sources of applications/aftermarket-service-management.md).
- art-gallery-management vs museum-collections-management (sibling under §27): the boundary is the commercial disposition loop — galleries hold stock whose terminal state is a sale (offer→invoice→payment, consignment settlement); museums hold a permanent collection under accession/deaccession/conservation with no sale loop; market evidence supports the split: Veevart (formerly gallery-side) now positions as museum operations on Salesforce and Artfundi repositioned to enterprise collection stewardship (custody/provenance/condition/valuations, no sale loop marketed) — remove the sale loop from gallery management and the remaining structure is collection management; flagged for joint review when Museum Collections Management is processed (research/art-gallery-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- art-gallery-management vs artwork-consignment-management (sibling under §27): in all three sampled gallery products consignment is one module inside the full inventory/CRM/sales world (consign-in, terms/percentages, returns, settlement computed from invoice history); a standalone consignment-management leaf would center only the consignor↔gallery relationship — probable narrower-sibling/Capability relationship; structural test = strip inventory, clients and direct sales, keeping only the consignment relationship; flagged for joint review when Artwork Consignment Management is processed (research/art-gallery-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- art-gallery-management sourcing limitation: a fourth candidate (ArtBinder, mobile-first inventory/sales) returned empty responses ×2 and was abandoned; two other "art management" vendors (Veevart, Artfundi) were examined and found repositioned to museum operations / collection stewardship — used as boundary evidence only; no claims in the final document depend on the unreachable product (recorded in Sources of applications/art-gallery-management.md).
- ai-coding-assistant vs ai-coding-agent (joint-review pass completed from the assistant side, closing the flag raised by research/ai-coding-agent.md): all four sampled assistant products (GitHub Copilot, JetBrains AI Assistant, Tabnine, Amazon Q Developer) document the assistive/agent contrast themselves — assistive = synchronous suggestions "as people work", applied manually by the human; agentic = autonomous multi-step loop — and ship both structures inside one product line; boundary test confirmed = who holds the execution loop; one sampled assistant (Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins) is being discontinued in favor of an agentic successor while chat/completions carry over; recommendation: keep both leaves as adjacent points on an autonomy gradient with a shared framing, rather than merging (research/ai-coding-assistant.md §Boundary Findings).
- actuarial-modeling-platform vs financial-modeling-application (sibling under §08): both "build models and project numbers" — the boundary is semantics, not structure: actuarial platforms model insurance products/liabilities with actuarial assumption machinery (mortality/lapse/curves as versioned first-class inputs) over policy/experience data, financial modeling applications model corporate statements/valuation for finance teams; the pricing segment of actuarial platforms (fitting on historical experience) narrows the gap further — gradient, not a wall; flagged for joint review when Financial Modeling Application is processed (research/actuarial-modeling-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- actuarial-modeling-platform vs market-risk-platform / financial-risk-management-platform / regulatory-reporting-platform (§08 siblings): actuarial platforms center on liability/product models and feed capital, risk and reporting processes; vendors ship scenario generators, credit solutions and IFRS 17/LDTI reporting engines as companion products around the actuarial core — capability/adjacency relationships rather than duplicates; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/actuarial-modeling-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- actuarial-modeling-platform internal segment gradient: "actuarial modeling" spans projection/valuation engines (central data object: in-force portfolio) and pricing/reserving model builders (central data object: historical experience/triangles); the definition was deliberately phrased to cover both ("policy/experience data", "projection/calibration runs") — recorded as an observation; if a future review prefers a projection-centered definition, the pricing/reserving segment would need its own Type decision (research/actuarial-modeling-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- actuarial-modeling-platform sourcing limitation: official operational docs for Milliman MG-ALFA and WTW Unify/ResQ unreachable (404s on all attempted URL patterns; search engines/encyclopedia lookups timed out or unusable); claims grounded in three directly fetched products (Moody's AXIS solution pages, Slope Software platform pages, Akur8) — unreachable vendors used only as market anchors, no precise vendor-specific numbers asserted in the final document (recorded in Sources of applications/actuarial-modeling-platform.md).
- employee-onboarding-platform vs employee-offboarding-platform (sibling under §09): mirror symmetry now confirmed from the onboarding side across all five sampled products — every vendor ships onboarding+offboarding (+crossboarding/reboarding/M&A) as one product on one employee record (Personio On-/Offboarding settings, GoCo workflows+termination guides, Click Boarding pre/on/off pillars, HR Cloud Onboard/Offboard modules, Enboarder onboarding/offboarding/transition journeys); same template/task/oversight machinery, opposite anchor (start date vs last working day) — strengthens the earlier joint-review flag toward a shared "employee transition journey" structure (research/employee-onboarding-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-onboarding-platform vs customer-onboarding-platform (§07 sibling): identical leaf names, different subjects — customer-side orchestrates product/service adoption (accounts, usage, success milestones), employee-side orchestrates entry into employment (compliance paperwork, pay setup, workplace, team); no shared structure beyond the generic journey/checklist pattern — recorded as a naming-collision observation, §07 vs §09 placement is correct (research/employee-onboarding-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-onboarding-platform packaging observation: no sampled vendor markets onboarding as a pure-play standalone point product — it always ships inside an HRIS, a journey platform, a suite, or an orchestration layer; the Type is structurally real (same core model across very different packagings) but has no pure-play market anchor, same pattern as the offboarding leaf (research/employee-onboarding-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-avatar-video-generator vs real-time conversational avatar products (no dedicated leaf in DIRECTORY): all three researched vendors ship live/interactive avatar lines as separate products or modules (D-ID Realtime agents — avatar+LLM+knowledge+tools over WebRTC; DeepBrain "AI Human" virtual-employee line with its own SDK family; Synthesia Roleplay Sessions), sharing the same presenter+lip-sync technology but delivering live interactive sessions instead of rendered videos — the async rendered-video Type and the real-time avatar surface are market-separated; probable missing Type or a relationship with agent leaves in §13 — flagged for review (research/ai-avatar-video-generator.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-avatar-video-generator vs ai-video-generator (sibling under 04.21): boundary is the center of gravity — authored spoken content delivered by a depicted presenter vs imagined scenes generated from prompts; products borrow from each other in both directions (avatar products add AI-generated scenes/B-roll, text-to-video products add talking avatars), a gradient rather than a wall — flagged for joint review when AI Video Generator is processed (research/ai-avatar-video-generator.md §Boundary Findings).
- artist-booking-platform vs talent-agency-management (sibling under §27): agency-side booking suites and agency management systems overlap on roster/offers/contracts/settlements; structural test = booking transaction (artist × date × terms × lifecycle) as center vs artist career/agency operations as center — a marketplace booking platform needs no career-management objects at all; probable partial-overlap gradient, flagged for joint review when Talent Agency Management is processed (research/artist-booking-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- artist-booking-platform naming collision: Gigwell markets its talent-buyer product as "Venue Management Software" while its object is artist bookings for the venue, not physical space/event operations — beware search-based mis-linking when Venue Management System (§26) is processed (research/artist-booking-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agribusiness-erp vs farm-management-platform (sibling under §20): boundary is a center-of-gravity gradient, not a wall — vendors themselves package "farm operations without ERP" and "full ERP" tiers of one product line (AgriERP Lite vs Standard/Advance), and the researched ag-retail ERP (Agvance) is marketed as "fully integrated ERP" while carrying deep agronomy modules; structural test = integrated financial/commercial core as center (ERP) vs agronomic operations as center with books absent/peripheral (farm management) — flagged for joint review when Farm Management Platform is processed (research/agribusiness-erp.md §Boundary Findings).
- artist-booking-platform vs service-marketplace (§05.02): structurally similar supply-profile + demand-request + transaction, but the performance-specific lifecycle (dated occasion, holds, contracts, deposits, settlement) is domain machinery, not generic marketplace structure — treated as a domain-specific Type in §27, no taxonomy change proposed (research/artist-booking-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- payment-gateway vs payment-processing-platform (siblings under §08): classic industry model separates gateway (merchant-facing acceptance + secure transmission) from processor (acquiring/authorization/settlement backend), but every modern researched product (Stripe, Adyen, Braintree, Checkout.com) bundles both under one platform — Authorize.Net is the only sampled product keeping them structurally separable (requires external merchant account); the boundary is stack-position emphasis, not structure, and the two leaves overlap on the same products — flagged for joint review when Payment Processing Platform is processed (research/payment-gateway.md §Boundary Findings).
- payment-gateway vs merchant-payment-platform (sibling under §08): terminology sibling; sampled products self-describe as "payments platforms" serving merchants and no structural difference was observable at research depth — probable Alias/overlap; flagged for joint review when Merchant Payment Platform is processed (research/payment-gateway.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-design-generator vs ai-image-generator (sibling under 04.20): gradient, not a wall — the discriminator is the deliverable class (design composition with format-for-purpose semantics + workability vs flat image as final artifact); products straddle it (Designer's engine generates images as material inside designs; Recraft sells image generation and a design studio in one product and its own nav leads with "AI image generator"); structural test = remove design-purpose composition/format semantics → image generator remains; flagged for joint review when AI Image Generator is processed (research/ai-design-generator.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-design-generator vs template-based-design-platform (04.01 sibling): the discriminator is the origin of the first-pass composition (machine-generated from described intent vs pre-made and browsed); products bundle both (Designer ships template search beside generation; Canva-class platforms embed generation) — gradient; flagged for joint review when Template-based Design Platform is processed (research/ai-design-generator.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-design-generator vs graphic-design-application (04.01 sibling): editing toolsets overlap almost entirely; the difference is who composes the first pass (system vs user) — workflow center-of-gravity gradient, recorded as observation (research/ai-design-generator.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-design-generator vs ui-design-application / ux-prototyping-application (04.15 siblings): Uizard-class UI generation (multi-screen editable prototypes from text) is a domain variant of design generation, but the boundary against manual UI-design/prototyping tooling needs joint review when 04.15 leaves are processed (research/ai-design-generator.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-design-generator vs visual-website-builder (04.16): clean split at research depth — deliverable container differs (design artifact vs functioning website with structure/content/hosting); AI site generators fail the design-artifact test; recorded as observation (research/ai-design-generator.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-design-generator capability-embedding pattern: the generation loop ships both standalone (Designer web, Recraft studio, Uizard) and embedded as a capability inside broader products (Designer-in-M365 via Copilot, Recraft-in-Figma/Framer, generation inside template platforms) — packaging, not structure; leaf defined intake-agnostic (research/ai-design-generator.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-design-generator sourcing limitation: Canva (browser-sniffing block ×2), Adobe Express (helpx + product page timeouts ×2 each), Looka (403) unreachable on 2026-09-06 — template-platform-embedded, suite-embedded, and logo-generator segments under-evidenced; no claims made about them; Tier-1 operational docs available only for Microsoft Designer, Uizard/Recraft/Designs.ai evidenced at official-product-page level with no numeric limits/defaults/pricing asserted (recorded in Sources of applications/ai-design-generator.md).
- accreditation-management (§25) vs accreditation-certification-management (§11): the two leaves are opposite seats of one accreditation relationship — §11 manages the seeking organization's own compliance posture toward an external standard, §25 manages the accrediting body's program that awards and maintains standing; structural test = whose workflow the system runs (body receiving/deciding/maintaining a population vs organization assembling its own evidence); documented in research/accreditation-management.md §Boundary Findings.
- accreditation-management (§25) vs academic-accreditation-management (§23): the market itself ships separate products for the two seats (Weave Education institution-side vs Weave Accreditation accreditor-side; Watermark/Nuventive also institution-side); §23 should anchor the institution side when processed, otherwise the two leaves would collide — flagged for joint review when Academic Accreditation Management is processed (research/accreditation-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- accreditation-management (§25) vs certification-management (§25 sibling): same intake→review→decision→credential machinery, different credential population (organizations vs individuals); one sampled platform (OpenWater) runs both accreditation and certification programs from one codebase and several bodies operate both — probable near-duplicate pairing; flagged for joint review when Certification Management is processed (research/accreditation-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- payment-orchestration-platform vs payment-gateway / payment-processing-platform (siblings under §08): the structural test is whether the routed targets are independent external providers under the merchant's own contracts — orchestrator = decisioning layer above authorizing paths (gateways are its routable targets); remove multi-provider connectivity+selection → orchestrator collapses into a gateway; remove the authorizing backend → gateway collapses into an orchestrator; gradient risk: PSPs market routing across their own acquiring configurations/MIDs as "orchestration" — flagged for joint review when Payment Processing Platform is processed (research/payment-orchestration-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- payment-orchestration-platform vs fraud-detection-platform / checkout-platform / billing-platform: boundaries drawn structurally — fraud vendors appear inside the orchestration flow as connected services (decisions used as routing conditions, model owned by the fraud vendor); checkout UIs are an optional acceptance surface (API-only operation is a common variant); billing decides what/when to charge while orchestration executes and routes the charge — recorded as observations with tests, no taxonomy change proposed (research/payment-orchestration-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- artwork-consignment-management vs art-gallery-management (sibling under §27): joint-review flag from the gallery pass confirmed from the consignment side — the consignment-centered structure is real and fully describable (consignor/consignee/specific works/terms/disposition/settlement, evidenced at Tier 1 in ArtCloud KB and Artlogic support), but in the reachable market it always ships as a module inside gallery management (consignee side) or artist studio tools (consignor side); no standalone dedicated artwork-consignment product was identified (Artwork Archive unreachable 403×2; search engines unusable); probable narrower-sibling/Capability relationship — structural test stands: strip inventory, clients and direct sales, keeping only the consignor↔consignee relationship → this leaf's core remains; flagged for joint review (research/artwork-consignment-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-gateway-model-routing-platform vs model-api-platform (sibling under §13): boundary = who owns/serves the models — the gateway intermediates and owns none; managed unified-API gateways (Vercel: usage-billed pass-through pricing, BYOK, provider failover) drift toward aggregation but remain intermediaries; OpenRouter-class aggregators (not fetched) likely sit on the model-API side — flagged for joint review when Model API Platform is processed (research/ai-gateway-model-routing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-gateway-model-routing-platform vs api-gateway-management-console (§12): Kong's own FAQ draws the line — behind a generic gateway you "can only interact at the API level", while an AI gateway "can understand the prompts" (token metering, prompt inspection, model-level fallback); Kong AI Gateway is literally a generic gateway plus AI entities/policies, so the boundary is a capability gradient inside one vendor — flagged for joint review when API Gateway Management Console is processed (research/ai-gateway-model-routing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-gateway-model-routing-platform vs llm-observability-platform / ai-cost-finops-platform / ai-safety-guardrail-platform (siblings under §13): gateway logging is a byproduct of being on the path (Portkey bundles a full observability suite; Cloudflare offers dashboard analytics only; LiteLLM exports outward), budget enforcement at the request path is the shared zone with FinOps (confirms the ai-cost-finops pass from the gateway side), and guardrails ship as bundled capabilities (Portkey suite, Kong prompt/response guards, LiteLLM module) alongside standalone products — capability/gradient relationships; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/ai-gateway-model-routing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-gateway-model-routing-platform naming & scope drift: market uses "AI gateway"/"LLM gateway"/"LLM proxy" interchangeably and "model routing" names the gateway's mature core function, not a separate structure; vendors are repositioning toward "governance layer" (Kong) and expanding into MCP/agent/CLI traffic (Kong, Portkey, LiteLLM, Vercel) — treated as scope variants of one Type, no taxonomy change proposed (research/ai-gateway-model-routing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-gateway-model-routing-platform sourcing limitation: Kong docs subpages (load balancing, AI Model entity, llms.txt) 404'd on 2026-09-06 — Kong asserted at overview-page level only; OpenRouter not fetched (aggregator boundary positioning-level); Vercel root-doc level; vendor performance figures (latency/uptime/volume) observed but excluded from all claims (recorded in Sources of applications/ai-gateway-model-routing-platform.md).
- employee-portal vs intranet-platform / employee-service-portal / employee-service-management (§10/§09 siblings): market label "employee portal" spans two poles — content-first (intranet-flavored) and transaction-first (HCM self-service) — sharing one aggregation spine (employment-based authenticated membership + single aggregated organization-curated entry surface); Powell's own help center markets its intranet product as "build a complete employee portal" and Microsoft positions the SharePoint home site as the intranet's "main entry-point", so the portal is typically built ON intranet machinery, while service portals surface as one service stream inside a portal (requests handed off to ITSM/HRIS); probable gradient/Variant relationships across these leaves rather than fully independent Types — flagged for joint review when Intranet Platform, Employee Service Portal, and Employee Service Management are processed (research/employee-portal.md §Boundary Findings).
- agricultural-dealer-management vs agribusiness-erp (§20 siblings): the input-retail "ag dealer" family (Agvance/Merchant Ag/AgVantage/Tronia-class systems confirmed via AgVend's integration list) is assigned to Agribusiness ERP per that pass's segment framing; this leaf is defined as the equipment-dealership DMS (serialized units/parts/service work orders/rentals/OEM price files+warranty) — structural tests recorded (remove units+work orders → ag-retail ERP remains; remove grower production/commodity flow → the DMS remains) (research/agricultural-dealer-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- agricultural-dealer-management taxonomy observation: the same equipment-DMS structure is sold by the same vendors into rural-lifestyle/construction/golf & turf trades (one product family, segmented industries) — "agricultural" binds the segment (farm customers, farm equipment, precision ag), not the structure; no generic equipment-dealer-DMS leaf exists in the directory, so the leaf stands as-is; source limitation: DIS Corporation unreachable (2× transport error) and no Tier-1 help centers public for sampled DMS vendors — department/feature structure rests on official product pages, precise operational defaults not asserted (research/agricultural-dealer-management.md §Boundary Findings, §Uncertainties).
- ad-server vs ad-delivery-platform joint review COMPLETED (2026-09-06, research/ad-server.md §Boundary Findings): alias finding confirmed from the Ad Server side — all four directly evidenced products self-identify as "ad server"/"ad serving" (Kevel "fully featured ad server", Xandr Monetize explicit "Ad server" role, AdButler "ad serving platform", Revive "ad serving tool"), Equativ names a "CTV Ad Server" product line, and no product primarily self-identifies as an "ad delivery platform"; recommendation: Ad Server is the canonical Type, Ad Delivery Platform is an alias/merge candidate — no unilateral DIRECTORY change made.
- ai-governance-platform boundary observations (research/ai-governance-platform.md §Boundary Findings): (1) vs AI Safety / Guardrail Platform (§13 sibling): market convergence is active — 2026-generation governance platforms embed runtime observation and enforcement (block/redact/route/kill-switch, agent-tool permissioning) that previously defined the guardrail Type; structural test recorded (remove registry/review-lifecycle/evidence → guardrail platform; remove runtime interception → governance platform remains); flagged for joint review when AI Safety / Guardrail Platform is processed. (2) vs Governance Risk & Compliance Platform (§11): distinct (AI-scoped governed object + AI frameworks vs enterprise-wide machinery), but suite vendors ship AI governance as a GRC-suite module and pure-plays integrate into GRC stacks — adjacency, not alias; no taxonomy change proposed. (3) vs Model Registry: distinct (artifact/version store vs business-risk-review record over the same assets); integration-coupled, test recorded.
- admissions-management vs enrollment-management / student-recruitment-crm (§23 siblings): market uses "enrollment management" as the strategic umbrella spanning recruitment → admissions → yield → retention (Slate self-describes "Admissions & Enrollment"; Finalsite's product is literally named "Enrollment Management System" while covering inquiry→application→enrollment→re-enrollment), and modern admissions products bundle the recruitment-CRM layer so thoroughly that the funnel-phase edge blurs; structural test recorded (remove the application→evaluation→decision pipeline → recruitment CRM + yield/retention work remains; keep only the pipeline → Admissions Management remains intact); probable superset/umbrella framing for Enrollment Management and phase-gradient for Student Recruitment CRM — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/admissions-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- admissions-management boundary observations (research/admissions-management.md §Boundary Findings): (1) vs SIS: matriculation is the seam — admissions owns candidates until they become students of record, then hands off (SIS suites historically embed admissions modules with the same core spine; deployment posture is L2). (2) vs Financial Aid Management: admissions products carry only shallow aid components (aid checklists, scholarship letters); deep aid processing is its own Type. (3) vs hiring ATS: structural analog (application → review → decision → offer) but different population/objects/rules — related, not the same Type. (4) centralized application portals (UCAS/Common-App pattern) are an intake channel feeding institutional admissions systems (importer-side evidence only; UCAS provider page 404 — kept general). (5) K-12 re-enrolment of returning students has no admission decision — segment variant (L2), not part of the defining core.
- artwork-exhibition-logistics vs §27 siblings (Exhibition Planning Platform / Exhibition Installation Management / Museum Object Movement Management / Museum Loan Management) and vs museum CMS / gallery suites: in the reachable sample no standalone dedicated "artwork exhibition logistics" product exists — the logistics structure (checklist + movement chain + custody continuity + handover documentation) ships as modules inside museum collection systems (TMS Collections Loans/Exhibitions/Shipping modules; Zetcom MuseumPlus Exhibition Management beside Contracts) and gallery suites (Artlogic location/shipping + exhibition/fair records), with specialized point tools at the edges (ARTA transport execution without a display occasion; Articheck condition/transit documentation as a cross-party point tool) — probable Module/Capability-of-suite relationship, consistent with the artwork-consignment-management flag; structural tests recorded (remove the display occasion → object movement/art shipping remains; remove the movement chain → planning/loan management remains); flagged for joint review when those sibling leaves are processed (research/artwork-exhibition-logistics.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-image-editing-application vs ai-image-generator / photo-editor / raster-image-editor (04.20/04.04/04.02): both load-bearing boundaries are gradients, not walls — vs AI Image Generator the discriminator is the object of work (existing source image vs description-from-scratch; Photoleap/Facetune bundle text-to-image beside their editors), vs Photo/Raster Editor it is who executes the edit (system models interpret content and produce the change vs user-driven deterministic tools; BeFunky ships a named AI set inside a conventional editor, Facetune/Photoleap keep manual toolchains, and the raster-editor pass already classifies AI generative editing as its L2 drift); structural tests recorded (remove the source image → generator remains; remove AI-executed operations → photo/raster editor remains); also vs AI Design Generator (deliverable = edited image vs design composition; Microsoft Designer's Edit-with-AI tab straddles) — flagged for joint review when AI Image Generator and Photo Editor are processed (research/ai-image-editing-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-recognition-platform vs employee-engagement-platform (sibling under §09): confirms the engagement-pass flag from the recognition side — recognition vendors bundle surveys as clearly separate adjacent modules (Awardco Engage, Achievers Voice of Employee/Pulse) while engagement vendors bundle recognition as secondary modules or sibling products (WorkTango two-product evidence); structural test holds both ways (remove the measurement loop → recognition platform remains; remove the recognition event → survey platform remains) — flagged for joint review; employee-experience-platform umbrella also confirmed (recognition is one consolidated EX domain, consistent with the EX-pass flag); terminology note: market sells this Type as "employee recognition" and "rewards & recognition (R&R)" — rewards names the redemption layer of the same Type, no separate leaf exists (research/employee-recognition-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-cost-finops-platform vs cloud-cost-management-finops (§14 sibling): same allocation/budget/anomaly/showback machinery, different metered object — AI consumption (models, tokens, AI providers, gateway telemetry) vs infrastructure consumption (compute/storage/network); cloud FinOps platforms absorb AI cost as additional data sources (Vantage, CloudZero) while AI-native tools grow cost features, so the boundary is a gradient, not a wall — probable scope-variant relationship; flagged for joint review when Cloud Cost Management / FinOps is processed (research/ai-cost-finops-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-cost-finops-platform vs llm-observability-platform / ai-gateway-model-routing-platform (§13 siblings): observability centers traces/quality with cost as one metric and the gateway centers routing with cost as a byproduct, while this Type centers money (attribution, budgets, chargeback); Helicone/Portkey implement cost + observability on one request log, and budget enforcement at the request path is the shared zone with gateways (confirmed from the gateway side in the ai-gateway pass) — gradient/capability relationships; flagged for joint review when LLM Observability Platform is processed (research/ai-cost-finops-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agricultural-gis vs precision-agriculture-platform (sibling under §20): sharpest overlap — all sampled precision-ag platforms (GeoPard, OneSoil, Climate FieldView) implement the full ag-GIS core (land base + layers + map canvas + spatial operations), and VRA/prescription machinery appears in every ag-GIS-adjacent product; the working distinction is center of gravity (spatial data base & analysis vs variable-rate execution loop prescription→machine→as-applied verification with equipment data as first-class citizen) — a gradient, not a wall; structural test recorded (remove the execution loop → ag GIS remains; remove the land base/layer model → precision ag collapses into equipment control); flagged for joint review when Precision Agriculture Platform is processed (research/agricultural-gis.md §Boundary Findings).
- agricultural-gis vs government-gis / utility-gis (§24/§19): all three are domain specializations of the same generic GIS engine (create/manage/analyze/map spatial data — vendor-standard definition), differing in domain data model (administrative parcels & public assets / utility networks / farm fields & agronomic layers), users, and workflows; the directory has no generic "GIS" leaf, so the three domain leaves share a common core and may deserve a shared framing — flagged for joint review when Government GIS and Utility GIS are processed (research/agricultural-gis.md §Boundary Findings).
- agricultural-gis naming observation: the market rarely sells "agricultural GIS" as a category label — products are marketed as precision-agriculture platforms, field-data platforms, or farm mapping software; the leaf is best understood as the GIS-structured segment of agricultural software, defined by structure (land base + layers + map + spatial operations) rather than vendor vocabulary; recorded as observation, no taxonomy change proposed (research/agricultural-gis.md §Boundary Findings).
- agricultural-gis sourcing limitation: classic desktop/dealer-tier ag GIS lineage (Ag Leader SMS, Trimble Ag Software/Farm Works, Agrian) unreachable on 2026-09-06 (404/transport/403) and John Deere Operations Center JS-rendered (structure evidenced only indirectly via GeoPard integration docs); sample anchored by GeoPard Tier-1 docs + Esri/FieldView/OneSoil Tier-2 pages; no claims made about the unreachable products (recorded in Sources of applications/agricultural-gis.md).
- payment-processing-platform vs payment-gateway (siblings under §08): joint-review flag CONFIRMED from the processing side — Finix/Stax/Worldpay all bundle the front-end acceptance stack with the processing back end (Finix ships tokenization forms/links/terminals beside seller underwriting+settlement; Worldpay ships Accept beside Move Money payouts), and the classic decoupled split (front-end vs back-end) is evidenced only structurally since classic-processor docs (Fiserv/CardConnect/Global Payments) were unreachable; the two leaves describe the same products from opposite stack ends — recommended joint review before either leaf is treated as a fully independent Type (research/payment-processing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- payment-processing-platform vs merchant-payment-platform (sibling under §08): from the processing side the alias finding repeats — "payments platform for merchants" names the same bundled product class and no distinct structure was observable at research depth; probable Alias — flagged for joint review when Merchant Payment Platform is processed (research/payment-processing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- payment-processing-platform vs card-processing-platform (sibling under §08): same word "processing", expected opposite network sides — this leaf is merchant-side acquiring (underwriting/provisioning, network authorization routing, settlement/funding); Card Processing Platform is expected to be issuer-side (cardholder accounts, issuer authorizations); boundary expected to hold but untested (no issuer-side product sampled) — confirm when Card Processing Platform is processed (research/payment-processing-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- advertising-campaign-management vs search-engine-marketing-management-platform (§06 siblings): SEM management is the search-channel-specific embodiment of the same advertiser-side campaign lifecycle (keywords/search terms/bids as the core machinery vs the channel-agnostic campaign model) — probable Variant relationship; flagged for joint review when Search Engine Marketing Management Platform is processed (research/advertising-campaign-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- advertising-campaign-management vs demand-side-platform-dsp (§06 sibling): gradient, not a wall — DSP bids on individual impressions in real time through exchanges with its own bid engine, while campaign management governs campaign-level configuration/spend/performance on publisher platforms; overlap zone is real (Skai officially manages Amazon DSP; modern DSPs expose campaign objects) — flagged for joint review when Demand-side Platform / DSP is processed (research/advertising-campaign-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- advertising-campaign-management sourcing limitation: Google Ads and Meta Ads Manager official help centers unreachable on 2026-09-06 (repeated timeouts/transport errors; also Pinterest/TikTok help and Google developers docs); native-platform structure anchored by Amazon Ads console pages + LinkedIn Campaign Manager help articles instead; no load-bearing claims made about Google/Meta structure (recorded in Sources of applications/advertising-campaign-management.md).
- academic-accreditation-management vs accreditation-management (§25 sibling): seat split CONFIRMED empirically — all five sampled products (Watermark P&SS, Weave Education, SPOL, eLumen, Nuventive) serve the institution seat, none records the accreditor's decision, and the market itself ships separate products per seat (Weave Education vs Weave Accreditation; Watermark help center heritage lineage all institution-side); both prior passes' predictions upheld, no collision — structural test = whose workflow the system runs (institution preparing responses/evidence for someone else's standards vs body receiving/deciding/maintaining accredited members) (research/academic-accreditation-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-accreditation-management vs accreditation-certification-management (§11): same seat (seeking organization), different domain substrate — shared spine (external standard → mapped compliance records → evidence → assessment event → status/renewal) but educational evidence base (curriculum maps, learning-outcomes assessment, program review, faculty qualifications vs corporate controls/policies), faculty/committee governance, self-study deliverable, education-vendor market; probable Variant or closely-related Type, consistent with the §11 document's own flag — joint review recommended (research/academic-accreditation-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- academic-accreditation-management vs institutional-effectiveness-platform (§23 sibling): strongest internal tension — the same products (Watermark P&SS, Nuventive, SPOL, Weave) market as both "accreditation management" and "institutional effectiveness"; working distinction recorded = this leaf is organized around the external accreditor's standards and cycle (standards → responses → evidence → report → reaffirmation) while IE is organized around the institution's own planning/assessment/improvement loop even without an accreditor; in practice one product usually serves both — flagged for joint review when Institutional Effectiveness Platform is processed (research/academic-accreditation-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- institutional-effectiveness-platform vs academic-accreditation-management — RESOLVED from the IE side (2026-09-08): keep-both RATIFIED with the organizing-structure seam confirmed against IE-side evidence — the accreditation leaf is structured by the external accreditor's standards and cycle; the IE leaf is structured by the institution's own mission-outcome-assessment-improvement loop, which runs with no accreditor involved (strategic plans, administrative units, program review); removal tests: drop the accreditor's standards → the IE platform remains fully functional while the accreditation product collapses to standards-response machinery; drop the institution's own loop → only standards-response machinery remains; same vendors ship both and the products interlock (IE record feeds accreditation self-studies) — products converge, Types stay distinct (research/institutional-effectiveness-platform.md Boundary Findings).
- athlete-injury-availability-management vs athlete-management-system (§28 sibling): the injury/availability core (roster + injury record + availability state) usually ships inside an AMS or a sports-medicine EMR rather than as a standalone product — Teamworks sells the same concern both as an AMS module and as a separate Sports EMR product, and Kitman positions its medical solution ("more than an EMR") beside its AMS-replacement performance solution; the leaf remains a definable Type (analogous to Leave & Absence Management inside HRIS), but joint review recommended when Athlete Management System is processed; note also the directory has no sports-medicine-EMR leaf, so documentation-first products (Healthy Roster) are documented under this leaf (research/athlete-injury-availability-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-model-evaluation-platform vs llm-evaluation-platform / agent-evaluation-platform (siblings under §13): market naming is loose — "evaluation platform" is used for all three and some LLM-eval vendors publish model leaderboards as content; structurally distinct (market models + standardized instruments + selection/ranking decision vs own app/agent + own test cases + ship decision), consistent with the agent-evaluation pass's "clean" call — flagged for joint review when LLM Evaluation Platform is processed (research/ai-model-evaluation-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-model-evaluation-platform positioning observation: the leaf sits in §13 among enterprise AI-infrastructure leaves, but the dominant market form is a public web platform (often free) operated by an independent operator/consortium/academic lab/open community rather than enterprise software — positioning observation only, no taxonomy change proposed (research/ai-model-evaluation-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- advocacy-platform (§25) vs customer-advocacy-platform (§06): same word "advocacy", different domains — the §25 leaf is organization-operated policy mobilization (org-authored campaign → supporters → decision-maker targets → action execution → participation tracking), while §06 Customer Advocacy Platform mobilizes customers for commercial references/reviews/referrals with no policy targets or civic datasets; structural test recorded (remove policy-directed targets → marketing tool; remove supporter base → civic/petition platform) — NOT aliases; flagged so the §06 pass documents the name collision rather than conflating the two (research/advocacy-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- advocacy-platform sourcing limitation: only New/Mode yielded Tier-1 help-center docs; One Click Politics and Actionable evidenced at official-product-page level; Quorum/Phone2Action, VoterVoice, Action Network, Muster, Speak4, Capitol Canary, Rally Congress all unreachable (403/timeout/transport/parked) — cross-product claims calibrated to a three-product sample, one with Tier-1 docs (recorded in Sources of applications/advocacy-platform.md).
- employee-record-system (§09) vs HRIS/HCM: no sampled product sells itself as a standalone "employee record system" — the record layer is marketed as the core of Core-HR/HRIS products (Personio "Core HR"/Personnel Files, BambooHR HRIS, SAP SuccessFactors "Core HR"/Employee Central "single source of truth for people data"); leaf documented as the record-centric view of the core-HR layer (custody of the record vs operation of HR processes as the distinguishing center of gravity), remains a definable Type; joint review with the HRIS leaf recommended when Human Resource Information System / HRIS is processed (research/employee-record-system.md §Boundary Findings).
- payroll-system vs global-payroll-platform (sibling under §09): scope gradient, not a wall — Rippling ships "Payroll" (US) and "Global Payroll" as separate products (vendor-confirmed split) while Zoho ships one payroll product as regional editions (GCC/Canada/India/USA); structural test = single-jurisdiction depth (deep local statutory machinery, pay run per jurisdiction) vs multi-country consolidation/orchestration as the primary object; probable adjacent-Types-sharing-a-core relationship — flagged for joint review when Global Payroll Platform is processed (research/payroll-system.md §Boundary Findings).
- payroll-system sourcing limitation: Gusto, ADP, Paylocity, Sage, Patriot, QuickBooks Payroll unreachable on 2026-09-06 (403/JS/timeout); sample anchored by Square (Tier-1 help articles: pay-run workflow + federal tax loop), Xero (Gusto-powered), Zoho (regional editions), Rippling (HCM-platform); enterprise bureau-class mechanics (multi-entity payroll accounting, union/certified payroll) unverified and not claimed (recorded in Sources of applications/payroll-system.md).
- agricultural-iot-platform vs irrigation-management (§20 sibling): gradient, not a wall — soil-moisture networks exist largely to feed irrigation decisions and sampled products span both (Semios irrigation module with scheduler+control; CropX irrigation planning); structural test recorded (remove the device fleet → irrigation management survives on public/third-party data; remove irrigation scheduling → the IoT platform still monitors frost/pest/disease/climate); center of gravity = sensing backbone vs water decision; flagged for joint review when Irrigation Management is processed (research/agricultural-iot-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agricultural-iot-platform vs farm-equipment-telematics (§20 sibling): same engine family (connected fleet + telemetry + monitoring + alerts); boundary = device population (stationary environmental/condition sensors vs moving machines); telematics data can feed an IoT platform; gradient relationship recorded, no taxonomy change proposed (research/agricultural-iot-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agricultural-iot-platform naming & taxonomy observation: "Agricultural IoT Platform" is rarely used as a market category label (products marketed as sensor networks, monitoring platforms, ag telemetry, cultivation automation); the leaf is the device-connectivity-structured segment of agricultural software; also the directory has no generic "IoT Platform" leaf (only Industrial IoT Platform under §16) while a sampled platform spans crop/animal/smart-city/OEM sectors — same engine-family situation as agricultural-gis vs government/utility GIS; recorded as observation, no taxonomy change proposed (research/agricultural-iot-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- agricultural-iot-platform sourcing limitation: vendor help centers/user manuals unreachable in this pass — evidence is Tier-2 product/solution documentation (CropX FAQ and FieldClimate feature lists operationally specific; Growlink marketing-tier); no precise operational numbers (devices per gateway, battery life, polling intervals, notification channels) asserted anywhere; control/automation depth documented as variant, not universal (recorded in Sources of applications/agricultural-iot-platform.md).
- athlete-injury-availability-management vs athlete-management-system joint review COMPLETED (2026-09-06): both leaves confirmed as definable Types — AMS defining core = roster + training/development program as managed work + longitudinal preparation record feeding a staff review/adjust loop; injury/availability defining core = roster + injury record lifecycle + availability state; directional tests hold both ways (remove programming → sibling Type or monitoring platform; remove injury/availability → still an AMS); the medical slice usually ships inside elite-tier AMS products as an embedded module (Teamworks medical record vocabulary inside its AMS; Kitman medical + performance solutions on one platform) while the S&C-first pole (TeamBuildr) packages the readiness layer as an add-on with no medical module; no taxonomy change. Naming hazard recorded: "AMS" is applied by vendors to Athlete Management Systems, Athlete Monitoring Systems, platform solutions, and add-ons alike (Kitman's own page title reads "Athlete Monitoring System (AMS)"); monitoring-first products (Catapult) sit at the AMS/Sports-Performance-Analytics boundary; directory has no S&C-programming leaf, so programming-first products are documented under this leaf (research/athlete-management-system.md §Boundary Findings).
- affiliate-management-platform vs affiliate-network (siblings under §06): the split is vendor-confirmed — Post Affiliate Pro ships "Affiliate Program Software" (create and manage affiliate programs) and "Affiliate Network Software" (set up your own affiliate network to manage merchants and affiliates) as separate products; marketplace/network connectivity also appears as an optional feature inside merchant-side tools (Tapfiliate Offers marketplace + admitad network access, impact.com vetted two-sided marketplace) while Rewardful explicitly positions against marketplaces — structural test = remove single-merchant operation (many merchants + publisher-discovery marketplace + network-mediated economics) → Affiliate Network; keep one merchant's own program with its own commission ledger → this Type; no taxonomy conflict, recorded for joint reference when Affiliate Network is processed (research/affiliate-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-image-generator joint review with ai-design-generator and ai-image-editing-application (04.20 siblings) COMPLETED from this side (2026-09-06): both pending flags confirmed as gradient boundaries with heavy real-world bundling — vs AI Image Editing the discriminator is the object of work (description → new image vs existing image → changed image; ChatGPT Images runs both loops under one roof, Stability ships editing as a separate service catalog beside generation, Bing supports upload-to-personalize within a creation-centric surface), vs AI Design Generator the discriminator is the deliverable class (the picture itself as final artifact vs workable design composition with format-for-purpose semantics; Brand Studio's brand machinery still outputs images, not compositions); structural tests recorded both ways; also confirmed clean split vs Model API Platform / open-weights infrastructure (Stability ships the same model family as API, two applications, and open weights — only the application surfaces are this Type); no taxonomy change (research/ai-image-generator.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-tutoring-application boundary observations (2026-09-06): (1) vs Language Learning Application — modern language apps execute the same loop (adaptive practice + feedback + mastery state) in the language domain; Language Learning Application may be better modeled as a subject-domain sibling of the tutoring loop rather than a fully independent structure — flagged for joint review when Language Learning Application is processed; (2) vs Tutoring Platform — clean structural split (software executes the pedagogy vs human tutors brokered through the app), but hybrid products exist (AI-owned learning path + human mini-lessons in learning centers) and vendors sell human-tutoring services alongside the AI software — packaging overlap, not a Type conflict; (3) homework-helper/answer apps (camera math solvers, search study helpers) are a distinct neighboring surface (no curriculum, no persistent learner state), not a variant of this Type; no taxonomy change proposed (research/ai-tutoring-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-model-hosting-platform vs model-api-platform (sibling under §13): both expose models through metered APIs; the discriminator is model provenance relative to the platform operator (hosting = models whose creation it does not own — third-party open weights, community, customer-uploaded/fine-tuned; model API = the developer serving its own models); the edge converges — hyperscalers host their own models alongside third-party ones (Bedrock: Amazon Nova beside Claude/GPT/Grok) and model vendors host each other's open weights — a gradient, not a wall; flagged for joint review when Model API Platform is processed (research/ai-model-hosting-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-model-hosting-platform vs model-registry (§13 sibling): registry catalogs/governs model versions (metadata, stages, approvals) without operating serving; hosting runs them — a weights repository without an invocation surface fails the hosting core; registries can feed hosting platforms (train → register → deploy); flagged for joint review when Model Registry is processed (research/ai-model-hosting-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-model-hosting-platform vs machine-learning-platform / mlops-platform (§13 siblings): lifecycle-breadth gradient — ML/MLOps platforms span data/training/pipelines/deployment/monitoring (often over user-owned infra) while hosting centers on operating serving for consumption, with training as an adjacent bundle (Baseten/Together/Fireworks bundle training; SageMaker/Vertex-class platforms bundle hosting); flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/ai-model-hosting-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-model-hosting-platform vs serverless-management-platform / GPU cloud (§14): unit-of-deployment test — functions/containers/instances vs models with catalog semantics (weights, versions, licenses, per-token pricing); custom-container packaging (Baseten custom Docker server, Replicate packaging) blurs toward containers — gradient, not a wall; flagged for joint review when Serverless Management Platform is processed (research/ai-model-hosting-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-model-hosting-platform vs ai-gateway-model-routing-platform: clean structural split confirmed from both sides — the gateway is an intermediary that runs no inference and routes to upstreams; the hosting platform IS the upstream that runs inference (ai-gateway pass: "routes to hosted endpoints like any other upstream"); recorded as confirmation, no flag (research/ai-model-hosting-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-model-hosting-platform sourcing limitation: Hugging Face — arguably the most prominent community model hub — unreachable on 2026-09-06 (repeated timeouts) and dropped from the sample; the community-hub shape is covered via Replicate's docs; Bedrock custom-weight import and Fireworks serverless rate-limit mechanics unverified; no claims made beyond the reachable layer (recorded in Sources of applications/ai-model-hosting-platform.md).
- peer-to-peer-payment-application vs digital-wallet / mobile-wallet / stored-value-wallet (siblings under §08): in the current market P2P is almost always embedded inside a wallet product (PayPal self-describes its app as a digital wallet; Apple Cash lives inside Apple Wallet; Venmo ships cards/checkout around the P2P core), and stored value is one funding implementation rather than the boundary (Zelle moves money bank-to-bank with no balance) — related Types frequently shipping as one product; structural test = remove merchant payment → P2P remains; remove P2P → wallet remains — flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/peer-to-peer-payment-application.md §Boundary Findings).
- agronomy-management vs farm-management-platform (§20 sibling): center-of-gravity gradient, not a wall — the researched agronomist platform (Agworld) self-describes as farm management software while shipping a dedicated "For Agronomists" solution, so vendors legitimately span both; working distinction = input-decision practice (test data → recommendation → execution record) vs whole-farm operations (finance/inventory/labor/equipment); structural test = remove recommendations/testing → farm management remains; remove whole-farm business ops → agronomy management remains; consistent with the earlier agribusiness-erp flag — flagged for joint review when Farm Management Platform is processed (research/agronomy-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- agronomy-management vs nutrient-management / crop-protection-management / soil-management / crop-management (§20 siblings): agronomy management integrates across input domains in one field-level recommendation while the siblings appear to center single domains (one input class, or the crop cycle); probable superset/capability relationships — each domain leaf may exist as a module inside agronomy suites; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/agronomy-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- agronomy-management naming & taxonomy observation: no market category is literally named "agronomy management" — products are marketed as agronomy software/modules, crop planning, prescription/consulting software; the leaf is the agronomy-practice-structured segment of agricultural software, defined by structure (field record + test data + recommendation + execution linkage) rather than vendor vocabulary; recorded as observation, no taxonomy change proposed (research/agronomy-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- agronomy-management sourcing limitation: Agvance and E4 help centers unreachable on 2026-09-06 (support subdomains empty/absent) and Agrian 403'd on first attempt and was dropped; sample anchored by Agworld Tier-1 help center (soil sampling) + Agvance/E4 Tier-2 product pages; execution mechanics for the consultant model (E4) inferred from services framing and marked as inference; no precise operational details asserted (recorded in Sources of applications/agronomy-management.md).
- ai-meeting-assistant vs virtual-meeting-platform (§01.04): platform-native assistants blur the Type boundary — Zoom's assistant (ZoomMate/My Notes) is a licensed capability inside the meeting platform, structurally identical to standalone AI Meeting Assistants (native capture instead of a bot, same transcript+summary+action-items+Q&A record); the leaf remains valid (standalone products clearly exist), but the boundary is porous as meeting platforms increasingly bundle assistants — flagged for joint review when Virtual Meeting Platform is processed (research/ai-meeting-assistant.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-meeting-assistant vs conversation-intelligence-platform (§07): gradient, not a wall — team-oriented assistants increasingly bundle conversation-intelligence analytics (Fireflies ships talk-time/sentiment/topics natively; Fathom is sales/CRM-oriented; Zoom sells CI as a separate Revenue Accelerator line); the working distinction is the primary object (single-meeting record + immediate use vs org-scale analytics/coaching over many recorded calls) — flagged for joint review when Conversation Intelligence Platform is processed (research/ai-meeting-assistant.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-relations-case-management vs hr-case-management (§09 siblings): the boundary is matter-vs-request framing — ER case management handles sensitive people-matters (complaints/allegations/grievances) with investigation logic, per-case access isolation, privilege marking and defensibility, while HR service-delivery case management handles employee-as-customer service requests against SLAs/knowledge bases; the market blurs the naming (HR Acuity brands its ER product "HR Case Management" and explicitly contrasts itself with ticketing tools), so the two leaves need a joint pass when HR Case Management is processed (research/employee-relations-case-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-relations-case-management vs whistleblowing-speak-up-platform / corporate-investigation-management (§11): sampled products bundle anonymous-reporting/hotline intake with case handling (intake auto-converts to cases) and multi-department products share one case engine across HR/ER, ethics, fraud, security and Title IX — intake channel vs handled case, and HR-owned vs legal-owned slices of one investigation pattern; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/employee-relations-case-management.md §Boundary Findings).
- employee-relations-case-management sourcing limitation: NAVEX (case-management page 404 ×2), ServiceNow HR Service Delivery (timeout ×2) and Atlassian JSM HR page (404) unreachable on 2026-09-06; no Tier-1 help-center docs reachable in-sample — all evidence is Tier-2 official product pages/FAQs (HR Acuity, Case IQ, Culture Shift); suite-embedding claims kept indirect (integration/partnership evidence only) and no precise state names/numeric limits asserted (recorded in Sources of applications/employee-relations-case-management.md).
- affiliate-management-platform vs affiliate-network joint review COMPLETED from the network side (2026-09-06): sibling flag discharged — all four sampled networks (Awin, CJ Affiliate, ClickBank, Admitad) are intermediary-operated with publisher-facing multi-program discovery and network-mediated settlement, none is a merchant's own-program tool; Post Affiliate Pro's dual-SKU split corroborated from this side; gradient cases recorded (merchant-side tools with optional marketplace connectivity; Awin Access = merchant self-serve plan inside a network — operator identity + money path, not self-serve posture, decide the side); structural test confirmed both ways; no taxonomy change (research/affiliate-network.md §Boundary Findings).
- affiliate-network sourcing limitation: Awin partner help center under construction (success.awin.com article fetch failed, portal JS-rendered), CJ and Admitad help centers not fetched — evidence anchored by Awin advertiser pricing/help (Tier 1: fee economics, transaction validation) and ClickBank help center (Tier 1: HopLinks/attribution, payment mechanics), with Tier-2 product pages for CJ/Admitad; precise operational details stated only where documented; vendor scale figures attributed as claims (recorded in Sources of applications/affiliate-network.md).
- ai-safety-guardrail-platform vs ai-governance-platform / llm-observability-platform / ai-gateway-model-routing-platform / llm-evaluation-platform (siblings under §13): the litmus is runtime content screening on the LLM I/O path + per-content decision (block/alter/flag/allow) — governance = org/process level (registry/review/evidence), observability = measurement without decisions, gateway = routing/cost decisions, evaluation = pre-release testing; all four bundle or consume guardrail findings (the gateway pass already flagged guardrails as bundled capabilities) — gradient/capability relationships; flagged for joint review when those leaves are processed (research/ai-safety-guardrail-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-safety-guardrail-platform vs ai-security-platform (§15): Check Point/Lakera straddles both — estate-level AI security programs (red teaming, threat intel, posture) vs the runtime I/O screening slice; the runtime screening-and-decision function is this Type; flagged for joint review when AI Security Platform is processed (research/ai-safety-guardrail-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- ai-safety-guardrail-platform vs content moderation (no dedicated leaf in the directory): Azure AI Content Safety explicitly serves UGC-moderation scenarios alongside LLM I/O protection; the LLM-path orientation (paired input/output screening, prompt-attack family, grounding checks) is the distinguishing center of gravity — recorded as observation, no taxonomy change proposed (research/ai-safety-guardrail-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- athlete-recruiting-marketplace vs sports-scouting-platform (§28 siblings): adjacent, both definable, but vocabulary collides — US vendors/regulators use "recruiting" and "scouting" interchangeably (NCAA bylaws govern "recruiting or scouting services"; the market leader's legal name contains "Scouting Association"; one sports-suite vendor sells both a Recruiting and a Scouting product), so the boundary must be structural: recruiting marketplace L0 = athlete/family/club-authored profiles + coach-side discovery + two-way interest/contact oriented to placement; scouting platform (proposed for that leaf's research) = evaluator-side talent identification/evaluation over athlete/video registries without athlete-side marketplace participation; directional test = remove athlete authorship/participation → scouting platform; add scout-side evaluation machinery → still a marketplace; recommend joint boundary check when Sports Scouting Platform is processed (research/athlete-recruiting-marketplace.md §Boundary Findings).
- athlete-recruiting-marketplace sourcing limitation: FieldLevel (network/endorsement pole) blocked (HTTP 403 ×2), SportsRecruits help center unreachable (timeout ×2), BeRecruited (early-web historical sample) returned empty — sample anchored by NCSA/SportsRecruits/CaptainU product pages (Tier 2); no help-center-level operational detail (profile field lists, message mechanics, eligibility gates) evidenced, so none asserted; vendor scale figures kept in research notes only (recorded in Sources of applications/athlete-recruiting-marketplace.md).
- pension-administration-platform: US-style DC retirement-plan recordkeeping (401(k)-type participant recordkeeping) fits this Type's L0 (plan-governed participant accounts + contribution accrual + distribution/vesting calculation + payment administration) and is treated as a Variant within this leaf; the directory has no dedicated "retirement plan recordkeeping" leaf — if that market is later split out it should become a sibling with a shared boundary note, not a silent rewrite (research/pension-administration-platform.md §Boundary Findings).
- pension-administration-platform vs insurance-policy-administration-system: structurally closest neighbor pair (both long-horizon governed records → rule-based entitlement → payment runs); distinguishing axis is the governance basis of the entitlement — scheme/trust/statute + employer participation + employment-based accrual vs commercial contract + premiums; buy-out/bulk-annuity books sit near the boundary (scheme on pension admin, resulting annuity contracts in policy admin); recommend boundary cross-check when Insurance Policy Administration System is processed (research/pension-administration-platform.md §Boundary Findings).

- ai-voice-generator joint-review completion (closes the ai-audio-generator / ai-music-generator three-way-split flag under 04.22): the voice side confirms the deliverable-class boundary — AI Voice Generator = spoken performance of user-supplied words (ElevenLabs TTS/voice family, Murf, Speechify, Amazon Polly; none of the sampled products generates songs or sound material), sung vocals inside a generated song remain with AI Music Generator, non-verbal sound material with AI Audio Generator; the voice Type's distinctive structures are the voice as a persistent identity-bearing reusable object with consent/verification/provenance machinery (clone verification, permission statements, voice-actor royalties) and input-as-content (the script is the words, not a description of desired output); conversational agents/IVR consume the capability and are not this Type; sourcing limitation recorded: PlayHT unreachable (transport error ×2, abandoned) — the API-first independent-platform segment is under-evidenced beyond the sampled vendors' own APIs; Polly evidence page-level (research/ai-voice-generator.md §Boundary Findings).

- api-design-platform vs api-documentation-platform (§12 sibling): two-sided drift observed — the design platform Stoplight self-describes as an "OpenAPI Design & Documentation Management Tool" and the docs-platform Redocly's collaboration product now includes "design, edit, and review" with an OpenAPI editor; boundary held on the central-artifact test (authoring/maintaining the machine-readable contract is primary vs rendering/publishing it for consumers); flagged for joint review when API Documentation Platform is processed (research/api-design-platform.md §Boundary Findings).

- product-discovery-application name-collision guard (§05.05 vs §12): "Product Discovery Application" (consumer shopping discovery — this leaf) and "Product Discovery Platform" (§12 software product management, Productboard-class) are unrelated Types sharing near-identical names — recorded so neither is ever merged or confused; also flagged: the §05.05 family (Shopping Search Engine / Product Discovery Application / Shopping Comparison Platform / Deal Discovery Platform) shares one product-record substrate and differs on what organizes the session (query vs browse vs offer-set vs deal) — recommend joint review when the sibling leaves are processed; sourcing limitation: LTK/Pinterest/Houzz/Shopify-merchant-docs unreachable (transport errors/timeouts/403) — documented sample rests on Shop + Thingtesting + Klarna, historical/regional forms (Wanelo/Polyvore/Kaboodle/ThisNext/Xiaohongshu/TikTok Shop/Instagram Shopping/Pinterest) qualitative only, no precise operational claims (research/product-discovery-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- board-corporate-governance-platform (§10) vs corporate-governance-platform (§11): probable duplicate/alias leaves — market products conflate board management with broader corporate-governance suites (Diligent One sells board management as the entry point to entities/risk/compliance; OnBoard brands itself "governance system of record") — §10 leaf documented as the board-meeting-cycle-centered Type with suite extensions as optional; recommend joint review for merge or an explicit center-of-gravity split when the §11 leaf is processed (research/board-corporate-governance-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- board-corporate-governance-platform (§10) vs committee-board-management (§25): association-market instance of the same software (OnBoard maintains an association industry page; BoardPro sells nonprofit/school editions) — core model identical, vocabulary differs (trustees/chapters); probable audience-variant/alias — flagged for joint review when Committee / Board Management is processed
- board-corporate-governance-platform (§10) vs legislative-management-system / government-meeting-agenda-management (§24): real overlap via public-sector board portals (Diligent Community sells board-portal-lineage software to school boards/municipal councils with agenda approval workflows + public transparency publishing) — boundary held on center of gravity (a governed body's confidential meeting cycle + official record vs the public legislative/clerk workflow), but the public-sector board variant sits between the Types — recommend joint review when the §24 leaves are processed; sourcing limitation: operational help docs reachable only for BoardPro (OnBoard support transport error; Diligent/Convene at product-page level) — state-machine mechanics attributed to one product's implementation pattern, no numeric limits asserted (recorded in Sources of applications/board-corporate-governance-platform.md)

- enterprise-service-management vs employee-service-management (§10 siblings, both now processed): resolves the pre-existing flag — the two leaf names sit over one continuous market category (the same products — JSM/Freshservice/ServiceDesk Plus/SolarWinds — populate both, and the analyst category "ESM Platforms" is employee-facing in its requester population); orientation gradient, not a structure wall: employee-service-management defines by requester population (employee as internal service customer), enterprise-service-management by provider span (all internal departments as managed service units under one discipline, generalized out of ITSM); probable near-alias — recommend joint review to either keep both with orientation-based boundary statements (current state, both docs cross-reference consistently) or merge under one canonical name; boundary vs ITSM (§14, unprocessed) is a vendor-stated scope gradient (ManageEngine FAQ: "ITSM focuses on IT operations, ESM applies the same proven processes across other business departments") — flag for joint review when ITSM is processed; ServiceNow sourcing limitation carries over (unreachable in both passes) — enterprise-suite pole of the category uncharacterized

- brand-creator-marketplace vs influencer-marketing-platform / influencer-campaign-management / ugc-creator-marketplace (§27 siblings, all unprocessed at this pass): product reality straddles the seams — leading self-described "platforms" ship explicit marketplace modules with creator-side portals and platform-executed payments, while marketplaces grow platform-ish strategy/managed services; structural separator recorded: creator as first-class platform participant (own portal + incoming opportunities + platform-executed compensation) = marketplace core present regardless of vendor positioning; vs UGC Creator Marketplace held on publication-to-own-audience (UGC-only deliverable = ad-asset scope variant, not a separate venue shape); vs Affiliate Network held on compensation form (negotiated deliverable fee vs sales commission; affiliate ships as an add-on module inside sampled marketplace products); recommend joint review when the three sibling leaves are processed; sourcing limitation: Upfluence 403, TikTok/Instagram platform-native marketplace docs unreachable (timeouts ×2), one sampled product verified at positioning level only — no fee/timing/rights figures asserted in the final doc (research/brand-creator-marketplace.md §Boundary Findings)

- product-catalog-management vs product-information-management-pim (§05.04 siblings, both now processed): resolves the pre-existing joint-review flag — boundary confirmed by center of gravity with direct PIM-side evidence (all five sampled PIMs center on governed product content as master data + delivery to any channel incl. other parties' selling systems; none treats price/stock-as-selling-state as its center — price appears as an attribute type, data not offer state); blur documented both directions (commerce platforms embed PIM-like content authoring; PIM vendors publish buyer-facing outputs — catalog sites/brand stores/portals); Digital Product Catalog confirmed as the published buyer-facing output surface of PIM/PCM, not the management system; recommend keeping both leaves with the center-of-gravity boundary statement (research/product-information-management-pim.md §Boundary Findings)

- entity-compliance-management vs legal-entity-management (§10/§11 cross-section pair; legal-entity-management unprocessed at this pass): the market sells one product category ("entity management software" — Diligent Entities, CSC Entity Management, Athennian all self-describe this way) serving both directory leaves; working split recorded by emphasis — Entity Compliance Management centers on the obligation/deadline/filing loop and the entity's compliance state (good standing), Legal Entity Management on the entity record corpus and structure (org/ownership charts, minute books, entity lifecycle events); probable near-duplicate/heavy-overlap pair — recommend joint review when legal-entity-management is processed (research/entity-compliance-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- artifact-repository vs package-registry (§12 siblings; package-registry unprocessed): overlap is the sharpest in the dev-tooling block — two of five sampled artifact-repository products are literally vendor-named "package registry", and platform-embedded products (GitLab-class, GitHub Packages-class, Azure Artifacts) sit on both sides of any name-based split; split recorded by center of gravity: Artifact Repository = organization-operated custody of build outputs across formats (repository topology + upstream proxying/aggregation + pipeline governance as the differentiating layer); Package Registry = publication/consumption of a package-manager ecosystem packages (public registries npm/PyPI/Maven-Central and single-ecosystem registries as prototypes; whether public registries belong to that leaf is an open question recorded there); recommend joint review when Package Registry is processed — likely outcomes are single-ecosystem subset/variant or an explicit center-of-gravity split; secondary parallel-registry flag: Model Registry (§13) boundary (model lifecycle governance vs artifact custody) to confirm when that leaf is processed (research/artifact-repository.md §Boundary Findings)
