- capital-improvement-planning vs public-budgeting-platform (sibling in §24, unprocessed): packaging seam — multiple public budgeting suites ship capital-planning modules (verified in Euna Budget Capital; market anchors suggest the pattern is common), so the product-level boundary between "CIP application" and "budgeting suite with a capital module" is fuzzy; type-level boundary held by center of gravity (multi-year project register + funding-source allocation + governed multi-year adoption vs annual expense authority by fund/line item); no alias/duplicate declared — recommend joint review when Public Budgeting Platform is processed

- broadcast-management-system vs radio-station-management (§27 siblings; radio-station-management unprocessed at this pass): radio traffic/billing systems are structurally instances of the BMS model (order → inventory → log → as-run → reconciliation → billing; WO Traffic explicitly covers "TV and radio traffic and billing"); the two leaves are separable only by medium scope (radio station-wide operations incl. music scheduling/voice tracking/automation vs cross-medium channel commercial management) — soft boundary, joint review suggested when radio-station-management is processed (research/broadcast-management-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- boat-yacht-charter-platform (§18, processed): open question — membership-based boat clubs (fleet access by subscription entitlement rather than per-charter mediated transactions) appear to be a different access model that does not fit the charter-platform core (no per-charter mediated transaction); could not be verified against a live product this pass (Borrow a Boat 403×2) — if a boat-club leaf or product sample surfaces later, decide variant-vs-separate-Type jointly; secondary note: the boundary vs Vacation Rental Marketplace (§26, unprocessed) is the sharpest structural seam in this pass — same two-sided time-based rental skeleton, held on vessel-operation semantics (qualification/operating deposits/handover/weather); recommend re-confirming when vacation-rental-marketplace is processed (research/boat-yacht-charter-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- chat-room-application vs group-messaging-application / team-messaging-application / community-chat-platform (01.01 siblings; all three unprocessed at pass time): boundary held on the place test — room = addressable conversation place existing apart from its members + self-service entry by directory/link/invite + pseudonymous stranger co-presence + room-local operator governance; group messaging = member-defined private thread among known people (invitation-flow, no self-service discovery by address), team messaging = org-roster membership and org identity behind room-shaped channels, community platform = community container that users join first with rooms underneath; drift cases observed inside the sample (Element Spaces = container layer above rooms with "space members" access gating; IRCCloud team servers = private team rooms with modern chat features) confirm products of this Type extend into both neighbor territories — joint review recommended when Group Messaging, Team Messaging, and Community Chat Platform are processed; secondary note: the standalone consumer "chat room" (portal-era category) has largely migrated into community platforms, while the room structure itself remains alive through IRC and Matrix ecosystems — market observation only, no taxonomy change proposed (research/chat-room-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- community-chat-platform (01.01, processed) — discharges the community-chat side of the chat-room joint-review flag: container test confirmed with direct evidence (Stoat/Revolt servers and Element Spaces both show community-first membership held above rooms; Element retained as the deliberate room-first straddler with a container layer); boundary vs chat-room-application held on what the user joins first; group-messaging-application and team-messaging-application sides of the flag remain open (both still unprocessed); new flag: vs the 01.06 Community Platform family (online-forum / community-platform / interest-community-platform / private-community-platform, all unprocessed) — seam held on primary object (live rooms under a container vs asynchronous content), joint review recommended if 01.06 processing encounters chat-centric community products; hosted consumer pole (Discord/Guilded) docs unreachable — described structurally, no product claims (research/community-chat-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- care-coordination-platform vs chronic-care-management / care-plan-management (§22 siblings, both unprocessed at pass time): probable overlap — market evidence shows chronic-care-management software and care coordination software are the same products under a program overlay (ThoroughCare sells both as functions of one platform; eClinicalWorks ships CCM as one module of its care-coordination/population-health suite), and care plans are a central object in both coordination and plan management; working split recorded: chronic-care-management = care coordination Type carrying a specific chronic-care program's eligibility/consent/time/billing rules, care-plan-management = plan-as-authored-document system vs coordination's plan-as-execution-engine (remove the team-execution loop and it becomes plan management; remove document depth and keep the loop and it stays coordination); recommend joint review when both sibling leaves are processed; secondary fuzzy edge: social care coordination (WellSky line) sits between this Type and Social Services Case Management (research/care-coordination-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- collaborative-canvas vs digital-whiteboard (§03.05 siblings; digital-whiteboard unprocessed at pass time): probable alias — the researched market runs one product family behind the two names (Figma's own help center labels FigJam "a digital whiteboard"; Excalidraw self-titles "Whiteboard"; Mural sells a "shared infinite canvas"; Miro's board is documented as "endless"; official migration tooling on Miro/FigJam treats Mural/FigJam/Jamboard/Conceptboard boards as one migration family while separating Lucidchart/draw.io "diagrams"); working lens split recorded: whiteboard = live session/facilitation-surface emphasis, collaborative canvas = board-as-persistent-co-created-artifact emphasis, products straddle both — recommend joint review when digital-whiteboard is processed (likely outcomes: explicit merge or a lens-based boundary statement); secondary boundary vs diagramming-application held on the vendors' own board-vs-diagram import taxonomy — re-confirm when diagramming-application is processed (research/collaborative-canvas.md §Boundary Findings)

- brewery-management (§20, processed) vs winery-management (§20 sibling, unprocessed): same fermented-beverage production-management family — one sampled platform (BrewPlanner) sells brewery+winery(+cidery/meadery/distillery) from a single product and another vendor ships a kombucha sister product, and the canonical record structure (recipe→batch→time-extended fermentation measurement→materials in/packaged product out) holds across beverages; differentiation is process vocabulary and record flavor (grain bills/hop schedules/gravity/conditioning vs vintages/grape lots/crush-press-aging-blending) — recommend joint review when winery-management is processed to decide sibling-split vs family treatment (research/brewery-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- care-plan-management (§22, processed) sibling-pass answer to the care-coordination-platform joint-review flag: the recorded working split holds under care-plan-centric evidence — care plan management centers the plan as an authored, structured, controlled record (needs→goals→interventions structure, accountable authorship, living revision) while care coordination centers the team-execution loop; the behavioral-health treatment-plan variant (Qualifacts) is plan management operating without task generation, proving the execution loop is not definitional for plan management, and agency platforms (AxisCare/Birdie/Nourish/PointClickCare) bundle both layers as packaging rather than Type collapse; chronic-care-management sibling remains unprocessed — its flag stands for its own pass; secondary market note: care plan management is rarely sold standalone (module-in-platform or EHR-embedded packaging is the norm), relevant when Home Care Agency Management / Home Health EHR / Hospice Management / Skilled Nursing Facility Management leaves are processed (research/care-plan-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- brand-management-platform (§06, processed) answers the joint-review flag from brand-asset-guideline-platform: the two leaves share their defining core (governed brand record + controlled reach beyond the brand team) and the same market product set is marketed under both labels — probable partial alias, not two disjoint Types; workable distinction is center of gravity (sibling = record + consumption surface with production as optional depth; this leaf = record + application/production layer + governance workflow as first-class structure); recommend taxonomy consolidation review of the pair; secondary note stands: no general-DAM leaf exists in the directory while DAM platforms are the dominant substrate for both leaves (research/brand-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- professional-trading-terminal (§08, processed) answers the joint-review flag from algorithmic-trading-platform (retail-trading-platform / professional-trading-terminal / brokerage-platform): the structural test holds from the terminal side — who makes the trading decision at trade time separates the terminal (human decision loop) from Algorithmic Trading Platform, and conditional order types (stop/bracket/OCO/trailing/iceberg) observed across TT/CQG/Quantower/DAS are order-management primitives, not strategies; the three-way Retail/Brokerage/Terminal seam is held by center of gravity (live trading workspace vs account administration vs consumer account surface) with real straddles: broker-native pro platforms (TWS/thinkorswim pattern) straddle Retail↔Terminal, brokerage-embedded algo platforms (TradeStation pattern) straddle Brokerage↔Algo; retail-trading-platform and brokerage-platform remain unprocessed — recommend joint review when they are; secondary light flag: Financial Market Data Terminal sibling — data terminals with execution add-ons (Bloomberg Terminal pattern) straddle toward this Type (test: remove order routing → data terminal) (research/professional-trading-terminal.md §Boundary Findings)

- breach-attack-simulation (§15, processed) vs security-validation-platform (§15 sibling, unprocessed): umbrella overlap — all three commercial products in the BAS sample self-name under "security validation"/"exposure validation"/"Automated Security Validation" (Pentera "Security Validation Platform", SafeBreach "Exposure Validation Platform", Picus "Autonomous Exposure Validation Platform"; G2 category "Breach and Attack Simulation", Frost Radar "Automated Security Validation"), while BAS is the attack-execution core inside those platforms; if the sibling leaf is kept distinct, workable seam = BAS (safe execution of attack simulations + recorded per-technique control response + closed re-test loop) vs security validation as program/verdict layer incl. non-execution inference (Picus Exposure Validation "proves exploitability without firing an exploit") and cross-source aggregation; secondary straddle: "automated pentesting"/attack-path-execution products (Pentera Surface/Core, Picus APV) sit between this Type and Penetration Testing Management — recommend joint review when security-validation-platform and penetration-testing-management are processed (research/breach-attack-simulation.md §Boundary Findings)

- brand-reputation-management (§06) vs social-listening-platform / media-monitoring-platform (§06 siblings, both unprocessed): market "reputation" splits into two poles — (1) review/feedback-centric reputation loop (capture external signals → per-signal organizational action: public response / solicitation / routing → tracked entity reputation state), documented as this leaf's defining core; (2) corporate reputation-intelligence pole (Signal AI-style media/narrative sensing, benchmarking, reporting for comms/risk teams) which calls itself "reputation management" but has no review loop and belongs with Media Monitoring/Social Listening; structural test = remove per-signal organizational action → a listening/monitoring platform remains; flag for joint review when both siblings are processed (research/brand-reputation-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- collaborative-design-platform vs ui-design-application / ux-prototyping-application (04.15 siblings, unprocessed): probable partial overlap — the market flagship collaborative design platform is simultaneously the archetype UI design tool and prototyping tool; working distinction adopted: Collaborative Design Platform is defined by its collaboration structure (shared multi-user design files, subject-agnostic — its own docs position design files for graphic design, social posts, presentations, wireframes, illustrations, "anyone who wants to create or communicate visually") while UI Design Application is defined by target artifact (user interfaces) and UX Prototyping Application by the interactive prototype as central artifact; products straddle — recommend joint review when 04.15 leaves are processed (research/collaborative-design-platform.md §Boundary Findings #2)
- collaborative-design-platform vs template-based-design-platform (04.01 sibling, unprocessed): template-first platforms start from browsed pre-made compositions constrained for non-designer audiences vs this Type starting from blank/shared freeform design files for designers (templates optional starters only); Canva unreachable this pass (browser gate ×1, abandoned) — boundary drawn conceptually, no operational claims; flag for joint review when template-based-design-platform is processed; secondary gradient vs graphic-design-application (single-user local files vs shared multi-user files; seam = whether the shared multi-user file is the unit of work or a distribution convenience) (research/collaborative-design-platform.md §Boundary Findings #1,#3)

- building-access-visitor-management (§17): the market actually contains two separately-sold product families — physical access control systems (door/credential/event decisioning) and visitor management systems (registration/check-in/hosting) — while the directory holds one combined leaf; documented as one boundary-control Type with two person-poles (occupant credential path + visitor registration path), since every sampled product carries both natively or as companion modules; if the atlas later wants finer granularity, a split into separate Access Control and Visitor Management leaves is plausible — joint review recommended; secondary: Envoy self-positions as a workplace management platform (its visitor module is the in-scope slice), and no separate physical-access-control leaf exists in the directory (research/building-access-visitor-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- certification-management (§25) resolves the two prior joint-review flags recorded by accreditation-certification-management (§11) and accreditation-management (§25): (1) §11 prediction CONFIRMED — §25 certification-management manages credentials issued to individuals (certificants, CE/renewal tracking, member credentials), sharing only vocabulary with the §11 organizational-compliance Type; (2) §25 "probable near-duplicate" with accreditation-management REVISED to distinct Types sharing the front half — intake→review→decision→standing-status machinery is genuinely shared and one codebase demonstrably runs both (OpenWater: accreditation offering documented in that pass; LearningBuilder markets certification + accreditation on one platform), but the structural split holds on managed population (individuals vs organizations) and maintenance spine (person-bound renewal/CE/audit/lapse machinery vs standards-based organizational evidence/peer review/interim reporting), with purpose-built products carrying one spine and not the other; recommend keeping both leaves with this boundary statement (research/certification-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- certification-management vs continuing-education-management (§25 sibling, unprocessed): gradient — CE tracking is the renewal input of certification management and the same vendor ships CE Management as its own solution (approved-provider networks, course catalogs); working split: CE management centers learning-activity approval/credit capture, certification management centers the credential lifecycle and consumes CE as maintenance evidence; flagged for joint review when continuing-education-management is processed (research/certification-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- programmatic-advertising-platform vs demand-side-platform-dsp / supply-side-platform-ssp (§06 siblings, both unprocessed): "Programmatic Advertising Platform" is the market-category term for the two-sided automated impression-trading layer; concrete products instantiate the buy-side pole (DSP), the sell-side pole (SSP), the exchange venue, or a full-stack suite, and no sampled product (Monetize/TTD/StackAdapt/Basis/Magnite/PubMatic) carries a distinct "programmatic platform" architecture beyond those roles — products once self-labeling "programmatic advertising platform" (StackAdapt, Basis) now anchor to DSP/advertising-automation positioning; both prior sibling passes (ad-server, ad-delivery-platform) independently recorded the same umbrella judgment; this leaf is documented as the two-sided trading category; recommend joint review when DSP and SSP leaves are processed — decide whether the leaf remains a category-level Type or becomes a category alias/see-also of the two poles (research/programmatic-advertising-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- broker-management-platform (§08, processed) vs insurance-agency-management (§08 sibling, unprocessed): probable regional-naming alias — the US market sells the identical intermediary back-office as "agency management system" (Vertafore AMS360, HawkSoft, EZLynx) while the UK market sells it as broker software / "broker management system" (Acturis, SSP); Vertafore's own AMS FAQ names "agents, brokers, CSRs, and agency principals" as the same system's users and HawkSoft copy addresses "agents and brokers" interchangeably; no sampled structural difference separates the two leaves (both = client + policy/placement + carrier panel + commission + renewal + documents + accounting); recommend joint review when insurance-agency-management is processed (merge vs keep-as-regional-naming-variant pair); secondary intent check: this pass read the leaf as broker-side software, supported by §08 placement between Insurance Agency Management and Insurance Quote Platform and by market usage — if the taxonomy intended insurer-side broker-network management, the framing would need revision (research/broker-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- agent-tool-computer-use-platform vs browser-compatibility-testing-platform (§12; joint-review flag from the tool-platform pass): answered from the testing side — same cloud-browser substrate confirmed as shared infrastructure (this pass observed compat vendors packaging agent-consumable session substrates — SDK/agent-skill session launch + connect-to-session, MCP servers, agent-framework integrations — alongside their testing products); Type boundary held on invoker + job: human tester or human-written test suites verifying expected behavior of the customer's own web app vs model-driven sessions accomplishing tasks; no merge, both Types defensible; device-testing-platform remains unprocessed — flag stays open for that sibling (research/browser-compatibility-testing-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- building-asset-management (§17, processed) vs CMMS / Maintenance Management + Enterprise Asset Management (§16 siblings): conceptually an industry-scoped member of the asset-management/CMMS family — every sampled building-asset product contains a CMMS-shaped care loop, and generic CMMS products (Fiix) serve facility managers too; the differentiators are the building/location model (site→building→floor/room, floor-plan mapping) and the lifecycle/renewal economics (condition, FCI, deferred maintenance, funding scenarios); market naming ("facility asset management" as a named Accruent solution category; "facility asset lifecycle" as AkitaBox positioning) supports keeping the leaf as an independent Type; recommend joint review with the CMMS/EAM leaves for a possible family-level statement (research/building-asset-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- chapter-management-platform (§25, processed) sibling-pass answer to the association-management-system-ams flag: confirmed separable Types by center of gravity — AMS = staff-operated system of record for one membership organization (constituent registry + membership status + dues/renewal spine) with chapters as one optional structural variant; Chapter Management Platform = the multi-unit network itself as the managed object (unit registry + per-unit population/leadership + parent oversight/roll-up/fund flows); removal tests recorded both directions (remove the chapter structure → AMS/membership management; remove the parent's own membership spine but keep unit operations → still chapter management); overlap is real at suite level (the re:Members family ships both an AMS and a chapter-financial product; Glue Up sells chapter management and association management as separate solutions on one site) — no merge recommended; the AMS doc already treats chapters as a structural variant, and this pass documents the unit-network center (research/chapter-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- browser-security-platform (§15, processed) vs Endpoint Management / UEM-style browser management: sharpest unresolved seam — browser configuration management (settings, updates, extension allowlists) without session-level protective enforcement is browser management, but the market is converging from both sides (security vendors integrating into browser-management consoles, e.g. LayerX into the Chrome Enterprise console; browser/OS vendors adding security tiers, e.g. Chrome Enterprise Premium — the latter unverified, site unreachable), so the boundary deserves joint review when a browser-management leaf is processed; secondary flag: category consolidation (SquareX→Zscaler, LayerX→Akamai; enterprise-browser market naming by analysts) may eventually fold standalone browser security into SSE suites — structural distinctness of browser-layer enforcement holds today (research/browser-security-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- financial-close-management (§08, processed) resolves the account-reconciliation-platform joint-review flag: two Types confirmed separable by central record (close management = per-period assigned task/checklist tracked to attributable completion; reconciliation = two-sided balance comparison with attributed certification and reconciling items); overlap is surface-level (both track status/due dates) and vendors ship them as one suite with a documented object-level link (checklist items can depend on reconciliations — FloQast dependency targets; BlackLine/Trintech/Oracle ship separate modules) — no merge recommended; secondary taxonomy note: the market category ("Financial Close and Consolidation Solutions" per Gartner, cited on Oracle's FCCS page) bundles close + consolidation, and consolidation-led suites embed close orchestration — the directory's separate leaves are structurally justified but suite bundling should be expected; ERP-embedded close (SAP close-cockpit lineage, NetSuite) not directly observed (fetch-blocked) — variant posture recorded at low strength (research/financial-close-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- child-welfare-management (§24, processed) vs social-services-case-management / public-sector-case-management (§24 siblings, both unprocessed): closest seams — child welfare management is the statutory child-protection specialization (protected minor + mandated report screening + safety assessment + placement/permanency + need-to-know confidentiality); removal test recorded both directions (strip statutory loop + placement/permanency → generic social services case management; a generic case system with a placement search does not become child welfare); products like Casebook span public/nonprofit/agency tiers from one platform (packaging overlap, not Type collapse); secondary: nonprofit-case-management (§25, unprocessed) shares the casework spine for private delivery agencies — same joint-review cluster; recommend joint review when the siblings are processed (research/child-welfare-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- budgeting-application (§08, processed) resolves the expense-tracking-application joint-review flag: two Types confirmed separable by center of gravity (budgeting = plan-first allocation container with actuals feeding the plan-vs-actual comparison; expense tracking = record-first classified log with budgets as an optional comparison layer); strongest evidence is the asymmetric existence proof — Fudget markets a budgeting app with "no bank connections, no tracking" (no record layer at all) while the expense-tracking sample carried budgets only as an optional layer over records; no merge recommended; secondary note: Monarch and Quicken Simplifi ship budgeting as a module inside PFM suites — bundle posture, not Type collapse; name-collision note: Budgeting & Forecasting Platform (§08 corporate sibling, unprocessed) shares the root term — distinct on actors/objects (organizational planning cycles vs personal period plan), joint review recommended when that leaf is processed (research/budgeting-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- casting-platform (§27, processed) closes the audition-management joint-review flag: boundary held from the platform side — Casting Platform's defining work is the market exchange (published opportunities under publisher-controlled visibility, talent-profile population, submissions moving across the match, two-sided discovery at multi-production scale); Audition Management's defining work is running the selection funnel to a recorded decision; two-directional removal tests recorded (strip market/discovery → management products like Cast It studio workspace and education adjudication remain themselves; strip funnel machinery → open listing-and-submission marketplaces remain themselves); real products bundle both (Casting Networks runs the full funnel inside the platform; Cast It Talent feeds a separate studio-side system) — porous in the market, distinct at Type level, both leaves stay, no taxonomy change (research/casting-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- psychometric-assessment-platform vs candidate-assessment-platform / technical-assessment-platform (§09 siblings, both unprocessed): one delivery mechanics, three leaves — seam is what is measured and how interpreted (psychometric = attribute measurement with vendor-owned normed instruments and reference-anchored interpretation; candidate/technical = job-skill and work-sample demonstration); market deliberately straddles (TestGorilla, Mercer Mettl, Criteria all sell psychometric + skills families in one platform; SHL bundles both under one assessment portfolio) — flagged for joint review when the sibling leaves are processed; candidate outcomes are three attribute/skill Types with product-level straddling, or a spectrum/consolidation view; also recorded: background-check/employment-verification (records vs attributes), employee-survey/engagement (opinions vs scored individuals) and ATS (pipeline owner vs measurement step) boundaries held cleanly (research/psychometric-assessment-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- chromatography-data-system (§22, processed): taxonomy placement note — the Type sits under Healthcare & Life Sciences but is domain-generic: pharmaceutical/biopharma QC is the dominant market (GMP/Part 11 posture) while the same products serve food, environmental, petrochemical, contract and academic labs; placement kept (pharma is the center of market gravity and the leaf naturally groups with lab-informatics siblings), no alias/variant problem found — boundaries held cleanly vs LIMS, LIS, ELN, Scientific Instrument Management, Stability Study Management; minor observation: modern instrument firmware with built-in integration blurs the CDS/firmware edge but documented products retain the persistent-reprocessing/result-record gap; no joint review required (research/chromatography-data-system.md §Boundary Findings)
- build-automation-system (§12) vs continuous-integration-platform (§12 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in this dev-tooling block — build tool = how one project builds (project-resident definition + dependency-ordered execution + artifact production, invoked interactively by developers or unattended by CI agents); CI = when/where builds run for whom (triggers, hosted shared execution, orchestration across jobs, run history); the subordination is documented from the build-tool side (Gradle ships dedicated per-CI integration chapters for GitHub Actions/GitLab CI/Jenkins/TeamCity/Travis; Bazel positions itself as the build+test tool that CI runs) — recommend joint review when continuous-integration-platform is processed; secondary straddle to settle in the same joint review: ecosystem-native build tools (cargo/npm-class) fuse build + dependency resolution + publishing and will need a three-way statement with dependency-management-application and package-registry (research/build-automation-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- catering-management vs banquet-management (§26 siblings): joint-review flag from the banquet pass answered — boundary held from both sides: banquet's spine is the venue's function-space schedule (function diary, room setups, BEO, on-premise execution); catering's spine is the food operation itself (menu/recipe/production machinery, quantities, delivery/service logistics) with no function-space substrate required; the overlap zone is real and products span both (Caterease serves "offsite-teams to full-service venues" and carries a Banquet Rooms module; Tripleseat sells to both catering operations and event venues; hotel vendors market the same structure as "sales & catering software") — both leaves kept, boundary = operational center of gravity; also flagged for the venue-management-system pass: remove the F&B/production layer from catering → VMS (research/catering-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- public-relations-management-platform (§06, processed) vs media-relations-platform (§06 sibling, unprocessed): closest boundary pair in the PR cluster — both center media relationship records and pitch/outreach sending, and market vocabulary straddles (Meltwater sells its "Media Relations" capability inside the full intelligence suite; Agility's all-in-one platform lives on a /media-relations solution page; Prezly self-describes as a "PR CRM") — boundary held in this pass on scope of the loop: media relations = the relationship-and-pitching slice (database + lists + pitches), PR management = that slice plus organized campaigns, coverage capture, and reporting across the whole PR function; removal test recorded both directions (remove campaigns/coverage/reporting → media relations; remove contacts/outreach → monitoring); recommend joint review when media-relations-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are two Types by scope (slice vs whole function) or a consolidation view; secondary seams held vs press-release-distribution-platform (consistent with that pass's "broader suite" note), media-monitoring-platform, social-listening-platform, social-media-management-platform, marketing-campaign-management, email-marketing, brand-reputation-management (research/public-relations-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)


- budgeting-forecasting-platform (§08, processed) vs financial-planning-analysis-platform (§08 sibling, unprocessed): umbrella-vs-slice overlap flagged — the same product family (Workday Adaptive Planning, Anaplan, Oracle EPM Planning, Planful, Prophix, Board) is marketed under both names; "FP&A platform" is the broader category framing (analysis/reporting/strategic-planning emphasis) while "budgeting & forecasting" names the planning-cycle-centered slice; no clean product partition by name was possible; this pass holds the defining core at the governed budget/forecast cycle (versioned plan data + contribution/approval loop over the financial planning model) and recommends joint review when financial-planning-analysis-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are emphasis-slice Types under one category or a consolidation view; secondary joint-review flag vs sales-forecasting-platform (§07, unprocessed): finance-side revenue projection inside the financial planning model vs sales-owned CRM-pipeline forecasting — sales-quota/account-planning modules inside budgeting platforms (e.g. Oracle Sales Planning) straddle the seam (research/budgeting-forecasting-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- collaborative-video-editor (§04.06, processed): market-category gap — products branded "video collaboration" (Frame.io-class: file management + review/approval + workflow management + camera-to-cloud) execute no editing operations; feedback notes flow *to* an external editor, so they fail the Type's editing test and are excluded from Collaborative Video Editor; the directory has no leaf for this review/collaboration-platform category (nearest existing: Media Asset Management §27) — recommend a future leaf or explicit alias decision when MAM / Video Editor / NLE leaves are reviewed

- collaborative-video-editor (§04.06, processed) vs video-editor / non-linear-editing-system-nle (§04.06 siblings, unprocessed): collaboration is shipped as a built-in capability of several NLE products rather than as a separate product category, making the boundary a posture gradient rather than a hard product split; leaf held as a distinct Type on the market-cluster test (an identifiable cluster organized around team editing workflow: post facilities, cloud team editors, classroom co-editing) — joint review recommended when Video Editor and NLE leaves are processed (research/collaborative-video-editor.md §Boundary Findings)
- building-management-system-bms (§17, processed) vs SCADA / DCS / HMI (§16 siblings, unprocessed): the same supervisory-control grammar (field devices + automated configured control + operator stations + alarms + trends) exists on both sides; the discriminator is the managed domain (building plant/comfort/energy vs industrial production) — recommend a family-level joint statement when the SCADA/DCS/HMI leaves are processed; secondary: Building Maintenance Management (§17 sibling, run failed mid-batch 2026-09-06) shares the fault→action seam (BMS flags off-normal behavior, the maintenance system owns the work order) — joint review when that sibling is processed (research/building-management-system-bms.md §Boundary Findings)

- chronic-care-management (§22, processed) vs care-coordination-platform (§22, processed — answering that pass's joint-review flag): overlap CONFIRMED from the CCM side — the same products sell both (ThoroughCare lists Care Coordination and Chronic Care Management as sibling functions of one platform; HealthArc defines CCM as "non-face-to-face care coordination" and ships a care-coordination solution alongside it; eClinicalWorks ships CCM as one module of its care-coordination/population-health suite; ChartSpan's FAQ describes CCM as monthly "care coordination activities" delivered as a managed program); the sibling pass's recorded working split holds under CCM-first evidence: care coordination = person + team + plan + tracked-activity loop as the general Type; chronic care management = that machinery bound to a defined chronic-care program whose own rules (chronic-condition eligibility, consented enrollment, per-period service/time documentation, billing outputs) are first-class, machine-enforced objects; removal test recorded both directions (remove the program machinery → care coordination platform; remove the chronic-condition anchor → generic program coordination; remove the recurring documented service cycle → care plan management); both leaves documented with distinct centers of gravity and cross-references; NOT unilaterally merged — recommend joint consolidation review of the care-coordination family (care-coordination-platform / chronic-care-management / care-plan-management) to decide whether CCM is formalized as the program-shaped variant-of-record or retained as a family-member leaf (research/chronic-care-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- cemetery-management (§29, processed) vs funeral-home-management + crematory-management (§29 siblings, unprocessed): deathcare vendors increasingly bundle all three operator domains in one platform (PlotBox ships cemetery+crematory+funeral modules; OpusXenta ships cemetery+crematoria), yet the core objects remain distinct — cemetery = burial-space inventory + interment register + interment rights; funeral home = funeral case (care of the deceased, visitation, ceremony, disposition paperwork, funeral merchandise); crematory = cremation operation (authorizations, chamber scheduling, remains tracking); webCemeteries integrates with funeral case management (Passare) rather than absorbing it, documenting the seam from inside the market; removal tests recorded (remove the burial-space inventory → funeral home software; remove the ground/space inventory → crematory software); recommend joint review when both siblings are processed — candidate outcomes are three domain Types sold as one suite (current view) or a consolidated deathcare-platform view with three operator modules (research/cemetery-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- ad-hoc-query-application vs business-intelligence-platform (§13 siblings; joint-review flag from the ad-hoc pass DISCHARGED from the BI side): confirmed — every sampled BI platform (Tableau, Power BI, Qlik, Metabase; ThoughtSpot/Zoho via the paired pass) bundles the interactive question loop as a core capability (field-drag composition, search/NL question surfaces, drill), while the BI defining core is the governed artifact lifecycle (authored content + hosted persistent repository + consumer audience + content-and-data access control); structural tests recorded both directions (strip the platform to the loop alone → ad-hoc query application; wrap the loop's saved questions in repository+audience+governance → BI platform); recommendation to taxonomy owner: keep both Types with the loop-as-capability seam documented on both sides, or re-scope ad-hoc-query-application as the interactive slice of the BI family — both documents are consistent either way (research/business-intelligence-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- business-intelligence-platform (§13, processed) vs dashboard-platform / reporting-platform / data-visualization-application / olap-multidimensional-analytics-platform (§13 siblings, all unprocessed): boundaries held structurally with removal tests and joint-review flags — dashboards are the BI flagship artifact, so Dashboard Platform is a probable capability-slice/partial-alias (lightweight dashboard-first composition/sharing with thinner modeling/governance/repository); Reporting Platform seam = interactive visual analytics over a governed hosted repository vs formatted document-shaped output and its delivery (BI ships formatted reporting as a capability via paginated-report/companion engines); Data Visualization Application seam = remove multi-user hosted repository + consumer audience + access governance → single-user viz authoring; OLAP seam = cube/multidimensional model as defining object vs model-agnostic consumption lifecycle (BI has absorbed OLAP-style slice-drill interactions); Data Warehouse Platform = clean substrate boundary (BI is one of its principal clients), no conflict; Data Science Workbench (code-notebook analysis) and Enterprise AI Assistant (conversational knowledge/task access — in-BI AI features are capabilities of this Type) carry light flags; sourcing: Looker + IBM Cognos unreachable — no claims drawn from either (research/business-intelligence-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- business-banking-portal (§08, processed) vs commercial-banking-platform / cash-management-platform (§08 siblings, unprocessed): the corporate tier is structurally a different product, not a bigger portal — every sampled bank that operates a business portal also sells a separate corporate/cash-management platform (BofA CashPro vs Business Advantage 360; J.P. Morgan Commercial Banking vs Chase Business Online; Wells Fargo Commercial Banking; CommBank Institutional split) with file/API-scale payments, liquidity and treasury machinery; some banks blur upward by attaching treasury services to top-tier business checking; boundary held in this pass on SMB self-service payments + per-user entitlement model vs treasury-grade rail machinery; removal test recorded (scale up rails + treasury machinery → commercial/cash-management platform); recommend joint review when commercial-banking-platform is processed; second flag: consumer-surface siblings (online-banking-portal / mobile-banking-application / digital-banking-application, all unprocessed) are surface-defined while this leaf is customer-type-defined — the owner-managed sole-trader segment is absorbed differently per bank (consumer-portal routing, separate sole-trader product, or personal-business linking rule), so the business↔consumer seam is real but its product expression varies by bank (research/business-banking-portal.md §Boundary Findings)

- purchase-order-management vs procure-to-pay-platform / procurement-management-platform (§10, both siblings processed; P2P's pre-flagged seam DISCHARGED from the POM side): center-of-gravity gradient

- church-communication-platform (§25, processed) vs email-marketing-platform / sms-marketing-platform (§06 siblings, unprocessed): probable audience/domain-specialized sibling relationship — the messaging grammar (compose → list → schedule → send → track → unsubscribe) is shared; the distinguishing structure is the audience substrate (the church's own people records with membership/attendance/group context, often ChMS-synced), consent captured through church-life mechanisms (text-a-keyword, digital connect cards, group membership) rather than commercial newsletter signup, and congregational message jobs (guest follow-up, volunteer coordination, pastoral care); a church using a generic marketing tool performs the same job without the Type's product — joint-review flag when the §06 siblings are processed; also note the ChMS spectrum: standalone comms platforms integrate with ChMS, some ChMS embed the module (Tithe.ly), and at least one major ChMS (Planning Center) ships no comms product and delegates the loop to integrations — supports the loop as its own center of gravity, not a ChMS submodule confirmed — P2P centers the transactional chain (approved demand → PO → receipt → matched invoice → payment-ready payable, invoice matching as definitional gate), PMP centers the procurement operation (managed supplier base, sourcing context, policy), POM centers the single PO object's lifecycle (types, revision, transmission/acknowledgment, closure machinery documented in depth independent of the invoice pipeline); standalone PO-first products exist (ProcureDesk sells a "Purchasing Automation" package engineered for front-end PO control; the PO module is the documented hinge in Precoro/Procurify), so the Type is defensible as a component-centered sibling — but every sampled vendor ships both centers in one product, so the seam is a gradient, not a wall; removal tests recorded (strip requisitions + invoice pipeline, keep PO lifecycle → still POM; remove the PO as center → AP automation or P2P); recommend joint consolidation review of the P2P/PMP/POM family for an explicit center-of-gravity split or capability re-scope; related boundaries held on object/center tests: AP automation (starts at invoice), Sales Order Capture/OMS (supplier-side mirror of the same document), Inventory Management (stock-centered, PO as replenishment instrument), Approval Workflow (generic routing vs order-specific commitment), CLM (framework vs transactional commitment), Supplier Portal (external slice), EDI (transport vs lifecycle), Government Procurement (sector-adjacent) (research/purchase-order-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- childcare-management-system (§29, processed) vs daycare-preschool-management (§29 sibling, unprocessed): probable alias / segment-slice — no sampled vendor maintains a distinct daycare-management or preschool-management product category separate from childcare management (Procare's one product line addresses "daycare, preschool, Head Start or ECE center"; Smartcare presents Childcare & Daycare Centers and Preschool & Early Childhood Programs as segments of one product; Kangarootime and Lillio serve preschools and daycares interchangeably); preschool = learning-layer emphasis inside the same Type — joint review recommended when daycare-preschool-management is processed (research/childcare-management-system.md §Boundary Findings #2). Also: after-school-program-management's joint-review flag vs childcare-management-system DISCHARGED from the childcare side — sibling Types sharing the family-enrollment-attendance-billing spine, split by care context (full-day custody care + care-day documentation vs scheduled part-day session programs); vendors ship both as sibling solutions (Procare, Kangarootime, Smartcare); both leaves stand.
- capacity-management sourcing limitation: the classic standalone capacity-suite pole could not be documented from public sources (ServiceNow product page timeout ×2 + docs.servicenow.com JS-gated; docs.bmc.com 403; ibm.com/docs 403; docs.sciencelogic.com empty; Wikipedia ITIL reference timed out) — evidence rests on four reachable representatives (VMware Aria Operations 8.18 via Broadcom TechDocs, Virtana IO, Cast AI, Kubex/Densify, all Tier-1); no claims made for unreachable vendors; no precise vendor defaults/numeric limits/thresholds asserted in the final document (product-specific figures recorded in research notes only); failed fetches not retried beyond the 1–2 attempt limit

- push-notification-marketing-platform (§06, processed) vs Email/SMS Marketing Platform + Mobile Marketing Platform (§06 siblings): §06 contains a family of channel-defined marketing platforms (email/SMS/push) sharing one campaign grammar (audience → message → schedule → measure), split by delivery substrate (inbox/carrier vs OS/browser push services) and audience registry (personal addresses vs device/browser tokens behind an OS permission gate); market positioning has drifted — all five sampled push vendors (OneSignal/Braze/Airship/CleverTap/Pushwoosh) now self-describe as "customer engagement"/"omnichannel messaging" platforms with push as one channel, and pure-play push-only positioning survives mainly at entry tiers; the leaf remains valid as a channel-defined Type (push mechanics are distinct and era-stable; developer push gateways are the negative case that isolates the marketing layer), but a joint family review of the §06 channel-platform leaves (Email/SMS/Push/Mobile Marketing) is recommended to make the shared-grammar framing explicit and to fix Mobile Marketing Platform's umbrella scope vs this channel slice (research/push-notification-marketing-platform.md §Boundary Findings)


- cdn-management (§14, processed): third-party multi-CDN management/steering tooling (control planes that operate delivery across several CDN providers simultaneously) was not researched and no claims were made; if the directory ever needs it, it is likely a distinct Type or a Variant of global traffic management rather than this provider-console Type — flagged for future review. Also noted: cloud providers are converging standalone CDN products into broader edge/application-delivery platforms (Azure CDN classic → Azure Front Door documented on official pages); the CDN Management Type persists as the operator-facing control plane inside those platforms, but future joint review with edge/app-delivery leaves may be warranted (research/cdn-management.md §Uncertainties)

- financial-planning-analysis-platform (§08, processed) RESOLVES the budgeting-forecasting-platform umbrella-vs-slice joint-review flag: confirmed one product category sold under two names with no partition by name — new FP&A-marketed evidence: Datarails sells "Datarails FP&A" with Planning/Budgeting & Forecasting as a solution inside it; Vena carries /solutions/financial-planning-analysis and /solutions/budgeting-forecasting as sibling pages of one platform, its FAQ naming the FP&A lifecycle "beyond budgeting and forecasting" (long-range planning, rolling forecasts, scenario analysis, management reporting, variance analysis); OneStream's FP&A page URL is /financial-planning-analysis/ while its footer links "CPM Software" to /solutions/planning-budgeting-forecasting; Vena's comparison menu treats Planful/Prophix/Adaptive/Cube/Anaplan/OneStream/Board/Jedox/Solver/NetSuite as one competitive set — resolution held by this pass: emphasis-slice Types of one category (budgeting-forecasting-platform = planning-cycle-centered slice: model + versioned plan data + governed cycle; financial-planning-analysis-platform = full-function slice adding the performance-analysis-and-management-reporting layer as definitional); both documents cross-reference; candidate outcomes for the taxonomy owner: keep both as emphasis-slice Types (current treatment) or consolidate under one category with the other as an alias — no product partition supports two fully independent Types; also answered the financial-modeling-application proposed seam (model-artifact-centered vs governed-function-centered — holds; FMA products market into FP&A vocabulary but lack the governed org-wide cycle and management-reporting apparatus); sales-forecasting-platform secondary flag remains open for that leaf (finance-side model projection vs sales-owned CRM pipeline; sales/quota planning modules straddle) (research/financial-planning-analysis-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- cam (§16, processed) vs cnc-programming-application (§16 sibling, unprocessed): probable alias — the market uses "CAM software" and "CNC programming software" interchangeably; Mastercam (the category's leading vendor) titles its own homepage "Mastercam Software: Your Solution for CNC Programming" and its products page "Program your CNC machines with the world's leading CAD/CAM software"; CAM's defining output IS a CNC program (geometry → computed toolpath → post-processed NC code); the only candidate distinction is manual hand-written G-code programming without geometry-driven computation, but that is a capability boundary inside the market, and vendors selling "CNC programming software" are CAM vendors; recommend joint review when cnc-programming-application is processed — candidate outcomes are consolidation (alias) or a manual-programming-activity slice; secondary seam vs additive-manufacturing-software (§16 sibling, unprocessed): additive slicing shares the geometry → computed motion → machine-output skeleton with build-vs-remove as the material direction — CAM leaf scoped to the machining/cutting sense, additive extensions in some CAM suites noted as optional (research/cam.md §Boundary Findings)

- church-management-system-chms (§25, processed) vs congregation-membership-management (§25 sibling, unprocessed): probable partial-overlap pair — membership records, households, and directories are one slice of the ChMS record core, and this pass documented membership as a module of ChMS rather than a separate Type; recommend joint review when congregation-membership-management is processed — candidate outcomes are consolidation (membership as the record-core slice of ChMS) or a distinct narrow Type if standalone membership-only products with no participation machinery surface; related watch-items: ministry-scheduling / worship-planning / religious-small-group-management / pastoral-care-management / religious-volunteer-management (§25 siblings, unprocessed) are capability slices that exist both as ChMS modules and as standalone specialists — the same module↔standalone spectrum the church-communication-platform leaf documented; ChMS boundary held on the record-core center of gravity (research/church-management-system-chms.md §Boundary Findings)

- comparison-platform (§02.10, processed) vs review-platform (§02.10 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the family — Review Platform centers on evaluation of individual options (reviews/ratings as the primary object); Comparison Platform centers on structured comparison across options (comparison set + aligned attributes + comparison presentation + decision orientation); overlap is bidirectional (documented comparison platforms carry reviews and third-party rating badges; review platforms commonly offer compare views — G2/Capterra unreachable this pass, expected structurally); removal test recorded both directions (remove the comparison structure, keep evaluations → Review Platform; remove reviews, keep the comparison set + attributes + presentation → still a Comparison Platform); joint-review flag when review-platform is processed. Second flag: comparison-platform vs shopping-comparison-platform (§05.05 sibling, unprocessed) — seam = same-SKU seller offers ending in a purchase vs different-product attribute comparison ending in a choice; joint-review flag. Secondary: insurance-quote comparison surfaces (quote-request flows inside documented comparison platforms) overlap with insurance-quote-platform (§08, unprocessed) — capability-vs-Type question flagged for that leaf. Boundary case documented: StackShare-class directory products with attached "alternatives" links fail the comparison-center test and belong to the Directory side (research/comparison-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- cleaning-business-management vs small-business-field-service-management (§29 sibling, unprocessed): researched sample (Kickserv as horizontal control + ZenMaid/Launch27/MaidCentral residential + Swept commercial) shows the identical structural spine (client+location → visit/job lifecycle → staff assignment → billing) across both; the difference is trade semantics — recurring cadence as the dominant pattern (series-vs-occurrence cancellation), crew-based execution, per-property checklist/task specification, unoccupied-premises access handling (entry codes/approved cleaners per location), and quality proof as a contract-retention instrument (scorecards residentially, inspections commercially); MaidCentral's own FAQ positions cleaning scheduling software as "a subtype of field service management software used specifically for cleaning companies" — probable trade-Variant relationship rather than two independent Types; flagged for joint review when Small Business Field Service Management is processed (research/cleaning-business-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- recommendation-personalization-engine (§06, processed) vs marketing-personalization-platform (§06 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the section — the recommendation engine's managed object is the ranked item decision (which items, in what order, for which request context, computed from behavioral signals) while the marketing personalization platform's managed object is the audience-experience decision (which content/experience variation per segment); products straddle heavily (Adobe Target ships both — activities+audiences vs criteria+designs; the pure-play pole could not be sampled this pass, Dynamic Yield unreachable), and the leaf name itself ("Recommendation / Personalization Engine") maps to the two poles of one context-conditioning (item-conditioned vs user-conditioned) rather than two Types; recommend joint review when marketing-personalization-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are two Types split by managed object with a documented straddle zone, or a consolidation view treating the engine as the ranked-item capability slice of the broader personalization platform (research/recommendation-personalization-engine.md §Boundary Findings)

- change-data-capture-platform (§13, processed) vs data-replication-platform (§13 sibling, unprocessed): taxonomy-level finding — the two leaves describe two delivery contracts over the same machinery, and the market's flagship products implement CDC as the capture mechanism of replication while branding themselves as replication/migration products (Oracle GoldenGate self-described "foundational product for data replication and change data capture"; Qlik Replicate; AWS DMS); seam test recorded both directions (remove the event-delivery contract, keep state-sync → Data Replication Platform; remove continuous capture, keep batch full-state movement → ETL/ELT Platform); recommend joint review when data-replication-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are two Types split by delivery contract (ordered event stream to consumers vs synchronized target copy) with a documented straddle zone, or a consolidation view treating CDC as the capture-capability slice of replication platforms (research/change-data-capture-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- church-website-builder (§25, processed) vs visual-website-builder (§04.16 sibling, unprocessed): probable audience/domain-specialized sibling relationship — same website-building substrate (hosted site, templates, visual editing, custom domain, SEO); the distinguishing structure is church-shaped content objects as first-class building blocks (service info, sermons+podcast, events, giving, guest welcome) plus church-operations integration (giving/ChMS/app) and the non-technical church-operator framing; a church using a generic builder performs the same job without the Type's product shape (vendors themselves articulate "churches are moving beyond generic website platforms") — joint-review flag when visual-website-builder is processed; also recorded: market consolidation of legacy standalone church builders (Clover Sites, Ekklesia 360, Sharefaith absorbed into Ministry Brands Amplify) while the standalone pole persists (Nucleus) — suite-bundling is a posture shift, not a Type change (research/church-website-builder.md §Boundary Findings)
- business-management-suite (§10, processed) vs enterprise-resource-planning-erp (§10 sibling, processed): JOINT-REVIEW FLAG DISCHARGED from this side — the ERP pass suspected a probable Alias/umbrella; this pass finds a depth gradient, not an alias and not a wall: at the finance-deep pole the suite IS functionally an ERP (NetSuite tagline "unified business management suite encompassing ERP/Financials+CRM+ecommerce"; Odoo titles itself "Open Source ERP and CRM"; Striven industry slugs "erp-software-for..."; SAP B1 — same product class — now positioned purely as SMB ERP; alias CONFIRMED there), but at the light pole (Bitrix24, SuiteDash — both marketed as all-in-one business management software) the money function is billing/invoicing with no GL ledger, failing the ERP definition (alias REJECTED there); discriminating test = does the money function post into a general ledger; RECOMMENDATION: keep both leaves — Business Management Suite = packaging-led umbrella (bundle + shared data core + customer/money/work three-pole span), ERP = finance-deep functional Type; cross-references added in both directions (applications/business-management-suite.md and applications/enterprise-resource-planning-erp.md); no DIRECTORY change made
- fraud-detection-platform (§08, processed) vs fraud-prevention-platform (§15, unprocessed) + account-abuse-protection (§15, unprocessed): PROBABLE OVERLAP/SCOPE FLAG — the directory carries a same-named fraud family in both the finance domain (§08) and the cybersecurity domain (§15); sampled fraud products (Sift especially) straddle both framings (account takeover, fake accounts, promo abuse sit next to payment fraud in the same product); this pass documented the §08 leaf as transaction/activity fraud operations (decision loop + review + chargeback feedback); the §15 leaf's exact scope (abuse/attack prevention posture vs the same decision loop) needs joint review when fraud-prevention-platform is processed; discriminating test proposed: money-loss decision loop on customer activity records (fraud detection) vs attack/abuse prevention posture on identity/session surfaces (fraud prevention §15)
- fraud-detection-platform (§08, processed) vs aml-platform + transaction-monitoring-platform (§08 siblings, unprocessed): JOINT-REVIEW FLAG — machinery shape is nearly identical (records → rules/scenarios → alerts → cases → dispositions) and vendors increasingly ship fraud+AML unified (SEON shared case management, SAS financial-crime family, Sardine positioning); honest distinction is objective and outputs (regulatory compliance artifacts: SARs/sanctions-PEP screening vs loss-preventing decisions with chargeback feedback), not structure; both siblings should be processed with this flag in mind; no taxonomy change proposed from this side
- car-sharing-platform (§18, processed) vs vehicle-rental-platform (§18 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the mobility family — rental centers on staffed-counter handover, per-day pricing, multi-day durations, vehicle-class booking; car sharing centers on self-service (operator fleet) or platform-mediated peer handover, short time-metered turns, specific vehicles circulating among many users, membership/eligibility gate; the P2P segment straddles the vocabulary (Turo/Getaround trips are often multi-day; Getaround's own logo alt text reads "Peer-to-peer car rental" while its about-text claims "largest car-sharing service in Europe") — structural tests recorded in research/car-sharing-platform.md §Boundary Findings (fleet circulation, access mode, pricing granularity); flagged for joint review when vehicle-rental-platform is processed; secondary note: micromobility-sharing-platform shares the free-floating loop (find-unlock-drive-release, per-minute billing) — seam is vehicle class + driver-licensing gate, both leaves stand

- recommerce-platform (§05.19, processed) vs resale-marketplace (§05.19 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the Resale family — the recommerce platform is brand-side program infrastructure (brand-operated supply: trade-in/take-back, brand-scoped curated P2P with listing approval, returns-to-resale, excess; selling under the brand's identity; value returned as credit/cash/margin) while the resale marketplace is expected to be an open multi-seller consumer venue (any seller self-lists to any buyer; platform is a neutral venue); structural test recorded: remove the brand-operator relationship and open listing to any seller → marketplace; terminology collision noted: "recommerce platform" is loosely applied to consumer marketplaces in industry usage, but all four sampled B2B vendors (Trove/Treet/Archive/ThredUp RaaS) use recommerce/branded-resale for the brand-side infrastructure; marketplace-side evidence (Vinted/Depop/Poshmark class) not fetched in this pass — flagged for joint review when resale-marketplace is processed (research/recommerce-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- recommerce-platform (§05.19, processed) vs consignment-management-platform (§05.19 sibling, unprocessed): both run a consign-in → sell → settle loop, but the operators and surfaces differ — consignment management is expected to be store-operator software (consignor accounts, intake, store POS, settlements for consignment shops) while the recommerce platform is brand-program infrastructure with a national e-commerce surface and reverse logistics; overlap risk is real (both center the item-level consignment relationship and seller settlement); flagged for joint review when consignment-management-platform is processed — candidate outcomes are two Types (store-operator vs brand-program) or a consolidation view; note the artwork-consignment-management (§27) module-delivery flag as prior art on consignment-centered leaves (research/recommerce-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- cloud-cost-management-finops (§14, processed) vs ai-cost-finops-platform (§13 sibling, processed): JOINT REVIEW DISCHARGED — confirmed from the cloud side that the machinery (allocation / budgets / anomaly detection / showback / unit economics / recommendations) is identical across both Types and the difference is the metered object: infrastructure consumption (compute/storage/network) vs AI consumption (models/tokens/AI providers); direct gradient evidence: Vantage and CloudZero ingest AI providers (OpenAI/Anthropic/Cursor) through the same connection + allocation machinery as cloud providers — AI cost is absorbed as additional data sources, not a separate subsystem; the AI leaf's directional test holds both ways (remove AI-specific consumption/pricing → generic cloud FinOps remains; remove infrastructure cost → AI cost platform remains); conclusion: probable scope-variant relationship, both leaves stand — the AI leaf is justified by AI-specific data paths (request-side telemetry, token-level pricing volatility) that cloud FinOps platforms treat as just another source (research/cloud-cost-management-finops.md §Boundary Findings; research/ai-cost-finops-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- carbon-accounting-platform (§21, processed) vs greenhouse-gas-accounting (§21 sibling, unprocessed): PROBABLE NEAR-ALIAS — "GHG accounting" names the methodology; "Carbon Accounting Platform" names the software that performs it; sampled products use both terms interchangeably (Watershed's own page is titled "carbon accounting", Envizi's engine is "built on the GHG Protocol", Microsoft's docs speak of "GHG emissions" accounting); recommend joint review when greenhouse-gas-accounting is processed — candidate outcomes are merge, or an explicit methodology-vs-software-realization split; secondary seams held in this pass vs ESG/Sustainability Management Platform and ESG Reporting Platform (center-of-gravity test: emissions inventory as system of record vs broader ESG metrics or disclosure-output-first), Emissions Monitoring/CEMS (computed from activity data × factors vs physical instrument measurement at sources), Energy & Carbon Management (organization-wide incl. value chain vs energy-consumption-first), Product Carbon Footprint Platform / LCA (organization vs product as unit of account), Decarbonization Planning Platform (measured inventory vs forward-looking abatement), Carbon Credit Management (emissions inventory vs credit instruments) (research/carbon-accounting-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- civic-engagement-platform (§24, processed) vs petition-public-comment-platform / 311-citizen-service-request-platform / rulemaking-public-consultation-platform (§24 siblings, unprocessed): seams recorded from the engagement side — petition: signature-campaign object vs composed engagement space (Decidim's Initiatives space is petition-shaped inside an engagement platform — evidence petitioning can be a component rather than the Type); 311: operational case lifecycle vs decision-oriented input (Granicus ships service-request management as a separate product family from EngagementHQ — vendor-side seam confirmation); rulemaking: statutory docket comment vs project-based advisory engagement; all three flagged for joint review when the siblings are processed (research/civic-engagement-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- coaching-commerce-platform (§27, processed) vs creator-course-commerce-platform / creator-storefront / digital-product-commerce-platform / paid-community-platform / fan-membership-platform / creator-subscription-platform (§27 siblings, unprocessed): cluster seam test = what a purchase converts into — coaching commerce converts a purchase into a tracked human-service engagement (session credits/program/subscription period tracked to delivery), course commerce into self-serve content access, storefronts into goods/downloads, community/membership into access to a venue or stream; the seam is fulfillment structure, not feature presence (coaching platforms ship courses/downloads; course platforms add coaching product types — Kajabi-class evidence unfetchable this pass), so recommend applying the fulfillment-structure test when the siblings are processed; secondary note: the leaf sits in the creator-economy cluster but the researched market category ("coaching software / coaching management platform") is dominated by professional coaches (executive/life/health) with creator-coaches as one customer posture — the commerce-first↔delivery-first emphasis spectrum (coaching practice management) has no separate directory leaf and is covered by this single leaf (research/coaching-commerce-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- applicant-tracking-system-ats (§09, processed) vs recruiting-management-platform (§09, processed this pass): JOINT REVIEW DISCHARGED — confirmed alias/umbrella relationship, not two Types: every product sampled across both passes carries both names for itself (Lever page title "Modern Recruiting Software & ATS" with FAQ defining it as "an ATS and recruiting CRM"; Pinpoint title "Leading Global Applicant Tracking System" structuring the same product as a five-pillar platform; Manatal lists "Applicant Tracking System" as one feature row of its "AI Recruitment Software"; Zoho Recruit FAQ explains the product "comes with both an ATS and a recruitment CRM"; SmartRecruiters presents "Applicant Tracking" as one page inside its SmartOS platform while publishing an "Applicant Tracking System RFP Template"; G2 lists the same product under both "Applicant Tracking Systems" and "Recruitment Platforms" categories); reading: "ATS" names the candidate-tracking core (shared four-property defining core: employer-side operation, position as demand-side object, candidate records with per-position applications, tracked selection workflow toward recorded outcomes), "recruiting management platform" the same core plus bundled sourcing/scheduling/analytics/onboarding; recommendation: keep both leaves (both are live market names; the directory's capability leaves hang off the platform framing), cross-reference as alias/umbrella, do not treat as two Types (research/recruiting-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- fund-administration-platform (§08, processed) vs investment-fund-accounting / transfer-agency-platform (§08 siblings, unprocessed): umbrella-vs-slice — market evidence (FundCount, Allvue, Juniper Square, Carta, Alter Domus) shows fund administration bundling the fund-accounting leg (books/NAV/valuations) + the register leg (investor capital accounts/dealing) + investor services (statements/notices/portal); Allvue brands its module "Fund Accounting" and sells it to fund administrators, confirming the accounting slice is contained within administration; working seams: remove investor register + investor services from fund administration → investment fund accounting; remove the fund's portfolio books → transfer-agency-shaped register machinery; recommend joint review when both siblings are processed — candidate outcomes are keep-all-three (umbrella + accounting slice + open-ended register slice, each also existing standalone) or consolidation; secondary note: nonprofit-fund-accounting (§25) is a terminology false friend only (restricted-fund ledgers, no pooled investor capital/NAV) (research/fund-administration-platform.md §Boundary Findings)


- collision-repair-management vs auto-repair-shop-management (§29 siblings): joint-review flag from the auto-repair pass DISCHARGED — separate Types confirmed, NOT aliases or a trade-variant pair; structural evidence: (a) intake artifact — the job is defined by an accident-damage estimate imported from specialized estimating systems in all 4 sampled collision products (Mitchell Cloud Repair "import estimates from all major platforms as opportunities", RepairCenter "Estimate Conversion Compatibility with All Major Estimating Systems", AutoFocus "Import from estimating systems with correct data translation", Nexsyis "created... by importing an estimate") vs internally-created service requests/DVI inspections in the mechanical sample; (b) paying-party structure — persistent customer-vs-insurer split with insurer AR and payment certification ("track customer and insurer payment amounts... certify amounts paid and dates received") vs customer/warranty-pay; (c) shop model — department/stage production with vehicle-location tracking (body/paint/frame) vs bay/technician-based; (d) supplement re-authorization loop and paint-&-materials/sublet/towing cost categories are collision-first-class; existence proof of separate markets: same parents ship separate product lines (Enlyte: Mitchell collision vs Mitchell1 mechanical; Solera: Audatex/Qapter vs Identifix Direct-Hit); shared abstraction = generic repair-order business pattern (customer → vehicle → RO → labor/parts → invoice → accounting) — analogous to the appliance/auto split; also recorded: collision repair's estimating-system dependency is a coupling seam (management imports, estimating authors; CCC ONE bundles both — posture not merger) (research/collision-repair-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- carbon-trading-platform (§21, processed) vs energy-trading-platform (§19 sibling, unprocessed): OVERLAP SEAM FOR JOINT REVIEW — sampled carbon venues sit inside multi-commodity platform families that also span energy/power instruments (Xpansiv: carbon alongside renewables/power/fuels/water; ICE: EUA futures on a general derivatives exchange), while this leaf defines the venue organized around carbon/environmental instruments; seam held this pass via the instrument-scope test (remove energy commodities → the carbon venue stands; remove carbon → the energy exchange continues); recommend joint review when energy-trading-platform is processed, including whether government-run allowance allocation auctions and cash-settled carbon derivatives belong to either leaf (plausible market forms, not directly observed this pass — no claims made); secondary note: sample limitation — two planned carbon-venue samples (Climate Impact X, Carbon Trade Exchange) unreachable ×2 each, so a marketplace-form "carbon trading platform", if one exists, may be under-sampled; the L0 deliberately does not assume exchange-form mechanics to cover this; boundary with Carbon Credit Management held cleanly and consistently with that leaf's recorded seam (research/carbon-trading-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- call-center-platform (§07, processed) vs contact-center-platform (§07 sibling, unprocessed): JOINT-REVIEW FLAG — both Types share the entire call→queue→ACD→agent machinery; the only structural seam found is media scope (Genesys's own glossary defines "call center" as voice-only inbound/outbound/limited self-service and "contact center" as "a modern call center" across channels), but all four sampled vendors position omnichannel suites with voice at the core, so a standalone voice-only platform product may no longer meaningfully exist; candidate outcomes: keep-both-Types with the strip-the-voice-machinery test as the recorded seam (a contact center can lose voice and survive on email+chat; a call center cannot), or treat call-center-platform as the voice-scope variant/alias of contact-center-platform; recommend joint review when contact-center-platform is processed (research/call-center-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- call-center-platform (§07, processed) vs cloud-contact-center-ccaas (§07 sibling, unprocessed): PROBABLE DELIVERY-FORM VARIANT, not a separate structure — CCaaS names the cloud consumption model of the same machinery (Genesys glossary: "cloud-based customer experience solution that allows companies to utilize a contact center provider's software"); recommend joint review when cloud-contact-center-ccaas is processed deciding whether it merges into contact-center-platform as the cloud-posture leaf or stands alone; the call-center side of the flag is discharged (a call center is not defined by delivery form) (research/call-center-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- call-center-platform (§07, processed) — family seam notes for unprocessed siblings (no action until those leaves are processed): IVR Platform = intake/automation component, standalone Type stands; Contact Center Routing Platform = routing component layer; Workforce Management for Contact Centers / Agent Scheduling / Contact Center Quality Management = separable operational modules (existence proof: Genesys Cloud EX ships workforce engagement with no interaction handling); Sales Dialer = individual-rep outbound inside sales workflow vs team-scale campaign machinery + compliance; Government Contact Center (§24) = domain variant of this Type, candidate alias note at that leaf's pass (research/call-center-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- cloud-management-platform (§14, processed) — pole-drift flags for unprocessed/adjacent siblings, no DIRECTORY change proposed: the CMP market splits by philosophy and its poles drift toward neighboring Types — cost-led products marketed as CMP (CloudHealth/Cloudability class; not directly fetched this pass, argued structurally via a sampled vendor's own CMP-vs-Cost-product split) belong with cloud-cost-management-finops (§14, processed — seam held from this side: spend data vs estate lifecycle); IaC-operations products (Scalr/Terraform Cloud class, Tier-1 evidence) are IaC platforms, not CMPs — the discriminating test recorded is the managed object (code/state/runs vs estate inventory+lifecycle), recommend applying it when infrastructure-as-code-platform (§14) is processed; also recorded: naming collision — "cloud management platform" historically also names a cloud platform's own control plane (OpenStack Horizon, Apache CloudStack management server), treated as a terminology false friend, not a Type overlap (research/cloud-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- content-distribution-platform (§27, processed) — name-ambiguity note, no joint review required: "content distribution" is used in two unrelated industries — the media supply-chain Type documented here (provider→destination content delivery; sampled market usage: Amagi/Wurl/Frequency/Vubiquity) and the marketing-world sense of distributing marketing content/native ads (§06 territory: content syndication networks, press-release-distribution-platform); the directory's §27 placement between MAM and Media Rights Management confirms the media reading; flag for awareness when §06 marketing-distribution leaves are processed — same words, different object worlds, no overlap
