- general-ledger-system (§08, processed) discharges the accounting-software joint-review flag from the GL side: confirmed related Types sharing one ledger engine, not duplicates — accounting software = engine + SMB money-capture surfaces (invoicing/AR, bills/AP, bank feeds, sales-tax UX) + owner/bookkeeper UX; GL System = engine + institutional ledger governance (entity/ledger config, calendar/period control, subledger posting machinery, dimensional CoA, consolidation, close) sold mid/enterprise as suite core or standalone financial system; the accounting-software note's "ERP module" framing refined — standalone packaging (SunSystems-class ledger-first systems) is native to the Type; secondary flag: nonprofit-fund-accounting (§25, unprocessed) is a probable GL variant (funds as balancing dimensions + encumbrance; encumbrance evidenced as in-GL machinery in Dynamics docs) — joint review recommended when that leaf is processed (research/general-ledger-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- candidate-assessment-platform (§09, processed) updates the psychometric-assessment-platform joint-review flag from the candidate side: the recorded seam holds and is now documented from both directions — psychometric centers vendor-owned normed psychological instruments with norm-anchored interpretation (attribute measurement; science-house posture; selection+development reuse; often consultant-delivered — Hogan ships no assessment builder and no candidate ranking at all), while candidate assessment centers the per-role evaluation workflow in the hiring funnel (configure → deliver → score → compare → advance); market straddling confirmed deliberate (TestGorilla/Criteria/Harver all include psychometric families; SHL/Mettl sell skills families per the sibling pass) — the three-leaves-vs-spectrum question (candidate / technical / psychometric) remains open for joint review; technical-assessment-platform side still open for that leaf's own pass (coding-environment center vs role-agnostic evaluation loop) (research/candidate-assessment-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- carrier-management (§19, processed) — leaf-name ambiguity + heavy sibling overlap: (1) second-referent risk — "carrier management" could in principle be read as carrier-to-carrier wholesale/interconnect partner management (interconnect agreements, routing, settlement), but sampled market evidence (Tangoe, Calero, Sakon, vCom) uniformly supports the enterprise buy-side reading (carriers as vendors of the buying organization), matching the neighboring enterprise-side leaves Telecom Inventory Management / Telecom Expense Management; wholesale/interconnect partner management has no directory leaf — flag for taxonomy review if that practice should ever be documented; (2) analytic-split note — market products bundle this Type with telecom expense machinery and the telecom inventory record as one lifecycle/platform (Tangoe's own documented lifecycle Order→Inventory→Invoice→Expense→Audit→Pay spans three directory leaves); recommend joint review when telecom-expense-management and telecom-inventory-management (§19 siblings, unprocessed) are processed — candidate outcome is keep-all-three with the recorded seam (carrier-contract-order-enforcement core vs invoice/expense/payment machinery vs estate record) and cross-references; (3) homonym note — logistics "carrier management" (motor/parcel carriers, TMS/freight-brokerage world, §18/§05 territory) is a different Type family sharing only the word; no action needed beyond awareness (research/carrier-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- clinical-data-management (§22, processed) vs electronic-data-capture-edc (§22 sibling, unprocessed): joint-review flag — the market's own naming actively entangles the two leaves: Ennov groups its MACRO EDC and DataLabs EDC products under a "Data Management" nav group and frames EDC as a capability inside its "Clinical Data Management Software (CDMS)" offering; OpenClinica's EDC product page headlines "One EDC Platform. No More Switching Between Clinical Data Management Tools" (market context, unfetched: Medidata Rave historically marketed as EDC/CDMS; Veeva names Vault CDMS with EDC inside); working seam proposed from the CDM side: EDC = the capture instrument (form/eCRF design, site-facing data entry, at-entry validation), CDM = the management discipline over the collected data (validation-plan ownership, discrepancy/query resolution, coding, external-data reconciliation, cleaning metrics, database lock, analysis-ready extraction); the CDM core is provable without operating capture (paper-era data management satisfies it; sponsor-side review layers like CluePoints run over external EDC systems), while capture without the management machinery is just capture — recommend joint review when electronic-data-capture-edc is processed; candidate outcomes: keep both leaves with the recorded discipline-vs-instrument seam, or umbrella+slice (research/clinical-data-management.md)

- clinical-data-management (§22, processed) — taxonomy-gap note for review: the market has a distinct sponsor/CRO-side category of risk-based quality management / central statistical monitoring / clinical data review platforms (CluePoints: central monitoring, intelligent medical coding, medical & safety review, intelligent query detection; "regulatory-grade, ICH E6(R3)-aligned" oversight spanning EDC systems, CTMS platforms, and safety databases) with no obvious corresponding leaf in the directory's §22 list; treated here as a variant posture of clinical data management (management-over-external-capture), flagged so taxonomy owners can decide whether a dedicated RBQM leaf is warranted (research/clinical-data-management.md)

- convention-exhibition-management (§26, processed) vs exhibitor-management (§26 sibling, unprocessed): probable parent-child/slice relationship — Cvent sells "Exhibitor Management" as a standalone product (exhibitor logistics/tasks/communications) and Stova ships an Exhibitor Resource Center, while the convention/exhibition leaf's defining core adds the sellable-floor inventory (booth states on a floor plan) and the space-sale machinery that none of the broad suites headline; recommend joint review deciding keep-both-with-containment vs fold; secondary note: seam vs event-management-platform (§26 sibling) is real but documented and held in the leaf itself — broad suites (Cvent/Stova/RainFocus) straddle it and both Types stand (research/convention-exhibition-management.md)


- gift-card-management (§05.15, processed) vs loyalty-program-management + store-credit-stored-value-platform (§05.15 siblings, both unprocessed): shared balance-drawdown machinery over an identified value instrument, different provenance of value — gift card = purchased by a giver under a merchant program, loyalty points = earned through behavior under accrual rules, store credit = owed by the merchant (refunds/goodwill); direct market evidence that the machinery is shared while issuance intent differs: Rise.ai explicitly merges gift cards, store credit, cashback and rewards into one customer wallet, and Square frames refunds-to-gift-card as store credit; loyalty-suite bundling of gift card modules (Paytronix/Givex-class) could not be observed (sites unreachable) and is treated structurally; recommend joint review when both siblings are processed; secondary boundaries recorded in the leaf: promotion codes (price change vs prepaid value), network-branded prepaid cards (card-issuing territory), and third-party rewards/incentive distribution platforms (Tango/Blackhawk-class — distributes other brands' catalog cards, owns no merchant program ledger) are outside the Type (research/gift-card-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- change-order-management (§17, processed) vs engineering-change-management (§16 sibling, unprocessed): same-word overlap flag for joint review — both Types share the proposal→review→approve→implement shape and itemized-impact thinking, but the worlds differ structurally: construction change orders modify a commercial contract's scope/price/time among contracting parties with payment consequences and a counterparty approval gate, while engineering change management modifies design/product data (ECR/ECN against parts/BOMs/revisions) with design-review semantics and no commercial counterparty; seam test = remove the commercial contract/counterparty/money structure (→ ECM territory) or the design-data/BOM structure (→ change order management territory); recommend joint review when engineering-change-management is processed; secondary §17 seams recorded from this side for unprocessed siblings: Construction Cost Management = broader host (change machinery is one lane of cost control), Progress Billing = downstream consumer of approved changes, Construction Claims Management = the disagreement path (agreed vs asserted; directive instruments in between), RFI Management = question-not-change (research/change-order-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- customer-to-business-messaging-application (§01.01, processed) vs business-messaging-application (§01.01, processed): JOINT-REVIEW FLAG CONFIRMED WITH STRONGER EVIDENCE from the C2B side — market evidence continues to show one shared conversation model (identified org participant + two-way thread with an external individual + org-held history) with no market partition along the directory line: every product sampled this pass (Apple Messages for Business, Twilio, LINE, WhatsApp via third-party platform docs) could equally serve as a Business Messaging sample; the distinguishing emphasis is conversational initiative — C2B foregrounds customer-initiated entry through public business-published points (structurally enforced on the strictest sampled channel: proactive messages restricted to the customer's direct interest, and the customer must start a new conversation after one ends), while Business Messaging includes business-initiated exchange as a first-class loop; outbound-initiative policy varies continuously across channels (free push ↔ time-boxed template gating ↔ in-interest-only + customer-controlled re-entry), so it is a spectrum, not a binary that cleanly separates two Types; candidate outcomes: keep both leaves as documented views of one model (initiative-axis seam recorded) or consolidate; recommend taxonomy-owner joint review; secondary boundaries held: vs SMS Marketing (conversation-first vs campaign-first), vs Help Desk/Ticketing (thread vs ticket as central object), vs Customer Support Chat (intent-agnostic vs support-scoped), vs IM (org participant vs personal identity) (research/customer-to-business-messaging-application.md §Boundary Findings)
- candidate-search-platform (§09, processed) vs talent-sourcing-platform (§09 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest remaining seam in the recruiting cluster — the two Types share nearly complete capability lists (every sampled search product attaches outreach: InMail messaging, integrated email campaigns/sequences, built-in reply management; every sourcing tool embeds search), so capability lists cannot separate them; proposed seam for joint review = center-of-gravity test: a product whose workflows/data model/analytics are organized around searches and their results (saved searches, corpus choice, result-quality calibration, search open/hold/closed lifecycle) is the search Type; one organized around engagement workflows over identified people (sequences, deliverability, reply-rate operations) is the sourcing Type; Fetcher is the instructive middle case (marketed as managed sourcing, operationally search-organized — its unit of work is the Search/Position); recommend joint review when talent-sourcing-platform is processed (research/candidate-search-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- candidate-search-platform (§09, processed) — joint review with candidate-profile-platform (processed 2026-09-07) RESOLVED: the managed-object seam proposed by the sibling pass is confirmed and sharpened — test = can the product fulfill its purpose without the customer curating a persistent one-record-per-person layer; corpus-lens products (network-native recruiter search with platform-owned corpus, aggregated-index people-search engines, managed batch sourcers, job-board resume search) are the search Type; record-layer products (Gem/Beamery/Eightfold) are the profile Type with search as a capability; SeekOut's straddle is a packaging posture (search-first suite with an attached lightweight record layer), not evidence of a merged Type; taxonomy note: "Candidate Search Platform" is a descriptive construction, not a market category (the market says sourcing tool / talent search / people search / AI sourcing / outbound recruiting, or sells the referent as "Recruiter" / "Smart Sourcing"); the Type is real where the search engine is the product's center of gravity (research/candidate-search-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- cloud-workload-protection-cwpp (§15, processed) vs CNAPP (§15 sibling, unprocessed): market packaging has folded CWPP into CNAPP suites (CSPM+CWPP+CIEM/DSPM pillars over one inventory), but the runtime-defense pillar remains structurally distinct — and one sampled vendor still self-describes its self-hosted product as a CWPP in 2026 documentation; recommend joint review when the CNAPP leaf is processed (research/cloud-workload-protection-cwpp.md §Boundary Findings)
- cloud-workload-protection-cwpp (§15, processed) vs container-kubernetes-security (§15 sibling, unprocessed): overlap flag — container runtime defense, image/registry scanning, and admission control all sit inside the sampled CWPPs' scope; working seam = estate breadth (host/VM estate plus container children, cross-platform) vs container/K8s-native depth; candidate outcomes: separate Types with the estate-scope seam, or object-domain variant; recommend joint review (research/cloud-workload-protection-cwpp.md §Boundary Findings)
- cloud-workload-protection-cwpp (§15, processed) vs endpoint-detection-response-edr (§15 sibling, unprocessed): convergence flag — one sampled product reuses its EDR agent machinery for servers and several EDR vendors sell workload protection from the same lineage; the Type boundary rests on object domain + operational workflow (user endpoints vs the server/container estate), not on agent technology; record so the EDR pass does not absorb CWPP on mechanism grounds (research/cloud-workload-protection-cwpp.md §Boundary Findings)

- corporate-wellness-platform (§28, processed) vs employee-wellbeing-platform (§09, processed): PROBABLE ALIAS/UMBRELLA — joint-review flag — both passes converge on the same defining core (sponsored program + enrolled eligible population + wellbeing offerings + per-participant participation records + operator-side aggregate reporting with the personal-data split); the §09 pass sampled Wellable (a classic corporate wellness platform) and anchors its historical check on "2000s-era corporate wellness portals"; this pass's products self-label employee wellness platform / corporate wellness platform / corporate wellness software interchangeably; the §28 activity/incentive pole and the §09 care-led pole are connected by products spanning both (Wellable, Personify Health); recommend joint review — candidate outcomes: alias consolidation into one Type, or keep-both with a recorded emphasis seam (wellbeing = whole-person incl. care-led delivery; wellness = activity/challenge/incentive program delivery) with the explicit note that products straddle the seam (research/corporate-wellness-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- payroll-system vs global-payroll-platform joint review COMPLETED (2026-09-07, research/global-payroll-platform.md §Boundary Findings): the global-payroll pass resolves the scope-gradient flag from the global side — both Types confirmed as adjacent-Types-sharing-a-core, keep both; the distinguishing object of management: a Payroll System's primary object is the pay run under one (or few) jurisdiction(s) with deep locally owned statutory machinery, while a Global Payroll Platform's primary managed object is the multi-country payroll portfolio — country payrolls as coordinated units plus the consolidation/orchestration layer (standardized process, one approval workflow, standardized/validated data, unified status, multi-currency funding, consolidated cost/reporting) over them; structural tests hold both ways (remove multi-country scope → Payroll System; remove the consolidation layer → a set of disconnected local payrolls = the market's "distributed" pre-platform pattern the Type exists to replace; make the vendor the legal employer → EOR); vendor-confirmed product separations reconfirmed (Rippling Payroll vs Global Payroll product lines; Papaya/Remote/CloudPay entity-based payroll distinct from their EOR offerings; Remote's entity-requirement FAQ routes entity-less employers to EOR); secondary seams recorded: vs EOR (sharpest boundary — legal-employer identity), vs global payments infrastructure (computed compliance-bound workforce obligations vs merchant rails), vs contractor management (adjacent worker type), vs HRIS (record master)
- data-explorer (§02.12, processed) — name-collision note, no joint review required: the product name "Data Explorer" is also used by enterprise-facing surfaces in §13 territory (BI tools' "explore" modes, database consoles/storage browsers, ad-hoc query UIs); documented the published-data consumer-facing sense per the directory's §02 Content & Knowledge placement (sibling leaf: Public Data Portal); §13 leaves whose products ship surfaces literally named "data explorer" should note the collision at their own passes; seam vs Public Data Portal held from this side: portal = catalog of dataset files (find→download with license/metadata), explorer = observations query-able and rendered in-app (remove live view composition/rendering → it becomes a portal) (research/data-explorer.md §Boundary Findings)
- clinical-trial-management-system-ctms (§22, processed) vs clinical-trial-site-management (§22 sibling, unprocessed): site-operated products self-label "CTMS" (RealTime-CTMS, Advarra Clinical Conductor, OnCore are all marketed as CTMS while serving sites/networks/institutions), so the two directory labels overlap on the real market; this pass documented one Type with sponsor/CRO-centric vs site/institution-centric operational poles sharing the study×site×participant skeleton; recommend joint review when the sibling leaf is processed — either confirm the pole-variant framing or split by operator object (trial-operational system vs site-business management) (research/clinical-trial-management-system-ctms.md §Boundary Findings)
- cmdb (§14, processed) vs IT Asset Management (§14 sibling, unprocessed) vs Enterprise Asset Registry (§10, unprocessed): heavy market convergence — CMDB products ship asset-financial fields and are marketed inside ITAM umbrellas (Freshservice sells its CMDB under IT Asset Management; Device42 packages DCIM+CMDB+ITAM as one platform), so the CMDB/ITAM seam is structural (CI + relationships + impact model vs asset + financial lifecycle) rather than commercial; recommend joint review when IT Asset Management is processed — consider recording the remove-relationships test (→ asset register) as the canonical seam, and treat the Enterprise Asset Registry leaf as the physical-estate analogue of the same inventory+relationships pattern; also note Configuration Management (§14) is the practice/discipline the CMDB is the system of record for, not a duplicate of it (research/cmdb.md §Boundary Findings)
- creator-affiliate-dashboard (§27, processed) vs Affiliate Network / Affiliate Management Platform / Influencer Campaign Management / Influencer Marketing Platform (§06 siblings) + Creator Storefront / Creator Revenue Management / Link-in-Bio Platform (§27 siblings): naming-vs-taxonomy flag — "Creator Affiliate Dashboard" names a surface, and in the market the creator-side affiliate experience is delivered as four product families (merchant-program dashboards, network/platform partner dashboards, creator-first commerce platforms, cross-network analytics layers) rather than one standalone product species; the pass documents the Type as the creator-side affiliate monetization application (enrollment × creator-attributed trackable assets × commission ledger × earnings view) — the creator-side counterpart of the §06 brand-side affiliate leaves; sharpest seams held from this side: brand-side operator vs creator-side account (vs Affiliate Management Platform — same contract terms/tasks/payouts seen from the other end), marketplace infrastructure vs side-experience (vs Affiliate Network), commission ledger vs storefront/commerce objects (vs Creator Storefront) and vs own-product revenue objects (vs Creator Revenue Management), program enrollment + ledger vs bare link aggregation (vs Link-in-Bio); recommend joint review when the §06 affiliate leaves are processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with an explicit side-of-marketplace seam, or re-parent this leaf into the affiliate domain as the affiliate-side experience (research/creator-affiliate-dashboard.md §Boundary Findings)
- remote-customer-support-platform (§07, processed) — leaf-name ambiguity note, no joint review required: "remote customer support" could be misread as "support delivered remotely" (remote-agent contact center), but that reading is already owned by the neighboring Contact Center / CCaaS / Omnichannel / Customer Support Chat leaves; this pass documented the distinct remote-support-software category (live agent session into a customer device: TeamViewer/Zoho Assist/Splashtop/BeyondTrust RS pole); the seam vs Customer Support Chat and vs RMM is documented in applications/remote-customer-support-platform.md §Related Application Types and should be re-checked when those siblings are processed

- card-issuing-platform vs card-management-system / card-processing-platform (siblings under §08): the three card leaves overlap on the same modern vendors — sampled issuing platforms all manage card records (status/PIN/limits) and run issuer-side authorization processing themselves, so program governance vs rail processing vs record administration is not crisply separated in the market; working distinctions recorded: Card Issuing = program/card governance + funding binding + spend-control decisioning + transaction lifecycle; Card Processing = transaction-rail machinery (switching/interchange/clearing-settlement as infrastructure); Card Management = issuer-side card record administration (traditional bank shape, unsampled — docs gated); this also partially resolves the payment-processing-platform leaf's recorded open flag ("card-processing boundary untested, no issuer-side product sampled"): modern issuer-side products fuse issuing+processing, so the same-products overlap pattern repeats; removal tests in research notes — flagged for joint review when both siblings are processed (research/card-issuing-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- cnapp (§15, processed) platform-composition flag: CNAPP's defining core is the unification of sibling pillar types (CSPM/CWPP + vulnerability/identity-entitlement domains) over one shared estate inventory — it contains no security behavior that is not one of those pillars' behaviors; kept as a distinct platform-level Type (the market treats it as an externally-validated category with a distinct buying/operating model — platform vs point tools) rather than merged into cloud-security-posture-management-cspm; structural tests recorded: one shared inventory + one risk picture = CNAPP; separate consoles/inventories = portfolio; remove a domain = that domain's tool; note that many "CSPM" product pages now describe CNAPP platforms (pillars sold as plans/modules of one product) — joint awareness recommended whenever CSPM/CWPP-family leaves are re-reviewed (research/cnapp.md §Boundary Findings)

- renewal-management-platform (§07, processed) vs customer-success-platform (§07 sibling, unprocessed): module-convergence flag for joint review — all three sampled implementations (Gainsight Renewal Center add-on, Totango Renewals SuccessBLOC, ChurnZero Renewal and Forecast Hub) ship renewal management INSIDE CS platforms, yet each carries renewal-specific objects (decision/due vs close dates, up-for-renewal vs final recurring amounts, outcome taxonomy + churn reasons, retention metrics, renewal forecast categories) behind separately-licensed/permission-gated surfaces, and a dedicated renewal-manager role exists as a job function — working seam: CS platform centers the ongoing managed relationship (health/adoption/success plans at any lifecycle point), renewal management centers the renewal decision event and the forward renewal book; candidate outcomes: keep-both with the renewal-decision-record test, or absorb as CS-platform module if joint review finds no standalone pole holds (no standalone pure-play renewal product was directly documented — sample limitation recorded in research notes); secondary seams held vs subscription-billing-platform (billing executes charging/auto-renewal/dunning with no decision object — Stripe lifecycle documented as boundary pole), vs CRM opportunity management (renewal-specific structure: up-for-renewal-vs-final amounts, early/on-time/late decision timing, retention metrics), vs contract-lifecycle-management (revenue motion vs contract-document system of record) (research/renewal-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- governance-risk-compliance-platform (§11, processed) joint-review discharges & new flags: enterprise-risk-management's recorded flag DISCHARGED — GRC confirmed as the umbrella Type (shared interlocking risk×control×requirement core + evaluation-and-issue loop + consolidated oversight reporting) with ERM as its register-centric child application, delivered as a module/solution inside all five sampled platforms (Archer, LogicGate, Optro, Diligent, LogicManager); new joint-review flags for unprocessed §11 siblings: compliance-management-platform (obligations-program-centered child vs umbrella — candidate outcomes keep-both or documented containment), third-party-risk-management and business-continuity-management-platform (same child-module pattern, all five sampled platforms ship them as modules); naming note: "Integrated Risk Management" (IRM) is a market naming era of this Type (ServiceNow/Archer rebrand), not a separate one; market-context note: OneTrust no longer exposes a standalone GRC product URL (folded into Tech Risk & Compliance / privacy-AI-trust umbrella) (research/governance-risk-compliance-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- card-processing-platform (§08, processed) — JOINT-REVIEW FLAGS DISCHARGED/UPDATED for the card cluster: (1) payment-processing-platform's open flag RESOLVED — issuer-side card processing confirmed as the opposite network side (the issuer's processing point: cardholder accounts, issuer authorizations, settlement as the scheme's issuer-side counterparty; issuer-side products document presentments arriving TO the issuer side and the ISSUER transferring settlement amounts), boundary holds; (2) card-issuing-platform's working split CONFIRMED AND SHARPENED with direct Tier-1 evidence — issuing centers the programme side (cards/cardholders/funding binding/spend controls), processing centers the rail (scheme connectivity/authorization switching/balance ledger/clearing-settlement/interchange/STIP/reconciliation); market fusion reconfirmed (Thredd "end-to-end card issuing and processing", Paymentology "issuing & processing platform", plus the issuing pass's Stripe/Adyen/Marqeta/Lithic evidence) — the two leaves overlap on the same product families and differ in emphasis (same-products overlap pattern as payment-gateway vs payment-processing-platform); removal tests recorded: strip rail machinery → issuing emphasis, strip programme/card governance → pure rail processing; (3) card-management-system flag RETAINED — card management appears as a component of processing at both deeply sampled products ("full card management toolset" provided alongside connectivity), supporting the reading of Card Management System as record administration without rail participation (traditional bank shape, still unsampled — docs gated); recommend joint review of all three card leaves (research/card-processing-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- clinical-trial-site-management (§22, processed this pass) vs clinical-trial-management-system-ctms (§22, processed): joint-review flag raised by the CTMS pass now evidence-backed but not edit-resolved — the site-side sample (RealTime-CTMS, Advarra Clinical Conductor, Advarra OnCore, CRIO "Site CTMS") all self-label CTMS while sharing the study×participant×visit×money skeleton with the trial-operational frame; the stable distinction is the operator object/seat: CTMS = trial-operational system of record (study as subject, sites as resources, plan-vs-actual protocol execution), site management = site-business system (site organization as subject, sponsor-originated study portfolio as demand, per-study operation + site-side money record; removal tests in research notes — strip site-subject → CTMS, strip sponsor-originated portfolio → clinic scheduling, strip participant/visit records → CRM, strip money record → site enablement like the Florence boundary pole); this pass documented the leaf from the site-business seat and did NOT edit the CTMS document, whose site/institution-centric pole still covers the same products; recommendation: either (a) confirm the seat-split and revise the CTMS document's site pole to defer to applications/clinical-trial-site-management.md, or (b) treat clinical-trial-site-management as the alias/umbrella label of the CTMS site pole and merge the documents; secondary note: the sponsor/CRO-side reading of "site management" (feasibility/selection/activation modules inside sponsor CTMS & start-up tools) was rejected as this leaf's referent (tool-level capability cluster, not a management product) — if directory intent was that reading instead, revisit referent choice (research/clinical-trial-site-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- resale-marketplace (§05.19, processed) — joint-review flag from the recommerce-platform pass RESOLVED with marketplace-side evidence (the side that pass could not fetch): Grailed/Reverb/OfferUp onboarding is generic member onboarding with no brand affiliation, sellers retain possession and self-list, and the platform's trust machinery governs arbitrary buyer-seller pairs (the offsite-transaction prohibition directly documents the mediated transaction as the product's center), confirming the recorded structural test — remove the brand-operator relationship and open listing to any seller → resale marketplace; both leaves stand. Secondary seams held from this side: vs classifieds-platform (§05.03 sibling, unprocessed) — the seam is the mediated transaction (in-platform order + payment + dispute machinery vs contact-and-arrange-yourself), directly evidenced by Grailed's offsite-activity warning and OfferUp/Grailed in-platform payments; the classifieds side rests on structural inference (Craigslist unreachable), recheck when the sibling is processed; vs online-marketplace / multi-vendor-marketplace (§05.02 siblings, unprocessed) — supply-identity seam (pre-owned one-off owner-listed items vs merchant new-goods catalogs), horizontal marketplaces blur at the edges (eBay sells new at scale), joint awareness recommended; vs consignment-management-platform (§05.19 sibling, unprocessed) — custody seam (seller retains possession and self-lists vs operator intake/pricing/sale); vs online-auction-platform (§05.18 sibling, unprocessed) — bidding is a pricing-mode variant here (eBay heritage), with the auction Type reserved for price-discovery-centered products; vs ticket-resale-marketplace (§26 sibling, unprocessed) — same name, different object world (dated seat-bound entitlements with transfer mechanics); sample limitation recorded: consumer-C2C class (Vinted/Depop/Mercari/Poshmark) unfetched and eBay deep articles bot-blocked, so US/EU-weighted evidence (research/resale-marketplace.md §Boundary Findings)

- headless-commerce-platform (§05.01, processed) vs e-commerce-platform (§05.01 sibling, unprocessed) + online-store-builder (§05.01 sibling, unprocessed): posture-spectrum flag for joint review — sampled evidence shows the headless/monolithic distinction is a primary-posture continuum rather than a hard product-class division: dominant storefront-first platforms (Shopify, BigCommerce) now ship first-class headless surfaces (storefront APIs + official headless frameworks) alongside their coupled storefronts, while pure-play headless vendors (commercetools) ship optional storefront tooling (launchpads/storefront studio) and open-source engines (Medusa) ship only starter templates; working seam = center-of-gravity test (is the coupled storefront the product's center, or a disposable convenience while engine+API is the product?) plus the by-design test (can the product run commerce with no platform-shipped storefront at all?); removal tests recorded: require platform-owned presentation → monolith territory; strip transactional commerce → headless CMS territory; recommend joint review when e-commerce-platform and online-store-builder are processed (research/headless-commerce-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- application-modernization-platform (§12, processed) vs code-migration-platform (§12 sibling) — JOINT-REVIEW FLAG RESOLVED with both leaves now processed: the program-wrapper vs conversion-act test CONFIRMED from the migration side — the code migration platform starts from a source→target conversion contract (recipe/codemod/version matrix) and executes the conversion act at whatever scale (single repo→fleet) without estate-level portfolio assessment or per-application route decisions, while the application modernization platform starts from the estate (inventory→assessment→per-application modernization decision→tracked program) of which conversion is one phase; convergence documented on both sides (modernization platforms embed agentic conversion; migration platforms add cross-repo project tracking — Codemod Campaigns documented) but the discriminator "what the product starts from and owns" held; both leaves stand (research/code-migration-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- coaching-commerce-platform (§27, processed) + creator-course-commerce-platform (§27, processed) vs creator-storefront / digital-product-commerce-platform / paid-community-platform / fan-membership-platform / creator-subscription-platform (§27 siblings, unprocessed): the fulfillment-structure seam test recommended by the coaching pass is now confirmed with direct course-side evidence (course platforms model purchase → standing operator-managed access entitlement to curriculum content consumed self-serve via member library/player; subscription cancellation ends access to included products; manual grant/remove; access durations/seats) — recommend applying the same test (what the purchase converts into) when the storefront/community/membership/subscription siblings are processed; note: course platforms ship the siblings' product types alongside courses (downloads/coaching/communities/memberships sold through the same offers and checkout), so feature presence is explicitly NOT the seam — the fulfillment object is; creator-course-commerce-platform stands as an independent Type, no alias/merge recommended (research/creator-course-commerce-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- code-enforcement-management (§24, processed) vs government-inspection-management (§24 sibling, unprocessed) + permit-management + planning-zoning-management (§24 siblings, unprocessed): this pass documents code enforcement as a distinct Type (property-anchored violation case + directed enforcement instrument + compliance loop) whose inspections are a step and whose permits/planning are adjacent suite products on a shared parcel spine — the boundary rests on the object and flow, not on vendor packaging (all sampled vendors ship Code Enforcement as a separate product from Permitting/Inspections/Planning); joint-review note for government-inspection-management: inspections-inside-enforcement must not be absorbed as evidence that generic inspection management owns the notice/citation/compliance track (research/code-enforcement-management.md §Boundary Findings); the 311 and animal-control passes' recorded seams (service-request vs violation case; shared enforcement grammar with different objects) are consistent with and reconfirmed by this pass's evidence

- climate-scenario-analysis (§21, processed) vs climate-risk-management (§21, processed) / physical-climate-risk-platform (§21 sibling, unprocessed): three-way seam confirmed with one amendment — this pass documents climate scenario analysis as the scenario-projection machinery layer (managed scenario set + projection machinery + comparative exploratory posture; analyzed subject is input configuration, not a maintained exposure population), consistent with the CRM pass's recorded seam; product overlap is real and bidirectional (Jupiter/XDI were the CRM pass's strongest engine samples yet carry partial loop features — adaptation ROI, screen→deep-dive — so both passes' seams must be read as center-of-gravity, not mutual exclusion; a single product can legitimately instantiate both Types); physical-climate-risk-platform still unprocessed — when processed, distinguish from CSA by absence of scenario-family/cross-future comparison structure (hazard-loss computation without the scenario set as first-class object); keep-all-three with process-scope seams remains the working outcome, joint review recommended when physical-climate-risk-platform is processed; secondary drifts reconfirmed: current-state-only data providers (Carbon4-class) dissolve into climate data products, disclosure-led suites dissolve into ESG disclosure management, and broad suites (MSCI-class) legitimately ship data + scenario capabilities side by side within one vendor
- help-desk (§07, processed) vs ticketing-system (§07 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest sibling overlap in §07 — both track discrete requests in queues with lifecycles on identical machinery (every sampled help desk IS a ticketing system over its own records); working seam recorded: help desk = requester-serving application (the record exists to deliver help back to the person who asked — requester correspondence and resolution-for-requester semantics are definitional), ticketing system = generic request-tracking machinery usable across operational contexts (facilities/events/IT/engineering) without requester-facing support semantics; removal test recorded (remove requester correspondence and serve internal work-item tracking → ticketing system; keep the requester-serving loop → help desk); recommend joint review when ticketing-system is processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with the requester-serving seam (current framing), or treat ticketing-system as the machinery umbrella with help desk as its support-context instance; secondary notes: internal-IT pole (Jira Service Management sampled) shades toward ITSM, consistent with the ITSM (§14) and employee-service-portal/employee-service-management (§10) passes' recorded splits (research/help-desk.md §Boundary Findings)

- agent-tool-computer-use-platform vs robotic-process-automation-platform (§10) / desktop-automation-application (§03.16) — open flag PARTIALLY DISCHARGED from the desktop-automation side (this pass): mechanism-level boundary confirmed — desktop automation executes human-designed deterministic sequences fixed at authoring time (manual/hotkey/schedule triggers), and the AI features observed in sampled desktop-automation products act only as authoring aids (suggested next actions) or callable processing steps, never as the runtime task decision-maker, so no convergence on the decision mechanism; the RPA half of the flag stays open until robotic-process-automation-platform is processed (research/desktop-automation-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- desktop-automation-application (§03.16, processed) vs robotic-process-automation-platform (§10, unprocessed): same mechanism family (human-designed deterministic automations); discriminator recorded from this side = ownership and scale — desktop automation is owned and operated on the user's own machine for the user's own work, RPA centers centrally managed bot fleets (deployment, unattended machines, queues, governance) as organizational assets; the low-code-designer pole is the bridge product (local designer + local desktop runtime = this Type's core; machine registration/groups, unattended licensing, cloud orchestration, work queues = the RPA layer), and the vendor itself frames desktop flows as broadening its existing RPA — removal test: strip central bot-fleet management → still this Type; make the fleet the product's center → RPA; flagged for joint review when robotic-process-automation-platform is processed (research/desktop-automation-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- desktop-automation-application (§03.16, processed) vs personal-workflow-automation-platform + no-code-personal-automation-application (§03.16 siblings, both unprocessed): surface-level boundary hypothesis recorded from this side — the automation artifact targets the local desktop environment (apps/windows/input/files/OS executed by a local engine) vs orchestrating cloud services/app events from a vendor's cloud; the seam is artifact-surface-level, not vendor-level (one sampled vendor ships desktop flows and cloud flows as two artifact types in one product, bridging both), so sibling passes should use "what does the artifact act on, and where does it execute" as the test; flagged for joint review when both sibling leaves are processed (research/desktop-automation-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- code-quality-platform (§12, processed) vs static-code-analysis-platform (§12 sibling, unprocessed): heavy-overlap flag — market products (SonarQube/Codacy/Qlty-class) self-describe as both "static analysis" and "code quality platform"; the recorded seam is the layer: analyzer = runs checks and reports findings for a run (no persistent state, no standard, no verdict), platform = system of record (recorded runs + persistent issues/metrics/history + configurable standard + pass/fail verdict in the delivery workflow); many products are both (embed engines), so the two leaf definitions must be written at different layers; recommend joint review when static-code-analysis-platform is processed (research/code-quality-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- creator-crm (§27, processed) vs email-marketing-platform + newsletter-marketing-platform (§06, unprocessed): heavy-overlap flag — flagship creator-side products (Kit-class) self-describe as "email marketing platform for creators"; recorded seam = the monetization spine: person records with consent state + purchase history + audience→payer progression attached to persons make a Creator CRM; strip the commerce/monetization layer and creator-audience context → generic email marketing platform; taxonomy note: Creator CRM is a domain instantiation of the CRM family (person-centric vertical CRM, sibling of Nonprofit CRM §25 / Real Estate Brokerage CRM §17 — no account layer, no deal pipeline); recommend joint review when email-marketing-platform is processed (research/creator-crm.md §Boundary Findings)
- resume-builder (§09, processed) vs job-board + professional-social-network (§01.05/§09, both unprocessed): platform-native-builder hybrid flag — job boards and professional networks commonly ship résumé-creation surfaces that generate the application document from the user's existing platform profile (Indeed/LinkedIn-class; unreachable this pass, so structurally reasoned not directly evidenced); the hybrid keeps the résumé-builder core (structured career content + tool-owned rendering + portable artifact) inside a demand-side or network container — when those sibling leaves are processed, apply the artifact test (does the surface produce a portable point-in-time document, or only a living profile?) to decide whether the builder surface is a capability of the platform or evidence of Type straddling (research/resume-builder.md §Boundary Findings)

- cmms-maintenance-management (§16, processed) vs enterprise-asset-management-eam (§16 sibling, unprocessed) + enterprise-asset-registry (§10 sibling, unprocessed): convergent-market gradient flag — sampled CMMS vendors position EAM as the superset (one vendor FAQ: "every EAM contains a CMMS") and CMMS products already ship EAM-leaning capabilities (asset depreciation, lifecycle tracking, TCO, purchasing/POs), so the working seam is center-of-gravity: CMMS = maintenance work management (assets + work orders + history as the defining core; PM scheduling/requests/parts/mobile/cloud deliberately NOT definitional — entry tiers and on-premise/perpetual deployments ship without them), EAM = first-class asset financial/lifecycle governance (procurement/accounting/depreciation/capital-planning/disposal) over the same work-management core; removal tests recorded (strip asset financial lifecycle → CMMS; strip work orders → asset registry); recommend joint review when enterprise-asset-management-eam is processed; secondary seams held: reliability-management consumes CMMS data for strategy (predictive triggers inside a CMMS are an extension, not the discipline), facility-management/IWMS centers buildings-space-leases with CMMS-like maintenance modules, property-maintenance centers tenancy, fleet-management and aircraft-maintenance are domain cousins with their own spines, tool-management/calibration-management are narrow siblings commonly riding inside a CMMS (research/cmms-maintenance-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- hr-case-management joint pass COMPLETED (2026-09-07, resolving the flags recorded by the employee-relations-case-management, employee-service-management, enterprise-request-management and employee-service-portal passes): three-leaf seam confirmed as two Types + one machinery — HR Case Management = HR's case desk (workforce-raised work → typed case bound to the employee → HR handler → managed lifecycle to recorded resolution under confidentiality discipline), Employee Relations Case Management = the investigation-grade sensitive-matter specialization (its defining core: confidential case record of a reported people-matter with privilege marking, fairness constraints, defensibility), Employee Service Management = the general cross-department machinery the HR desk instantiates; sensitive-matter handling appears inside HR case products as a case type or sibling module at varying depth (Oracle: "complex employee relations cases" inside case management; Dovetail: separate ER module; JSM: case work category with allegations/findings/outcomes invisible to help seekers) but the investigation regime (privilege marking, guided investigation methodology, anonymous intake, aftercare/retaliation monitoring) stays ER's core; naming blur documented from both sides (HR Acuity markets its ER platform as "HR Case Management"; its own FAQ draws the help-desk-vs-matter seam: "a help desk queue has no privilege flag, no guided investigation workflow"); removal tests hold both ways (strip sensitive-matter machinery → the HR case desk remains; strip transactional machinery → ER case management remains; strip HR case semantics → generic ESM remains); no taxonomy change — both §09 leaves stand with cross-referencing boundary statements (research/hr-case-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- hr-case-management sourcing limitation: ServiceNow HR Service Delivery (the enterprise flagship) unreachable (servicenow.com timeout ×2 this run, consistent with two prior passes; docs.servicenow.com JS-only shell), Zoho People (404 ×2), Neocase (timeout ×2), UKG (404) — enterprise-suite and SMB-suite poles under-sampled; evidence is Tier-2 official product pages (Oracle HR Help Desk, Dovetail home + product page, Freshservice HR) + Tier-1 support docs (Jira Service Management case management); no exact state names, field lists, numeric limits or defaults asserted in the final doc (recorded in Sources of applications/hr-case-management.md)

- code-review-platform (§12, processed) vs source-code-hosting-platform (§12 sibling, unprocessed): co-delivery flag — the dominant modern delivery of code review is embedded in hosting platforms (GitHub PR / GitLab MR; Bitbucket / Azure DevOps by market position), while standalone review-first products (Gerrit, Review Board) keep the Type distinct; recorded seam = the organizing spine (repository storage/browsing/permissions vs the change-review workflow); remove-test: remove the review workflow → hosting platform remains; remove repository hosting → standalone review platform remains (Review Board proves the no-hosting pole; Gerrit straddles by also serving as central repo); recommend the hosting-platform pass treat PR/MR machinery as an embedded instance of this Type and adopt the spine test explicitly (research/code-review-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- desktop-publishing-application (§04.17, processed) vs page-layout-application (§04.17 sibling, unprocessed): ALIAS flag — direct vendor evidence that the two labels name one product category (Quark's own product page titles QuarkXPress "Desktop Publishing Software & Page Layout Software"; the professional market uses "page layout application" as the modern functional term for the same InDesign-class software); no structural difference found in research; recommend joint review when page-layout-application is processed — candidate outcomes: merge as one Type (desktop publishing = historical label, page layout = functional label), or keep-both with explicit alias cross-reference (research/desktop-publishing-application.md §Boundary Findings)
- desktop-publishing-application (§04.17, processed) vs professional-typesetting-application (§04.17 sibling, unprocessed): adjacent-mechanism flag — both produce paginated output but the authoring mechanisms differ (interactive WYSIWYG frame layout vs markup/batch-driven composition); this pass did not research typesetting products, so keep-separate vs variant is unresolved; recommend the typesetting pass apply the mechanism test (interactive frame manipulation vs markup-driven batch composition) and decide the Type boundary there (research/desktop-publishing-application.md §Boundary Findings)
- hr-compliance-management (§09, processed) umbrella-shape note: one Type confirmed across four product poles (intelligence platform / postings-requirements specialist / training-led compliance LMS / catalog-content-licensing vendor) — all satisfy the same employer-side loop (applicability-matched obligation knowledge → fulfillment → retained evidence); joint-review flags for unprocessed neighbors: vs compliance-management-platform (§11) and regulatory-change-management (§11) — the employment-domain + HR-operator restriction and the fulfillment+evidence legs are the current separators, but RCM's change→obligation→response machinery overlaps the monitoring leg; vs corporate-lms (§09) — the training pole (mandate-driven compliance training) straddles the seam and both leaves should be reviewed together; suite-embedded compliance modules (HCM/payroll suites) evidenced only structurally this pass (ADP/Paychex/Paycor/Insperity/J.J. Keller sites unreachable) — revisit if a suite leaf is processed later (research/hr-compliance-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- congregation-membership-management (§25, processed) — joint-review flag from church-management-system-chms DISCHARGED: keep-both with a center-of-gravity seam — this Type is the congregation's membership roll (people + households + membership status + directories/lists/reports) without participation machinery; ChMS is the roll plus the machinery (attendance/check-in, giving records, groups, events, follow-up workflows) operated as one ministry system; standalone roll-only realizations documented (Planning Center People "free membership database… use it all on its own" with no check-in/giving/groups/events inside the product; Church Windows Membership purchasable as a standalone module with Donations/Accounting/Payroll separate; ParishSOFT Families census/records module with Offering separate), while the dominant market pattern embeds the roll inside full ChMS products (Breeze/Servant Keeper/Churchteams) — the same embedded-core pattern as case-law-research-platform inside legal-research-platform; removal tests recorded both ways (strip participation machinery → still this Type; make the machinery the center → ChMS; remove membership status → contact database); secondary flags for unprocessed §25 siblings: vs membership-management-system — probable domain-sibling pair, generic membership centers dues/renewals/benefits/self-governed member bodies vs congregation status/households/pastoral records with no dues machinery, joint review recommended when that leaf is processed; vs member-directory — the directory is one output of the roll (print and/or member-facing, privacy-controlled), watch-item for capability-slice consolidation (research/congregation-membership-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- RESOLVED (2026-09-07): cam (§16, processed) vs cnc-programming-application (§16 sibling) — joint review completed by the cnc-programming-application pass: leaf CONFIRMED AS ALIAS of cam; market evidence: Mastercam homepage "Your Solution for CNC Programming" + "#1 most widely used CAM software" (same page, same product), OneCNC "CAM system for NC part programming", SprutCAM "CNC programming workflow" for its CAD/CAM product — three independent vendors use the names interchangeably for the same geometry-driven products; the candidate manual-programming-activity slice rejected: the code-direct family self-identifies as editors/DNC/verification/post-processing (Predator CNC Editor "G code editing software", Vericut "CNC verification, simulation and analysis" consuming the finished NC program, Predator Post Processor translating existing CL/NCI data) and conversational programming is a control-side mode (Centroid), so no distinct "CNC programming application" product category exists outside CAM; both leaves now documented (applications/cam.md + applications/cnc-programming-application.md describe the same Type — the latter from the program-artifact vantage with the companion toolchain developed); RECOMMEND taxonomy-owner consolidation of the duplicate leaf; secondary seams unchanged: vs additive-manufacturing-software (same skeleton, build-vs-remove) and vs PLC Programming Environment (logic control vs machining motion) (research/cnc-programming-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- human-capital-management-hcm (§09, processed) vs human-resource-information-system-hris (§09 sibling, unprocessed): ALIAS/umbrella flag — the market uses HCM, HRIS, and HRMS as overlapping labels for one product category; direct vendor evidence: SAP FAQ states HCM and HRMS "are often used interchangeably", Workday's Core HCM page describes the product as "a comprehensive HRMS solution", Personio's homepage displays both a "Core HR" and an "HCM Software" G2 badge for the same product; the claimed distinction (HCM = HRIS + talent + analytics + strategy) describes a breadth posture, not a different structure — the defining core (workers + org structure + employment lifecycle) is identical; HCM documented as the suite-breadth expression of the workforce system of record; recommend joint review when human-resource-information-system-hris is processed — candidate outcomes: merge as one Type (HCM = suite-breadth label, HRIS = core-records label), or keep-both with explicit alias cross-reference; secondary seams held: Payroll System (money execution; HCM products exist without native payroll), ATS (requisition/candidate pipeline; handoff at offer-acceptance seam), Workforce Management (scheduling-first), People Analytics (measurement-first), Employee Record System (records without managed lifecycle), single-process talent Types (own defining cores); BambooHR (the dedicated HRIS-pole sample) unreachable this pass (403 + JS-gated help center) — label-overlap finding rests on three vendors' own statements (research/human-capital-management-hcm.md §Boundary Findings)

- diagramming-application (§03.05, processed) vs collaborative-canvas + digital-whiteboard (§03.05 siblings): boundary RE-CONFIRMED as requested by the collaborative-canvas pass — the diagram-vs-board seam holds on four independent vendor evidence pieces (Lucid ships diagramming and whiteboarding as separate products with freehand drawing explicitly assigned to the whiteboard side; Lucid's import flow separates diagram files [Visio/Gliffy/draw.io/OmniGraffle] from board files [Miro/MURAL/FigJam]; Miro's help center is board-centric with diagramming as a capability inside boards; SmartDraw sells Diagramming and Whiteboarding as separate solutions); structural discriminator: in diagramming the shape+connector graph with routing behavior and notation semantics IS the artifact, in whiteboards/canvases free placement of heterogeneous content is the artifact and connections are auxiliary lines; convergence trend flagged: whiteboard products ship diagramming shape packs and diagramming products bridge into canvas surfaces (Lucid universal canvas), so expect continued product-level blur while the object models stay distinct — the digital-whiteboard vs collaborative-canvas alias question remains open for its own pass (research/diagramming-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- cold-chain-transportation-monitoring (§18, processed) vs shipment-visibility-platform + vehicle-telematics-platform (§18 siblings, unprocessed) and food-cold-chain-management (§20 sibling, unprocessed): seam flags for joint review — shipment-visibility platforms share the live-shipment surface and several vendors (Tive, Sensitech) market one platform for both, so feature presence is explicitly NOT the seam; the boundary drawn here is the condition-vs-requirement core (knowing where a shipment is vs whether the cargo environment held against a defined requirement, with the evidence record that follows) — apply the condition test when shipment-visibility-platform is processed; vehicle-telematics-platform shares the in-vehicle data layer and equipment-native cold chain products (reefer telematics with remote unit control) sit at that seam — apply the cargo-environment test (vehicle/asset health vs what the cargo experiences) when that sibling is processed; food-cold-chain-management owns food-supply-chain-wide scope (production/storage/retail, food-industry semantics) while this Type is the transport leg and cargo-agnostic (pharma/chemicals/floral/organs) — apply the scope test when that sibling is processed; facility-vs-transport split is confirmed by vendor product-line structure (one vendor ships stationary monitoring and in-transit monitoring as separate lines) (research/cold-chain-transportation-monitoring.md §Boundary Findings)

- cash-management-platform (§08, processed) vs treasury-management-system + commercial-banking-platform + liquidity-management-platform (§08 siblings, all unprocessed): three seams recorded for joint review — (1) vs treasury-management-system: side seam, every sampled bank platform's own words place the corporate TMS/ERP outside the platform (HSBCnet "align with your in-house TMS and ERP"; J.P. Morgan Access "embedded directly in your ERP/TMS" and advertising "manage multi-bank cash balances" — the bank platform aggregates data about accounts at other banks but executes money movement only on its own rails; WF transmits payment files "directly from an ERP... to the bank" and posts cash-receipt files "back to your ERP"); test: move the operator from the bank to the corporate treasury department → TMS; (2) vs commercial-banking-platform: breadth seam — the cash management platform is the treasury-operations channel of the broader commercial relationship (WF sells Vantage as the digital platform of its Commercial Banking division; JPM Access sits under the Payments family serving commercial and corporate clients); test: strip credit/lending and keep account operations → this Type; (3) vs liquidity-management-platform: family seam — liquidity structures (concentration/pooling/virtual accounts) are a service family inside cash management with varying self-service depth (one product offers in-platform self-service structure management; another implements pooling advisory-led), so the standalone leaf likely means corporate-side liquidity analytics or short-term-investment/MMF portals; test: remove visibility+payments and keep only liquidity optimization → liquidity platform; also: business-banking-portal's deferred tier-seam flag DISCHARGED — confirmed as a Type seam, not merely a tier (all sampled banks operate the SMB portal and the corporate platform as separate products); naming collision: consumer brokerage "cash-management accounts" are banking overlays on investment relationships (recorded in the brokerage-platform pass), not this Type (research/cash-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- human-resource-information-system-hris vs human-capital-management-hcm (§09 siblings) JOINT REVIEW COMPLETED (2026-09-07, resolving the alias/umbrella flag recorded by the HCM pass): confirmed ONE Type with two labels for two breadth postures, not two Types — the defining core (employee record as single source of truth + organization structure + managed core-HR operations) is identical on both sides; the labels describe how much a product ships, not a different structure: HRIS = the core-records + core-HR-operations expression, the foundation every suite builds on (the label favored by the SMB/mid-market pole AND by the core product inside enterprise platforms — Rippling lists "HRIS" as the first product under its HCM heading; HiBob names its foundation product "HRIS" and sells Talent/Payroll/Planning suites on top, claiming "the breadth of an HCM, not just core HRIS functionality"); HRMS ≈ HRIS (Personio FAQ: "often little difference between the two, with some vendors using HRIS and HRMS interchangeably"; SAP FAQ: "often used interchangeably"; Zoho People self-labels HRMS with the same structure); HCM = the full-suite expression (Personio dual-badged "Core HR Leader" + "HCM Software Leader" for one product; Personio's own HRIS→HRMS→HCM gradient table closes with "focus on the capabilities of specific platforms and the outcomes they can deliver — not the labels"); outcome: keep both leaves (directory not modifiable in a leaf pass), cross-referenced as alias/umbrella — applications/human-resource-information-system-hris.md defines the Type from the HRIS pole, applications/human-capital-management-hcm.md from the suite-breadth pole; secondary joint review with employee-record-system also discharged from this side (the record layer IS the HRIS foundation — Personio's first HRIS role is "system of record", Zoho calls it an "employee DBMS" — but HRIS adds the managed operations; record-custody-without-operations seam holds, both leaves stand); people-analytics suite-embedded flag consistent from this side (Personio People Analytics / HiBob Data & Analytics / Rippling Analytics satisfy the people-analytics defining core with the suite as primary source; boundary is data-scope posture, not feature presence); BMS drift seam recorded (Factorial self-labels "All-in-one Business Management Software", Rippling spans HR+IT+Payroll+Finance on one employee-data core — when non-HR domains become co-equal product centers rather than extensions of the people record, drift toward business-management-suite); sourcing limitation: BambooHR (the dedicated HRIS-pole brand) unreachable across both passes (403 ×2 + 403 ×2) — HRIS-pole evidence rests on HiBob/Personio/Rippling/Zoho/Factorial, all Tier-2 official product+glossary pages, no Tier-1 help-center docs fetched, no numeric limits asserted (research/human-resource-information-system-hris.md §Boundary Findings)

- constituent-relationship-management (§24, processed) vs 311-citizen-service-request-platform (§24 sibling, processed) — JOINT REVIEW COMPLETED (2026-09-07, resolving the adjacency/overlap flag recorded by the 311 pass): seam CONFIRMED as two Types on the object-primary test the 311 pass proposed — the service request lifecycle is the primary object in 311 (requester incidental), the constituent record + cumulative relationship history is the primary object here (requests are interactions attached to the person); removal test recorded: strip persistent constituent records and keep requests → still a 311 platform; strip requests and keep person + history + outreach → still a (thin) constituent CRM; Accela's own "Service Request Management (SRM/CRM)" module confirmed request-centric without a relationship spine (boundary evidence, not a counterexample); Granicus OneView/govService documented as the deliberate straddle pole ("citizen relationship and service request management system" — suite bundling of both Types, not evidence of one Type); early request-only 311 systems without persistent requester records excluded from this Type by the historical check, reinforcing the split (research/constituent-relationship-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- retail-shrink-management (§05.25, processed) — RESOLVES the overlap flag recorded by the retail-loss-prevention-platform pass: object test applied and PASSED for keep-both — the shrink-management Type's central object is the quantified, attributed loss picture (measurement/program layer: valued variance from counts/reads/cash/waste records, decomposed by cause × location/category/item/time), while the LP platform's central object is the loss-event case record with a response workflow; evidence: shrink-side products hand events TO case management rather than owning cases (one vendor's shrink application "links loss events with video verification for case management investigations"; another's RFID platform centers on inventory accuracy/discrepancy resolution with no case object), one LP-suite vendor ships shrink analytics and case management as separate products, and most shrink (spoilage/error/process loss) never becomes a case at all; overlap acknowledged (LP platforms embed shrink analytics as a first-class capability — the seam is the object, not the feature list); market-shape note: the layer rarely appears as a standalone horizontal product — realized as LP-platform modules, RFID/EAS solution stacks, or vertical shrink-cause tools; no DIRECTORY change made; secondary seams held: Retail Inventory Management (stock record vs variance consumption), Retail POS (creation vs consumption), Fraud Detection (real-time decisioning vs retrospective attribution), VMS (cameras vs loss picture) (research/retail-shrink-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- container-management (§14, processed) vs kubernetes-management-platform (§14 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the §14 container cluster — the managed-substrate axis (containerized workloads across arbitrary runtimes — Docker/Swarm/Podman/Nomad/cloud services, Kubernetes among them — vs Kubernetes clusters and K8s-native objects specifically); overlap zone is commercially large and vendor-confirmed (Rancher own documentation describes the same product as both a "container management platform" and a "Kubernetes management tool"; Portainer largest surface is Kubernetes); working test recorded: restrict the managed substrate to Kubernetes clusters + K8s objects + cluster lifecycle/GitOps → Kubernetes Management Platform; operate non-K8s runtimes → Container Management; seam is consistent with the container-kubernetes-security pass recorded function split (operate vs assess/enforce/gate); recommend joint review when kubernetes-management-platform is processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with the substrate-breadth seam (current framing), or treat container-management as the umbrella with Kubernetes management as its dominant modern realization (research/container-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- digital-painting-application (§04.02, processed) vs raster-image-editor (§04.02, processed): this pass CONFIRMS the raster pass's recorded primary-job gradient from the painting side and DISCHARGES that joint-review flag from this side — both passes independently reached the same discriminator (primary job: create artwork from scratch vs modify existing pixels), and vendor self-positioning anchors it (Krita's own manual: "creating artworks from scratch… not intended as a replacement for Photoshop" for image-manipulation tasks); machinery overlap acknowledged (layers/brushes/filters nearly identical standard-capability sets — the seam is the starting point, not the feature list); residual note: the platform-native simple paint-program lineage (MS Paint-class) sits genuinely on the gradient — the raster pass claimed it as its historical sample, this pass used painting-specific lineage instead (Deluxe Paint, Paint Tool SAI, ArtRage, Tux Paint); both claims coexist because the class straddles the boundary; no taxonomy change proposed; no new joint-review flags (research/digital-painting-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- continuous-delivery-platform (§12, processed) vs continuous-integration-platform (§12 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the dev-delivery block — CI ends at producing validated build artifacts (commit-triggered build/test feedback), CD owns environments, executes deployments, and keeps the record of what is deployed where; vendor-documented from the CD side (Octopus docs: "CI is not CD", "takes over where your CI server ends", CI's job is turning source into deployable artifacts; Spinnaker/Argo CD integrate external CI; GitLab bundles both — suite packaging, not Type fusion); working test: center of gravity ends at validated artifact → CI; extends to environment delivery + deployment records → CD; recommend joint review when continuous-integration-platform is processed (build-automation-system pass already recorded a related flag); secondary flag vs release-management-platform (§12 sibling, unprocessed): deployment execution machinery vs release governance/planning — "release orchestration" vocabulary straddles (Octopus self-describes with it); test: executes deployments against environments → CD; coordinates/plans/governs releases as management objects → Release Management; joint review recommended when that leaf is processed (research/continuous-delivery-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- influencer-marketing-platform (§06, processed) — DISCHARGES the central taxonomy-tension flag raised by the influencer-campaign-management pass, from the platform side; adopted the proposed seam and recommends keeping BOTH Types: Influencer Marketing Platform = brand-side program system of record (creator population records + discovery/evaluation + cross-engagement relationship records + program-level measurement, with campaign execution as one module) vs Influencer Campaign Management = the campaign-execution layer (campaign container + participation workflow + brief/deliverables + content binding + campaign results as defining objects); classification test recorded both directions: center of gravity on the creator relationship across campaigns → platform leaf, on the campaign lifecycle → campaign leaf; market-shape evidence: every sampled product contains both layers (CreatorIQ's own capability menu separates "Creator Management" from "Campaign Execution"; Traackr stacks Plan/Activate/Measure with campaign execution as the middle stage; Meltwater's FAQ lists campaign management inside a full-cycle description; the three carried help-center products document execution deepest) — no standalone campaign-only product verified at scale, so the campaign leaf stands as the execution-layer Type realized inside platforms; secondary seams confirmed this pass: brand-creator-marketplace venue test adopted (creator as first-class transacting participant = marketplace core; marketplace/application modules inside platforms = recruitment surfaces, not venue conversion), affiliate-management-platform + affiliate-network held on primary object (commission-per-conversion economics vs creator relationship and content collaboration; platforms integrate affiliate networks for attribution rather than owning the economics), public-relations-management-platform held on population + job (journalists/earned-media pitching vs creators as partnership subjects with audience-performance evaluation; listening-suite vendors ship both as sibling capabilities), social-media-management + social-media-analytics + social-listening held on actor/object (brand's own content, aggregate measurement, monitoring vs third-party creator population), creator-crm + creator-audience-analytics = creator-side opposites of the same data objects; no DIRECTORY change made (research/influencer-marketing-platform.md §Boundary Findings)


- creator-storefront (§27, processed) vs Online Store Builder / E-commerce Platform (§05.01, unprocessed) + Digital Product Commerce Platform / Link-in-Bio Platform (§27 siblings, unprocessed): spectrum flag — the researched market shows a continuum from fully bundled creator-commerce platforms (production network + merchant-of-record payments + taxes + support + audience-native distribution) to artist-operated shop builders (seller connects processors, configures shipping, handles support — Big Cartel pole), so the seam vs Online Store Builder is a machinery-posture + audience-goods spectrum rather than a hard line; diagnostic recorded: remove the bundled machinery and audience-native posture → store builder; add them → creator storefront; recommend joint review when §05.01 leaves are processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with the machinery/audience seam (current framing), or re-scope Big Cartel-class products as the store-builder pole; secondary: the fulfillment-structure test (purchase → goods/downloads) is confirmed from this side for the digital-product-commerce-platform and link-in-bio-platform joint reviews; naming-overlap note: market language "creator storefront" also covers affiliate-curated shop surfaces (LTK/Amazon-Influencer-class), which the creator-affiliate-dashboard pass assigned to that Type — this leaf documents the own-goods selling surface (research/creator-storefront.md §Boundary Findings)

- retail-space-planning-application (§05.13, processed) — CLOSES the 05.13 family review: the object-of-record removal tests recorded by retail-merchandising-platform ("replace merchandise lifecycle with shelf-layout objects"), assortment-planning-application ("replace the offering decision with shelf-layout objects"), and category-management-application ("replace the category performance loop with shelf-layout objects") are all APPLIED AND CONFIRMED from this side — the shelf-layout object (measured fixture/shelf structures + planogram + performance-informed placement) cleanly separates the leaf from all three siblings, and vendors bundling space with category/assortment (DotActiv, Quant, Oracle legacy packaging) match the predicted product-level overlap without collapsing the Types; all four 05.13 leaves now processed with boundaries held, no DIRECTORY change; secondary market-structure note: enterprise retail-suite pole evidenced only by Oracle (current cloud portfolio has no space planning product; legacy on-prem planning product named "Category Management Planning and Optimization and Macro Space Optimization") — Blue Yonder/RELEX/Aptos unreachable, so the enterprise-suite space planning positioning remains unverified; if a future pass reaches those vendors, re-check the packaging variant only, not the core (research/retail-space-planning-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- claims-adjuster-platform (§08, processed) vs insurance-claims-management (§08 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the claims family — the adjuster platform centers the adjuster's individual-claim adjudication loop (assess → value → review → settle) and typically attaches to the payer's system (Cotality listed on Guidewire Marketplace; XactAnalysis as an estimate-exchange network), while Insurance Claims Management centers the payer's claim lifecycle and book of claims (FNOL intake, registration, reserving, payment ledger, recoveries, reporting); the overlap zone is real (Snapsheet-class platforms sell the whole loop and embed the workbench) so feature lists cannot separate the Types — recorded seam test: whose work does the product center (the claims organization's lifecycle and ledger vs the adjuster's assessment-to-settlement loop on an individual file); recommend joint review when insurance-claims-management is processed — candidate outcomes: keep-both with the whose-work seam (current framing), or treat the adjuster platform as the workbench facet of one claims Type; secondary polysemy note: "claims" in §22 (Provider Claims Management / Payer Claims Processing = healthcare billing adjudication) and §17 (Construction Claims Management = contract disputes) are different object worlds — no merge risk, recorded so future passes don't conflate the word (research/claims-adjuster-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- continuous-integration-platform (§12, processed) — CLOSES both pending joint-review flags from the CI side: (1) vs build-automation-system — seam confirmed, CI answers when/where builds run for whom with what history (triggers, shared capacity, run records), the build tool answers how one project builds; delegation evidence from the CI side: Jenkins invokes build tools as steps (`sh 'make'`, Using-Build-Tools tutorials) and CruiseControl ships builders for Ant/NAnt/Maven/Rake/exec while remaining a CI record layer — the two coexist in one pipeline without fusion; removal tests recorded both directions; (2) vs continuous-delivery-platform — seam confirmed, deploy stages appear inside CI pipeline examples on every sampled product (GitLab `deploy` stage, Jenkins Deploy stages, Buildkite block-gate before production deployment) but environments/deployment records are absent from every sampled CI object model (Jenkins artifacts "archived… for later retrieval by users"; Buildkite trigger step hands off to a separate deployment pipeline), matching the Octopus-side statements already recorded by the CD pass; working test now validated from both sides: center of gravity ends at validated artifact + feedback → CI; extends to environment delivery + deployment records → CD; "CI/CD platform" self-branding (GitHub Actions, GitLab) is suite packaging across the CD seam, not Type fusion — consistent with the CD pass's GitLab observation; the build-automation pass's secondary three-way question (ecosystem build tools × dependency-management × package-registry) is out of CI scope and left for that joint review; boundaries vs Code Quality Platform (consistent with code-quality pass: CI triggered-by/reports-into, no long-term quality ledger), test tooling (execution shell + report consumption), Artifact Repository/Package Registry (Buildkite ships Package Registries as a separate product — vendor's own split), Source Code Hosting (event source + bundling), and job schedulers (change-binding as discriminator) also held (research/continuous-integration-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
