- creator-subscription-platform (§27, processed) vs fan-membership-platform (§27 sibling, unprocessed) + paid-community-platform (§27 sibling, unprocessed): NEAR-ALIAS RISK — direct evidence shows "membership" and "subscription" used interchangeably for the same recurring fan→creator structure (BMAC's recurring product is "memberships" bought with "subscription fees"; Memberful sells "membership plans" that are auto-renewing subscriptions; Ghost calls paid subscribers "paid members" with "paid subscriptions"; Patreon's patrons are "members"), so fan-membership-platform is the highest alias risk in the creator cluster; working distinction if the taxonomy keeps both: subscription emphasizes the recurring payment relationship and gated output stream, membership emphasizes belonging to a roster with benefits/perks — but every sampled product exhibits both emphases in one structure; vs paid-community-platform the fulfillment-structure seam holds (venue access vs creator output stream — subscription platforms sync community access as a declared benefit while the venue is hosted elsewhere, e.g. Memberful's Discord/Discourse/Circle integrations manage access "as memberships change"); recommend joint review of the three leaves when they are processed — candidate outcomes: merge subscription+membership (one Type, two market names) or keep-both on the payment-vs-belonging emphasis axis; secondary: lifetime membership (one-time payment, permanent standing) bends the recurrence invariant — flagged for the same review (research/creator-subscription-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- retail-store-management-system (§05.11, processed) vs store-operations-platform + store-task-management (§05.11 siblings, both unprocessed): intra-family joint-review flag — the three leaves plausibly split into TWO product families: this pass's market referent ("retail management system/platform", the back office behind "retail POS") is the commerce-operations system of record for the store (offering/stock/staff/cash/sales behind the register), while current retail-tech usage of "store operations platform" names the frontline-execution family (task management, execution audits, workforce scheduling, frontline communication across a chain) and "store task management" is the task-only slice of that family; alias risk is real because market labels drift between the families; working seam recorded: system of record for the store's commerce operation vs coordination layer for the store's workforce activity; recommend joint review when the siblings are processed — candidate outcomes: keep-all-three with the record-base-vs-activity seam and an explicit two-family split inside 05.11, or re-scope leaf labels to match the families (research/retail-store-management-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- retail-store-management-system (§05.11, processed) vs retail-inventory-management (§05.12, processed) + store-inventory-application (§05.12 sibling, unprocessed): same-substrate consistency note — the inventory pass sampled Square/Erply/NetSuite/Cin7 and this pass sampled Square/Erply/KORONA/Retail Pro: the same back-office products realize both Types, differing by center (item-level stock ledger vs store as operating unit); the two documents are readable as span-slices over shared machinery; no conflict found with the inventory pass's definitions; carried into the pending store-inventory-application joint review (research/retail-store-management-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- retail-store-management-system (§05.11, processed) vs retail-point-of-sale (§05.10, processed): consistency note, no action — seam held structurally (POS centers the transaction spine priced-catalog→sale→tender→completed transaction; this Type centers the store's governance record base behind it) and is consistent with the POS pass's own placement of permissions/inventory/reporting as secondary structure; the market usually sells both as one suite — both Types stand because register-only and back-office-first deployments both exist (research/retail-store-management-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- insurance-agency-management (§08, processed) vs broker-management-platform (§08, processed): alias CONFIRMED from the agency side — Vertafore's own AMS FAQ names "agents, brokers, CSRs, and agency principals" as the AMS's users, HawkSoft copy addresses "agents and brokers" interchangeably, AgencyBloc's client roster includes brokerage-named firms while the product is marketed as an AMS, and the UK broker-software sample (Acturis, SSP) exhibits the identical structure (client + placed policy + carrier panel + commission + renewal + documents + accounting); no structural difference separates the two leaves; this pass's defining core was deliberately written structure-compatible with the sibling pass's (client records + placed-policy records binding client × external carrier × terms × period + renewal-driven lifecycle); recommend joint review to decide merge vs keep-as-regional-naming-variant pair (US "agency management system" vs UK "broker management system"); secondary intent check resolved: the leaf is agency-side back-office software, not carrier-side distribution-network management (research/insurance-agency-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- claims-adjuster-platform (§08, processed) vs insurance-claims-management (§08, processed): joint-review flag DISCHARGED from the insurance-claims-management side — keep-both confirmed with the whose-work seam: the claims management system centers the claims organization's lifecycle and book of claims (FNOL intake, registration, coverage verification, assignment, reserving, payment ledger, recoveries, QA, reporting) while the adjuster platform centers the individual adjuster's assessment-to-settlement loop on one file; overlap zone real (Snapsheet sells both a complete claims system and virtual appraisals/total-loss settlement; suite products embed claim-file work surfaces) so feature lists cannot separate the Types, but the vocabulary split holds (reserves/payments/recoveries/coverage-verification vs estimates/scopes/depreciation/pricing-data) and the failure test discriminates (a claims system can run a book with no estimate machinery — e.g. liability/life settlements; an adjuster platform cannot run without valuation machinery); structural relationship recorded: the adjuster platform is the workbench facet that attaches to or is embedded in the claims system of record (research/insurance-claims-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- court-case-management-system (§24, processed) vs court-e-filing-platform (§24, processed): joint-review flag RESOLVED — the e-filing pass confirms two Types with a mandatory integration seam: the CMS is the court's record of reference (case/docket/hearings/outcomes), e-filing is the intake machinery (packaged submission → court-controlled review gate → accept/reject → record handoff); the market realizes the seam both as separate integrated products (EFSP/EFM architecture, OASIS ECF 4.0 conformance; Journal eFile-it) and as one bundled program (federal CM/ECF, where filing auto-creates docket entries); tests both ways hold (remove the case record from an e-filing platform → still an e-filing platform; remove intake from the CMS → still a CMS); both documents record the seam and cross-reference (research/court-e-filing-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- digital-whiteboard (§03.05, processed) vs collaborative-canvas (§03.05, processed): joint-review flag from the collaborative-canvas pass DISCHARGED as ALIAS CONFIRMED — the digital-whiteboard pass adds independent evidence that one market family runs behind the two directory names: vendor self-descriptions uniformly say "whiteboard" (Figma's help center labels FigJam "a digital whiteboard"; Lucid's help center defines Lucidspark as "a virtual whiteboard for freeform ideation, group brainstorming, and real-time hybrid collaboration"; Conceptboard self-titles "the online whiteboard"; Excalidraw's page title is "Whiteboard"; Microsoft's product is named "Whiteboard") while "infinite/endless canvas" appears only as a surface description (Miro "endless", Mural "shared infinite canvas"); the board-migration family (Miro/FigJam/Mural/Jamboard/Conceptboard/Lucidspark) is closed under the whiteboard name; Conceptboard ships official head-to-head comparison pages against other whiteboards (Microsoft Whiteboard, Miro); no product population answering to "collaborative canvas" but not "whiteboard" (or vice versa) was found in either pass; the working lens split (whiteboard = live session/facilitation-surface emphasis; collaborative canvas = board-as-persistent-co-created-artifact emphasis) is descriptive, not structural — products straddle both; RECOMMENDATION: merge the two leaves or declare one canonical name with the other as alias — taxonomy-level decision deliberately not made in this pass (DIRECTORY.md untouched); both application documents are written to stand alone and cross-reference each other; the diagramming boundary was re-confirmed on this pass's evidence (Lucid's own FAQ separates "Lucidchart — build intelligent diagrams" from "Lucidspark — collaborate in a virtual whiteboard"; Lucidchart imports Visio/Gliffy/draw.io/OmniGraffle diagram files while Lucidspark imports Miro/MURAL boards) (research/digital-whiteboard.md §Boundary Findings)

- punch-list-management (§17, unprocessed) vs construction-closeout-management (§17, processed): overlap-zone flag from the closeout side — every closeout product contains punch/snag machinery, and GC suites realize closeout by composing the punch tool with documents/submittals, so feature lists cannot separate the Types; the held seam is scope (deficiency loop to verified closure vs the phase outcome: deliverable fulfillment + recorded owner acceptance/turnover + retained owner-controlled record); when punch-list-management is processed, define it by the loop-only scope (regional names: punch US / snag UK-UAE / defect AU-SG / deficiency CA) and keep the acceptance/handover machinery on the closeout side; joint awareness recommended (research/construction-closeout-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- retail-trading-platform (§08, processed) — ANSWERS the pending three-way joint-review flag (retail-trading-platform / professional-trading-terminal / brokerage-platform) from the retail side, DISCHARGING the flag for this sibling: seam CONFIRMED by center of gravity — the retail platform centers the self-directed trading loop for the individual's own money (instrument universe with prices → human order construction → real execution → tracked positions/holdings), the brokerage platform centers the account relationship (gated creation, funding, custody records, statements), the terminal centers market-centric workspace density; structural tests recorded both directions (remove the trading loop → statement portal; remove account administration → this Type; remove order entry → data terminal); the instrument/quote/order/position objects are shared across the family — the seam is the center, not disjoint objects; straddles are structural and expected (Robinhood merged app; Schwab simplified→thinkorswim ladder — the vendor's own copy names the "simplified mobile experience vs professional-grade trading workstation" split; Zerodha Kite/Console split products) — recommendation: KEEP both Types; secondary: answers the brokerage pass's crypto-inside-brokerage convergence flag from this side — sampled US retail platforms operate crypto through separately licensed entities with distinct/weaker protection (Robinhood RHC / Webull Pay / Schwab Premier Bank pattern) while the cryptocurrency-exchange leaf owns venue+custody — joint review with cryptocurrency-exchange recommended when that leaf is processed; historical note recorded: the pre-electronic phone-order brokerage relationship instantiates NO self-directed electronic surface, sharpening this Type's boundary rather than breaking it; no DIRECTORY change made (research/retail-trading-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- cloud-contact-center-ccaas (§07, processed) vs contact-center-platform (§07 sibling, unprocessed) + call-center-platform (§07, processed): JOINT-REVIEW ANSWER from the CCaaS side — the call-center pass's flag ("CCaaS = probable delivery-form variant of the contact-center machinery") is CONFIRMED from direct vendor/analyst evidence: CCaaS is a delivery/consumption designation, not a separate structure — the market-leader glossary defines it as "a cloud-based customer experience solution that allows companies to utilize a contact center provider's software… purchase only the technology they need… scalability as operational needs change", analysts name the market category "Contact Center as a Service" (cited on sampled vendors' own pages), and no sampled CCaaS product (5 primary + 1 secondary) contains interaction machinery a premise contact center lacks — every distinguishing property is consumption-shaped (web/console access, subscription-or-usage purchasing, vendor-operated telephony/capacity/updates, elastic scale, residency/sovereign postures, APIs/marketplaces); the call-center and CCaaS documents are written structure-compatible and cross-reference each other; DECISION PENDING with the contact-center-platform pass: merge CCaaS into it as the cloud-posture leaf (leading candidate) or keep both leaves with CCaaS documenting the consumption form as currently written — no DIRECTORY change made in this pass; secondary seams held: UCaaS (all-employee communications without ACD/agent-operation semantics — suite vendors police the seam themselves by naming UCaaS/CCaaS/CPaaS as distinct products), CPaaS (developer API building blocks), IVR/Routing/WFM/QM leaves (decomposed component layers; a WEM-only license shipping without interaction handling is the inverse existence proof) (research/cloud-contact-center-ccaas.md §Boundary Findings)

- insurance-marketplace (§08, processed) vs insurance-quote-platform (§08 sibling, unprocessed): nearest-sibling joint-review flag — working seam recorded this pass: the quote platform centers the quote/rating transaction machinery (rate quoting, quote-and-buy, often sold to or embedded in intermediaries), while the marketplace centers the standing consumer venue (multi-insurer inventory + shopping journey + enrollment connection + post-sale cycle); many products embody both (quote machinery is a capability of the marketplace), so candidate outcomes are keep-both with venue-vs-transaction seam, or re-scope insurance-quote-platform as the quoting capability/infrastructure layer; recommend explicit adoption of the purchase-connection discriminator when that leaf is processed (research/insurance-marketplace.md §Boundary Findings). Secondary confirmations: insurance-agency-management pass seam (agency-side back office vs consumer-side venue) confirmed and sharpened; comparison-platform pass capability-vs-Type flag (§02.10) answered from this side — purchase connection + post-sale cycle is the discriminator; US naming collision recorded: "Health Insurance Marketplace®" legally denotes the government exchange (ACA) — private marketplaces carry mandated disclaimers, government exchange treated as the public-operator variant of this Type rather than a merge with Government Service Portal.

- crematory-management (§29, processed) vs funeral-home-management (§29 sibling, unprocessed) + cemetery-management (§29, processed): crematory-management pass confirms and refines the joint-review flag recorded by cemetery-management — the three-way split of core objects held from the crematory side (crematory = decedent custody + cremation register + authorization paperwork + remains custody; no ground inventory, no funeral case); new evidence: PlotBox Rushcliffe Oaks case study documents a crematorium-only deployment with no cemetery objects purchased ("we don't have a cemetery" — buyer-side seam), and Passare (funeral-first case management with barcode chain-of-custody for decedents/items) documents the funeral side of the seam with no cremation register or remains-release workflow; market reality unchanged: crematory is sold mainly as a module of deathcare suites (PlotBox cemetery+crematory+funeral; OpusXenta cemetery+crematoria); standalone crematory-first vendors unverified this pass (search engines unavailable, Crezura domain defunct) — keep "three domain Types sold as one suite" as the working view; run the deferred joint review when funeral-home-management is processed

- retirement-planning-application (§08, processed) — consumer retirement planning is realized in the market heavily as embedded modules of PFM/brokerage/wealth ecosystems and as advisor-facing planning platforms (advisor-built client plans, rosters, permissioned client access, AUA tracking); boundary held structurally this pass (household plan + multi-decade projection + sufficiency evaluation = the Type; present-state tracking = PFM; portfolio construction/execution = robo-advisor); when robo-advisor and wealth-management-platform are processed, joint review recommended on the embedded-planner capability-overlap pattern (research/retirement-planning-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- construction-contract-administration (§17, processed) vs progress-billing (§17, unprocessed): joint-review flag for the progress-billing pass — the construction market does not draw the contract-record/billing-cycle line where the directory draws it: InEight bundles pay applications, retainage calculation, and invoice status tracking inside its Contract module while shipping a separate Billings product; Procore hosts owner invoices under Prime Contracts and subcontractor invoicing under Commitments. This pass defined contract administration as the contract-side anchor (contract value, schedule of values, retainage terms, payment status) and left the periodic billing/pay-application cycle to the progress-billing leaf — the progress-billing pass must define its center (the billing cycle/application document itself) from the other side of this seam so the two leaves do not duplicate or orphan retainage/pay-app machinery. Related processed-leaf consistency held: change-order-management ("broader" boundary confirmed), business-contract-administration ("industry sibling" confirmed), construction-closeout-management (retainage/lien mechanics located here confirmed).

- pension-administration-platform (§08, processed) vs insurance-policy-administration-system (§08, processed): joint-review flag from the pension pass DISCHARGED from the policy-administration side — structurally closest neighbor confirmed as two Types on the governance-basis axis: the policy admin record is a commercial contract (insurer ↔ policyholder, premiums, coverage, cancellation/reinstatement, effective-dated changes) while the pension record is scheme/trust/statute-governed membership (employer participation, employment-based accrual, indexation); the buy-out/bulk-annuity seam the pension pass predicted is real and market-confirmed — life & annuity PAS products (Sapiens CoreSuite for Life & Pensions; EIS Life & Annuities line) are where resulting annuity contracts live, so a bulk-annuity conversion moves a book from pension-administration structures to policy-administration structures; both documents cross-reference (research/insurance-policy-administration-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- insurance-policy-administration-system (§08, processed) vs insurance-quote-platform (§08 sibling, unprocessed): joint-review flag for the quote-platform pass — modern PAS products embed the quote/rating transaction as the front of the policy lifecycle (documented quote states through issuance in one product's public developer docs; quote→issuance named in all sampled lifecycles), so quote machinery alone cannot separate the Types; the recorded seam test is persistence: does the product keep the master policy record and carry the post-issuance lifecycle (endorsements, renewals, cancellations)? yes → policy administration; quote/rating transactions without a persistent book → quote platform; candidate outcomes: keep-both with the master-record test, or re-scope the quote leaf as the quoting capability layer (consistent with the insurance-marketplace pass's purchase-connection discriminator) (research/insurance-policy-administration-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- insurance-policy-administration-system (§08, processed) vs underwriting-workbench + insurance-underwriting-platform (§08 siblings, unprocessed): seam recorded for those passes — underwriting decision machinery (risk selection, rules, referrals, workbench) vs the policy record lifecycle those decisions act on; sampled suites integrate underwriting steps into policy creation (gated issuance, re-underwriting at renewal) but ship underwriting workbenches as separate products, so the Types are distinct in vendor packaging; when the underwriting leaves are processed, apply the whose-decision test (decision machinery vs contract record) (research/insurance-policy-administration-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- insurance-policy-administration-system (§08, processed) vs health-plan-administration-system (§22 sibling, unprocessed): family note for that pass — health plan administration is structurally a health-insurance instantiation of the policy-administration family (plan contracts, enrollment/eligibility machinery, member-level records under group master contracts; EIS Census & Enrollment Intake and Sapiens CoreSuite health scope show the overlap); recommend the health pass define its center from the health-specific machinery (enrollment events, eligibility, provider-facing seams) and cross-reference this leaf rather than duplicating the contract-lifecycle core (research/insurance-policy-administration-system.md §Boundary Findings)

- discussion-board (§01.06, processed) vs online-forum (§01.06 sibling, unprocessed): ALIAS-RISK flag — the standalone products embodying this Type (Discourse/XenForo/Flarum class) are the same market family "Online Forum" describes, and everyday usage treats discussion board/message board/forum/bulletin board as near-synonyms; the only defensible line found: Discussion Board = the discussion surface/tool (topic+reply machinery), which also exists embedded without any public community venue (LMS course boards, organizational/group boards), while Online Forum = the standing public community venue built from boards (member base, public identity, moderation culture); every standalone forum product instantiates both, so candidate outcomes are keep-both with tool-vs-venue emphasis or merge as one Type with surface variants; recommend joint review when online-forum is processed (research/discussion-board.md §Boundary Findings)

- curriculum-management (§23, processed): (1) catalog publishing has no separate directory leaf — this pass records the academic catalog as the standard publication surface INSIDE Curriculum Management (all sampled higher-ed products bundle or partner catalog tooling: CourseLeaf CAT, Coursedog Catalog & Handbook, Modern Campus Catalog, CourseLoop Publisher); if maintainers later split catalog tooling into its own leaf, the split should be governance-of-record (curriculum) vs published-view (catalog) as tightly coupled siblings, not duplicates; (2) the K-12 realization (curriculum mapping/planning, Atlas-class) shades into the §23 Lesson Planning Application leaf — lesson planning is the individual teacher authoring layer, K-12 curriculum management the institutional governance/publication layer around it, and K-12 vendors ship both together — joint review recommended when Lesson Planning Application is processed; (3) prior-pass consistency confirmed from this side: academic-accreditation-management's "curriculum mapping as evidence — a curriculum product may feed this Type; it is not this Type" holds, and academic-timetabling's curriculum-attachment seam (timetabling consumes approved curriculum downstream) holds (research/curriculum-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- returns-exchange-portal (§05.09, processed) vs returns-management-platform (§05.09 sibling, unprocessed): joint-review flag — the market sells the shopper-facing returns/exchange portal and the merchant-side returns operation as one product family (all four sampled products bundle both surfaces in one product; one vendor literally names its product "Return & Exchange Portal" while self-positioning as a returns management platform), so the directory's two-leaf split within 05.09 Returns needs a defensible seam or a merge; this pass defined the Portal leaf as the shopper-facing self-service initiation/tracking surface plus its policy/branding configuration, and left merchant-side end-to-end operations (request queue at scale, disposition, restocking, reverse-logistics orchestration, refund execution machinery) to the Returns Management Platform leaf; candidate outcomes: keep-both with the shopper-surface-vs-merchant-operations seam, or merge as one Type with two documented surfaces; the returns-management-platform pass must define its center from the merchant side and cross-reference research/returns-exchange-portal.md §Boundary Findings
- returns-management-platform (§05.09, processed) — joint-review flag from returns-exchange-portal DISCHARGED from this side: keep-both with the shopper-surface-vs-merchant-operations seam — this pass defines the merchant-side center of gravity (request queue at scale + policy decisioning + financial resolution execution + goods receipt/disposition, i.e. exactly the operations the portal pass deferred), and the sibling defines the shopper-facing self-service surface; seam test = who acts on the request (shopper self-serves on the portal; staff/systems work the platform), with one-product-two-surfaces as the dominant market packaging; secondary flag: ERP/OMS suites embedding RMA machinery carry the same functional core — recommend joint review when order-management-system / distributed-order-management / order-orchestration-platform leaves are processed, with the recorded seam "forward order lifecycle vs reverse operation" (research/returns-management-platform.md §Boundary Findings)
- insurance-quote-platform (§08, processed) vs insurance-marketplace (§08 sibling, processed): joint-review flag DISCHARGED from this side — KEEP-BOTH with the venue-vs-transaction seam confirmed by direct product evidence: the marketplace centers the standing consumer venue (multi-insurer inventory + shopping journey + enrollment connection + post-sale cycle), the quote platform centers the quote transaction (risk submission captured once → several insurers' rating applied → comparative per-insurer result set → progression toward the selected insurer), with no venue, no book, no master record; the industry's own category vocabulary (comparative rater = "single-entry multiple-company interface", quoted verbatim in a sampled product's FAQ) supports the transaction reading; overlap is real and bidirectional (quote machinery is a capability of marketplaces; raters attach consumer front doors and destination comparison sites are quote platforms with a venue skin), and the removal test separates them (remove venue/journey/post-sale → still a quote platform; remove the rating transaction → still a venue). Secondary boundary recorded: vs Lead Generation Platform (§06) — match-and-connect services that explicitly produce no quotes (one sampled product's own FAQ: "we don't provide quotes directly") are the Type's drift pole; when no quote transaction is produced the product is lead generation, not a quote platform. Open item: a single-insurer quote-and-buy *platform* realization (anticipated in sibling seams as "quote-and-buy widget sold to others") was not directly evidenced this pass — single-insurer quoting appears in evidence only as carrier-storefront/PAS capability; left as a variant note for future passes. Evidence gap: the consumer D2C quote-comparison class (The Zebra, QuoteWizard, Insurify, EverQuote, SelectQuote, Simply Business) and the ITC/TurboRater agent-rater family were unreachable (403/redirect shells) across both the marketplace pass and this pass — the consumer pole is documented structurally only; recommend a source-retry against that class when reachable (research/insurance-quote-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- distraction-free-writing-application (§03.01, processed) vs markdown-editor (§03.01 sibling, unprocessed): overlap flag — the commercial flagship distraction-free writing apps (iA Writer, Ulysses) draft in Markdown with preview, and several products are positioned in both camps, so the two leaves share products; discriminator adopted this pass: the attention-preserving composition surface as the product's central promise (chrome hidden/on-demand, drafting primacy, formatting deferred) vs markup source handling as the central object (syntax, preview, live rendering); when markdown-editor is processed, apply the whose-central-promise test and decide keep-both with the promise-vs-markup seam or a shared-family note; related anti-case recorded: a word processor offering a full-screen toggle inside a chrome-heavy formatting-first interface is not this Type (research/distraction-free-writing-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- collections-platform (§08, processed 2026-09-07) RESOLVES the collision flag raised by collections-automation-platform: "Collections Platform" and "Collections Automation Platform" are distinct Types sharing an abstract shape (money-owed population + recorded pursuit + money-state outcome loop) but differing in object class — open trade invoices staged by due-date aging, fed from ERP/accounting books (B2B AR collections automation) vs delinquent repayment obligations on credit accounts staged by missed payments/days past due, fed from servicing/core books (creditor delinquency collections & recovery with arrangements/hardship/charge-off/recovery machinery); the two research samples share zero products and the populations use distinct vocabularies (dunning/DSO/credit-to-cash vs delinquency/settlement/charge-off/recovery); recommendation recorded: keep both leaves as distinct Types with the object-class boundary — joint review available to confirm. ADDITIONALLY flagged for the unprocessed Debt Collection Management pass: platform families straddle the first-party/third-party seam (Qualco QCR's client roster includes debt purchasers Intrum/Hoist Finance/Cabot/doValue; Finvi sells Katabat to first-party lenders and Velosidy/Simplicity to collection agencies; C&R Debt Manager markets vendor oversight of agencies/law firms) — that leaf's core should anchor on the agency-native object model (placed/purchased accounts, creditor-client portals, skip tracing, contingency economics) rather than platform family membership; joint review recommended

- construction-document-management (§17, processed 2026-09-07) vs engineering-document-management (§16 sibling, unprocessed): same object family (register + revisions + controlled access) with the seam drawn on custody and consumption — construction = the multi-party project's cross-organization issue and field consumption (owner/contractor/subcontractor parties, site access, markups, as-built record); engineering = the design/EPC organization's authoring-side deliverable vault; products straddle the seam (a construction platform's document tool can serve the engineering org; CAD-vault products reach into project distribution), and construction-document-management was NOT sampled against a ProjectWise-class product (unreachable/not retried per network rule), so the engineering side of the boundary rests on market-structure reasoning only; when engineering-document-management is processed, apply the custody/consumption test from both sides and consider a joint review (research/construction-document-management.md §Boundary Findings)
- cycling-application (§28, processed 2026-09-07) — sibling-seam note: Running Application (§28, unprocessed) shares the identical record→analyze→share skeleton with a different sport data model (pace/cadence/stride + shoes vs speed/elevation + bikes/components/bike-type routing); Cycling Application kept as a separate Type because §28 deliberately enumerates sport-specific applications, but the running-application pass should apply the same sport-semantics discriminator and a joint review across the sport-family leaves (Running / Cycling / Swimming Training / Endurance Training) would keep the family consistent; secondary: segment/leaderboard competition on real-world stretches is the identity-defining feature of one sampled vendor but absent from the rest of the sample — documented as variant, later sport-family passes should not promote it to definitional

- dj-software (§04.12, processed) vs live-music-performance-software (§04.12 sibling, unprocessed): same Family, both perform live — the discriminator held from the DJ side is the working material (mixing finished recorded tracks vs performing musical material the user authors/prepares as clips/patterns/instruments), the same seam the DAW pass (2026-09-07) flagged from the production side ("DJ software performs finished tracks; live performance software centers the show"); clip-launch DAWs and DJ products' loopers/samplers blur the seam at the edges; joint review recommended when live-music-performance-software is processed — that pass should also decide whether automation-first surfaces (Auto DJ/Automix) and the hardware-ecosystem export posture (library prepared on computer, performed from standalone club players via USB/cloud) are best documented inside DJ Software as variants or as separately named Types

- cyber-risk-quantification (§15, processed 2026-09-07) — convergence flag toward Governance Risk & Compliance Platform (§11 sibling, unprocessed): CRQ products increasingly ship the register workflow itself ("CRQ-powered cyber risk register" with owners/response plans/workflow integration; one sampled vendor markets a "Putting the R in GRC" use case), so the quantified-risk-register surface overlaps the GRC register; discriminator adopted this pass: the probabilistic frequency×magnitude financial engine beneath the register (remove it and the product is a GRC register, not CRQ); when GRC-type leaves are processed, decide keep-both-with-seam vs capability-of-suite presentation for CRQ-powered registers; secondary note: suite-embedded quantification modules (GRC/ERM platforms shipping CRQ modules) were not sampled this pass — the canonical model is asserted to hold for them by inference, not direct evidence

- insurance-underwriting-platform (§08, processed 2026-09-07) vs underwriting-workbench (§08 sibling, unprocessed): probable alias — the sampled market uses "underwriting workbench", "underwriting platform", and "underwriting orchestration engine" for the same product population: Send's own FAQ describes the product as "an underwriting workbench and orchestration engine" and a carrier customer's testimonial names it "the Send Underwriting Workbench" while the same company markets it as the "AI-native underwriting orchestration platform"; Sapiens' product page is titled "Underwriting Workbench" and self-describes as "a future-proof underwriting platform"; Zinnia markets The Policy Processor as a "cloud-based underwriting platform" while its own published evaluation framework names "the underwriter workbench" as the decision surface; the defensible split is naming-perspective (workbench = the underwriter's decision surface; platform = the same product across the intake→decision→post-bind lifecycle), and no distinct product population was found for a second Type — recommend joint review/merge when underwriting-workbench is processed; secondary notes from this pass: the insurance-policy-administration-system pass's whose-decision flag is DISCHARGED (decision machinery vs contract record confirmed in vendor packaging — Duck Creek sells Policy and Send separately, Sapiens sells IDITSuite and the workbench separately, Zinnia TPP ends at issue handoff into policy administration), the insurance-quote-platform pass's underwriting seam is confirmed, and Duck Creek's separate "Agentic Underwriting Workbench" agentic app vs Send is a post-acquisition vendor-internal naming overlap rather than two market products (research/insurance-underwriting-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- commercial-banking-platform (§08, processed) vs cash-management-platform (§08, processed) — breadth-overlap flag from the cash-management pass DISCHARGED INTO JOINT REVIEW: the two leaves overlap to near-alias in the live market — at most sampled banks the same product instantiates both directory leaves (WF Vantage is the commercial division's treasury platform; HSBCnet spans treasury channel and relationship breadth in one profile), while at one sampled bank they are genuinely different products (JPMorganChase: Access = corporate treasury channel under the Payments organization vs Connect = commercial-division relationship platform spanning deposit + loan + credit card + merchant services accounts); the adopted working distinction is channel-within-relationship (cash management = the treasury-operations channel; commercial banking platform = the relationship container whose treasury channel is the largest module family), with credit-relationship servicing as the modern observable discriminator — but credit is deliberately NOT definitional (absent from the treasury-channel pole and from pre-web platforms; historical check passed), so a merge-vs-keep-both decision is recommended in joint review; second: the business-banking-portal tier seam is CONFIRMED held (two additional banks observed selling structurally separate tier platforms — JPM Connect/Access vs Chase business surfaces, ANZ Transactive Global vs its "other business banking options"); third: commercial-loan-origination + commercial-loan-management (both unprocessed) own the loan lifecycle — this leaf only surfaces and services held credit (loan accounts, e-statements, paydowns); joint review recommended when those leaves are processed (research/commercial-banking-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- dance-studio-management (§28, processed) — vertical-family taxonomy flag: market evidence shows ONE product family (class-management software for children's activity businesses) realized per vertical — the same spine (family account holding students, scheduled recurring classes, enrollment, tuition loop, attendance, parent/staff portals) is sold unchanged as Jackrabbit Dance/Class/Swim/Cheer/Music editions, The Studio Director industries (dance/cheer/gymnastics/fitness/martial arts/music/pilates/yoga/youth sports), Studio Pro solutions (dance/cheer/gymnastics/theatre/martial arts), and iClassPro industries (gymnastics/cheer/swim/dance); verticals differ mainly in signature extensions (dance: costumes/recitals/competition teams). The directory slices this family into separate leaves (Dance Studio Management, Martial Arts School Management, Swim School Management, Gymnastics Club Management, Fitness Studio Management, and adjacent Sports Academy/Club leaves). This pass held the boundary by documenting the dance realization (defining core kept at the shared spine, dance layer described as standard extension, not definition), but a family-level joint review across the sibling vertical leaves is recommended when they are processed to decide keep-both-with-seam vs variant presentation. Secondary seam: vs Fitness Studio Management the boundary is structural (family/guardian-child season tuition vs adult membership/drop-in) precisely because vendors literally sell one product into both markets.

- digital-credential-platform (§23, processed) — joint-review flag for the transcript-management pass: the credential-platform pass found the transcript/credential overlap structural, not incidental — credential platforms aggregate earner-presentable transcripts (one sampled product ships a registrar-consumable transcript guide; another markets digital credential transcripts), and record-exchange suites now embed badging outright (Badgr consolidated into Parchment Award, which issues "transcripts and diplomas to digital badges, CLRs, and certificates"); recorded seam: registrar-of-record authority (official academic record exchanged to authorized requesters) vs earner-presentable issuer-attested artifact (verified by anyone, presented by the earner); when transcript-management is processed, apply the whose-record/whose-audience test and consider joint review with this leaf (research/digital-credential-platform.md §Boundary Findings); secondary note for the LMS pass: LMS-native course-completion badging (Canvas-credentials class, documented as an integration trigger in two sampled credential platforms) is a capability, not this Type — the cross-program system-of-record test (issuer credential taxonomy + hosted verification + post-issuance lifecycle outside the course container) separates them
- intellectual-property-management (§11, processed) — in-family seam note for three unprocessed sibling leaves: Patent Management, Patent Prosecution Management, and Trademark Portfolio Management share the identical defining core of this leaf (IP asset record + deadline/docket tracking + recorded lifecycle); the observed market difference is asset-type scope and workflow emphasis, not structure — sampled products straddle the seam themselves (one vendor's platform ships Patent Management and Trademark Management as modules of a single system; another's single product dockets patents, trademarks, and copyrights together; a third self-titles "Prosecution Manager" while functioning as a full IPMS); when those three leaves are processed, apply the asset-type-scope test (narrowing the right type must not change the core model) and consider joint review / possible variant-or-alias treatment rather than four fully independent Types; secondary seams recorded in research/intellectual-property-management.md §Boundary Findings: vs Legal Matter Management (IP legal-time dimension — renewal/annuity law, jurisdiction-aware response windows, family/priority structure — is the discriminator) and vs Legal Docket Management (docketing is the deadline layer inside this Type; standalone docketing without the asset system of record is the narrower form); name collision flagged: Renewal Management Platform (customer subscriptions) vs IP renewals (government fees) share only the word

- dark-web-monitoring (§15, processed) vs digital-risk-protection (§15 sibling, unprocessed): heaviest bundling seam in this domain — the market packages underground-source monitoring and clear-web brand protection together (DRP suites, "external threat intelligence" analyst category), but vendors themselves keep the two separable (one sampled suite sells "Deep & Dark Web Monitoring" and "Digital Risk Protection" as distinct pillars; another sells "Dark Web Monitoring" and "Brand Intelligence & Protection" as distinct solutions) — adopted discriminators: subject's exposures surfacing in hidden/illicit source economies (this leaf) vs clear-web brand impersonation/phishing/social abuse plus the takedown workflow (DRP); apply the source-scope removal test when digital-risk-protection is processed and consider joint review; secondary consistency flags: dark web monitoring commonly ships as a module of Threat Intelligence Platforms (both sampled TIPs realize it as a module/solution — recommend the threat-intelligence-platform pass treat it as an embedded capability, not a duplicate leaf) and consumer dark web monitoring ships as an alert-source inside identity-theft-protection bundles (no separate consumer Type recommended) (research/dark-web-monitoring.md §Boundary Findings)

- robo-advisor (§08, processed 2026-09-07) — joint-review flag from retirement-planning-application DISCHARGED from this side: boundary held structurally (household plan + multi-decade projection + sufficiency evaluation = that Type; managed-portfolio construction/execution = this Type); the embedded-planner capability-overlap pattern confirmed (sampled robos embed retirement/goal planners as standard capability while the object of record remains the managed portfolio); open item for the wealth-management-platform pass (unprocessed): the advice-spectrum seam (robo = low-touch automated pole vs advisor-led comprehensive practice) plus the hybrid-advice-tier pattern (sampled robos ship premium human-advice tiers) should be decided there; secondary convergence note for brokerage-family passes: sampled robos and brokerages now ship each other's modes inside one brand (robos add self-directed trading; brokerages embed managed programs operated by affiliated registered-adviser entities) — the decision-authority test (who constructs and maintains the portfolio) held across all five sampled products (research/robo-advisor.md §Boundary Findings)

- commercial-loan-management (§08, processed) — two joint-review flags for the lending family: (1) vs Loan Management System (§08, unprocessed) + Consumer Lending Platform (§08, unprocessed): the directory splits one servicing family by sector, but the market sells single engines spanning consumer + commercial books (sampled servicing vendor explicitly sells one platform across both, with commercial as a solution line over the same system) — adopted working distinction: commercial = facility-shaped business credit population (commitments/lines/participations) under negotiated terms, servicing loop shared; when loan-management-system is processed, apply the population test (narrowing the sector must not change the core model) and consider variant/alias treatment vs full Type; (2) vs Commercial Loan Origination (§08, unprocessed): funding seam confirmed (origination = pre-funding pipeline; loan management = post-funding servicing ledger), but packaging blurs — origination-led cloud suites market "from origination to monitoring" lifecycle language while documenting no payment/accrual/servicing-ledger capability, and the analyst category itself is named "corporate loan lifecycle management" — when commercial-loan-origination is processed, apply the funded-position test (is a servicing ledger documented?) and consider joint review; secondary: partial discharge of the commercial-banking-platform pass flag (this pass confirms the loan lifecycle is owned by loan-lifecycle systems on the bank-staff side; the banking platform only surfaces/services held credit client-side; sibling portal packaged separately by the strongest-servicing vendor) (research/commercial-loan-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- childcare-management-system (§29, processed) vs daycare-preschool-management (§29 sibling, processed) — JOINT REVIEW DISCHARGED (daycare-preschool-management pass): alias / segment-slice CONFIRMED — one market family behind two directory names; fresh label-architecture evidence: brightwheel runs "#1 childcare management software" (root H1) and "#1 preschool management software" (segment-page H1) on one product whose preschool page cross-references "childcare management software" as the same category; illumine carries childcare/daycare/preschool labels plus a single FAQ definition ("helps preschools, daycares, and childcare centers run daily operations, including attendance, billing, enrollment, parent communication, and learning records") on one product; Procare ("daycare, preschool, Head Start or ECE center" — one product line), Smartcare (Childcare & Daycare Centers and Preschool & Early Childhood Programs as segments of one product), Kangarootime and Lillio (both segments interchangeably) corroborate from the sibling pass; Famly maps UK regional naming (nursery management software; childminders = home-based segment) onto the same structure; daycare vs preschool = emphasis poles (care logistics vs learning layer), learning tooling sold across the whole base, no school-of-record semantics observed in preschool segments; both leaves stand with separate lens documents (digital-whiteboard/collaborative-canvas precedent) — merge/alias/canonical-name decision escalated to directory-level review; recommendation: consolidate under one Type name with the other as an alias/segment note (research/daycare-preschool-management.md §Boundary Findings #1)

- internal-audit-management (§11, processed 2026-09-07) vs audit-assurance-platform (§11 sibling, processed) — MANDATORY JOINT REVIEW FLAG DISCHARGED (internal-audit-management pass): resolved as gradient overlap, NOT alias — verdict: both leaves stand as distinct Types with declared overlap; evidence: at product level the categories nearly coincide on the internal-audit side (two of four products sampled here — Optro, Ideagen — were sampled by the audit-assurance pass and self-describe as internal audit software; the dominant "audit management software" category IS internal-audit software), but the two leaves pick out different invariants: audit-assurance-platform = the side-agnostic engagement-execution spine (engagement → evidence/workpapers → findings → assurance output; its Caseware firm-side sample proves the Type with no standing program), internal-audit-management = the standing program of an in-house audit function (universe → risk-based plan → engagements → organization-wide findings ledger → governance reporting; firm-side or one-off engagement execution does not satisfy it; program-level machinery absent from the sibling's core) — neither core is contained in the other; the market sells one product family instantiating both layers and the directory's leaves describe different layers of that family; sibling boundary statement remains valid as written; recommendation: future §11 audit-family passes (governance-risk-compliance-platform, controls-management-platform, compliance-management-platform) cross-reference both documents to avoid re-divergence (research/internal-audit-management.md §Joint Review Resolution)

- digital-library-platform (§23, processed 2026-09-07) vs institutional-repository (§23 sibling, unprocessed): the market does not cleanly separate the two labels — DSpace, the canonical institutional-repository product, is equally the canonical digital-collections platform, and vendor positioning spans both (repository software hosting digitized heritage collections); this pass treats IR as a deployment/variant of the Digital Library Platform Type (scholarly-output scope + submission workflows + open-access machinery as the differentiating emphasis), but the institutional-repository leaf deserves joint review when processed to ratify keep-both-with-seam vs variant presentation; secondary seams recorded: vs Integrated Library System (§23) and Library Discovery Platform (§23) as ecosystem partners (collection host vs circulation operations vs cross-source search layer; delivery into OPAC/Primo-class surfaces and catalog/WorldCat sync documented as integration seams, not type identity), vs Archives Management System (§23) (public digital delivery vs finding-aid description; overlap via EAD finding-aid ingest and ArchivesSpace connectors — one sampled product accepts EAD files as items, another ships an ArchivesSpace connector)

- e-book-library-application (§02.09, processed 2026-09-07) vs e-book-reader (§02.09 sibling, unprocessed) and reading-library-application (§02.13, unprocessed): three confusable leaves recommended for joint review when the siblings are processed — sampled evidence shows reading-tracker functionality (want-to-read, finished with auto-detection on reaching the end, reading goals, progress) shipping as a standard capability INSIDE e-book libraries, so the tracker-alone product (records reading activity, may hold no book files at all) is the plausible distinct Type, and the reader/library pair splits on center of gravity; working discriminators adopted for this pass: E-book Library = holds book entries and makes them readable (collection management is the center of gravity), E-book Reader = the reading surface for one opened book (remove the collection → reader; remove the reading surface while keeping catalog + handoff → still a library), Reading Library Application = reading record/wishlist without the files; secondary note: comic/manga server products (Kavita-class) are a content-breadth variant of this Type, not a separate one (research/e-book-library-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- robotic-process-automation-platform (§10, processed 2026-09-07) — TWO OPEN FLAGS DISCHARGED (RPA pass): (1) desktop-automation-application joint-review flag CONFIRMED from the RPA side — same mechanism family, discriminator = ownership/scale: RPA's defining core centers the managed estate (publish → central control plane → registered machines/robot identities → triggered, monitored, governed executions) while desktop automation keeps authoring+execution local and user-owned; Power Automate reconfirms the bridge-product analysis from this side (its desktop-flow authoring layer is desktop-automation machinery; machine registration/groups/unattended bots/capacity/monitoring/security roles are the RPA layer; Microsoft's own docs frame desktop flows as "broadening the existing RPA capabilities"; Blue Prism ships a separate light "Desktop" product, corroborating the two-layer market framing); removal tests hold both ways — no merge, boundary is structural not vendor-level; (2) agent-tool-computer-use-platform flag RPA half CONFIRMED from the RPA side — runtime decision-maker boundary holds: UiPath ships Agents/Maestro as a separate agentic layer orchestrating "AI agents, automations, and people" with automations remaining a distinct deterministic instrument; Automation Anywhere's own FAQ draws the same line ("AI agents rely on RPA to provide the execution layer"); in-product AI features (Healing Agent, Automator AI) act on authoring/resilience, never as the runtime task decision-maker — both vendors police the boundary in their own docs; the agentic-suite bundling pattern mirrors the Copilot Studio observation (mechanism-level boundary, not vendor-level); secondary seams recorded for future passes: vs BPM/Workflow Management (§10 siblings, unprocessed) — executes machine-performed steps vs orchestrates processes (Blue Prism's "resource… human, or more commonly, machine" wording shows RPA managing the machine performer); vs Process Mining/Task Mining (§10/§13) — execution vs discovery, bundled by all sampled vendors as packaging; vs Test Automation Platform (§12) — same machinery, different job, vendor-policed via separate test product lines (research/robotic-process-automation-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- construction-labor-management (§17, processed 2026-09-07) — seam with Construction Field Management (§17, processed same day): both carry crew timesheets and the field pass noted the labor-population seam from its side; discriminator recorded this pass — field management's defining core is the day record + field work items (timesheets feed the day record there), labor management's is the worker population + tracked placement (the worker/time record IS the product here) — recommend joint review if either leaf is revised; secondary family-edge note: pure construction time-tracking products satisfy the labor core via recorded placement alone and sit between this Type and Time & Attendance System / Employee Scheduling Platform / Workforce Management Platform (§09) — the relationship is industry specialization and the taxonomy keeps both levels, but pure time-capture products are better filed as T&A variants; coverage note: LaborChart (prominent "workforce management for construction" product) unreachable during research (404/transport), so the planning pole is evidenced by Bridgit Bench alone — revisit if that pole's evidence is ever contested

- destination-discovery-application (§26, processed 2026-09-07) vs travel-itinerary-planner (§26 sibling, unprocessed): heaviest seam in the travel family — the two Types overlap structurally (planner-first products carry a full destination/place discovery layer as their explore phase; sampled evidence shows discovery ships both standalone — publisher/guide sites — and embedded in planners) but the primary-record discriminator held both ways in this pass's removal tests: remove the trip/itinerary machinery → a destination catalog still stands (this Type); remove the destination catalog and only a trip workspace remains (planner); recommend the itinerary-planner pass adopt the primary-record test and treat discovery-layer-inside-planner as layered packaging, not a duplicate leaf; secondary: travel-review-platform (§26, unprocessed) realizes destination pages as aggregation context over review records — same test applies from that side; single-destination official tourism sites are the degenerate one-record case, excluded from this Type by the multi-destination catalog requirement (research/destination-discovery-application.md §Boundary Findings)

- internal-knowledge-search (§10, processed 2026-09-07) vs enterprise-search-platform (§10, processed 2026-09-06) — joint review DISCHARGED from the Internal Knowledge Search side, resolving the flag recorded in the ESP pass: overlap confirmed from this side too — all five sampled IKS products (Guru, Glean, Onyx, Slite, Stack Internal) satisfy the ESP defining core (multi-source estate → ingestion → one query surface → merged results → access control); verdict: Internal Knowledge Search is best treated as a scope/emphasis Variant of Enterprise Search Platform (knowledge-content corpus + answer-first delivery + knowledge-trust layer as the current market's central discipline + KB-ownership pole) rather than a structurally independent Type — both leaves documented as the directory defines them, merge/canonical-name decision escalated to taxonomy maintainers; secondary observations: population naming is fluid (sampled vendors self-describe as "enterprise AI search"/"AI knowledge base"/"trusted knowledge layer"/"open source AI platform" — none markets primarily under the literal leaf name, further supporting Variant status), permission-mirroring is weaker in this population than the ESP sample (one product offers a product-scoped access model explicitly independent of source ACLs; another gates permission-aware retrieval to its enterprise edition), and convergence with Enterprise Knowledge Assistant (§13) continues (research/internal-knowledge-search.md §Boundary Findings)

- community-platform (§01.06, processed 2026-09-07) — DISCHARGES two flags from this side: (1) research-panel-platform's §01.06 straddle flag — the recorded structural test (operator-structured research participation vs member-initiated conversation/content) holds with direct evidence: none of the four sampled community platforms structures participation as research tasks; ideation/product-feedback modules exist as capabilities but the organizing structure remains the member conversation container, so insight communities stay documented as a panel-platform variant; (2) community-chat-platform's joint-review flag — no sampled community platform is chat-centric; chat appears only as a side surface (Discourse chat channels explicitly subordinate to topics, Circle chat alongside spaces) while the primary object is asynchronous content under an operated container; the live-rooms-vs-async-content seam holds; market corroboration: Hivebrite ("Community platform vs chat tools (like Slack & Discord)" resource), Vanilla FAQ ("Many online communities start as Slack channels or LinkedIn groups… give your community a home"), and Discourse (compare pages vs Slack/Discord/Reddit; customer quote "if you want the conversation forgotten, put it on Slack. If it matters, put it on Discourse") all police the seam themselves (research/community-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- community-platform (§01.06, processed) vs §01.06 siblings unprocessed: (1) online-forum — ALIAS-RISK: the sampled market straddles (Discourse self-describes as both "community platform" and "forum software"; organizations have run customer communities on classic forum software for two decades); defensible structural line recorded: forum = standing public venue organized around boards/topics with typically open registration; community platform = operated container with managed membership + multiple surface families + operator management and engagement measurement; nesting board⊂forum⊂community-platform; removal tests hold both ways (remove operator/management → public forum remains; strip to boards only → forum remains; community platform without forum boards → still a community platform); candidate outcomes for the online-forum pass: keep-both on venue-vs-container emphasis or documented overlap zone; (2) private-community-platform — VARIANT-RISK: gated/private access is a configuration of this Type (Higher Logic markets "private, secure communities" as its default posture; Discourse supports public-indexed and invite-only modes; Hivebrite markets "private community platform" as a positioning of the same product) — alias/variant candidate for its pass; (3) interest-community-platform — VARIANT-RISK: audience-axis variant (interest communities are frequently run ON community platforms) — flag for its pass; (4) q-a-community — format-vs-container seam (Q&A exists as a capability inside community platforms: Higher Logic "Q&A and discussions", Discourse accepted-answers plugin); (5) member-community-platform (§25) — segment realization of this Type, joint review recommended; (6) paid-community-platform (§27) — the fulfillment-structure seam recorded by the creator-cluster passes applies (purchase→venue access organizes there; monetization is a 2/4 variant capability here) — joint review recommended (research/community-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- community-platform sourcing limitation: Circle help center (help.circle.co, docs.circle.co) unreachable (transport errors ×2 each) and Hivebrite /product-overview/ 403 on 2026-09-07 — Circle and Hivebrite evidence is official-product-page level only; no operational mechanics (role models, moderation internals, plan gating) asserted for those products; no numeric limits anywhere in the final doc (recorded in Sources of applications/community-platform.md)

- account-management-crm (§07, processed 2026-09-07) vs customer-relationship-management-crm (§07 sibling, unprocessed): family-overlap flag — all four sampled products are recognizably CRMs with the account as one of the canonical CRM objects; this leaf stands on center of gravity (the standing customer-organization record as the organizing spine + ongoing relationship-stewardship emphasis) rather than on structurally disjoint machinery, so joint review with the generic CRM leaf is recommended when it is processed (candidate outcomes: keep-both with an account-vs-person/deal center-of-gravity seam, or variant presentation of the leaf); secondary notes: (1) in some market corners "account management software" denotes agency/client-account management (PSA-adjacent) — not evidenced in this sample, left for the PSA pass; (2) Salesforce official docs unreachable (403) so the market's most-cited canonical Account implementation is carried by the Dynamics 365/Dataverse enterprise-pole evidence only; parent-child account hierarchies claimed from a single product's direct evidence and worded accordingly (research/account-management-crm.md §Boundary Findings)

- destination-management-company-platform (§26, processed 2026-09-07) — joint-review flag vs tour-operator-management-system (§26, unprocessed): the two leaves name heavily overlapping software populations — one sampled vendor ships separate "Inbound Tour Operator Software" and "Destination Management Company Software" solutions as one product family, another addresses "DMCs, travel designers, travel advisors & inbound tour operators" as a single audience, and "inbound tour operator" is a market synonym for DMC; candidate outcomes recorded for that pass: keep-both on center of gravity (destination-local service assembly for trade clients operated on the ground vs package production and distribution to travellers) or documented overlap zone; secondary flag vs travel-agency-management-system (§26, unprocessed): principal-with-margin vs commission-intermediary money models — quoting features overlap but fulfillment responsibility and the two-sided money record do not; sourcing limitation: TourOffice (dedicated Swedish DMS) unreachable (3 empty responses), WETU/TourWriter help centers transport errors, Tourplan DMC solution page/FAQs 404, travelbox.cloud resolved to an unrelated French vendor — all four sampled products evidenced at official product/marketing-page level only; no procedure-level rules or numeric limits asserted anywhere (research/destination-management-company-platform.md §Boundary Findings, §Uncertainties)

- construction-materials-management (§17, processed 2026-09-07) vs Dispatch Management / Transportation Management System (§18, unprocessed): watch-item — the bulk-material hauling pole (producer-side dump-truck logistics: dispatch boards, loads, GPS cycle tracking, e-ticketing, delivered tons vs ordered) is documented inside Construction Materials Management because its object of record is material quantity against orders/jobs rather than trucks/carriers, but the machinery overlap is real and the TMS/Dispatch pass should treat this seam jointly; source-access note for the Type: the GC field-side delivery-management pole (StruxHub) and the materials-procurement pole (Kojo) were unreachable (transport errors ×2 each) and the classic EPC material-control suite (Hexagon Smart Materials) returned 403/JS-gated docs, so delivery-appointment scheduling and supplier-quote-comparison machinery are unasserted in the final document and the EPC pole is carried by Track'em evidence only (research/construction-materials-management.md §Boundary Findings, §Uncertainties)

- sales-call-coaching-platform vs conversation-intelligence-platform (§07 sibling, unprocessed): sharpest seam in the family — both capture and analyze sales conversations (recording, transcription, topics, scorecards); working split adopted this pass = primary object/end product (managed seller-development loop with tracked coaching activity vs org-scale conversation analytics/market insight as the end product); almost every CI product embeds coaching modules and coaching products embed analytics, so the boundary is by primary job, not features — flagged for joint review when Conversation Intelligence Platform is processed (research/sales-call-coaching-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- sales-call-coaching-platform vs contact-center-quality-management (§07 sibling, unprocessed): same evaluation machinery (recorded interactions + scoring forms + coaching) — split adopted this pass by population and criteria (sales reps coached against sales-skill/revenue criteria vs support agents evaluated against service-quality/compliance criteria, usually inside contact-center suites with calibration workflow); closest cross-family pair, flagged for joint review when Contact Center Quality Management is processed

- sales-call-coaching-platform sourcing limitation: Salesloft help center (404/JS-rendered) and Second Nature help desk (Pylon, JS-only) unreachable — both evidenced at official product-page level only with weakened operational claims; Chorus/ZoomInfo (help.zoominfo.com, chorus.ai) returned 403 ×2 and was dropped from the sample rather than filled from memory; whether first-class "coaching plans" are a standard object remains unverified (kept out of the standard-capability list as a named object; the routing/tracking function is evidenced)
- internal-talent-marketplace (§09, processed 2026-09-07) — joint-review notes: (1) vs career-development-platform (§09, processed) — that pass flagged the internal-opportunity-marketplace seam as bundled-adjacent; DISCHARGED from this side: object-of-record discriminator adopted (employee-owned development plan anchored to paths/competencies vs managed opportunity population with governed placement workflow); vendors bundle both as sibling sub-products (one sampled standalone vendor ships Mobility/Development/Gigs/Succession as separate product lines under one platform) — packaging, not type identity; (2) vs skills-management-platform (§09, unprocessed) — feeds-vs-consumes seam: skills ontology/inventory supplies marketplace matching; recommend that pass treat opportunity-less skills platforms as distinct from this Type; (3) vs succession-planning-platform (§09, unprocessed) — curated slate governance vs open expression of interest; linkage common (pipeline building appears on both sides); (4) vs applicant-tracking-system / recruiting-management-platform (§09, both processed) — internal candidates flow into requisition-managed hiring in suites; the marketplace does not claim requisition management and the ATS pass need not claim two-sided matching; (5) category naming drift recorded, not an alias problem: same referent sold as "talent marketplace" / "opportunity marketplace" / "project marketplace" / "AI for talent mobility" across the sample

- sales-compensation-management (§07, processed 2026-09-07) — two flags: (1) vs sales-performance-management (§07 sibling, unprocessed): this leaf is the operational payout core of the SPM umbrella — sampled vendors explicitly articulate the split ("ICM manages the payouts, SPM manages the entire sales strategy"), with SPM adding territory/quota planning and forecasting/insights as sibling products (Xactly Plan vs Incent; CaptivateIQ Planning vs Incentives); recommend joint review when that leaf is processed, candidate outcomes keep-both (focused payout system-of-record vs umbrella) or umbrella-with-core presentation; (2) name collision vs compensation-management-platform (§09, unprocessed): both say "compensation" but the objects differ structurally — incentive pay computed from credited sales outcomes under executable plans vs base-pay structures/merit cycles/workforce benchmarking; removal tests hold both ways (remove sales-outcome attribution → HR comp; remove pay calculation → target planning), the two should not be merged, and the §09 pass should carry a disambiguation note (research/sales-compensation-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- sales-compensation-management sourcing limitation: vendor help centers and docs domains unreachable on 2026-09-07 (docs.xactlycorp.com transport errors ×2, help.captivateiq.com ×1, performio.com + support.performio.com ×2 → Performio dropped from sample, replaced by QuotaPath) — all four sampled products evidenced at official product-page level only; internal object vocabularies, calculation-run states, approval chains, defaults and numeric limits unasserted in the final document; vendor performance statistics (accuracy %, volumes) recorded in research notes only, not reproduced (applications/sales-compensation-management.md Sources)

- compensation-management-platform — 2026-09-07 — organization pay-decisioning layer whose defining core is exactly four structures: the employee pay population (identified employee records carrying current pay, drawn from the org's HR system of record — a decisioning layer over people it does not register) + organization-defined compensation components/programs (base salary, bonus, stock/equity, incentive types — configuration of what can be awarded and under what rules) + the award proposal (authorized users — normally line managers — propose specific pay awards for specific employees, inside a governed cycle or as case-by-case adjustments) + governed determination closing on the pay of record (proposals validated against budgets/guidelines/equity → approval → finalized awards update the employee's pay record feeding HRIS/payroll — remove it and the Type collapses into surveys/reports; remove the proposal act → Payroll; remove programs+budgets → generic approval workflow); compensation cycles (focal/anniversary/periodic bases per Oracle user guide), top-down budget pools with live proposal validation, guidance layer (guideline ranges/matrices keyed to performance+market, auto-calculation models, anomaly guardrails), market benchmarking (native or data-provider integrations), pay-equity analysis (peer+demographic gap views), approval routing with role-dependent powers (comp managers: oversight/override/proxy/adjust-budgets), award communications + total-comp/total-rewards statements, scenario/cost modeling, off-cycle adjustments tied to HR events (hire/transfer/promote) + spot awards, effective-dated salary history, multi-currency, performance-data linkage as input only, HRIS/payroll write-back, audit trails, AI assistance are standard capabilities (AI common-not-definitional — spreadsheet-era merit cycles pass the historical check); variants: suite-embedded vs standalone-specialist-overlay packaging, component-scope poles (merit-centric vs total-comp STI+LTI+equity vs incentive-heavy), equity/LTI depth (vesting/cliffs), exec-comp privacy, sales-incentive planning drift seam, regulatory postures (EU Pay Transparency Directive, US disclosure), global multi-entity scale, cycle-cadence culture (focal/anniversary/periodic/continuous); deliberately NOT definitional: cycles/budgets/guidelines/equity dashboards/statements/AI/multi-currency (paper roster + salary schedule + manager merit recommendation form + approver posting to payroll ledger satisfy the core — historical check passed), and pay-range/grade/compa-ratio machinery NOT asserted (0/4 fetched sources verify it — uncertainty recorded); boundaries held: vs Payroll (decides vs executes — salary-basis→payroll-element handoff documented in Oracle Using Compensation guide), vs HRIS (record of what is vs decision cycle over it), vs Performance Management (ratings feed guidelines; evaluation is the neighbor's object), vs Sales Compensation Management (manager-proposed budget-governed awards vs transaction-driven commission calculation; beqom ships both under one suite — real adjacency, no conflict), vs Benefits Administration (enrollment vs pay awarding), vs Employee Recognition, vs FP&A budgeting (aggregate workforce cost vs employee-anchored awards); sample: Workday Compensation + Oracle Compensation (only Tier-1 user guide in sample: focal/anniversary/periodic cycles, plan-configured task model — Manage Budgets/Adjust Salary/Allocate Bonus/Allocate Stock/Communications/Approve, comp-manager override/proxy, admin "process and transfer approved workforce compensation to people's HR records") + SAP SuccessFactors Compensation + beqom (incentive-heavy standalone: STI/LTI/spot/exec/sales modules, top-down budgeting cascade, audit trails, HRIS-overlay integration); Payscale/Paylocity/HiBob/Salary.com unreachable (404/JS wall), SAP help + Workday community login-gated, search engines unusable → enterprise-skewed sample, SMB claims unasserted, precise limits/defaults unasserted (applications/compensation-management-platform.md Sources)

- content-aggregator (§02.08, processed) vs feed-reader / news-aggregator / personalized-content-feed (§02.08/§02.04, all unprocessed): intra-family seam = who assembles the item-level flow (product-side machinery vs user's subscription list vs per-user inference) plus scope (content kinds vs news-only); evidence: Feedspot runs a subscription RSS reader beside niche source catalogs in one company, Techmeme self-labels a 'tech news aggregator' (same machinery, narrower scope), AllTop's default view is shared with personal feeds as an optional layer; also CONFIRMS content-curation-platform's pending flag from this side (standing refilled stream + product-side selection vs persistent curated collection + curator — Techmeme/AllTop editors make final calls on a flow, not sets), so the §02.08 four-sibling family test now reads: collection+curator (curation) / stream+product-machinery (aggregator) / user-assembled subscription list (reader) / per-user inference (personalized feed); joint review recommended when each sibling is processed; Flipboard/Feedly unreachable so consumer-pole straddles (user-built magazines vs stream) unresolved (research/content-aggregator.md §Boundary Findings)

- data-center-infrastructure-management-dcim (§14, processed 2026-09-07) — sourcing limitation for the infrastructure-giant/enterprise poles: Schneider EcoStruxure IT (se.com + ecostruxureit.com 403 ×2), Nlyte (nlyte.com 403), and Eaton Brightlayer (not surfaced by reachable search) were all unverified, and Vertiv product catalogs are JS-gated (positioning text only) — the monitoring-led commercial-suite pole is carried by Sunbird evidence alone and the source-of-truth pole by NetBox alone; a future DCIM-adjacent pass (Hyperconverged Infrastructure Management, Server Management Platform, Capacity Management, IT Asset Management) that reaches Schneider/Vertiv/Nlyte/Eaton docs should re-verify whether real-time monitoring, work-order machinery, and energy/PUE are universal in commercial DCIM before treating them as standard capabilities (research/data-center-infrastructure-management-dcim.md §Uncertainties)
- sales-data-enrichment-platform (§07, processed 2026-09-07) vs contact-discovery-platform / sales-intelligence-platform / sales-prospecting-platform (§07 siblings, unprocessed): one market family behind multiple directory leaves — every sampled product ships discovery AND enrichment against the same data supply (Apollo People-search + Data Health Center; Lusha Prospecting endpoint + Person Enrichment; Cognism Sales Intelligence + CRM Enrichment product line; Clay Find/Audiences + waterfall), and vendors self-label the whole family "sales intelligence" (Lusha home page: "B2B data and intelligence layer"; Cognism flagship: "Sales Intelligence"), so vendor naming does not respect the directory split; adopted discriminator = direction of the loop (completing records the customer holds vs sourcing records it does not) with the enrichment-primary core defined in this pass; JOINT REVIEW recommended when contact-discovery-platform and sales-intelligence-platform are processed (candidate outcomes: keep-both on loop direction + primary job, or documented overlap zone); secondary observation: multi-provider waterfall is a capability (Apollo, Clay) not a Type invariant — only 2/4 sampled products ship it natively; sourcing limitation: ZoomInfo all four official domains unreachable (403/transport ×4), Cognism evidenced at marketing-page level only (help center timed out) — recorded in applications/sales-data-enrichment-platform.md Sources
