- competency-management-platform (§09, processed 2026-09-07) — flag for the skills-management-platform pass (§09 sibling, unprocessed): the competency/skills naming seam needs joint resolution — the sampled market mixes the two vocabularies at product level (Avilar titles its product "WebMentor Skills" under a "Competency Management System" umbrella; Kahuna alternates "skills management software" and "competency management software" across its pages; SAP/Oracle suites use "skills" only), so no clean product-level split exists in the sample; working resolution adopted by this pass: Competency Management Platform = the assessment-and-qualification process over an organization-defined model; Skills Management Platform's distinct pole = the skills ontology/inventory as a governed data asset supplying other systems (consistent with the internal-talent-marketplace pass's feeds-vs-consumes flag); candidate outcomes: keep-both with a process-vs-data-asset seam, or merge as one market family — recommend joint review when skills-management-platform is processed; secondary seams confirmed from this side: vs career-pathing-application (that pass's secondary seam DISCHARGED — competency management owns framework definition+assessment, pathing consumes as node requirements; TalentGuard and Kahuna both ship pathing/career modules separately), vs performance-management-platform (that pass's related-types entry confirmed — review cycle vs model+assessed standing; TalentGuard ships Performance as a separate module tied to the same standard), vs corporate-lms / employee-learning-platform (remedy seam: gaps flow to the LMS; completions do not confer standing — Kahuna explicit), vs succession-planning-platform + workforce-planning-platform (unprocessed consumers of readiness/gap data), vs certification-management (adjacent; credential tracking shipped as separate modules at TalentGuard and Kahuna)
- skills-management-platform (§09, processed 2026-09-07) — DISCHARGES the competency-management-platform pass's joint-review flag from this side: keep-both ratified on a center-of-gravity seam — Skills Management Platform manages the inventory as a data asset (taxonomy + per-person records + who-knows-what visibility; assessment is one input; role expectations optional — TechWolf and Gloat run no qualification process at all yet are unambiguous skills platforms), Competency Management Platform manages the assessment-and-qualification process over role-attached expectations (inventory as byproduct); the seam is a gradient, not a clean line — Kahuna-class operational products straddle it (product named Skills Manager, industry pages named competency management) and are cross-referenced in both documents; also confirms from this side the internal-talent-marketplace pass's feeds-vs-consumes flag (TechWolf lists internal mobility as a supply use case, Gloat's Talent Marketplace is a separate platform line — no opportunities in the skills Type) and the career-pathing/career-development library-instrumental-vs-primary seam; no directory change recommended

- construction-quality-management (§17, processed 2026-09-07) — deficiency-register machinery is shared across three leaves: Construction Field Management's field work item, this pass's non-conformance record, and the unprocessed Punch List Management register; this pass draws Construction Quality Management as the conformance loop (template-driven inspections against project requirements + non-conformance correction closed only on verified acceptance) vs Field Management's site-execution center (day record + general field items) and the Punch List leaf's expected handover-register center — JOINT REVIEW of construction-quality-management ↔ construction-field-management ↔ punch-list-management recommended when punch-list-management is processed; secondary: quality products commonly host punch machinery (one sampled platform ships quality tools and a punch tool side by side; the specialist labels its register "deficiency/work-to-complete punchlist"), so the punch/quality seam is bundling, not type fusion; tertiary: shared checklist engine across quality/safety/environmental (vendors ship one template library with regime-specific observation categories) — Construction Safety Management boundary confirmed on regime object, no merge (research/construction-quality-management.md §Boundary Findings)

- disposable-email-service (§01.02, processed 2026-09-07): taxonomy gap — account-based email aliasing/forwarding services (addy.io / SimpleLogin class: account + verified recipients, forwarding-first, no self-contained inbox; addy.io API confirmed to contain no inbox/messages surface) have no leaf under §01.02 Email Communication; they are structurally distinct from Disposable Email Service (issuance requires an identity and no inbox exists — not a variant), yet several such products market themselves with "disposable email" vocabulary, creating misclassification pressure; recommend a future leaf or explicit alias decision. Secondary adjacency: capture-style email-testing sandboxes (Mailtrap class) vs the developer/QA pole of disposable email (Mailsac/Mailinator class) share a buyer but differ in mechanism (intercept outgoing app mail vs issue receive-capable addresses) — cross-reference recommended when any email-testing leaf is processed.

- digital-product-commerce-platform (§27, processed 2026-09-07) vs Digital Goods Store / Digital Download Commerce Platform (§05.22, unprocessed): name-space overlap flag — the directory carries both this §27 creator-cluster leaf and §05.22 commerce-section leaves whose names cover the same activity ("digital goods store", "digital download commerce platform"); the researched market does NOT split by seller type (the same platforms serve creators, educators, and software companies within one product — merchant-of-record software platforms and indie creator storefronts sell the same core loop), so a creator-vs-generic split is unlikely to be a real seam; candidate outcomes when §05.22 is processed: keep-both with a buyer/storefront-facing vs seller/operations-facing seam (if §05.22 evidence shows a consumer-facing store product) or duplicate/alias resolution (if it shows the same seller-side tooling); recommend joint review, do not resolve unilaterally. Secondary: the Creator Storefront joint-review flag is DISCHARGED from this side — the fulfillment-structure test is confirmed bidirectionally (storefront = goods-centered with physical fulfillment machinery standard; digital-product platform = delivered file/key centered with storefront optional and physical outside the core; documented near-seam spectrum, keep-both recommended) (research/digital-product-commerce-platform.md §Boundary Findings)

- election-results-management (§24, processed 2026-09-07): (1) DISCHARGES the election-management-system pass's joint-review flag from the results side — the EMS/ERM seam is drawn at "prepares the vote" (definition → ballot styles → votable artifacts) vs "counts what was voted" (results intake → contest-scoped accumulation → adjudication/reconciliation → official outcomes → reporting); umbrella-labeling pressure confirmed bidirectionally: one sampled vendor (Clear Ballot) files its central-count tabulation product under the same "Election Management" nav bucket as ballot design, and vendors co-package both halves in one certified family — recommend the seam be ratified when voter-registration-system is processed; (2) realization note — in the US market the results half is mostly realized inside a certified voting system (standalone central-count, ENR-specialist and statewide-suite realizations exist); treated as a packaging variant, not separate Types; (3) EAC/ESTEP recognizes "election night reporting systems" as a certification technology family separate from VVSG voting systems — publication capability kept inside this Type; if a future pass argues for an ENR split, the tabulation/publication seam should be the proposed boundary


- data-fabric-platform (§13, processed 2026-09-07): (1) cross-check request REPEATED from the data-exchange pass — vs data-integration-platform and data-virtualization-platform (both unprocessed): the fabric population structurally overlaps the integration-suite population (one sampled namesake bundle ships integration+catalog+stewardship with no virtualization and no own store; another ships federation+warehousing), proposed split ratified this pass: fabric = estate-spanning unified metadata layer with integration+governance+delivery as functions of one system; integration platform = pipeline building/running as the center; virtualization platform = logical access technique as the center — joint review recommended when either leaf is processed; (2) naming collisions recorded: Microsoft's Fabric product is a unified SaaS analytics suite (lakehouse/warehouse/BI/notebooks over owned compute+storage) → lakehouse/analytics-platform family, NOT this Type despite the name (note for the future lakehouse-platform pass); NetApp's "data fabric" is storage-layer abstraction (§14 territory); both excluded from the sample on structural grounds; (3) taxonomy risk recorded: "data fabric" is marketing-loaded (one vendor explicitly frames it as an architecture, not software) and positioning labels are drifting ("logical data management", "business data fabric", "AI data layer") — the Type stands on the productized population, but future passes on warehouse/lakehouse/metadata leaves should not assume the label maps 1:1 to this directory leaf.

- e-book-reader (§02.09, processed 2026-09-07) — DISCHARGES the e-book-library-application pass's reader/library joint-review flag from this side: the adopted working discriminators hold with direct reader-side evidence — sampled readers (Apple Books, KOReader, Thorium Reader) all carry entry/bookshelf surfaces yet center on the one-opened-book reading session; KOReader's library layer is file-browser/history-grade while Apple embeds a full store library, and both remain recognizably readers; the removal tests hold both ways (remove the collection → a reader remains; remove the reading surface keeping catalog + handoff → still a library), so E-book Reader and E-book Library Application stand as separate Types with a declared straddle zone (store-first products embed both sides); the three-leaf joint review remains open only for Reading Library Application (§02.13, unprocessed tracker leaf); secondary boundary notes: vs PDF/Document Reader the seam is presentation semantics (book-reading position life + comfort re-layout of reflowable text vs faithful fixed-layout rendering of arbitrary documents) not file format — readers commonly open PDFs as content breadth and one sampled platform deliberately hands PDFs to the OS viewer; sourcing limitation: Google Play Books and Kobo unreachable (timeouts; ≥2 fails across both passes) and Thorium documentation sites unreachable (product-page evidence only) — the store-first cloud and device-companion poles are described generically with no product-level claims for unreachable products (research/e-book-reader.md §Boundary Findings, §Uncertainties)

- knowledge-base-application (§02.06, processed 2026-09-08) — DISCHARGES both carried joint-review flags. (1) vs help-center (§02.06, processed): keep-both RATIFIED with the seam REFINED from the KB side — the help-center pass proposed audience as the seam (HC external vs KB internal), but KB-side evidence shows the market's self-labeled "knowledge base software" is audience-agnostic machinery (Document360 public/private/mixed projects + per-audience workspaces; KBPublisher positions one product for customer-support AND internal-employee poles; Zendesk documents internal+external KBs as one machinery with user-segment visibility and itself migrated multibrand→single shared help center; Zendesk's own market guide typologizes the category as "employees, customers, or both"), so audience is a VARIANT axis of the KB Type, not its definition; the ratified seam is purpose & center of gravity — HC: external support publication, the reader-facing site is the product's center, success measured by deflection/resolution, contact affordances hand off to the support operation vs KB: the curated corpus and its authoring/ownership/review governance is the product's center, success measured by questions answered and knowledge kept current; removal tests recorded both directions (strip the corpus governance machinery from a help center → a static hand-published FAQ page, not a managed KB; strip the external support-publication purpose from a dual-audience tool → internal KB machinery remains, unambiguously KB — Guru/Tettra-class products have no reader-facing public site at all); a customer-facing KB deployment = KB machinery realizing the help-center purpose, which is why the market uses the labels interchangeably for that realization; packaging drives neither Type. (2) vs enterprise-wiki (§02.06, processed): keep-both RATIFIED — curated, owned, review-managed answer corpus with restricted authorship vs emergent interlinked page corpus with open member editing; market-language blur acknowledged (Slite self-labels "AI knowledge base", Confluence documents "use as a knowledge base", Zendesk's market guide lists wiki-adjacent products as KB software) but the organizing principles differ; both passes now record the same seam. Advance notes for unprocessed §02.06/§02.07 siblings: wiki-application (the KB/wiki seam is organizing principle, not audience — relevant to that pass's variant-vs-type decision) and product-documentation-portal (genre/lifecycle seam: question-driven, continuously maintained answer corpus vs release-versioned structured documentation; tooling overlap is vendor-declared — Document360 sells API documentation as a use case of the same tool). Taxonomy observation: the leaf name matches the market's own category label, but the market applies "knowledge base software" to both this Type and the Help Center realization — the directory's split is defensible on purpose/center-of-gravity, not on audience.

remove loop → static status list; remove handoff → worklog that never feeds the operation); jointly-held is load-bearing (1 alone = room status list; 2 alone = abstract schedule; 3 without 1+2 = generic task board; 1+2 without 3 = monitoring without work); historical check passed (paper-era room board + attendant assignment sheet + supervisor inspection slip + desk informed via the board satisfies the core — no mobile/cloud/PMS-integration/AI in the core; the inspected quality gate held common-mature NOT definitional since small properties run serviced→ready directly); market shape is two packagings of one core — the housekeeping module inside every full PMS and standalone PMS-integrated housekeeping-operations suites (sampled both; boundaries held: vs hotel-front-desk-application mirror-image axis split RATIFIED from this side (desk owns occupancy and consumes readiness, housekeeping owns readiness and consumes occupancy — the desk pass's cross-reference discharged), vs Hotel PMS keep-both (whole-property system of record vs servicing operations), vs Property Maintenance Management/CMMS (asset-repair work orders vs room-readiness servicing; - online-auction-platform — 2026-09-08 — the bidder-facing venue of the auction business whose defining core is exactly four jointly-held structures: the lot (item offered as an individually biddable unit whose price is discovered through competition rather than posted; remove → fixed-price marketplace/webstore) + the auction as bounded competition with a defined close (scheduled staggered lot closes or the live session's hammer; remove → always-open listings = marketplace) + the bid (recorded competing offer from an identified bidder, ordered by increment rules with the competition made visible; remove → anonymous interest poll) + the definite per-lot award (sold to the highest qualifying bidder at the final bid per the lot's terms / unsold or passed; remove → bid recorder, not a venue) — plus the participant-facing posture (users are bidders and sellers, not the operator's staff; remove → auction-management-system, the sibling); jointly-held is load-bearing (money loop deliberately NOT definitional — three placement patterns observed: platform checkout / seller invoicing / house-as-platform — the venue ends at the award + winner notification, the sharpest discriminator vs the AMS whose money loop IS definitional); reserves NOT definitional (charity pole sells to highest bid above opening bid with no separate reserve); soft-close extension NOT definitional (proxy-bid-only closing is a deliberate alternative mechanism); live webcast consoles NOT definitional (timed-only venues satisfy); marketplace aggregation NOT definitional (house-direct single-seller venue satisfies); historical check passed (paddle registration + absentee-bid book + hammer saleroom satisfies all four legs at analog level — the "Online" names the digitization of the bidder-facing participation layer, not a feature set; late-1990s timed online auctions satisfy with none of the modern machinery); standard capabilities NOT definitional: per-sale registration with approval/card-on-file/deposits/KYC, increments, max/proxy/absentee execution with hidden maximum, outbid notifications, reserves with not-met indicators, premium display + cost calculators, won-items dashboards, award contestability (seller discretion, disputes, next-highest-bidder reassignment on some venues), post-auction Buy-It-Now/Make-Offer channels, price archives, discovery machinery, mobile apps; market realizes ONE Type in poles — aggregator marketplace (Invaluable, LiveAuctioneers: Tier-1 help centers; per-sale registration with house approval, SecureBid-class hidden maxima, absentee-push tie-breaks, soft-close extension, BIN/Make-Offer on unsold lots, invoice from house OR platform), house-direct (Christie's: LIVE console "online saleroom", quick vs max bids, binding bids, soft close, cost calculator, financial references), charity (BiddingOwl: registration-required-no-card, proxy-only closing by design, opening-bid-as-reserve, cart checkout, next-highest-bidder reassignment, premium-as-platform-fee-offset); boundaries held: vs auction-management-system (§05.18 sibling — PRE-HUNG JOINT-REVIEW FLAG DISCHARGED from this side, boundary holds, removal tests both ways, money loop is the discriminator, bundling universal but non-merging, both leaves distinct), vs resale-marketplace (§05.19 — PRE-HUNG SEAM CONFIRMED: bidding is the defining mechanism here, fixed-price modes only secondary post-auction channels; eBay straddle carried as boundary anchor, unreachable ×2), vs online/multi-vendor-marketplace (posted price vs discovered price), vs classifieds (no venue-recorded award), vs e-sourcing (reverse direction), vs trading venues (instruments + settlement rails vs goods lots), vs fundraising-management (operator frame of the charity pole), vs event-management, vs ticket-resale-marketplace; sourcing limitation: consumer C2C pole (eBay), ATG industrial marketplaces (Proxibid/HiBid/the-saleroom/BidSpotter/EasyLive), Catawiki, GovDeals/PublicSurplus all unreachable (bot walls/403/405/JS shells/timeouts) — no claims about them, regional check structural only (research/online-auction-platform.md §Uncertainties)

- log-management — 2026-09-08 — the operational event-record system of record whose defining core is exactly three jointly-held structures: multi-source collection of timestamped log records emitted by other systems (agents/file shippers/syslog receivers/API endpoints/cloud integrations; remove → standalone shipper/forwarder) + a centralized persistent store organizing the accumulated corpus for retrieval (time-organized, source-attributed, retention-bounded, indexed or scanned; remove → pass-through pipe or ephemeral tail) + time-anchored search & examination over the corpus as the primary interaction (filter by time/source/content/fields, inspect entries, aggregate; remove → archive dump / search engine over nothing); jointly-held load-bearing (1+2 without 3 = compliance archive; 2+3 without 1 = manual imports with no operational corpus; 1+3 without 2 = live tail with no history); historical check passed (syslog-era central host + rotated files + grep satisfies all three legs; ELK-era shipper+store+search stack satisfies; indexing/parsing/alerting/dashboards/retention-tiers/RBAC/AI all era or common-NOT-definitional); standard capabilities NOT definitional: processing/parsing pipelines, retention tiering & archiving/forwarding-out, aggregation & pattern analytics, dashboards, log-condition alerting, saved searches, trace/metric correlation, RBAC/audit, metrics-from-logs (one-vendor-explicit → optional), data-quality views (one-vendor-explicit → optional), ML anomaly detection, AI query assistants; variants: self-hosted stack vs SaaS vs OSS-core+commercial, standalone pure-play vs observability-suite pillar vs SIEM substrate, full-text vs metadata-focused vs decoupled ingest/index, query-language style, syslog heritage; boundaries held vs APM/Distributed-Tracing/Infrastructure-Monitoring/Incident-Management (consistent with their processed passes); flags for unprocessed neighbors in Boundary Issues
- log-management (§14, processed 2026-09-08) vs metrics-monitoring (§14, unprocessed) — JOINT REVIEW RECOMMENDED: sharpest seam is the unit of record — log management holds individual timestamped event records inspected one-by-one; metrics monitoring holds numeric series evaluated over time; metrics-from-logs derivation (Datadog explicit, Sumo pre-aggregated views related) is the one-way bridge — once the object is a derived numeric series with its own query/alerting it has crossed into the sibling Type; shared alerting/dashboard/time-organized-storage vocabulary must not drive a merge
- log-management (§14, processed 2026-09-08) — flags for other unprocessed neighbors, no directory change from this side: SIEM (§15) must not treat log storage/search as SIEM-defining — vendors build SIEM ON the log corpus (Splunk Enterprise Security, Datadog Cloud SIEM "without requiring you to index logs", Graylog Security with Sigma rules/risk scores): same substrate, the seam is the security analytics/detection/investigation layer; observability-platform (§14) is the umbrella unifying metrics/logs/traces — log management is one pillar of such a suite, do not define the umbrella by any pillar; error-tracking-platform (§12) centers exceptions grouped/deduplicated into issues with release context vs the raw ungrouped record stream; event-stream-processing (§13) processes in motion vs persisting for retrieval (log products USE stream processors, e.g. pipeline shippers, but the terminus is the retrievable corpus)
